Longest mobile internet shutdown in Delhi's history eases as CJP withdraws protest
With the seventh extension that came on Saturday, mobile internet in the area remained repeatedly suspended for five days.

Delhi witnessed its longest internet shutdown during the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest demanding the resignation of (now former) education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. On Saturday morning, the government issued a seventh order extending the suspension of mobile internet services around Jantar Mantar until 12 midnight.

However, people in and around the affected area said mobile internet services were restored shortly after Pradhan announced his resignation on X and the CJP called off its protest, saying the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government had agreed to its demands.

The restoration came well before the scheduled midnight deadline for the suspension. Despite the restoration, telecom service providers (TSPs) had not received any formal order revoking the suspension until late Saturday evening, said people aware of the matter.

In the last five days, it was only on July 21 when the government did not issue a suspension order. With the seventh extension that came Saturday, mobile internet in the area remained repeatedly suspended for five days, making it the longest such disruption recorded in the national capital.
Also Read | Jantar Mantar protest: Delhi Police FIR includes charge of attempt to murder

The shutdown began on July 20, when the government directed TSPs, including Airtel, Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea, to suspend mobile internet services from 10 am to 6 pm in parts of central Delhi around Jantar Mantar. A second order followed on July 22, directing operators to suspend services from 6 pm until 6 am the next morning.

On July 23, the government first extended the suspension from 9.30 am to 4.30 pm before issuing another order extending it until midnight. On Friday, authorities again suspended mobile internet until noon before issuing a sixth order extending the shutdown till 12 midnight. On Saturday, a seventh order further extended the suspension till 12 midnight.

The orders require telecom companies to suspend mobile internet services within a 1.5-km radius of the protest site. Affected areas include Janpath Market near Connaught Place, Le Meridien, Shangri-La hotel, the National Media Centre and the Indian Women’s Press Corps office.

Digital rights organisation SFLC.in also challenged the internet shutdown orders before the Delhi High Court, arguing that the suspension of mobile internet services in parts of central Delhi during the July 2026 protests was unlawful.
While Delhi has seen internet shutdowns before, they have been shorter and linked to specific law-and-order situations.

One such instance was in December 2019, during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), when mobile internet services were suspended for several hours in parts of the capital. The shutdown was ordered by Delhi Police, which is empowered to direct telecom operators to suspend services under the temporary telecom suspension rules.

Another instance of internet shutdown occurred during the farmers’ protests in 2021. In January 2021, the government suspended mobile internet services in adjoining areas of Delhi. The suspension was later extended at some of the Delhi border protest sites, including Singhu, Ghazipur and Tikri, as the farmers’ agitation continued.
Unlike the 2019 and 2021 disruptions, the current shutdown was extended through multiple consecutive government orders over several days.

The repeated internet suspensions pushed protesters to look for alternative ways to communicate. Some turned to apps such as Bitchat Mesh, which do not depend on mobile internet. Instead, the app creates a Bluetooth-based mesh network that connects nearby users, allowing messages to be exchanged without an internet connection.

The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Home Ministry, also issued a notice to GitHub under section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, directing it to remove URLs hosting BitChat, said the messaging app’s founder Jack Dorsey on X on Friday.

Wangchuk responds to criticism

Dharmendra Pradhan resigns LIVE: Pradhan's exit joins short list of Modi govt's climbdowns since 2014

Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation on Saturday over the NEET paper leak controversy was not the sole instance when the Narendra Modi government yielded to sustained public or political pressure since coming to power in 2014.
The first major retreat came in 2015 when the government sought to amend the land acquisition law to make it easier to acquire land for infrastructure and industrial projects.

The move triggered widespread opposition from farmer organisations, opposition parties and several NDA allies, who argued that the changes diluted existing safeguards and were anti-people. The government eventually allowed the proposal to lapse. Modi announced that the existing law would remain unchanged.
Three years later came the first ministerial resignation under public pressure.

In October 2018, then minister of state for external affairs M J Akbar resigned during the Me Too movement after several women accused him of sexual harassment during his days as an editor. Akbar denied the allegations but stepped down.
The government's biggest policy reversal came in November 2021 when Modi announced the repeal of the three farm laws.

The laws triggered a yearlong agitation, with thousands of farmers camping at Delhi's borders demanding their withdrawal. Although the government consistently defended the reforms, it eventually gave in, with Parliament passing the repeal legislation.

In August 2024, the Centre withdrew a UPSC advertisement for lateral recruitment to senior civil services after objections from opposition parties and NDA ally Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) over the absence of reservation provisions.

Another retreat followed in November 2025 when the government decided against introducing the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill after facing strong political opposition, particularly from parties in Punjab, which argued that the proposal would dilute the state's political representation.
Pradhan's resignation on Saturday marks the latest instance of the government conceding to pressure.

Scientist and activist Sonam Wangchuk's wife Gitanjali Angmo questioned the heavy deployment of police in the hospital where he is admitting, claiming that the authorities are deciding who “may or may not meet him”.

21 is the new political age: Revanth Reddy seeks lower age to contest MLA, MP polls

A Revanth Reddy said Telangana will move a resolution to lower the minimum age for contesting Assembly and Lok Sabha elections to 21. He presented it as a push for stronger youth representation and wider student participation in national politics.

In a major political pitch aimed at empowering India's youth, Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Saturday announced that his government would move a resolution in the State Assembly urging the Centre to reduce the minimum age to contest Assembly and Lok Sabha elections from 25 years to 21 years.

Addressing a massive Gen Z rally in Hyderabad, Revanth Reddy said the time had come to give young Indians a greater role in shaping the country's future. "If a 21-year-old can become an IAS officer, contest local body elections, and even serve the nation through the civil services, why can't they contest Assembly and Parliament elections?" he asked.

The Chief Minister said the Telangana government would convene a special session of the Assembly and Legislative Council in the first week of August to pass a resolution seeking the constitutional amendment. He added that Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge would pursue the issue in Parliament.

Making a strong case for lowering the age limit, Revanth Reddy cited former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's decision to reduce the voting age from 21 to 18 through the 61st Constitutional Amendment and PV Narasimha Rao's 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, which enabled 21-year-olds to contest local body elections. He also referred to countries such as Germany, the United Kingdom and Singapore, where younger leaders are allowed to contest elections at an earlier age.

The Chief Minister said Gen Z accounts for nearly 30 per cent of India's population but has less than one per cent representation in Parliament. "India's future lies in the hands of its youth. The country's legislatures must reflect that reality," he said.

Revanth Reddy also praised the nationwide Gen Z movement over the alleged NEET paper leak, claiming it had compelled the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. He demanded that the Centre withdraw cases filed against protesting students and provide compensation to the families of students who allegedly died by suicide in connection with the controversy.

Calling the movement a victory for India's youth rather than any political party, the Chief Minister urged young people to continue their fight for justice and greater representation. "This tsunami of youth must not stop here. The voice of Gen Z should be heard from Jantar Mantar to Parliament," he said.
Ayodhya donation theft: UP to propose 3-IPS panel for new SIT to Supreme Court

Uttar Pradesh is set to place the names of three senior IPS officers before the Supreme Court for a new SIT in the Ayodhya temple donation case. The move follows the court's insistence on a team that conducts the probe itself rather than merely supervising it.

The Uttar Pradesh government is set to submit a panel of three senior IPS officers before the Supreme Court on Monday for the constitution of a new Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the alleged theft and misappropriation of donations at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya.

The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing before the apex court, which had earlier directed the state government to constitute an SIT headed by a senior IPS officer to ensure an independent and effective investigation into the alleged embezzlement of devotees' donations.

According to sources, the state government is likely to propose the names of Inspector General (IG), Lucknow Range, Kiran S, Deputy Inspector General (DIG), Ayodhya Range, Somen Verma, and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Ayodhya, Gaurav Grover for the new SIT. The proposed team is expected to function under the leadership of IG Kiran S and submit its findings to the Supreme Court.

The proposed panel marks a change from the existing SIT. Earlier, the committee included Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant and Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan Kumar. Under the revised proposal, the two civil officers have been replaced by senior IPS officers in line with the Supreme Court's observations.

The Supreme Court, while hearing a batch of petitions on July 20 seeking a fair, impartial and time-bound investigation into the alleged embezzlement, had questioned whether the existing SIT was directly investigating the case.

Responding to the Bench, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Uttar Pradesh government, had informed the court that the investigation was being carried out by the Uttar Pradesh Police, while the SIT was only supervising the probe.

Expressing dissatisfaction with the arrangement, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant directed the state government to obtain instructions on constituting an SIT that would itself conduct the investigation. The Bench suggested that the team be headed by a senior IPS officer, such as the IG of the Lucknow Range, who was already a member of the existing SIT.

The matter is being heard by a bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohan in a batch of petitions seeking an independent probe into the alleged embezzlement of donations made by devotees at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple.

The allegations relate to an FIR registered over the alleged diversion of temple donations. Police have arrested all eight persons named in the case, including the official responsible for counting cash donations at the temple's pilgrim facilitation centre. The accused have been booked under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita on charges including criminal breach of trust, cheating and criminal conspiracy. Investigators suspect the alleged fraud was carried out over a period of time through manipulation of the temple's donation collection and accounting process.
The Supreme Court is expected to consider the panel proposed by the Uttar Pradesh government during Monday's hearing and take a call on the constitution of the new SIT.

Dharmendra Pradhan steps down, Gen Z steps up
Minister Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of education, BJP leaders rally behind Pradhan after he resigns.

A 36-day stir by students achieved a landmark victory on Saturday as education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of sweeping protests that brought central Delhi to a halt, energised a moribund Opposition, and heralded the entry of a new generation of young people into politics.

The sprawling sit-in in Delhi’s historic Jantar Mantar was called off hours after the resignation was announced by the minister on X with leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) saying the government had accepted two other demands – compensation of ₹1 crore to the kin of every student who died by suicide following irregularities in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test, and the withdrawal of all first information reports against students who undertook a massive march to Parliament earlier this week.
“We have won. Gandhi has won. Ambedkar has won,” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said from the makeshift stage in Jantar Mantar as news trickled into the heavily barricaded site.

This is the first time that a popular street protest has forced the resignation of a Union minister in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government’s three terms. Union consumer affairs minister Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the education ministry.
Also read: Fear of losing Gen Z, poll math forced BJP's hand in Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation

Celebrations erupted soon after as young men and women – many of them Gen Z -- waved the Tricolour, climbed barricades and broke into impromptu jigs as makeshift loudspeakers belted out Bollywood favourites. Many briefly interrupted festivities to stand in attention and loudly sing along to the national anthem and Saare Jahan Se Acha, before unfurling their banners and posters featuring memes and slogans hitting out at the government.
“Our generation did it. We showed them that you cannot call us terrorists, hit us, and go scot free,” said Nachiket Malhotra, 22.

Pradhan – one of the seniormost ministers in the Cabinet who was a part of the council of ministers since Prime Minister Narendra Modi swept to power in 2014 and the longest serving education minister in almost two decades – announced his dramatic resignation on X.
In his two-page note in Hindi, the minister said he was disturbed to see the events of the past 10 days, and said he had resolved to not let the youth get ensnared in the web of confusion.

“Considering the situation at Jantar Mantar and across the country-with the aim of preventing anti-national forces from exploiting it, preserving national unity, ensuring that not a single Indian student’s future gets entangled in legal complexities, and allowing our children to devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers-I have submitted my resignation to prime minister,” he said.
“It is not a matter of individual prestige for me,” he added.

Rashtrapati Bhavan accepted his resignation even as senior ministers and Bharatiya Janata Party leaders rallied behind him. “His contribution to public service has been inclusive, future-ready, and aligned with the aspirations of a New India,” defence minister Rajnath Singh said on X.

Hours later, CJP representatives Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das met Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh – for the third time in as many days – and announced later that the government had accepted all their demands. The two sides will again meet after four weeks to discuss broader reforms in the examination system, the CJP said.
Also read: NEET can’t continue as a make-or-break exam

“The CJP declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith and understanding that the agreed-upon terms will be executed within the agreed-upon timeline,” Das said at a joint press conference with Nadda and Singh.
“As the government accepted all our demands after 36 days of protests, we appeal to everyone to peacefully withdraw from protest sites and go home,” Ranka said.

Das said they have shared a draft of the demands with the government and the government will share a written guarantee by Tuesday. There was no word on the demand for an apology from the government over clashes on July 20.

Nadda said the CJP representatives came to the meeting with a written draft on cases filed during the July 20 agitation. Delhi Police have filed at least 15 FIRs in connection with the protest when tens of thousands of young people broke barricades, braved tear gas shells and batons to march to Parliament.
Nadda said the government also discussed demands of no retaliatory measures against agitators, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died, and a five-point CJP charter.
Also read: New paper leak bill prescribes 2-month window for probes, speedy trials

“After the discussion, the first point was that no action should be taken and no FIRs should be filed. If any FIRs have already been registered, whether by the Delhi Police or in BJP-ruled states, it will be withdrawn,” Nadda said, adding that the government agreed to give “honourable compensation within the rules” to the families of NEET suicide victims.
“All our demands have been accepted by the government,” Das said. Nadda said the government will provide to CJP copies of FIRs registered.

The announcements drew a dramatic denouement to the sweeping protests that were birthed by a controversial comment by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant describing unemployed people and dubious degree holders earlier this year.

“I thank CJI Surya Kant ji for calling us cockroaches. If you had not called us cockroaches, I would not have returned to India. If you hadn’t called us cockroaches, the youth would not have been on the roads,” Dipke said at Jantar Mantar to cheers.

The CJP first garnered millions of followers on social media before launching an indefinite sit-in protest on June 20 demanding the resignation of Pradhan over repeated question paper leaks – including one earlier this year. After days of tepid crowds, the movement was galvanised by the hunger strike and forcible removal of activist Sonam Wangchuk last week.

Crowds swelled through the weekend and by Monday morning, columns of people –– many of them students, first-time agitators and young professionals –– had defied a steady drizzle and police barricading to join what became the largest street protests in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s third term. Over 100 protesters and 129 security personnel were injured. One protester remains in the ICU.

Over the past week, crowds swelled and spilled beyond the confines of Jantar Mantar as thousands of young people poured into central Delhi, despite the longest spells of internet shutdown and metro station closure in Delhi, scores of barricades that sparked traffic snarls across the Capital, and controversial police detention from roads over protesters carrying posters or pepper spray. Tensions sporadically flared at the site, most dramatically on Wednesday night when clashes between protesters and police led to injuries to five agitators and five police personnel.

As the storm of Gen Z protesters grew, the government’s efforts to break the impasse kicked into overdrive. Nadda and Singh convinced Wangchuk to break his fast, Modi made a rare personal appeal to young people on Instagram and promised a stringent new bill – which will come before Parliament on Monday – to tackle paper leaks, and the National Testing Agency fired top officials. The police continues to be under fire over allegations of excess force used to scatter crowds on July 20; the Supreme Court is set to hear two appeals on Monday even as four people have alleged that the security forces used pellet guns on them – an unprecedented occurrence in the Capital.

But on Saturday afternoon, as an avalanche of people – many of them school students, many first-time protesters who had never stepped outside campuses before, many who travelled a night or more to be there – thronged Jantar Mantar, the jubilation around their achievement had washed away the bitterness. “Everyone thought we were lazy, we don’t know anything beyond Instagram or our phones,” said Nikita Joshi, 19. “Today, our generation raised its voice.”

New Delhi: The Rajya Sabha Wednesday passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amid a heated debate, with the Opposition questioning the intent of the Bill and maintaining that reverence to the national song doesn’t come through legislation. The government said that opposing the national song Vande Mataram amounts to boosting the morale of the “Bharat tere tukde honge gang”.

The Act penalises insults to the national flag, the Constitution of India, and the national anthem. The Bill would give Vande Mataram the same statutory protection as the national anthem. The Bill was discussed amid Opposition staging protest and shouting slogans demanding a response from Union Home Minister Amit Shah over police action against protesters last week. Opposition members later staged a walkout in the middle of the debate.

During the debate on the Bill, RJD MP Prof Manoj Kumar Jha asked, “I am seeing for the first time that my national anthem and national song are being pitted against each other. Subhash Babu is being pitted against Nehru ji. What are we doing?”

He asserted that “reverence cannot be legislated”, and asked whether the slogan, “Vande Mataram. Kar le thodi sharam” will be considered an insult. Saying that during his student days, they used to raise this slogan, he asserted that he was asking this question on behalf of the youth of the country.

BJP MP Dr Radha Mohan Das Agrawal alleged that Vande Mataram was being insulted for the past 123 years, and claimed that the national song was never discussed in the Constituent Assembly. He alleged that “not just today’s Congress, but even the Congress of the time of Independence struggle” consistently insulted the national song.

Quoting several revolutionaries who sang Vande Mataram, he said, “Because revolutionaries drew inspiration from this song, members of the Congress felt inferior because of the song, they used to feel a sense of their own smallness.”
Agrawal referred to the 1923 Kakinada session of the Congress, whose president Muhammad Ali Jauhar protested when the singer Vishnu Digambar Paluskar rose to render the song.

He said, “In the 1923 session of the Indian National Congress, when the then-Congress president insulted Vande Mataram and said the song won’t be sung in the Congress session, they didn’t have the courage to remove that president, that Muslim League’s dalal, that anti-Indian who allowed Afghan attack on India, from the Congress…They laid the foundation for the Partition during the Non-Cooperation Movement.”
AAP MP Sanjay Singh said it was “laughable that such a bill is being brought by a party which didn’t have the Indian flag at the RSS headquarters for 52 years”.

“Today, people are talking about bringing in a strict law against (insult of) Vande Mataram. There is a patrika called Organiser which wrote in 1949 that the national anthem is an item of entertainment. You insulted that national anthem, there should be proceedings against such organisations, who insulted the national anthem and the national flag,” Singh added.
The AAP MP asked, “Why don’t you unfurl the flag at Sangh Shakhas?”, urging for a Bill for proceedings against people who have insulted the national flag and the national anthem as well.

In his response, Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai said the Bill was not just a legislative change but a “collective commitment to the soul of India, national consciousness, cultural heritage, and the ideals of the freedom struggle”.
“I don’t know why these 1-2 people are opposed to Vande Mataram. I don’t understand what opposition the Congress has towards Vande Mataram,” he added.

Nityanand Rai further said that the original 1971 law punishes insults to the national flag, the Constitution, and the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana. The amendment, he said, ensures the same respect and punishment for insult of the national song as well.

Rai then asserted, “Being against Vande Mataram means that the Congress always adopts the policy of polarisation to undermine the pride of the nation…Why is the Opposition against Vande Mataram? Opposing the Vande Mataram amounts to boosting the morale of ‘Bharat tere tukde honge’ gang. But the country’s youth, farmers, women and workers, won’t tolerate the slogan, Bharat tere tukde honge. Such people will be taught a lesson.”

He said that Swami Vivekananda had made a prediction that the 21st century would be India’s. “Swami Vivekananda’s childhood name was Narendra. One Narendra made a prediction, and it is being fulfilled by the world’s most popular leader, the messiah of the poor, the bringer of development, honorable Shri Narendra Modi ji.”

Respect of national symbols should be above any politics, he said, asserting that this Bill isn’t against any person or ideology, and is in the interest of the nation’s dignity and “our shared national consciousness”.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said he was forgiving students who hurled abuses at him and his late mother during the Jantar Mantar protest, describing them as "misguided children" who deserve guidance rather than punishment or prolonged legal action.

"Some mischievous children used very filthy abuses... Abuses were directed at me, and abuses were directed at my late mother as well."

NEW DELHI: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday moved the Supreme Court seeking directions to the Karnataka government to immediately release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, arguing that Karnataka must comply with the apex court's 2018 verdict and the recent directions issued by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA).The plea seeks an order directing Karnataka to implement the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's recommendation, upheld by the CWMA on Thursday, to release 3,500 cusecs of water per day for 15 days to Tamil Nadu at the inter-state border point of Biligundlu."Direct the State of Karnataka / Respondent No.

1 to forthwith and fully implement the direction of the CWRC dated July 28, 2026, as affirmed by the CWMA on July 30, 2026, by ensuring a flow of 3,500 cusecs per day at Biligundlu for the period of 15 days commencing from date of the order passed by this Hon'ble Court, and to make good the shortfall in compliance from July 29, 2026 onwards," the DMK said in its plea.The party also sought a direction to Karnataka to clear the accumulated shortfall in water releases.

It asked the court to direct the state to "make good the accumulated backlog of about 9.46 TMC due at Biligundlu as on July 26, 2026, computed on the pro-rata/distress-sharing basis, by ensuring releases such that about 7,000 cusecs per day is realised at Biligundlu over a period of 15 days".In addition, the DMK urged the Supreme Court to direct the CWMA to monitor reservoir releases in Karnataka and the flows realised at Biligundlu on a day-to-day basis and submit compliance reports.

The move comes amid renewed tensions between the two southern states over the sharing of Cauvery waters during the current monsoon season. The farmer groups and pro-Kannada organisations staged demonstrations across the Cauvery basin, arguing that the state could not spare even a drop of water for Tamil Nadu because major reservoirs did not have enough water even for drinking.Shivakumar said the Kabini reservoir was rapidly filling up and warned that water could not be retained once the reservoir reached full capacity."Kabini reservoir is filling up. The CBI has registered an FIR against Reliance Capital Limited (RCL) and its former chairman Anil D Ambani over allegations that the company caused a loss of Rs 1,816.22 crore to the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).

The case follows a complaint dated July 21 from the Union Ministry of Labour and Employment, which alleged cheating, criminal conspiracy and wrongful loss to the EPFO. Ambani has denied any wrongdoing through his spokesperson.

According to the complaint, now part of the CBI FIR, RCL issued secured non-convertible debentures during 2013 and 2014. The complaint said investments totalling Rs 2,500 crore were made by portfolio managers on behalf of the EPFO in these debentures, with maturity in 2023 and 2024.

The complaint alleged, "The present complaint is being lodged on behalf of EPFO through its authorised officer pursuant to the approval of the competent authority in relation to the substantial loss suffered by the EPFO arising out of its investment in the secured Non-Convertible Debentures issued by Reliance Capital Limited and the subsequently discovered material indicating fraudulent conduct connected with such investment."

It said the Ministry of Labour and Employment sent the complaint after being informed by the Enforcement Directorate that it had found documentary evidence and that a transaction audit by BDO India LLP showed, prima facie, a number of fraudulent transactions by RCL and those in charge of its management between December 7, 2019, and December 6, 2021.

The complaint further alleged, "In addition, during an earlier period as well, various fraudulent transactions have been found which also led to ultimate failure of RCL as a consequence of siphoning off of money of RCL." It said the ED probe prima facie pointed to a series of transactions involving irregular lending, diversion of funds, impairment of security and other acts by RCL that require investigation.

The complaint added, "If established upon investigation, such conduct may have materially contributed to the financial deterioration of RCL, its inability to honour its obligation towards Debenture Holders, and the consequent loss of Rs 1,816.22 crore suffered by EPFO."

Responding to the complaint, Ambani's spokesperson said, "The FIR registered by the CBI pertains to Reliance Capital Limited. Mr. Ambani served as a Non-Executive Director/Chairman of the Board of Reliance Capital Limited from 2005 until November 2021, when the Reserve Bank of India superseded the Board of Directors of the company and appointed an administrator." NEW DELHI: Saturday witnessed a series of major developments in the NEET paper leak controversy, beginning with Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation after weeks of nationwide protests.
Hours later, Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new education minister getting additional charge apart from portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution.
Meanwhile, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party (
CJP) held a third round of talks, after which the government agreed to withdraw FIRs filed against peaceful protesters.

CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
The protest site was cleared after the CJP demands were met.

Here are the top developments:Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of education ministry

Hours after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, President Droupadi Murmu assigned senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi the additional charge of the Union education ministry on the advice of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

A five-time Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka's Dharwad, Joshi will continue to hold the portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. He takes charge at a crucial time as the government rolls out reforms following the NEET-UG paper leak, including restructuring the NTA, tightening exam security and shifting NEET to computer-based testing from 2027.

Normal Metro access resumed across Delhi after the CJP called off its 36-day protest, with the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) reopening the entry gates of all stations that had been closed because of security arrangements.
The reopening came shortly after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the Centre reached an agreement with the CJP to end the agitation.

Earlier in the day, the DMRC had resumed services at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat stations before restoring entry and exit at all 18 affected stations, which had been placed under restrictions due to the protests near Jantar Mantar.
Pradhan resigns, cites moral responsibility

Announcing his resignation in a letter addressed to the country's youth, Pradhan said he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi after considering the situation that had developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country.

He said he had spent more than four decades working for students, teachers and education reforms and had always believed that a strong education system was the foundation of a strong nation. Pradhan said the government acted immediately after irregularities surfaced in the NEET-UG examination by handing the investigation to the CBI, cancelling the examination and announcing a fresh test, while also deciding to shift NEET to computer-based mode from next year.
He added that he had accepted responsibility from the very beginning and had worked to ensure that no deserving student suffered because of what he described as an examination mafia.

Recalling the events of the past few days had deeply saddened him, Pradhan said he was stepping down to prevent anti-national forces from exploiting the situation, safeguard national unity and allow students to focus on their education.
Centre and CJP reach agreement after third round of talks
Hours after Pradhan's resignation, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party held a third round of talks, following which the student group announced the immediate withdrawal of its 36-day protest.

Addressing a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das said the agitation was being withdrawn in good faith after the government accepted its key demands.

The CJP said its primary demand, Pradhan's resignation, had been fulfilled. It also said the Centre had agreed to withdraw FIRs and legal cases against peaceful protesters and assured that no retaliatory action would be taken.

The government further agreed to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide in accordance with existing rules and regulations and promised to consider the CJP's five-point charter on examination reforms.
JP Nadda said the government had sympathetically considered the delegation's demands and would hold further discussions on long-term reforms to strengthen the examination system.
Student movement ends after 36 days
The CJP protest began at Jantar Mantar on June 20, demanding accountability over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak, wider reforms in the examination system and Pradhan's resignation.
The movement gained national attention after climate activist
Sonam Wangchuk joined the agitation with an indefinite hunger strike. His deteriorating health and later hospitalisation intensified public attention and increased pressure on the government.
Although Wangchuk ended his 26-day fast after receiving written assurances from the Centre, the CJP continued its protest until Pradhan resigned and the remaining demands were addressed.

Speaking after the agreement, Ashutosh Ranka appealed to protesters across the country to withdraw peacefully, while Saurav Das said the movement was ending with the understanding that all commitments would be implemented within the agreed timelines.
"Government accepted all our demands after 36 days of protest; we urge everyone to peacefully withdraw from protest sites," CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said.

Earlier in the day, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had briefly said the protest would continue until all demands were accepted. After the talks concluded, however, the organisation announced the end of the agitation.

Dipke also urged supporters not to treat Pradhan's resignation as a personal victory for him, saying the movement was driven by thousands of young people and should remain focused on institutional reforms rather than individuals.
Amit Shah reacts to Pradhan's exit
Union home minister Amit Shah reacted to Dharmendra Pradhan's exit as education minister saying, "Modi government respects youth's sentiments".

"For BJP workers, the country, our youth, and students are far more important than any position. Today, the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan ji from his post exemplifies this very principle. The Modi government respects the sentiments of the country's youth and is committed to implementing the necessary reforms against paper leaks. The decisions taken by Modi ji to ensure strict punishment for those guilty of paper leaks are commendable. I am fully confident that these steps will ensure complete justice for the students who succeeded in the NEET examination.," he said.

"During his tenure, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji has brought about significant reforms in the effective implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), arrangements for examinations in mother tongues, expansion of PM SHRI Schools, promotion of digital education, skill development, and strengthening industry-academia coordination. His efforts toward making the examination system more inclusive and student-centric have also been noteworthy. His tenure is a testament to his dedication to the resolve of making India a developed nation," he added.
Opposition calls it a victory for students
The opposition described Pradhan's resignation as a major victory for students and renewed calls for broader reforms in the education system.

Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi called the resignation "the victory of the future of India", saying Pradhan had become a symbol of corruption, incompetence and the decline of the country's education system.
He said the government must now introduce meaningful reforms and alleged that the issue of police action against student protesters would remain a key matter during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge termed the resignation a "victory of truth" and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi should apologise to the country's youth while ensuring action against those responsible for the alleged use of force against protesters.
AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal described the development as a "big win for democracy", while Karnataka chief minister DK
Shivakumar said the Congress would continue raising issues concerning students and maintained that peaceful protests were an essential part of democracy.

Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk welcomed the developments, describing them as "a victory of democracy, direct democracy, peace, patience and perseverance". He congratulated the student movement and thanked citizens across the country for supporting the agitation.
His wife, Gitanjali Angmo, also praised the role played by India's younger generation, saying the protests had demonstrated courage, patriotism and commitment to democratic values without violence.
Tougher anti-paper leak law proposed

The Centre has proposed major amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure faster investigations, time-bound trials and stricter punishment for paper leaks and examination malpractice.

The proposed Bill provides for the creation of Special Task Forces (STFs) to investigate offences, completion of investigations within two months, day-to-day hearings in special fast-track courts and disposal of appeals by High Courts within three months.

It also significantly increases penalties, proposing jail terms of up to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 10 crore for organised paper leak rackets, along with tougher action against service providers and officials found involved in examination fraud.
Biggest political fallout of NEET controversy
Pradhan's resignation marks the most significant political consequence of the NEET-UG paper leak controversy, which began after allegations of question paper leaks in the May 3 examination.

The controversy led to the cancellation of the examination, a nationwide CBI investigation, repeated protests, parliamentary disruptions, changes to the anti-paper leak law and a major restructuring of the National Testing Agency.

‘Pakistan eroded faith’: India envoy to US calls out Islamabad's ‘distraction policy’ over Indus Waters Treaty
Vinay Kwatra said Indus Waters Treaty was founded on "goodwill and friendship", but Pakistan spent decades eroding those principles through its actions.

India's Ambassador to the United States, Vinay Kwatra, has strongly defended New Delhi's decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance, arguing that Pakistan had effectively "destroyed" the spirit of the agreement long before India took the step.

Writing in a recent opinion piece published in the US-based weekly magazine Newsweek, Kwatra said the treaty was founded on "goodwill and friendship", but Pakistan spent decades eroding those principles through its actions.
“Pakistan spent half a century dismantling that goodwill and friendship. The abeyance merely acknowledges what Pakistan's conduct had already destroyed,” the ambassador said.
Kwatra's remarks came weeks after Pakistan reportedly organised a conference in Islamabad to protest India's decision to suspend the treaty.
Referring to the event, he wrote, “At that gathering, a former foreign minister threatened war against India if Pakistan’s demands on the Indus River system go unmet.”
He further termed it a tactic of Islamabad to “distract from its internal problems.” He called it their “standard policy option”.

Recalling the history of the agreement, Kwatra noted that the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty divided the six rivers of the Indus basin between the two countries, giving India control over the three eastern rivers and Pakistan control over the three western rivers.

He said that while the arrangement gave Pakistan access to nearly 80 per cent of the basin's waters and limited India's share to around 20 per cent, New Delhi continued to honour the agreement despite the imbalance.
Kwatra also said Pakistan repeatedly blocked India's attempts to modernise or renegotiate the treaty to reflect technological changes and allow greater hydropower development.

“Bit by bit, Pakistan eroded India's faith that it could exercise its rights under the treaty, or hope for a better one suited to today's realities,” he wrote.
'Terror and talks cannot go together'
Addressing calls for renewed dialogue between India and Pakistan, Kwatra said past experience showed such engagement had failed to produce results.

“Those advocating talks between India and Pakistan have not taken note of the history of these talks in the past or they must believe that doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results is not insanity."
"Prime Minister Narendra Modi has clearly voiced India’s stand today, “Terror and talks cannot go together... Terror and trade cannot go together…. Water and blood cannot flow together.””

The ambassador also rejected Pakistan's allegations that India was acting as a "water aggressor," saying the country's water shortages stemmed primarily from poor domestic management rather than Indian actions.
He wrote that only around 40 per cent of the water Pakistan receives reaches its farms, while more than 30 per cent is lost in transit and the remainder flows unused into the sea.

For the unversed, New Delhi's decision to hold the treaty in abeyance came a day after the April 22, 2025 terror attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 people — 25 Indians and one Nepalese citizen — were killed. The attack was carried out by Pakistani and Pakistan-trained terrorists linked to the designated terror outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba.

The notification came hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that fast-track courts would be established to ensure speedy trials and strict action against those involved in examination paper leak cases. The announcement was made amid a growing agitation over NEET-related irregularities.

Four judges—Sandeep Yadav, Anuradha Shukla, Devendra Kumar Sharma and Bhupinder Singh—have been posted as Special Exclusive NDPS judges, while Gaurav Rao, Gagandeep Singh and Surbhi Sharma Vats have been appointed as Special Exclusive MCOCA judges.
All the new postings mentioned in the order, issued on Saturday, August 1, will be applicable with effect from Tuesday, August 4.

Speaking to India Today, the woman said her daughter should not have used abusive language against elders and apologised on her behalf to the entire country.

"My daughter made a mistake. She should not have abused people older than her. On behalf of my daughter, I apologise to the entire country. The most important thing for me is that today she realises her mistake and there is shame in her eyes," she said.

The mother said young people have every right to protest and raise their voices through demonstrations, social media or YouTube, but should avoid using abusive language. "Protests are a separate issue. Children should raise their voice, but they should not abuse elders. That is wrong," she said.

According to her, the girl had left home on July 23 saying she was going shopping ahead of her birthday on August 1. The family only learnt about the incident after relatives sent them the viral video.
The woman claimed the family has been forced to move from place to place after the video surfaced, alleging they have received no security or assistance from the authorities.

"We cannot step outside without covering our faces. Vehicles keep circling our neighbourhood. We have already left our previous residence and are constantly changing locations. We have received no protection and are struggling even for food," she alleged.
She further claimed that despite it becoming known that the girl is a minor, the FIR against her has not been withdrawn.
"No government help or protection has been provided. Even the FIR against my daughter has not been withdrawn. If it has been established that she is a minor, why is the FIR still there?" she asked.
Referring to the girl's public apology, the mother said, "If Prime Minister Modi has forgiven her, then the police should also close the matter and withdraw the FIR."

She also denied having links with any political party, saying the family's only demand is protection. "We are ordinary people. We don't understand politics or big political issues. We just want protection. The police has not contacted me regarding our safety," she said.
The mother said teenagers are easily influenced by their surroundings and social media, adding that her daughter got carried away by the atmosphere at the protest.

"Children between 12 and 18 are at a sensitive age. They have Instagram, Facebook and many other platforms. Sometimes, in the heat of the moment, they don't realise what they are saying because everyone around them is doing the same. Later, they understand what they have done," she said.
She reiterated that what mattered most to her was that her daughter now regrets her actions and understands that she spoke disrespectfully about someone much older than her.

The controversy began after a video of the girl making abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Jantar Mantar went viral on social media. Based on the complaint, the case was registered under Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. A Zero FIR allows a complaint to be registered at any police station regardless of jurisdiction before being transferred to the appropriate police station for investigation.

Vikram-1: All about India's first privately developed orbital rocket saying ‘hello’ to space
The launch witnessed a brief delay after the mission control team placed the countdown on a planned hold minutes before the scheduled liftoff.

Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace created history on Saturday with the successful launch of Vikram-1, India's first privately developed orbital launch vehicle. The mission, named Mission Aagaman, lifted off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.
Skyroot Aerospace wrote on X, "Hello space, we have arrived! Vikram-1's Test Flight-1 has completed it's mission. The first ever Indian private sector launch has been successfully completed."

Besides satellites, the rocket also carried a handwritten postcard from Prime Minister Narendra Modi bearing the message "Vande Mataram", along with postcards from engineers, scientists and Indian astronauts, PTI reported.
Ahead of the launch, Modi described Vikram-1 as "a historic new frontier for India's space journey."

Vikram-1 is an orbital launch vehicle developed by Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace. Unlike suborbital rockets, it is designed to place satellites into stable Earth orbit, enabling applications such as communications, navigation, Earth observation and scientific research, as per Skyroot website.
Vikram-1 is India's first privately developed orbital rocket, making Skyroot the first Indian private company to attempt an orbital satellite launch.
Vikram-1 is the entry of India's private space sector into the orbital launch market and is being seen as a major milestone in the country's commercial space ambitions.
It is also the first major demonstration of the government's space-sector reforms under the Indian Space Policy 2023, which opened the entire space value chain to private participation.
ALSO READ | India's first private orbital launch successful as Vikram-1 lifts off into space
- It stands 24 metres tall, roughly the height of a seven-storey building.
- Vikram-1 is designed to carry up to 350 kg of payload to a 450-km Low Earth Orbit (LEO) at a 60-degree inclination.
- It features an all-carbon composite structure, making it lightweight and durable.
- The four-stage rocket uses three solid-fuel stages and a liquid-fuelled orbital adjustment module.
- It is powered by 3D-printed liquid engines, helping reduce manufacturing time and complexity.
- It has been designed for rapid and on-demand launch services.
- Skyroot says Vikram-1 is among the few rockets globally capable of deploying satellites into orbit.
Mission Aagaman is the maiden flight of Vikram-1 and it lifted off from the first launch pad at ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, at 12:05.
ALSO READ | PM Modi wishes Skyroot success ahead of Vikram-1's first orbital launch: ‘A historic new frontier for India’

The mission deployed multiple customer payloads into a 450-km Low Earth Orbit while collecting engineering data that will be used to validate the rocket's guidance, navigation and control systems. The data also will help refine the vehicle for future commercial satellite launch missions.
What payloads is Vikram-1 carrying?
The rocket has deployed multiple domestic and international technology demonstration payloads -
- DCubed's technology demonstration payload.
- Grahaa Space's SOLARAS S3 satellite.
- Cosmoserve Space's Embrace, a robotic arm designed to capture orbital debris.
- Cosmic Bloom, a floral-shaped micro-art installation.
- An 18-karat gold micro-rocket featuring microscopic sculptures of CV Raman, Vikram Sarabhai and APJ Abdul Kalam, each smaller than a grain of rice.
- A handwritten postcard by PM Modi carrying the message "Vande Mataram".
- Handwritten postcards from engineers, scientists and Indian astronauts.
How is Vikram-1 different from Vikram-S?

Vikram-1 is Skyroot's second rocket. Its predecessor, Vikram-S, successfully flew on a suborbital mission in November 2022, becoming the first privately built rocket launched from an ISRO facility in Sriharikota.
While Vikram-S was a technology demonstration mission, Vikram-1 is designed to place satellites into orbit, representing a far more advanced capability.
The Vikram series is named after Dr Vikram Sarabhai, regarded as the father of India's space programme, in recognition of his pioneering contributions to the country's space efforts.

Dharmendra Pradhan, who stepped down as Union education minister on Saturday after a five-year tenure, leaves behind an education system more standardised, digitally connected and centrally regulated than the one he inherited â but also questions over examination credibility, institutional autonomy, data privacy and the Centreâs capacity to implement reforms on such a large scale.

Pradhan, the longest-serving education minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs cabinet, held the portfolio from July 7, 2021, to July 25, 2026. Until 2024, he was also minister for skill development and entrepreneurship.
His tenure was less about announcing a new education policy â the National Education Policy had been approved in 2020 â and more about constructing the machinery required to put it into operation.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates

The defining theme was standardisation and portability: common entrance examinations, transferable academic credits, permanent student identification numbers, comparable assessment standards and an attempted umbrella regulator for higher education.
The Common University Entrance Test, introduced in 2022, sought to replace differing Class XII board cut-offs with a common admission platform for central universities.
It also dramatically expanded the role of the National Testing Agency, whose functioning and credibility later became one of the biggest challenges of Pradhanâs tenure.

The National Credit Framework, Academic Bank of Credits and four-year undergraduate programmes were designed to allow students to accumulate and transfer credits, pursue multidisciplinary courses and enter or leave programmes without losing their academic record.

APAAR, envisaged as a permanent academic identity for every student, sought to link school, university and skill qualifications through DigiLocker and the credit bank. While intended to ease mobility, it triggered concerns over consent and protection of childrenâs data.

In school education, the ministry released curriculum frameworks for the foundational stage and school education, operationalising the NEPâs 5+3+3+4 structure. PM SHRI was launched to upgrade more than 14,500 existing government schools as models of NEP implementation, while PARAKH was established to develop common assessment standards and bring greater comparability among school boards.

Other big-ticket measures included the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, One Nation One Subscription for access to research journals, PM-USHA funding for state universities, permission for foreign universities to open campuses in India and the establishment of IIT campuses abroad.

Pradhan also pushed Indian-language textbooks, multidisciplinary education, vocational integration and apprenticeship programmes, drawing on the overlap between his education and skill-development portfolios.

The proposed replacement of UGC, AICTE and NCTE with an umbrella regulatory architecture remained unfinished. Implementation also met resistance from some states over language, curriculum and centrally sponsored schemes.

Ultimately, the sharpest contradiction of the Pradhan years lay in national testing. Common examinations were meant to deliver fairness and uniformity, but paper leaks, cancellations and administrative failures raised doubts about whether centralisation had moved faster than institutional capacity.
Dharmendra Pradhan, in a post on X on Saturday (July 25, 2026), announced that he has tendered his resignation from the post of Union Education Minister.

The President of India, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Shri Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India. Further, as advised by the Prime Minister, the President has directed that Shri Pralhad Joshi, Cabinet Minister, be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Education, in addition to his existing portfolio.
Prime Minister Narendra is yet to provide any public comment on this.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday (August 1, 2026) assured exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin of security in the State, saying the “days of threats are over”.

Sharing the stage with Ms. Nasrin at Kolkata’s Rabindra Sadan at an event that marked the writer’s return to the city after 19 years, Ms. Adhikari said: “You are most welcome to Bengal. Please come here whenever you want and as many times as you wish. Your safety is my responsibility.”

Ms. Nasrin was exiled from Bangladesh in 1994 over her writings after which she started living in Europe and then in Kolkata. But she had to leave Kolkata in November 2007, when violence erupted in the city after some organisations called for action against the author over her books. The violence reached such alarming proportions that the Army had to be deployed in the city to contain the situation. She had blamed the Left Front government and the Trinamool Congress government for not allowing her to return to the city.
She reached Kolkata on Friday (July 31, 2026) to attend the event at Rabindra Sadan.

The Chief Minister said Ms. Nasrin’s return indicated that not only had the face of the government changed but the entire system too. “This Bengal is free from any barriers and chains. Every single pillar of the Constitution is safe here. We all have the righteous opportunity for freedom of speech,” said Mr. Adhikari, welcoming the writer with a portrait of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, the writer of national song Vande Mataram.

Veteran BJP leader and former Tripura Governor Tathagata Roy also shared the stage with the writer. The audience comprised a number of State Ministers, including Swapan Dasgupta, Agnimitra Paul, and Kalyan Chakrabarti.

“I have always questioned this city. Did I ever harm you [Kolkata]? I haven’t come for any answer today. I have come back to Kolkata with tears in my eyes and also immense love in my heart. This was my dream for the last 19 years. History remembers who shut this door. Now, history will also remember who opened this door again,” said Ms. Nasrin, expressing gratitude to the West Bengal Chief Minister for facilitating her return.

“It is still painful that a writer had to return to the city of her own language with such high security. I am thankful to the government. But my gratitude is not my allegiance to any party. I have not come here for any political party. I came here to express my voice over women’s liberty and freedom of speech,” the 63-year-old writer said at the event.

India clears one China FDI proposal as Hong Kong gets 13 in FY26
India approved one Chinese FDI proposal worth Rs 1 crore and 13 from Hong Kong in 2025-26. The data highlights how Press Note 3 scrutiny continues for investors from land-border countries.

India approved only one foreign direct investment (FDI) proposal from China worth Rs 1 crore during the financial year 2025-26, while clearing 13 investment proposals from Hong Kong worth Rs 610.42 crore, according to official data released by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), reports PTI.

The figures come as investments from countries sharing a land border with India continue to require prior government approval under Press Note 3, introduced in April 2020 to prevent opportunistic takeovers of Indian companies during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Overall, the government approved 63 FDI proposals worth Rs 10,292.67 crore (USD 1.18 billion) under the government approval route during April 2025 to March 2026.
SINGAPORE TOPS APPROVED FDI PROPOSALS
Singapore emerged as the largest source of approved FDI proposals by value, with five proposals worth Rs 3,259.88 crore (USD 382.52 million) receiving government clearance.
The United Kingdom followed with five proposals worth Rs 2,477.67 crore ($283 million), while Thailand secured approval for two proposals worth Rs 1,600 crore (around $180 million).
PRESS NOTE 3 NORMS EASED BUT NOT FOR CHINA

In March, the government relaxed certain provisions under Press Note 3 by allowing investments through the automatic route where beneficial ownership from land-border countries does not exceed 10 per cent, subject to sectoral caps and other conditions.

However, the relaxation does not apply to entities registered in China, Hong Kong, or any other country sharing a land border with India. Such investments continue to require prior government approval.
India shares land borders with China, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar and Afghanistan.

According to DPIIT data, China has never been a major source of FDI into India. Between April 2000 and March 2026, Chinese investments accounted for just 0.32 per cent of India's total FDI equity inflows, amounting to $2.51 billion (Rs 16,162.25 crore), placing China 23rd among investing countries.
Hong Kong ranked 15th, contributing $4.91 billion (Rs 31,220.30 crore), or 0.62 per cent of total FDI equity inflows during the same period.

The trend was similar in 2024-25, when India also approved only one Chinese FDI proposal, valued at Rs 28.71 crore. During that financial year, 82 proposals worth Rs 39,758 crore ($4.72 billion) were cleared under the government route, including 11 proposals from Hong Kong worth Rs 1,225.28 crore.

Taslima Nasreen draws parallels between CJP protests and 2024 Bangladesh unrest
Days after the CJP protests in Delhi, Taslima Nasreen said the events in Bangladesh in 2024 and afterwards should serve as a warning for India.

Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday drew parallels between the recent protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi and the student-led movement that led to the ouster of former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in 2024, saying people should learn from what followed in her home country.
Speaking at a press conference in Kolkata, a day after her felicitation ceremony was briefly disrupted, Nasreen said the events in Bangladesh should serve as a warning.

"I felt what is happening here is similar to what happened in Bangladesh during the July student movement. People were fooled. The result in Bangladesh has not been good. Jihadis have taken over power there," she said.

Bangladesh witnessed months of student-led protests in 2024 over a controversial job quota system. The demonstrations soon turned into a wider anti-government movement that culminated in Sheikh Hasina leaving the country after weeks of violence. Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus later took charge of an interim government. Since then, Bangladesh has seen political uncertainty, while minority groups, including Hindus, have repeatedly raised concerns over attacks on their community.
Nasreen claimed the condition of Hindus had worsened under the interim government.

"Hindus faced torture during the Hasina government too, but there are more atrocities under the Yunus government," she alleged, attributing the situation to a lack of education and the growing influence of religious institutions.

Calling for secular reforms, Nasreen said religion should be kept separate from the state. She criticised the madrasa education system, alleging that it promoted communal thinking, and said Bangladesh should instead focus on secular education.
She also reiterated her support for a Uniform Civil Code, saying there should be "one law for everyone" in India, Bangladesh and Pakistan to ensure equal rights, particularly for women.
Nasreen also expressed support for jailed Hindu monk Chinmoy Krishna Das, saying she and several others had protested against his imprisonment.

Asked about the opposition in Bangladesh, she said it would have been better if the Awami League had remained the principal opposition instead of Jamaat-e-Islami. She opposed any move to ban the Awami League and said former prime minister Sheikh Hasina should be allowed to return to Bangladesh despite her criticism of some of the former government's policies.

The author also spoke about the disruption during her felicitation at Kolkata's Rabindra Sadan on Saturday, where noted Bengali poet Joy Goswami was prevented from addressing the audience after protests from a section of those present.

"I felt bad. It was not only Joy Goswami's humiliation but also mine because I had invited him. Political ideologies can differ, but everyone has the right to express their views," she said, adding that she planned to visit the poet at his residence.

On the political response she has received over the years, Nasreen said, "One government barred me, one government expelled me, and one government invited me," in an apparent reference to the Left Front, the Trinamool Congress and the BJP.
She also thanked West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for assuring her security during her visit to Kolkata.

Expressing hope for better ties between India and Bangladesh, Nasreen said India had played a key role in Bangladesh's liberation in 1971 and that relations between the two neighbours should remain friendly.

New Delhi: More than half of the overall respondents of the latest snap poll by CVoter were not satisfied with Modi government’s handling of the paper leaks issue, the polling agency said in a statement Sunday. This number was 40 percent among NDA voters.

The polling agency added that PM Narendra Modi Modi continues to command a 12-percentage point lead over Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi when it comes to ‘most popular youth leader among Indians’. It went further to add that opinion remains sharply divided over CJP’s demand for withdrawal of all FIRs against protesters.

The survey findings and projections are based on CVoter Snap Poll CATI (Computer Assisted Telephone Interviewing) interviews conducted among 18+ adults nationwide (BARC-HSM) between 29 and 30 July. The sample spread of 1,349 respondents is spread across all districts covering all states, said CVoter. According to the polling agency, the data is weighted to the known demographic profile as per the census and final ECI results.

“Though still far behind (Modi), Rahul Gandhi is gaining as the most popular youth leader,” read the statement by CVoter, adding that “anti-incumbency among the youth is a serious issue” and that while a “majority of Indians want proper investigations into alleged police brutality; a majority also (wants) police action against those who indulged in violence and were offensively abusive”.

The statement went on to add, “Overall, the paper leak and the CJP protests have inflicted political damage to the NDA government. But they are not the main challenge. The real challenge is the frustration of the youth whose rising aspirations are hitting a roadblock of limited opportunities.”

Protests spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over his handling of the NEET-UG (2026) paper leak last week forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The government also announced fast-track courts to deal with paper leak cases and steered an amendment to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, through both houses of Parliament, which proposes harsher punishment for those found using or facilitating unfair means.

58% NDA supporters want police brutality probed

According to the latest CVoter snap poll, 12 percent of respondents said they saw CJP being the voice of the youth and almost 50 percent said they would support the movement on other issues as well in the future.

As many as 31.7 percent of the respondents said stricter laws against paper leaks should have been the top priority for the government, followed by 27 percent who said it should have been Pradhan’s resignation, and 17 percent who said formation of an expert panel should have been top priority.
Were they satisfied with the discussion in Parliament on paper leaks? According to the polling agency, 35 percent of respondents were satisfied and 39 percent weren’t.
Opinion was sharply divided, however, on CJP’s demand for withdrawal of all FIRs against students who took part in demonstrations held across the country.

“On the face of it, a larger proportion of respondents (35.5 percent) want all FIRs to be withdrawn while less than one fourth say withdraw FIRs against only peaceful protestors. Significantly, more than one third of the respondents say investigative agencies should probe all FIRs first before arriving at a decision,” said CVoter.

However, 62.7 percent of respondents were of the opinion that allegations of police brutality during the protests must be investigated. “Interestingly, even almost 58 percent of those who support the NDA want a proper investigation,” the polling agency said.

At the same time, 54.2 percent of respondents want the police to act against protesters who used abusive language and uploaded objectionable content on social media. Among INDIA bloc supporters, 45 percent back police action in this regard.

For 27.6 percent of respondents, student anger over paper leaks was the trigger that earned the CJP its support. “Close to 50 percent of the respondents say they will support (CJP for other causes too) while less than 30 percent say they won’t. Almost 38 percent of NDA voters say they will support future CJP protests and movements,” CVoter said.

Taslima Nasreen backs UCC, says India, Bangladesh, Pakistan need it
Taslima Nasreen backed a Uniform Civil Code during her return visit to Kolkata. She said equal laws are essential for women's rights and defended free expression after a felicitation disruption.

Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday strongly backed the implementation of a Uniform Civil Code in India, saying such a law was essential to remove discrimination, especially against women. She said Bangladesh and Pakistan also needed a Uniform Civil Code, and argued that there should be equal laws for everyone.

Speaking to reporters in Kolkata during her first visit to the city in nearly 19 years, Nasreen also expressed anguish over a disruption at her felicitation ceremony a day earlier, when poet Joy Goswami was forced to leave the stage amid objections from a section of the audience. She said the incident went against the principle of freedom of expression, which Kolkata had long stood for.

"I have been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years. This is much needed in any civilised country. Bangladesh, Pakistan and India need a Uniform Civil Code. There should be equal laws for everyone. Women face a great deal of discrimination, and much of it can be removed through a UCC. It is essential," Nasreen said.

Her remarks came as the West Bengal government has constituted a high-level committee to examine a draft Uniform Civil Code for the state. A government notification said the panel was formed in view of the "wide ramifications and voluminous nature" of the proposed legislation and would undertake a comprehensive examination of the draft Bill before any further steps are taken.

Referring to Bangladesh, the 63-year-old writer said equality was the cornerstone of civilisation, but many women continued to face discrimination. "In Bangladesh, Hindu women do not have equal rights. They cannot inherit their father's property. If Hindu women are to enjoy freedom and equal rights, a Uniform Civil Code is necessary," she said.

Nasreen was felicitated at a state government programme at Rabindra Sadan on Saturday after returning to Kolkata for the first time since 2007, when protests over the publication of her book Dwikhandito forced the then Left Front government to move her out of the city. She had left Bangladesh in 1994 after receiving death threats from radical groups over her writings and views on religion.

Recalling the disruption at Saturday's event, Nasreen said she felt "insulted" after Goswami was prevented from speaking. "Not only was Joy insulted, but I was also insulted because I had invited him," she said. The controversy erupted after she invited Goswami onto the stage and asked him to address the gathering, but loud objections from a section of the audience forced him to step down without speaking.

"In my speech, I had spoken about freedom of expression. Everyone should be allowed to speak. It is not right to stop anyone from expressing their views," she said. Questioning the conduct of those who objected, she added, "Those who appreciated my speech were the ones who did not allow him to come on the stage. Didn't they also question me? It is contradictory. When someone speaks about freedom of expression, people support it, but when a poet is invited to speak, they do not want to hear him. That is not right." She said she would visit Goswami at his residence, adding, "I have not got the opportunity to speak to Joy (after the incident), but I will pay him a visit today or tomorrow."

Nasreen said she hoped such an incident would not happen again in her favourite city. "Kolkata is a city of progressives. People here believe in freedom of speech and the right to express one's views. People's political ideologies may differ, but everyone must be given the space to express one's opinions," she said.
Asked to compare the Left Front, the Trinamool Congress and the present BJP government in West Bengal, Nasreen praised the BJP-led dispensation for allowing her to visit Kolkata.

"There is, of course, a difference between the three governments. One government expelled me, another did not allow me to return, while the third has allowed me to come. Instead of focusing on those differences, I think we should celebrate the fact that I have been able to come back. I am very happy that I could return. I want to believe that this government believes in the right to freedom of expression and freedom of speech," she said.

Nasreen said she had been invited to Kolkata by an organisation called Secular Mission and that the state government later provided her security cover and facilitated her visit to West Bengal. On Saturday, she had said her return after 19 years showed that "injustice can be long but cannot be permanent", while maintaining that her fight had always been for women's rights and freedom of expression, and not for or against any political party.

When asked whether she wanted to return to Kolkata permanently, Nasreen said she had not yet "give it thought" but wanted to come back for the Kolkata Book Fair next year. "I surely want to come to Kolkata Book Fair. The Bengal chief minister has promised me security. So, I will definitely try to come. I will," she said. Stressing again that her views were independent of politics, she added, "I travel to many states. If I visit Kerala, does that make me part of that state's politics? Certainly not. I remain independent. Any government that provides me security is only discharging its responsibility. That has nothing to do with politics."

Nasreen's visit to Kolkata combined a renewed call for a Uniform Civil Code with a strong defence of equal rights and free speech, even as she spoke about her difficult history with the city and her wish to return again for the Book Fair.

Days after the 15-year-old apologised for using derogatory language against PM Modi, her mother said that the FIR against her has not been withdrawn despite her being a minor. The mother of the 15-year-old girl whose video abusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar went viral has appealed for the FIR against her daughter to be withdrawn, saying the teenager has realised her mistake and is deeply ashamed.

Speaking to India Today, the woman said her daughter should not have used abusive language against elders and apologised on her behalf to the entire country.

"My daughter made a mistake. She should not have abused people older than her. On behalf of my daughter, I apologise to the entire country. The most important thing for me is that today she realises her mistake and there is shame in her eyes," she said.

The mother said young people have every right to protest and raise their voices through demonstrations, social media or YouTube, but should avoid using abusive language. "Protests are a separate issue. Children should raise their voice, but they should not abuse elders. That is wrong," she said.

"We cannot step outside without covering our faces. Vehicles keep circling our neighbourhood. We have already left our previous residence and are constantly changing locations. We have received no protection and are struggling even for food," she alleged.

She also denied having links with any political party, saying the family's only demand is protection. "We are ordinary people. We don't understand politics or big political issues. We just want protection. The police has not contacted me regarding our safety," she said.
The mother said teenagers are easily influenced by their surroundings and social media, adding that her daughter got carried away by the atmosphere at the protest.

"Children between 12 and 18 are at a sensitive age. They have Instagram, Facebook and many other platforms. Sometimes, in the heat of the moment, they don't realise what they are saying because everyone around them is doing the same. Later, they understand what they have done," she said.
She reiterated that what mattered most to her was that her daughter now regrets her actions and understands that she spoke disrespectfully about someone much older than her.

The controversy began after a video of the girl making abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Jantar Mantar went viral on social media. A Zero FIR was subsequently registered on July 29 at the Expressway police station in Uttar Pradesh's Gautam Buddh Nagar on the complaint of a Ghaziabad resident.

The girl later released a video apologising with folded hands, claiming she was 15 years old and had been influenced by others at the protest. She said she deeply regretted her remarks and appealed for forgiveness, calling it the "first and last mistake" of her life.

Based on the complaint, the case was registered under Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. A Zero FIR allows a complaint to be registered at any police station regardless of jurisdiction before being transferred to the appropriate police station for investigation.
Meanwhile, Delhi Police said that they have not registered an FIRn in connection with the incident and that no fresh case will be filed by it.
