Govt introduces Bill to overhaul Indian Statistical Institute governance; faculties flag autonomy concerns
Centre said the legislation will modernise the institute and enable it to emerge as a globally recognised centre for statistical sciences and allied disciplines

The Union government on Monday introduced the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha, proposing to repeal the 67-year-old Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959 and replace the premier institution’s society-based governance structure with a statutory framework centred on a government-accountable Board of Governors (BoG), a move that would fundamentally alter how the institute is governed, how its director is appointed and how key academic decisions—from admissions and curriculum to new courses and collaborations—are taken.

The government said the legislation would modernise the institute and enable it to emerge as a globally recognised centre for statistical sciences and allied disciplines. However, sections of the ISI faculty, students and staff have opposed the move, arguing that it would dilute the institute’s autonomy by centralising decision-making through BoG and increasing the Centre’s control over academic and administrative affairs. A CPI(ML) MP has also sought the Bill’s scrutiny by a parliamentary committee.

Introducing the Bill, minister of state for statistics and programme implementation Rao Inderjit Singh said it seeks to provide a “comprehensive statutory framework” to enable ISI to “excel as a globally recognised centre in statistical sciences and allied fields.”

Under the existing legal framework, ISI is an Institution of National Importance under the ISI Act, 1959, but is administered through the ISI Society, which is registered under the West Bengal Societies Registration Act, 1961. The proposed legislation repeals the 1959 Act instead of amending it and converts ISI into a statutory body corporate governed by a Board of Governors. The new bill proposes that ISI would be incorporated as a statutory “body corporate,” replacing its current status as a registered society. This is aimed at strengthening its governance, promoting academic excellence and research, and enabling it to serve the emerging needs in the field of statistics and allied disciplines towards Viksit Bharat, bill says.

Founded by statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1931, ISI played a pioneering role in developing India’s statistical system, laid the foundation for the National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO), contributed to the country’s planning process and housed India’s first electronic computer in 1956. Parliament declared it an Institution of National Importance through the ISI Act, 1959, which was amended in 1995 to expand its degree-awarding powers beyond statistics to subjects such as mathematics, quantitative economics and computer science. Under the existing Act, ISI runs 3 undergraduate, 8 postgraduate, 6 diploma, certificate courses apart from the PhD programme.

The new Bill expands the institute’s mandate beyond statistics to include data science, computer science, cryptology and other quantitative sciences, while empowering it to establish campuses in India and abroad, promote industry collaborations, create endowment funds and generate its own revenue.
The most significant changes relate to governance. At present, ISI is governed through three principal bodies—the ISI Society, the ISI Council and the Academic Council.

The ISI Society, comprising elected and nominated members from within and outside the institute, is the apex representative body. Its president appoints the chairperson of the ISI Council. The Council, consisting of elected and nominated members, including eminent scientists, academicians and government nominees, oversees the institute’s administration and appoints the director. The director, in consultation with the Council chairperson, appoints the heads of ISI’s centres, all of whom report to the director at the Kolkata headquarters.

The Bill replaces this structure with a Board of Governors (BoGs), which will become the institute’s principal executive and policy-making authority. The Board, headed by a chairperson appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Central government, will appoint the director and exercise final authority over academic, administrative, financial, personnel and developmental matters. The Bill also states that the Board will be accountable to the Central government. The legislation further strengthens government oversight by making the President of India the Visitor of the institute with powers to order reviews and inquiries and authorising the Centre to issue directions to the institute.

The Bill retains the Academic Council, headed by the director and comprising all full-time professors and faculty members, as the institute’s principal academic body. However, several of its powers become recommendatory.

Decisions relating to admissions, curriculum, introduction or discontinuation of academic programmes, award of degrees and diplomas, academic collaborations and other academic matters would originate in the Academic Council but require the approval of the Board of Governors, which will have the final say. The appointment process for the director will also change. Under the existing system, the director is appointed through the institute’s society-based governance mechanism. Under the proposed law, the appointment will be made by the Visitor from a panel recommended by a search-cum-selection committee constituted under the new statutory framework.
Although the Bill enables ISI to institute fellowships and scholarships, it does not provide a statutory entitlement to research stipends, an issue flagged by sections of the student community.
Opposition from faculty and students

Sections of the ISI community have argued that the proposed law fundamentally alters the institute’s governance without adequate consultation. In a joint statement issued on August 1, faculty, students and staff said the Bill replaces a democratically represented Council with a central government-appointed Board of Governors, curtails the role of the Academic Council and converts ISI into a statutory body corporate “without consulting the ISI Society or the institute’s other bodies.”

Faculty members have further expressed concern that the Bill does not explicitly recognise Kolkata as ISI’s headquarters, could require years of rewriting rules and regulations and may disrupt academic functioning during the transition. Opposing the Bill, faculty members along with students and non-teaching staff held a protest March at ISI headquarters in Kolkata on Monday.

Separately, CPI(ML) Liberation MP Raja Ram Singh on Monday wroted minister Singh seeking that the Bill be referred to a parliamentary committee, arguing that legislation affecting an Institution of National Importance should undergo wider stakeholder consultation before being enacted as it has “far-reaching consequences.”

Lok Sabha passes bill to raise Supreme Court judges’ strength to 38
The Bill, passed by a voice vote, replaces an ordinance promulgated in May and comes amid a mounting “backlog” of cases before the court.

The Lok Sabha on Monday passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, raising the sanctioned strength of judges in the top court from 34 to 38, including the Chief Justice of India. The Bill, passed by a voice vote, replaces an ordinance promulgated in May and comes amid a mounting “backlog” of cases before the court.

Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal introduced the Bill amid Opposition protests. The Bill states that the persistent gap between institution and disposal of cases has made “docket management” increasingly difficult, particularly for older pending matters and cases needing larger Benches.

The Supreme Court’s sanctioned strength has been revised several times since 1950, when the court began with eight judges, including the Chief Justice of India. It was raised to 31 in 2008 and to 34 in 2019. The government now proposes taking it to 38, citing rising litigation and the need for more Benches to hear cases quickly.

According to a written reply by Meghwal in Parliament, more than 96,000 cases are currently pending in the Supreme Court, with 26 cases unresolved for over 30 years and 558 pending for more than two decades. The government maintains that adding judges is among the most effective ways to cut this backlog.

The Bill was first introduced in the Lok Sabha on July 20, before being taken up for consideration and passage on Monday. Piloting the Bill, Meghwal told the House, “The additional judges will help the Supreme Court function more efficiently and ensure speedier justice.” He added that the expansion was necessitated by a rising backlog of cases before the court.

The government has pointed to data showing that Supreme Court disposals outpaced fresh filings in three months this year, February, April and May, but says overall pendency continues to rise as more litigants approach the court each year. Officials argue that four additional judges will allow the formation of more Benches, helping clear both fresh cases and long-pending matters, including some tied up for over three decades.

The Centre has also flagged pendency in larger Constitution Benches as a concern. As of June 2026, 22 five-judge, five seven-judge and two nine-judge Bench matters remain undecided, with the government hoping a larger judge strength will speed up listing and disposal of such cases.

Legal experts note that simply adding judges may not by itself resolve pendency. The 18th Law Commission, in its 229th report, had recommended setting up a Constitution Bench in Delhi along with regional benches, rather than only expanding numbers, arguing that appointment delays, and not sanctioned strength, have historically driven vacancies and backlogs.
The Bill is yet to be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.

Supreme Court opens door for withdrawal of FIRs against student protestors
Supreme Court clarifies eligibility for withdrawal of criminal cases against student protesters, allowing states to close FIRs without serious offenses.

The Supreme Court on Monday said it was willing to facilitate the withdrawal of criminal cases against student protesters, clarifying that its previous order did not stand in the way of governments closing or withdrawing FIRs against eligible students and that only those with “grave and heinous” criminal antecedents would fall outside the protective umbrella granted last week.

The court’s clarification was welcomed by the Cockroach Janta Party, and its spokesperson Saurav Das said: “Another major victory was achieved for the youth. The Supreme Court clarified that the states that wish to withdraw the FIRs will have the liberty to do so, and the Supreme Court’s [earlier] order will not interfere with that.”

The court’s comment came after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Centre and the Delhi police, reiterated the Centre’s commitment to withdrawing cases against eligible protesters, saying the issue was now one of legal procedure rather than intent.

That was likely a reference to the court’s direction on July 28. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan submitted that this previous direction permitting investigation to continue was being construed as an impediment to the withdrawal of FIRs, while senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi pointed out that the phrase “criminal antecedents”, again used in that direction, could cover even trivial offences.

In response, a bench, comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, clarified its July 28 interim order to state that Delhi and all other states would be “at liberty to close/withdraw cases in accordance with law”, and that the expression “criminal antecedents” used in the earlier order referred only to grave and heinous offences.
The bench repeatedly emphasised that it did not want criminal cases to continue hanging over the future of students.

“If both of you agree on, we can facilitate the process so that FIRs do not keep hanging on the heads of the students,” it observed during the hearing after Mehta said: “The government is serious about its assurance on the withdrawal of FIRs...It may be a matter of following a process and semantics.” He added that those leading the protests were already in dialogue with the government.
Pellet gun use under judicial scrutiny

Appearing for former Intelligence Bureau special director Yashovardhan Azad and two pellet gun victims, advocate Vrinda Grover said the petitioners had been engaging with the government and stressed that the protesters were young people whose lives should not be permanently affected by pending criminal proceedings.

“These protesters are youth and they have their life ahead. Youth have to move on,” said Grover, while expressing concern that the statutory process for withdrawal of prosecutions could prove cumbersome.
The bench suggested that both sides work together to identify cases that could either be withdrawn by the public prosecutor or closed through appropriate police reports.
“Withdrawal within the legal framework is permissible,” observed the bench, urging the parties to “forge a convenient way”.

At the same time, the court clarified that it was not directing withdrawal in every case.

“We are not asking you to withdraw the FIRs against murderers,” remarked the bench after the solicitor general informed the court that 2,738 persons facing charges such as murder, rape, kidnapping and offences under the POCSO Act had been identified among the protestors.

The bench also disclosed that it was considering constituting two separate mechanisms -- a special investigation team comprising serving and former senior police officers to examine cases that are not withdrawn or closed, and a committee headed by a former judge to inquire into other issues arising from the nationwide protests.

Addressing concerns raised by petitioners over alleged police excesses, the bench said it wanted to ensure that neither police officials accused of wrongdoing nor persons responsible for violence escaped scrutiny.
“Let no such impression go that the police officials taking the law into their own hands are protected or those creating violence under the garb of protest are protected,” it underlined.

Underscoring the human dimension of the litigation, the court added: “We have to see that children are not dragged into any legal problem...this is also for the parents who with their hard-earned money have funded their education.”

The bench also continued its examination of the alleged use of pellet guns during the July 20 “Sansad Chalo” protest. India clears one China FDI proposal as Hong Kong gets 13 in FY26
India approved one Chinese FDI proposal worth Rs 1 crore and 13 from Hong Kong in 2025-26. The data highlights how Press Note 3 scrutiny continues for investors from land-border countries.

India approved only one foreign direct investment (FDI) proposal from China worth Rs 1 crore during the financial year 2025-26, while clearing 13 investment proposals from Hong Kong worth Rs 610.42 crore, according to official data released by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), reports PTI.

The figures come as investments from countries sharing a land border with India continue to require prior government approval under Press Note 3, introduced in April 2020 to prevent opportunistic takeovers of Indian companies during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Overall, the government approved 63 FDI proposals worth Rs 10,292.67 crore (USD 1.18 billion) under the government approval route during April 2025 to March 2026.
SINGAPORE TOPS APPROVED FDI PROPOSALS
Singapore emerged as the largest source of approved FDI proposals by value, with five proposals worth Rs 3,259.88 crore (USD 382.52 million) receiving government clearance.
The United Kingdom followed with five proposals worth Rs 2,477.67 crore ($283 million), while Thailand secured approval for two proposals worth Rs 1,600 crore (around $180 million).
PRESS NOTE 3 NORMS EASED BUT NOT FOR CHINA

In March, the government relaxed certain provisions under Press Note 3 by allowing investments through the automatic route where beneficial ownership from land-border countries does not exceed 10 per cent, subject to sectoral caps and other conditions.

However, the relaxation does not apply to entities registered in China, Hong Kong, or any other country sharing a land border with India. Such investments continue to require prior government approval.
India shares land borders with China, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar and Afghanistan.

According to DPIIT data, China has never been a major source of FDI into India. Between April 2000 and March 2026, Chinese investments accounted for just 0.32 per cent of India's total FDI equity inflows, amounting to $2.51 billion (Rs 16,162.25 crore), placing China 23rd among investing countries.
Hong Kong ranked 15th, contributing $4.91 billion (Rs 31,220.30 crore), or 0.62 per cent of total FDI equity inflows during the same period.

The trend was similar in 2024-25, when India also approved only one Chinese FDI proposal, valued at Rs 28.71 crore. During that financial year, 82 proposals worth Rs 39,758 crore ($4.72 billion) were cleared under the government route, including 11 proposals from Hong Kong worth Rs 1,225.28 crore.

On Monday, August 3, we will get a sense of the public mood in the country, or, to be specific, in Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) strongholds such as Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar. Three Assembly seats, one in each of these States, held bypolls on July 30.

The one that all of us should watch closely is Bankipur in Bihar’s capital city, Patna. Bankipur is the heart of the heartland. The outcome in this seat will provide an indication of heartland politics in the aftermath of the student protests that recently rocked the country. The seat was vacated by Nitin Nabin, the BJP’s national president, and Jan Suraj leader Prashant Kishor is contesting from the constituency, testing his caste-free, anti-BJP politics in one of the party’s strongest forts.

No BJP candidate has ever lost from this seat. Mr. Nabin himself won it four consecutive times, most recently in 2025. It is an urban constituency with a demographic composition that has long made the BJP appear invincible. Yet the party has been compelled to deploy all its might in this by-election. Hundreds of party leaders from within and outside Bihar have camped there, mobilising every resource at their disposal.
Why is this seat so important for the BJP, and why will Monday’s (August 3) result be indicative of the party’s standing?

Bankipur is the first election after the BJP took over the Chief Minister’s post from Nitish Kumar. The party won the 2025 Assembly election with Mr. Kumar as its leader, and he continued to command a strong following among Other Backward Classes (OBC) voters within the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in the State. Bankipur will test how the BJP fares when it is fully in command, with Mr. Kumar removed from the political scene.

Bankipur has 3.79 lakh voters, of whom about 1.6 lakh are upper-caste Hindus, the core of BJP support in the Hindi heartland. There are around 40,000 Yadavs and roughly the same number of Muslims. Yadav and Muslim voters usually tend to support the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), which has never been in contention for much more than a lakh votes here. There are around 50,000 Dalits. The anti-Yadav social polarisation that has been a defining feature of Bihar elections for several years has overwhelmingly worked in the BJP’s favour in this constituency.

Apart from that, Bankipur has also become a hotspot of Hindutva mobilisation. Mr. Nabin began organising large Ram Navami processions in the constituency, which observers estimate drew nearly a lakh participants last March. Muharram processions, in which Muslims gather in large numbers, have also long been a feature of the constituency. Though the two do not occur at the same time, there has been a sense of competitiveness between them, helping to keep communal divisions politically salient over the years.

Mr. Kishor’s candidacy and campaign have challenged this pattern. A Brahmin himself, Mr. Kishor has advanced a caste-free politics in the State, seeking votes on a development agenda. But identity politics still matters in Bihar. What became a concern for the BJP was that some caste arithmetic also appeared to shift in his favour. Since the RJD never stood a realistic chance in the constituency, and Mr. Kishor emerged as a viable alternative, a section of upper-caste voters appeared inclined towards him. Muslims found in him an attractive option, while non-Yadav OBCs seemed less enthusiastic about the NDA without Nitish Kumar. Given these factors, even a section of Yadav voters may have viewed Mr. Kishor as a credible choice.
All told, turnout was low, at 34.24%, representing a drop of more than seven percentage points from last year, and there were indications of remarkable social realignment.

Mr. Kishor told The Hindu on Saturday (August 1) that the State government had unleashed the police on polling day to suppress his voters. “The BJP knows that its communal politics is no longer working. So this time it tried to misuse the administration and the police. Still, they will get a shock on Monday.”

Regardless of who wins on Monday (August 3), there will be enough indicators to gauge the mood of the heartland. Patna University is located in Bankipur. Jayaprakash Narayan lived in the Kadam Kuan locality within the constituency. Gandhi Maidan, which has witnessed many turning points not only in Bihar’s politics but also in the political history of the country, is also in Bankipur.

New Delhi: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor dealt a major blow to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) as he defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by almost 19,000 votes in his electoral debut in the Bankipur assembly bypolls.
According to data released by the Election Commission, Kishor bagged 63,203 votes, followed by Sinha, who managed 44,250 votes in the high-stakes battle. RJD’s Rekha Gupta is in the distant third.

JSP party workers celebrated across Patna. Kishor thanked the Bankipur voters and said victories and defeats keep happening. “I am grateful to the people…I sincerely thank everyone who placed their trust and faith in Jan Suraaj and me. I also want to thank those who voted for our political opponents and assure them that after the election, those who voted for us and those who did not are equally ours,” he told the media.
The Bankipur seat fell vacant after BJP national president Nitin Nabin resigned as MLA following his election to the Rajya Sabha in April. Polling was held 30 July.
The seat had witnessed drama as barely 24 hours after nominating Abhishek Bunty from Bankipur, the BJP had replaced him with Neeraj Kumar Sinha for the bypoll.

Kishor had also accused Patna Senior Superintendent of Police Kartikey Kumar Sharma of misusing police powers to intimidate voters and unlawfully detaining local workers. The JSP leader while addressing a press conference said that homes of several persons were also raided. Kishor claimed that his party had taken up the matter with the ECI.

For the BJP, Bankipur is a prestige fight. The seat, considered high-profile, is a BJP stronghold. It was earlier known as the Patna West assembly constituency. Nabin’s father Kishore Prasad Sinha won it multiple times from 1995 until his demise in 2006.
More than 25 percent of voters in the constituency are Kayasthas, a community that Nabin belongs to. The constituency also has a sizable upper-caste mix of Bhumihars.

Nabin entered electoral politics after his father’s demise, first winning the seat in a 2006 by-election. In the assembly polls last year, he had won for a fifth consecutive term, defeating the RJD candidate by a margin of nearly 50,000 votes.

In the last year’s Bihar election, Nabin had won the seat for a fifth consecutive term, defeating the RJD candidate by a margin of nearly 50,000. The BJP set a target of increasing the winning margin, with its party president holding several meetings and campaigning extensively in the constituency.
Kishor launched the Jan Suraaj Party on 2 October 2024 after a two-year pan-Bihar march, the Jan Suraaj Padyatra. This was after exiting a career in political consulting in 2021.

A JSP functionary explained how professionals managed the entire campaign and key workers of the party were given charge of four booths each and after submitting the reports for each of them. A review meeting used to take place every night with Kishor, he said.

“Booth committees were also made for this purpose and it was ensure that a section of these members were local representatives from the area. Everything was meticulously planned and we are hoping to win the seat.”
In the last year’s Bihar elections, Kishor fielded candidates in 238 of the 243 seats, but he himself did not contest. The party drew a blank, getting just 3.4 percent vote share.

No Assembly bypoll has been watched with keener interest than the one that just concluded at Bankipur in Bihar in a resounding victory for Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) leader Prashant Kishor. He challenged the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in its fort, winning the seat that’s considered its stronghold since 1995 and was recently vacated by the party’s national president Nitin Nabin, a loss that comes on the heels of the Gen Z protests at the national capital.
For the BJP, losing the Bankipur bypoll goes beyond the more typical loss of a stronghold to probing internal issues and factoring the electorate’s changed demographic profile.

Gurugram: When Haryana BJP’s newly appointed state president Dr Archana Gupta rolled out her list of office-bearers this week, one pattern stood out—several party leaders who had been denied poll tickets or had openly expressed their ire against the senior leadership found themselves accommodated.

The list, cleared with the concurrence of BJP’s national president Nitin Nabin, names eight state vice-presidents, three general secretaries, nine state secretaries, four office-bearers handling treasury and administration, four in charge of media and IT, six morcha presidents and two cell in-charges.
The most striking name on the list is of Bhavya Bishnoi, son of former MP Kuldeep Bishnoi and grandson of former Haryana chief minister Bhajan Lal, who has been made a state vice president.

The Bishnois were at the centre of a public row just months earlier. In April, Rajya Sabha MP Rekha Sharma, addressing a meeting ahead of the Panchkula mayoral election, alleged that BJP candidate Sham Lal Bansal had lost the same seat years ago because of “badmaashi” by then CM Bhajan Lal and his men. Kuldeep and Bhavya reacted sharply and Sharma later apologised.
Since then, Kuldeep Bishnoi’s proximity to Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Saini has been visible, though he skipped Saini’s event at Guru Jambheshwar University in Hisar last month.

Earlier, in 2024, Kuldeep Bishnoi and his supporters had targeted former CM Manohar Lal Khattar in Hisar during the Lok Sabha campaign, after Khattar seemed to accuse Bhajan Lal, without naming him, of promoting corruption. Kuldeep was also passed over by the party for a poll ticket.
Bhavya Bishnoi’s own political run has had its share of setbacks.

Kuldeep fielded his son instead of contesting himself in the 2019 Lok Sabha election from Hisar, where he finished third. In 2022, when Kuldeep quit the Congress for the BJP, he fielded Bhavya for the bypoll in Adampur—a seat he himself had vacated and which Bhavya won comfortably.

Duggal, fielded once more from Ratia, lost to Congress’s Jarnail Singh.
Now, one of the men who defeated Duggal now figure alongside her on Gupta’s list. Ravinder Baliala, who beat her in 2014, joined the BJP in 2019 and has been named a state vice president.

Also on the list is Deepak Mangla, who won the Palwal assembly seat in 2019 after losing it to Congress’s Karan Singh Dalal in 2014, but was denied a ticket in 2024 when the party fielded Gaurav Gautam instead. Mangla has now been named a state vice president.

No insurance, no fuel? Supreme Court proposes pilot project at petrol pumps
A major road safety push could make insurance checks routine at fuel stations, while ANPR cameras, police apps and longer insurance cover for new vehicles are also proposed.

The Supreme Court has proposed a major crackdown on vehicles being driven without valid insurance, asking the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to prepare a pilot project that could see petrol pumps check a vehicle's insurance before supplying fuel.
Under the proposed system, vehicles without valid insurance could be denied petrol or diesel until the required cover is obtained.

The move is part of a wider set of road safety measures proposed by the court, including linking automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras with vehicle and insurance databases, giving traffic police mobile tools to check insurance instantly and extending the mandatory third-party insurance period for newly purchased vehicles.
The court has asked IRDAI and the road transport ministry to work on a pilot project that would allow petrol pumps to verify whether a vehicle has valid insurance before dispensing fuel.
If the vehicle is found to be uninsured, the proposed system could allow fuel stations to refuse the supply of petrol or diesel.
The measure is aimed at increasing compliance with mandatory motor insurance rules and making it harder for uninsured vehicles to remain on the roads.
The proposal is a pilot project and does not mean that petrol pumps across the country will immediately start refusing fuel to uninsured vehicles.
ANPR CAMERAS TO BE LINKED TO INSURANCE DATA
The Supreme Court has also proposed linking ANPR cameras installed on highways and roads with the VAHAN vehicle database and insurance databases.
The system could automatically identify vehicles without valid insurance and generate e-challans against them.

ANPR cameras are already used in several places to detect traffic violations such as speeding, jumping red lights and driving on the wrong side of the road. Linking them with insurance records could extend their use to identifying uninsured vehicles.
POLICE TO GET MOBILE INSURANCE CHECKS
Traffic police could also be provided with mobile applications or handheld devices to check a vehicle's insurance status instantly during roadside inspections.
The proposed devices would be linked to relevant vehicle and insurance databases, allowing officers to verify whether a vehicle has valid cover without relying on physical insurance documents.
LONGER INSURANCE COVER FOR NEW VEHICLES
The court has also proposed extending the mandatory third-party insurance period for newly purchased vehicles.
For new private cars, the compulsory third-party insurance period would increase from three years to four years.
For new two-wheelers, the period would rise from five years to six years.
The move is aimed at reducing the number of vehicles that become uninsured after their initial insurance period expires.
WHY THE COURT IS PUSHING FOR TIGHTER CHECKS
The court has taken a wider view of the problem of uninsured vehicles, with the proposed measures aimed at ensuring that mandatory third-party insurance requirements are actually followed.
The proposed fuel check, ANPR integration and police verification system would create multiple points at which an uninsured vehicle could be identified.
The measures would also make it easier for authorities to track vehicles that continue to operate without the legally required insurance.

The Supreme Court's proposals are now to be worked out by the concerned authorities, with the pilot project expected to examine how the insurance verification system can be implemented without disrupting the functioning of fuel stations or legitimate vehicle use.

For now, the proposals signal a significant tightening of India's approach to uninsured vehicles, with the court looking beyond conventional roadside enforcement towards technology and everyday services such as fuel purchases to improve compliance.

Bengaluru: The outpouring of dissent within Karnataka’s ruling Congress over the latest Cabinet expansion spilled into a second straight day Tuesday, with several senior and prominent leaders blaming infighting among top leaders and even the party high command for their exclusion from D.K. So far, at least one senior Congress legislator has resigned, and several others have indicated that their supporters are pressuring them to follow suit, compounding the challenges for Shivakumar, who himself was made the chief minister in June in place of Siddaramaiah after months of infighting.

“I was close to Siddaramaiah and respect him a great deal even today. But I never liked the behaviour of some people, the way they talk,” M.C. Sudhakar, the Congress legislator from Chikballapura, told Public TV.
The former minister for higher education said that he was “targeted” due to his proximity to Siddaramaiah—who heads one of the three main factions in the Congress party.

People aware of the developments say that after being replaced by Shivakuma as CM, Siddaramaiah nursed a feeling of neglect over the high command’s decision to drop his former colleagues and even stayed away from the 3 August swearing-in ceremony for 19 newly inducted ministers.

Legislators even trained their guns at the All India Congress Committee (AICC) leadership who took two months to draft the cabinet expansion list that threw up many surprises and dropped several seniors without intimation.

“If this process was done quickly, would so many people be upset? They dragged it on for two months and probably the high command did not take Karnataka seriously and did not deal with the situation properly,” Sudhakar said.
Senior legislators like T.B. Jayachandra, Dinesh Gundu Rao, Belur Srinivas, Rahim Khan, Tanveer Said and several others questioned the criteria used to finalise the list.

While dissent is not unusual after cabinet expansion exercises, it is bogging the CM down at a time when the state approaches crucial local elections. The severe drought condition also needs urgent government attention.

With Shanthegowda excluded, the current cabinet consists of 33 men and no women. Supporters of former minister Lakshmi Hebbalkar, who have been protesting since Monday afternoon, are now hoping for her reinstatement.
Other women leaders including Nayana Motamma, Annapoorna Tukaram and Kaneez Fathima have also demanded to be considered for the last remaining cabinet seat.

Meanwhile, supporters of senior Congress leader M. Krishnappa and his son, MLA Priya Krishna, stormed into the party office in Bengaluru, threatening to resign en masse over the exclusion of their leader(s).

S.R. Srinivas, the Congress legislator from Gubbi in Tumakuru, said that he cannot do much about being excluded from the cabinet. “It’s difficult for a farmer’s son to rise in politics. Rao, a six-time MLA from Gandhi Nagar in Bengaluru, said that he was disappointed at being given no reason for his exclusion.
“I am pained not for missing out on a cabinet berth but because I have been given no reason for being dropped,” Rao said.
He also said that it was the first time that a Brahmin would not be part of the state cabinet. Rao had served as the minister for health & family welfare in the previous Siddaramaiah government.
The Chief Minister Tuesday said that he will meet disgruntled MLAs and give them assignments in Boards and Corporations, and assign other roles within the government and party.
Shivakumar said that tendering resignations is common in politics and that he cannot stop anyone from doing so.

He reiterated his own exclusion from the cabinets of Dharam Singh and the earlier Siddaramaiah government (2013-18) and how patience was key to longevity in politics. “The Party is very important. India condemned Pakistan for using lethal force against protesters in PoK, urging global accountability for 90 civilian deaths amid ongoing violence.

India on Tuesday accused Pakistan of using lethal force, intimidation and repression against protesters in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), resulting in the death of 90 civilians, as it again urged the world community to hold Islamabad accountable for the human rights violations and atrocities.

The remarks by external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal at a regular media briefing came against the backdrop of Pakistani authorities holding elections in two constituencies in PoK to complete the second phase of polls to the local assembly.

Jaiswal, who was responding to a question on violence by Pakistani security forces against the protesters and the elections to the assembly in PoK, described the electoral exercise as a “complete farce” and called on the world community to focus on “wanton killings” in the region.

“This so-called local election in PoK is a complete farce. The real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by the Pakistani forces. Such hollow exercises cannot hide reality,” he said.

Jaiswal pointed out that at least 90 civilians had lost their lives in a continuing crackdown by Pakistani authorities since June. “Many more have been injured as you have seen. The Pakistani establishment has answered public discontent with bullets, blackouts, intimidation and repression, and now seeks to manufacture legitimacy through a hollow electoral exercise,” he said.

Pakistan “must be held accountable” and the world “should see through the veneer of Pakistan’s hypocritical lecturing on human rights”, Jaiswal said. “The international community must hold Pakistan accountable for these atrocities.”

PoK has been affected by violence since the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), a local organisation, launched a protest earlier this year against high inflation and cost of living in the region. It also demanded the abolition of seats reserved in the local assembly for refugees from the Indian region of Jammu and Kashmir, which experts have contended are used by Pakistan’s security establishment to manipulate the outcome of elections.

Elections to the assembly in PoK are being held in three phases, and the first and second phases on July 27 and August 2 were marred by firing by security forces on protesters and allegations of rigging. Elections could not be held in the two constituencies that voted on Tuesday because of landslides and bad weather on Sunday. The third phase will be held on August 10.

The Pakistan People’s Party (PPP), which is part of the PML-N-led ruling coalition in Islamabad, on Tuesday accused its political partner of rigging, violence and electoral malpractices during the second phase of polling.

Supreme Court proposes no fuel for uninsured vehicles, seeks Centre's plan
The top court also ordered a technology-driven enforcement mechanism to automatically identify and penalise such vehicles without an insurance.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Centre and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) to evolve a pilot project under which uninsured vehicles could be denied fuel at petrol pumps, while also ordering a technology-driven enforcement mechanism to automatically identify and penalise such vehicles.

In a landmark bid to tackle the menace of uninsured vehicles and ensure timely compensation for road accident victims, a bench of justice Sanjay Karol and Prashant Kumar Mishra issued a slew of directions, including integration of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras with insurance databases to generate automatic e-challans for uninsured vehicles, provision of handheld devices to traffic police for real-time verification of insurance status, enhancement of mandatory third-party insurance tenure for new vehicles, and expeditious disposal of old motor accident compensation cases.

Observing that nearly 56% of vehicles plying on Indian roads remain uninsured, the bench said that the statutory safeguard of compensating road accident victims was often “delayed, if not defeated”, forcing victims and their families into prolonged litigation.
Also Read | Insurer not liable to pay compensation for accidents if driver's licence invalid, says SC

“The object behind mandatory insurance under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act is not just that victims of road accidents are compensated, it is also that they are not drawn into prolonged litigation,” it noted.

The court directed the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and IRDAI to examine a pilot project under which fuel supply would be linked to a vehicle’s insurance status. “In the absence thereof, the vehicle concerned would be refused fuel at petrol pumps until such time that valid insurance is obtained,” ordered the bench, noting that the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas had, in principle, expressed no objection to the proposal.
Also Read | Time restrictions on filing insurance claims are void: HC

The bench underlined that such a mechanism would help identify uninsured and unregistered vehicles while nudging owners to maintain valid insurance. It suggested that the project could be implemented using ANPR cameras.

To strengthen enforcement, the court directed that ANPR cameras already deployed on highways and city roads for detecting traffic violations be integrated with the Insurance Information Bureau database and the VAHAN portal to enable automatic issuance of e-challans to uninsured vehicles. It also directed States to equip traffic police with handheld devices or mobile applications linked to these databases to verify insurance status on the spot and issue challans.

The court further directed strict implementation of the proposed amendment to Section 196 of the Motor Vehicles Act, which prescribes steeper penalties for driving uninsured vehicles once notified by the Centre.
Also Read | Insurers can deny claim over hiding drinking habit, says SC

In a significant change affecting new vehicle buyers, the bench directed that the mandatory third-party insurance cover be enhanced from three years to four years for new private cars and from five years to six years for new two-wheelers. The court said it was extending the period by one year despite IRDAI and the General Insurance Council recommending against such a move, holding that the measure was necessary in the interest of road safety.
The direction builds upon the Supreme Court’s ruling in S Rajaseekaran Vs Union of India (2018), which had mandated long-term third-party insurance at the time of registration of new vehicles.

The judgment also overhauls the structure of motor insurance policies. Accepting IRDAI’s proposal, the court directed implementation of a uniform four-layer framework comprising a mandatory third-party policy, an optional legal liability cover for occupants and pillion riders, an optional personal accident cover for the owner, driver and occupants, and an optional own-damage cover.
Also Read | Better ride quality, lower fuel average: Nitin Gadkari to Parliament on how E20 petrol affects vehicles

With a view to ensure informed consumer choice, every purchaser of motor insurance -- online or offline, will have to be provided with a standardised customer option form allowing them to opt into additional covers, along with a consumer-friendly information sheet explaining the mandatory and optional components of motor insurance. The court also directed IRDAI, in consultation with the General Insurance Council and insurers, to formulate uniform policy wordings for the optional covers while allowing insurers flexibility in pricing and innovation.
The bench additionally directed insurance companies to prominently display the benefits of comprehensive motor insurance policies on their websites in an easy-to-understand format.

Concerned over delays in compensation cases, the court further revived earlier directions governing motor accident claims for accidents that occurred before March 31, 2022, when the Detailed Accident Report (DAR) regime became operational under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules.
Also Read | Union cabinet approves scheme to replace old trucks, buses to curb air pollution

Relying on a clutch of previous rulings, the bench directed State police to promptly file DARs along with all relevant documents before motor accident claims tribunals (MACTs) in pending pre-March 2022 cases and ensure production of witnesses to facilitate speedy disposal.
The court noted that more than half of MACT cases continue to remain pending for over four years and stressed that road safety forms an integral part of the right to life under Article 21.
The bench directed all stakeholders to comply with its directions and file affidavits by August 14, and listed the matter for monitoring compliance on August 18.

The directions came while disposing of an appeal filed by National Insurance Company Ltd against a Telangana High Court judgment awarding compensation to the family of a man who died in a 1996 road accident while travelling in his own Maruti 800 car. The insurer had argued that the comprehensive insurance policy did not cover the owner’s risk. Affirming the high court’s view, the bench held that a comprehensive policy covered the owner travelling in the vehicle and declined to interfere, reiterating that courts should not adopt a hyper-technical approach in motor accident compensation matters.

Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi experienced turbulence-related event during cruise. (Photo: TOI)

NEW DELHI: Some passengers and crew members onboard Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight (AI 2379) suffered injuries when the aircraft encountered turbulence Tuesday morning, causing a sudden drop in altitude by 300 feet. An AI with medical support received the 134 passengers onboard the Airbus A320 on arrival just after 11 am. Over 10 passengers and two crew members are learnt to have been taken to the Medanta medical centre at the airport.

Subsequently, 14 injured - 10 passengers and four crew members - were shifted to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram and India Spinal Injury Centre in Vasant Kunj.An AI spokesperson said the aircraft âexperienced a brief in-flight turbulence-related event during cruise, resulting in a momentary change in altitude. The aircraft landed safely in Delhi and all passengers and crew have safely disembarked. There have been no serious injuries reported as of now.

A small number of passengers and crew members with minor injuries requiring medical assessment have been taken to a medical facility at the airport for precautionary examination and care by Air Indiaâs airport team and medical personnel.
âThe A320 had taken off from Phuket at 8.27 am and landed in Delhi just after 11 am (all timings local).

âThe safety and well-being of our passengers and crew remain Air Indiaâs highest priority. We are providing all necessary support to those affected and are cooperating fully with the relevant authorities as part of the investigation,â the spokesperson added.Aircraft frequently experience clear air turbulence (CAT), which International Civil Aviation Organisation defines as turbulence generated in clear air, in regions without clouds that is invisible to the pilot and by the US Federal Aviation Administration as sudden severe turbulence occurring in cloudless regions that causes violent buffeting of aircraft. Due to this possibility, it is advisable to have seatbelt loosely on during flight.
Supreme Court orders crackdown on digital arrest scams, faster money recovery

A Supreme Court panel seeks tighter coordination between banks, intermediaries and police as digital arrest scams grow, with new measures aimed at blocking mule accounts and helping victims recover defrauded funds.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued a slew of directions to strengthen the fight against digital fraud, asking the RBI to prepare and circulate a standard operating procedure for bank accounts linked to cybercrimes and directing states and Union Territories to speed up grievance redressal and money recovery mechanisms for victims.

A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also asked an Inter-Departmental Committee set up by the Centre to consult banks and financial intermediaries on ways to prevent "digital arrest" scams and help victims recover defrauded money.
The bench was hearing a suo motu matter, 'In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents'.
RBI SOP ON CYBER FRAUD, MULE ACCOUNTS
The Supreme Court directed the Reserve Bank of India to prepare and circulate an SOP for dealing with bank accounts linked to cyber frauds, including mule accounts.
The RBI has also been asked to provide copies of the SOP to the Registrars General of all high courts, allowing the guidelines to be made available across the judiciary.
STATES, UTs TOLD TO ACT ON GRIEVANCE, MONEY RECOVERY

The court directed all states, Union Territories and law enforcement agencies to ensure the expeditious adoption and operationalisation of grievance redressal and money restoration modules developed for victims of cyber-enabled financial frauds.

States and UTs were also asked to take steps to ensure public awareness about these grievance redressal and money restoration mechanisms so that citizens know where and how to seek help after being defrauded.

The Registrars General of all high courts were directed to apprise courts about the grievance redressal and money restoration modules, ensuring that victims are made aware of the remedies available to them.
STATE-WISE, BANK-WISE FRAUD DATA SOUGHT

Seeking greater accountability in the handling of cyber fraud complaints, the Supreme Court asked the authorities to submit a report providing state-wise and bank-wise details of grievances registered and disposed of under the cyber fraud redressal mechanism.
The data is expected to provide a clearer picture of how complaints are being handled across states and banking institutions.
FASTER DISPOSAL OF FROZEN BANK ACCOUNTS
The bench also directed authorities to take steps to ensure the expeditious disposal of matters relating to the freezing of bank accounts in cases involving cyber fraud investigations.
The direction comes amid the wider push to make the response to cyber-enabled financial crimes faster and more effective, particularly when money has already moved through banking channels.
PANEL TO CONSULT BANKS ON 'DIGITAL ARREST' SCAMS
The Supreme Court also asked the Inter-Departmental Committee constituted by the Centre to consult banks and financial intermediaries on measures to prevent "digital arrest" scams.
The committee has also been asked to explore ways to facilitate the recovery of money defrauded from victims.

The directions come a week after the apex court suggested that the Centre consider formally defining "digital arrest" in criminal law and treating it as a standalone offence carrying stringent punishment.

The latest directions seek to bring regulators, banks, financial intermediaries, state authorities, law enforcement agencies and the judiciary into a more coordinated framework to tackle digital fraud and improve the recovery of money lost by victims.
Meta's global team in India tomorrow: Govt amid row over PM Modi's reel removal
Govt summons Meta global team in India on August 5-6, says IT Secretary S Krishnan.

The government on Tuesday said it will raise a number of issues, including lapses in tackling of CSAM (Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material), as well as wrongful action on prominent account during the upcoming meeting with Meta's global team.
IT Secretary S Krishnan said that a company at the forefront of technology should have been able to make its systems work as they are supposed to.
Meta's global team will be in India on August 5 and 6, Krishnan added.
It was not immediately clear who will be part of the team that will travel to India. There have been demands by the ruling party BJP's leaders for a personal apology by CEO Mark Zuckerberg.
This comes after Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook reel addressing India's youth and promising stringent action against paper leaks, was briefly restricted on the platform.

The ministry further said that Meta has been under regulatory scrutiny over CSAM in paid advertisements on Instagram. The government had earlier slapped a notice on Meta over the issue, news agency PTI reported.

"There are a range of issues...the CSAM issue was raised, so what measures have been taken regarding that, and synthetically generated information ... to what extent that is being looked at. Then, of course, for prominent personalities, when they have verified accounts, if content has to be taken down, there have to be safeguards...all of these will be the issues," Krishnan told reporters on the sidelines of the launch of an independent multimodal AI evaluation platform by AI4Bharat at IIT Madras and Josh Talks AI.
"We would like to understand from them (Meta) as to why some of these things have not been working the way they are supposed to work, and what are the challenges," Krishnan added.
‘Zuckerberg should apologise or…’

The chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology, Nishikant Dubey, on Monday said Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg should apologise for the temporary removal of PM Modi’s Facebook reel, warning that the company could otherwise lose the “safe harbour” protection available to intermediaries under Section 79 of the Information Technology (IT) Act.

“Meta’s mindset is to destabilise the country. PM Modi’s video was taken down from 12.30 am to 5 am. This is a very serious issue. Our committee has said two things — the apology must come from Mark Zuckerberg or else we will take back the safe harbour given to Meta under Section 79,” Dubey told reporters.
Responding to the criticism, Meta apologised, attributing the removal to an algorithmic error, an MP said.

“An executive of Meta apologised for taking down PM Modi’s video from Facebook. He said there was some algorithm mistake. He also assured next time it won’t be repeated and that Meta will amend their algorithm,” one MP said.
Meta did not respond to HT’s request for comment.

India invites Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman to BRICS summit outreach session

India has invited Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to the BRICS outreach session as BIMSTEC chair. The move underlines New Delhi's wider regional outreach as it prepares to host the summit in September.

India has invited Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to attend the outreach session of the BRICS summit in New Delhi next month in his capacity as the current chair of BIMSTEC, while also extending a separate invitation for a bilateral visit to India.

The 18th BRICS Summit will be hosted by India on September 12 and 13, with the grouping expected to take up pressing global challenges, including the economic fallout from the ongoing crisis in West Asia.
External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal announced the invitation at a regular media briefing on Tuesday.

“As far as the BRICS summit is concerned, India has separately extended an invitation to the Bangladesh prime minister in his capacity as the current chair of BIMSTEC to attend the outreach session of the 18th BRICS Summit,” Jaiswal said.
INVITATION IN LINE WITH BRICS PRACTICE
Jaiswal said Rahman's invitation was part of the standard practice followed by BRICS for its outreach sessions, where leaders of regional groupings are invited.
“The invitation has been extended as per the standard practice being followed in BRICS for the outreach sessions. Other heads of regional groups have also been invited in a similar manner,” he said.

India is hosting the summit as the current chair of BRICS. Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Russian President Vladimir Putin are among the prominent leaders expected to attend.
New Delhi has also invited leaders from several non-BRICS countries to participate in the outreach session.
SEPARATE INVITATION FOR BILATERAL VISIT
Apart from the BRICS invitation, India has also invited Rahman for a bilateral visit after he assumed office as Bangladesh prime minister in February.
The two invitations come as India and Bangladesh seek to strengthen bilateral engagement following a prolonged period of diplomatic strain.

BRICS has expanded significantly since its formation by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates joined in 2024, followed by Indonesia in 2025.
The grouping now has 11 member countries, accounting for around 49.5 per cent of the world's population, about 40 per cent of global GDP and approximately 26 per cent of global trade.
The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation, or BIMSTEC, comprises India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan.
Rahman's invitation to the BRICS outreach session is therefore linked to Bangladesh's role as the current chair of the regional grouping.

With the BRICS summit approaching, India has extended the invitation to Rahman in his capacity as BIMSTEC chair while separately seeking a bilateral engagement with the Bangladesh prime minister during his tenure.

Hollow electoral exercise: India dismisses PoK local polls, flags killings by Pakistan
India called the local body elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir a complete farce. It said the polls cannot mask protests, killings and Pakistan's support for cross-border terrorism.

India on Tuesday dismissed the so-called local body elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir as a “complete farce”, saying the exercise could not conceal the situation on the ground as protests and a crackdown by Pakistani security forces continue in the region.

The Ministry of External Affairs also accused Pakistan of using force against protesters and said the international community should look beyond what it described as Islamabad's “hypocritical lecturing” on human rights.
Responding to a question on the elections at a regular media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the protests and killings by Pakistani forces were the real developments in PoK.

“This so-called local election in PoK is a complete farce. The real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by Pakistani forces. Such hollow exercises cannot hide reality,” Jaiswal said.
‘90 CIVILIANS KILLED SINCE JUNE’
Jaiswal said at least 90 civilians had been killed since June during the continuing crackdown.
“Since June this year, at least 90 civilians have lost their lives in the continuing crackdown,” he said.

According to Jaiswal, the Pakistani establishment had responded to public discontent with “bullets, black outs, intimidation and repression” and was now attempting to create legitimacy through what he called a “hollow electoral exercise”.
“It must be held accountable, and the world should see through the flimsy veneer of Pakistan's hypocritical lecturing on human rights,” he said.
PoK has witnessed protests since last month over rising living costs, alleged administrative apathy, political discrimination and alleged atrocities against minorities.
The Joint Awami Action Committee has been leading the protests in PoK amid the local body elections.

Pakistani security forces used lethal force against the JAAC during its long march from Rawalakote to Muzaffarabad late last month. The crackdown reportedly resulted in the deaths of 40 civilians and left more than 33 protesters injured.

The JAAC has also appealed to the United Nations Human Rights Council and international rights organisations for an immediate and independent investigation into what it described as “unlawful killings”.
INDIA DEMANDS ACTION ON CROSS-BORDER TERRORISM
Jaiswal also used the briefing to call for stronger international action against cross-border terrorism and terrorist networks operating from Pakistan.

“We call upon countries to take strong action against cross-border terrorism and those promoting it. We call upon Pakistan to take strong action against cross-border terrorism and dismantle the terrorist infrastructure operating from its soil,” he said.
INDUS WATERS TREATY TO REMAIN IN ABEYANCE
On the Indus Waters Treaty, Jaiswal said India's position remained unchanged.
“The treaty is in abeyance and will remain so until Pakistan irrevocably and credibly abjures its support for cross-border terrorism,” he said.
India decided to put the treaty in abeyance as part of a series of diplomatic and economic measures announced after the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year, in which 26 civilians were killed.

India's latest comments came as it rejected the PoK local body polls as an attempt to create an appearance of legitimacy, while pointing to continuing protests, alleged civilian killings and a security crackdown in the region.

New Delhi also reiterated its demand for action against cross-border terrorism and maintained that the Indus Waters Treaty would remain in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably ends its support for such activities.
WhatsApp accounts placed 'under review' without warning, app features blocked

The issue surfaced at around 8 pm IST, when affected users said they were unable to use WhatsApp's features after receiving an in-app notification stating that their accounts were being reviewed for compliance with the platform's Terms of Service.

Several WhatsApp users, including many in India, reported that their accounts had been unexpectedly placed "under review" on Monday evening, temporarily restricting access to the Meta-owned messaging platform and prompting complaints across social media.

The issue surfaced at around 8 pm IST, when affected users said they were unable to use WhatsApp's features after receiving an in-app notification stating that their accounts were being reviewed for compliance with the platform's Terms of Service, reports news agency PTI

The message displayed on the app read: "Account in review. Date requested: 3 Aug 2026. Your account activity and device info is being checked to make sure it follows our terms of service. We will notify you of the result, typically within 24 hours."
Below these remarks, the app shows an option to learn about account issues, which includes "How to use WhatsApp responsibly. See guidance" and an option "About stolen phone and accounts."
Responding to the reports, a WhatsApp spokesperson said the platform continuously works to detect and prevent abuse while protecting legitimate users.

"We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting," PTI quoted a WhatsApp spokesperson as saying.
The company did not disclose how many accounts were affected or whether the reviews were linked to a technical issue, an automated enforcement system, or a broader anti-spam initiative.
Many users claimed the review was triggered without any prior warning and said they had not engaged in any activity that would violate the platform's policies.
Several took to social media to question why their accounts had been restricted and to seek clarification from the company.
It remains unclear whether the issue was limited to specific regions or affected users globally.

Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief Arvind Kejriwal on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) warned the Centre that the country will be pushed to launch another major movement if it doesn’t stop forcing the E20-blended petrol on its citizens.

The AAP chief also alleged that the Union Government was imposing E20 petrol on the country under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump and urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to “stand up” to the former.

“PM Modi, what is the point of showing your strength against us? Show the same courage in front of Trump and stop imposing E20 on the country. Otherwise, the nation will once again be compelled to launch a major movement,” Mr. Kejriwal said.
Earlier in the day, Mr. Kejriwal led a march of around 100 people towards the PM’s residence, but was stopped by security forces.

“We had gone today to submit 2.3 lakh petitions to the Prime Minister. A month ago, we had sought time to discuss the forceful imposition of the E20-blended petrol issue with him, but we received no response. Today, when we went to hand over the petitions, we were informed that he would not meet us. This reflects the dictatorial attitude,” Mr. Kejriwal said.
He accused Mr. Modi of demonstrating the same “dictatorship” attitude he had shown against the NEET protests.
The march, which began from the AAP headquarters on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane, covered barely 1 km before being stopped near 5, Ferozshah Road.

The police had put up barricades at two locations, including the main blockade near 5, Ferozshah Road and another close to the Mandi House roundabout, preventing protesters from advancing towards the Prime Minister’s residence.

As protesters approached the barricades, police repeatedly announced over loudspeakers that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force and declared the march unlawful.

In a tense standoff that followed, the protesters continued to raise slogans while senior police officers held negotiations with AAP leaders. The police also denied a request to allow a small delegation to proceed to the PM’s residence to submit a representation against the E20 policy.
However, the impasse ended without any major confrontation after Delhi Police arranged for a police vehicle to carry the protesters’ memorandum to the Prime Minister’s residence.

The petition demanded to provide a choice between pure petrol and E20 at fuel stations, so that people are not forced to use fuel that “damages” vehicles. It also urged the government to reduce the price of E20 petrol to reflect the lower calorific value and reduced mileage it delivers.
The AAP chief also alleged that the Indian farmers are not benefitting from the shift to E20 petrol.

“Ethanol there (U.S.) is produced from maize, and American farmers have put tremendous pressure on Trump. Trump, in turn, put pressure on PM Modi to buy ethanol to protect American farmers. Our farmers are not benefitting at all. So, fundamentally, this entire exercise is being carried out solely under Trump’s pressure because our Prime Minister is a weak Prime Minister,” he said.

Senior AAP leader Manish Sisodia, who was also present at the march, said, “The issue of E20 is about forcing ethanol into the vehicles of 30 crore people across the country. Crores of people are saying that it is damaging their vehicles, reducing mileage, harming engines and increasing servicing costs. When the public is suffering such huge losses, why is PM Modi still adamant about it?”

New Delhi: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi Tuesday hit out at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his recent remarks about student protesters, questioning the PM’s “right to forgive” them.

Speaking at the launch of Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (MDMK) MP Durai Vaiko’s book, The Walls of Parliament Still Echo Vaiko’s Voice, Rahul referred to a recent video of the Prime Minister in which he spoke of “forgiving” students, asking why they needed to be forgiven when they were only demanding jobs, a fair examination system and better educational opportunities.

“We are going through a strange time. Students are on the street, in severe pain. They don’t have work. They’re asking for fairness in exams. They’re asking for an education system that works. On the other side, there is the Prime Minister who forgives them. Who gave him the right to forgive the students? Who is he to forgive the students?” the Congress leader said.
He then attacked RSS, accusing it of trying to reshape India’s identity. “RSS can’t change our history. India will not tolerate its history to be trampled upon by anybody.”

Referring to the Constitution, Rahul said India’s diversity was its greatest strength and that every state had an equal place in the Union. “In the Constitution, it is clearly written: India, that is Bharat, is a Union of States. A state is an expression of the people of India. Every state represents one history, one tradition, one language and one expression of our people. Every single state has the right to that expression, and every single state must be treated fairly.”

He also accused the RSS of attempting to impose a single idea of India. “There are some ignorant people who don’t understand the Bengali, Marathi or Tamil people and their languages. There is a belief being enforced that there is only one language. Behind this thinking is the RSS, which is a very dangerous idea.”

Earlier in his address, Rahul praised veteran MDMK leader Vaiko while also taking a swipe at BJP leaders. “Mr Vaiko is a student of life, he is always learning unlike many others,” he said in a veiled attack.
National Conference president Farooq Abdullah also addressed the gathering, calling for stronger democratic institutions.
He said the Election Commission should have been made autonomous and that the judiciary should not be “dependent on the government’s wishes”. He referred to these as “mistakes” that had been made.

Referring to the CJP’s Chalo Sansad march, Abdullah also criticised the treatment of student protesters. “Children had come out on the streets, and the way they were treated. The capital was in complete disarray. No one can forget how our children were treated. India needs to wake up now. Unless we fight the policies of the government, we will never make India great again,” he said, before urging opposition parties to “stand together to make India great again”.
He also slammed the central government for making the elected government in Kashmir “powerless”.

Abdullah further warned that Kashmir was a testing ground and the same treatment would eventually be given to other states as well. “The crown of India has been reduced to a Union Territory. The elected government has no power. Power is with the center. When we ask for statehood they say yes, but when will you do it? How long do we wait” he said at the event.

The book launch also served as a show of Opposition unity, with CPI(M) General Secretary M.A. Baby, CPI(ML) Liberation General Secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, CPI General Secretary D. Raja, Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav and senior Congress leader P. Chidambaram among those present.

Don't get bullied: Mahua Moitra's message to Mark Zuckerberg over PM video row

Mahua Moitra urged Meta CEO not to apologise over the brief restriction of PM's Facebook post, alleging that the Centre routinely pressures platforms to remove content critical of the government and saying the temporary takedown "didn't make heavens fall".

Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra on Monday came out in support of Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg after the social media giant indicated it was willing to apologise to a parliamentary panel over the brief restriction of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook post, saying the company should not be "bullied" into apologising.
In a post on X, Moitra alleged that the government routinely pressures social media platforms to remove content critical of it and downplayed the temporary restriction on the Prime Minister's post.

"Hello Mark please do not get bullied & apologise to anyone. Indian govt blackmails & threatens citizens all the time, gets content critical of it removed at will. One video mistakenly removed for few hours didn't make heavens fall!" she wrote in a post on X.

Her remarks came after Meta representatives appeared before the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology, where members questioned the company over the incident and its content moderation practices.

According to a news agency PTI report, Meta officials told the panel they were prepared to apologise for the brief restriction on PM Modi's Facebook post, which had been removed in error and later restored.
The company had earlier attributed the incident to a technical glitch, but the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) reportedly termed the explanation "inadequate".

During the meeting, committee members raised concerns over Meta's content moderation policies, questioning why the PM's post was removed while objectionable content, including pornography, continued to remain accessible on the platform. Members also sought to know who was ultimately responsible for the removal and whether accountability would be fixed.

According to sources, a BJP MP argued that an apology alone would not suffice and called for legal action against the company. Another member reportedly said that in a democracy, "if a video of the prime minister is not safe, then accountability needs to be fixed."
The panel also questioned Meta officials about algorithmic bias and the effectiveness of its systems in detecting deepfakes involving Prime Minister Modi.

The meeting, chaired by BJP MP Nishikant Dubey, was convened to discuss the regulation of social and digital media platforms. It was attended by Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, MeitY Secretary S Krishnan and representatives from Meta, Google, X, YouTube and Snapchat.
