Madhya Pradesh air ambulances, launched in 2024, served 159 people, 32 had BJP links
Only 13 have paid for the service -- those without an Ayushman card and being flown to a hospital outside the state have to pay for it according to the scheme.

Madhya Pradesh’s PM (Prime Minister) Shri Air Ambulance Service launched in May 2024 has benefited 159 patients; 32 of them are either leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party or their friends or relatives.

Of the 159, only 13 have paid for the service -- those without an Ayushman card and being flown to a hospital outside the state have to pay for it according to the contours of the scheme -- including a BJP leader and his relatives/friends.
The scheme comes under the health department and health minister Rajendra Shukla said people haven’t paid for the service because the government sometimes pays on humanitarian grounds.
What air ambulance operator said
The service is provided by Flyola, a private company that offers on-demand custom flight solutions. It handles operations via a 24-hour non-scheduled facility at the Bhopal Airport State Hangar.
Also read: ‘Resignations part of politics’: Karnataka CM Shivakumar on MLAs’ threats over cabinet expansion

The company’s director corporate affairs, Monika Tiwari, said, “ We own 22 aircraft, and two of them -- a helicopter and a six-seater plane -- are reserved for air ambulance services. We get approval from the health department, which checks whether the beneficiary is an Ayushman cardholder or not. We airlift non-Ayushman cardholders only upon reference from the CM’s office or as special cases involving accidents. We are trying to save lives. Until May, we were getting approvals offline, but now we are getting them online. We are providing quick service to every patient.”
₹36 crore spent on air ambulance in 2 years
In all, the state has spent ₹36 crore on the service till July 7, according to commissioner of the health department S Dhanraju.
HT has reviewed documents on the scheme and spoken to 119 of the 159 beneficiaries.

At least 44% of the beneficiaries (70) were from the Rewa division — Rewa, Sidhi, Singrauli, Mauganj, Satna and Maihar districts — the home turf of health minister Rajendra Shukla. “I am proud that most of the beneficiaries are from my region,” he said.
The 13 who paid for the service include BJP leader Ram Sajjan Shukla and businessmen from Indore, Bhopal, Ujjain, Rewa and Jabalpur; all paid ₹5-10 lakh each.
Also read: Complaint against Noida teen who ‘abused’ PM Modi at NEET protest dropped
Contours of the air ambulance scheme
Individuals affected by road accidents, industrial mishaps, or natural disasters can be flown to government or private hospitals within and outside the state for free, according to the scheme.

“Ayushman card holders are eligible for free transportation to government and Ayushman-affiliated hospitals, regardless of the location. For those who do not possess an Ayushman card, the service provides free transport to government hospitals only within the state, while transport to medical facilities outside the state is available at contracted rates,” read the service guidelines.

The service requires a recommendation of the district’s chief medical health officer. The contracted rate is ₹2.35 lakh per hour for a helicopter and ₹3.90 lakh per hour for a six-seater air ambulance. Of the 119 beneficiaries, 95 were airlifted within the state; 55 were taken to government hospitals — eight to the state government hospital and 47 to AIIMS Bhopal — and 40 were shifted to private hospitals.

Of the 64 people flown to other states, 31 were non-Ayushman card-holders, and 11 did not respond on whether they have Ayushman cards. Of the 31, only seven paid for the service, while seven other are special accident cases. Beneficiaries, who were flown outside the state and were required to pay, said nobody asked them for money.

Former minister and MLA Gaurishankar Bisen said, “I felt pain in my chest so I was airlifted to Medanta hospital in Gurugram. No money was demanded from me, so I didn’t pay anything.” The BJP MLA from Garoth Chandan Singh said. “My son was ill and the government made arrangements for an airlifting him to Ahmedabad. No one asked for any money.”

Suneet Makin, son of petrol pump owner and businessman Rakendra Kumar Makin from Satna, gave the same reason for not paying. “My father was admitted to a hospital in Rewa. Health minister Shukla helped us in airlifting him to Delhi for a problem in the heart valve,” he said.

Ghanshyam Tripathi, whose friend was flown to a private hospital in Bhopal from Rewa, said, “The service was provided free of cost on the recommendation of chief minister (Mohan Yadav) as I am his guru (teacher).”

HT found three individuals — businessman Madhu Wadhwani of Rewa, Umesh Gupta from Rewa, and former MP Ram Vilas Das Vedanti — were never airlifted but the company was paid for the trips. Health minister Shukla explained the company charges a fixed amount and once it is booked, the charges are applicable whether the service is used or not.

Wadhwani and Vedanti’s families said they died before being airlifted, while Gupta’s family refused transfer after seeing the condition of the plane, the family said. Tripathi also complained of the plane’s poor condition. “The oxygen cylinder was unlocked (when it was not in use) and most of the equipment was rusted. Nobody was ready to travel with him but I mustered courage and travelled to a private hospital in Bhopal,” he added.

Shukla agreed that the air ambulance fleet do not comprise new planes but added they have all the facilities. “Their engines are in good condition. It (the service) is serving the purpose effectively.”
To be sure, there are Ayushman card holders who have benefited from the scheme.

A resident of Rewa, Ramvati Gupta was airlifted twice, first from Rewa to Bhopal and then Bhopal to Delhi, said, “This service gave me a second life. I can’t thank the government in words for providing air ambulances.”

A resident of Chhatarpur, 49-year-old Meena Sahu, suffering from acute pancreatitis, was airlifted in the presence of BJP MLA Lalita Yadav. Her son Sumit Sahu said, “I never thought that my mother would be airlifted for treatment. I contacted BJP MLA Yadav and she helped without any delay.”

In at least three cases, the Air Ambulance Service was used for organ donation. In the first case, the heart and liver of Baliram Kushwaha were transported to Bhopal and Indore from Jabalpur; in another instance, Satendra Singh’s heart was transported from Indore to Bhopal.

When asked why many of the beneficiaries were BJP leaders or their relatives, Shukla said some people might have used it under the CM’s special discretionary fund. “In many cases, ministers, MLAs and former ministers got special funds from the CM’s Swekchanudan,” he said. CM’s Swekchanudan is a special fund used by the CM to provide quick financial grant for medical emergencies and natural disasters.

Shukla said some business persons have also benefited. He added that local public representatives provided this service on humanitarian grounds to small business owners and other non-Ayushman card holders. “Later, all these cases get Cabinet’s approval. Many have paid for the service too.”

NEW DELHI: Despite 75% reduction in cyber-crime and digital arrest incidents, Supreme Court continued to push authorities for prompt action against cyber fraudsters by issuing a slew of directives Tuesday, including an expeditious decision on a 'kill switch' in phones to prevent these crimes and placing on hold monies transferred to mule accounts.Attorney general R Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that number of complaints on national cyber crime portal had gone down from 1,23,672 in 2024 to 16,377 in 2026 (as of June 30).

Besides, an Rs 18 crore has been restored to around 36,000 cyber fraud victims, he said in a status report.While appreciating the progress made in the matter, which the court is monitoring after taking suo motu cognisance on Oct 16 last year, bench directed Reserve Bank of India to formally "adopt and circulate formal standard operating procedure within four weeks detailing the action to be taken by banks for placing temporary hold on amounts and accounts in mule accounts linked to cyber fraud".Accepting a suggestion of amicus curiae N S Nappinai, SC also directed states, UTs and law enforcing agencies to take steps for expeditious adoption and operationalisation of grievance redressal and money restoration modules of home ministry, which should be given adequate publicity to enable victims to take required remedial measures.CJI-led bench directed "all adjudicatory authorities, including RBI ombudsman, consumer fora, courts and law enforcing authorities - to ensure that amounts recovered from fraudsters are disbursed to victims of digital arrest expeditiously".

It asked RBI to file a status report on this aspect by Sept 16, the next date of hearing.Even as CBI continues investigations into digital scams, the court asked agency to examine AG's suggestion for lowering the present threshold of Rs 10 crore for taking up investigations into cases where the same gang of scamsters are involved.

"The proposal concerning a time-based 'Kill switch' for audio and video calls may be examined by ministry of information and technology, Department of Telecom and Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) in consultation with telecom intermediaries and a brief note on technical feasibility, efficacy, safeguards and alternatives be placed on record," the bench said.It asked Inter-Departmental Committee (IDC), which coordinates with various departments for steps to prevent digital arrest and cyber crime offences, to issue necessary directives on setting up of cyber crime grievance redressal mechanism and restoration of defrauded amounts to victims.
Supreme Court tightens rules to curb 'digital arrests', RBI to frame SOPs to deal with mule bank accounts
The RBI has been asked to prepare a comprehensive SOP for dealing with bank accounts opened or used to receive and transfer proceeds of cyber fraud.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday stepped up its oversight of the country’s battle against the growing menace of “digital arrest” scams, issuing a fresh set of nationwide directions aimed at plugging systemic gaps in cyber fraud investigations, speeding up the restoration of victims’ money and strengthening preventive mechanisms.

Among its key directions, the court asked the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to frame within four weeks a standard operating procedure (SOP) for dealing with mule bank accounts used to launder proceeds of cyber fraud, directed all states to operationalise cyber fraud grievance redressal and money restoration systems, called for the adoption of the e-Zero FIR mechanism across the country, and asked the Centre to examine a shared liability and victim compensation framework for victims of digital arrest scams.

The directions were passed by a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant hearing a suo motu case initiated to monitor the country’s response to digital arrest frauds, where fraudsters impersonate police officers, CBI officials, judges or other government functionaries to extort money from victims through prolonged video calls and psychological intimidation.

The bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, was considering the fourth status report submitted by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Union home ministry, along with notes filed by Attorney General R Venkataramani and senior advocate NS Nappinai, the amicus curiae assisting the court.
ALSO READ | Supreme Court proposes no fuel for uninsured vehicles, seeks Centre's plan
Vigilance remains essential: SC

While noting that the government’s coordinated efforts have led to a significant decline in reported cases, the bench emphasised that sustained vigilance remained essential and that institutional mechanisms had to be further strengthened. “The trend is certainly encouraging…but continued monitoring remains indispensable,” observed the bench while referring to the decline in complaints.

According to the status report, complaints relating to digital arrest scams on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal have fallen from 123,672 in 2024 to 58,249 in 2025 and further to 16,377 till June 30 this year. The reported amount lost to such frauds has also reduced substantially.

Venkataramani told the court that the law enforcement response had also improved considerably. Over 36,000 cases have been investigated, while more than ₹18 crore has been restored to victims through the government’s money restoration mechanism. High-value digital arrest cases continue to be investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), while other complaints are handled by state police forces.

At the same time, the court took note of submissions made by Nappinai that digital arrest frauds continue to evolve despite the fall in numbers. She suggested that the government examine a technological “kill switch” under which messaging platforms such as WhatsApp could automatically terminate unusually long video calls or display warning pop-ups to users where calls continue for six to twelve hours, a common feature in digital arrest scams.

Accepting that the proposal deserved examination, the bench directed the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and I4C, in consultation with intermediaries, to study the technical feasibility, safeguards, possible alternatives and use cases of imposing time-based restrictions on audio and video calls, and place a report before the court.
RBI asked to prepare SOPs within four weeks

One of the most significant directions issued on Monday concerned RBI. The central bank has been asked to prepare and circulate, within four weeks, a comprehensive SOP for dealing with mule accounts –– bank accounts opened or used to receive and transfer proceeds of cyber fraud and money laundering. The SOP will also be circulated to the registrar generals of all high courts.

The court also directed all states, Union territories and law enforcement agencies to operationalise without delay the grievance redressal module and the money restoration module developed under the home ministry’s January 2, 2026 SOP for handling cyber fraud complaints through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and Cyber RMS. States have also been directed to create public awareness about these mechanisms so that victims can seek quicker relief.

Recognising that victims frequently approach courts seeking de-freezing of bank accounts or recovery of money, the bench asked the registrar generals of every high court to inform all courts and adjudicating authorities dealing with cyber fraud matters about the grievance redressal mechanism. At the same time, it clarified that using this mechanism would not prevent any person from pursuing statutory or constitutional remedies before courts.

The court also sought greater transparency in measuring the effectiveness of the recovery mechanism. It directed that the next status report should include state-wise and bank-wise data on complaints registered, complaints disposed of, restoration orders issued, successful restorations and the amount restored.

Noting that only 14 states have so far operationalised State Cyber Crime Coordination Centres and that the e-Zero FIR mechanism is functional in only 19 states, the bench directed the remaining states to notify their coordination centres within four weeks and adopt the e-Zero FIR system in consultation with I4C. The central agency has been asked to assist states in implementing these measures.

The bench further directed authorities to ensure expeditious disposal of matters relating to freezing of bank accounts arising from cyber-enabled financial frauds, an issue that frequently delays recovery of funds for victims and businesses alike.

The Inter-Departmental Committee (IDC), which is coordinating the government’s response to digital arrest scams, has also been directed to intensify nationwide awareness campaigns on cyber frauds, the grievance redressal and money restoration mechanisms, cyber security measures and procedures available for recovery of defrauded money. The court also recommended that all State Legal Services Authorities undertake public awareness drives on preventing digital arrest scams.

In another important direction, the bench asked the IDC to consult banks and technology intermediaries on introducing technological safeguards to prevent digital arrest scams, improve recovery of money, facilitate investigations and ensure compliance with legal obligations.

The court also accepted Nappinai’s suggestion that victims require greater institutional support beyond existing legal remedies. It directed the IDC to examine and discuss a proposal for introducing a shared liability and victim compensation framework for digital arrest scams, potentially paving the way for a structured compensation mechanism for victims.

On the investigative front, the court took note of the CBI’s progress in handling organised cyber fraud networks. The status report records that the agency has registered 10 digital arrest cases and several connected matters. In one investigation alone, the CBI identified 238 victims, traced 67 first-layer bank accounts, tracked transactions worth nearly ₹80 crore and carried out searches at 93 locations spread across 16 states.

The bench also asked the IDC to continue examining whether the existing ₹10 crore threshold for mandatory CBI investigation should be lowered and whether multiple frauds committed by the same organised network should be aggregated for determining the threshold for central investigation.
The matter will next be heard on September 16, when the Centre is expected to file a fresh consolidated status report on compliance with the court’s directions.

No insurance, no fuel? Supreme Court proposes pilot project at petrol pumps
A major road safety push could make insurance checks routine at fuel stations, while ANPR cameras, police apps and longer insurance cover for new vehicles are also proposed.

The Supreme Court has proposed a major crackdown on vehicles being driven without valid insurance, asking the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to prepare a pilot project that could see petrol pumps check a vehicle's insurance before supplying fuel.
Under the proposed system, vehicles without valid insurance could be denied petrol or diesel until the required cover is obtained.

The move is part of a wider set of road safety measures proposed by the court, including linking automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras with vehicle and insurance databases, giving traffic police mobile tools to check insurance instantly and extending the mandatory third-party insurance period for newly purchased vehicles.
The court has asked IRDAI and the road transport ministry to work on a pilot project that would allow petrol pumps to verify whether a vehicle has valid insurance before dispensing fuel.
If the vehicle is found to be uninsured, the proposed system could allow fuel stations to refuse the supply of petrol or diesel.
The measure is aimed at increasing compliance with mandatory motor insurance rules and making it harder for uninsured vehicles to remain on the roads.
The proposal is a pilot project and does not mean that petrol pumps across the country will immediately start refusing fuel to uninsured vehicles.
ANPR CAMERAS TO BE LINKED TO INSURANCE DATA
The Supreme Court has also proposed linking ANPR cameras installed on highways and roads with the VAHAN vehicle database and insurance databases.
The system could automatically identify vehicles without valid insurance and generate e-challans against them.

ANPR cameras are already used in several places to detect traffic violations such as speeding, jumping red lights and driving on the wrong side of the road. Linking them with insurance records could extend their use to identifying uninsured vehicles.
POLICE TO GET MOBILE INSURANCE CHECKS
Traffic police could also be provided with mobile applications or handheld devices to check a vehicle's insurance status instantly during roadside inspections.
The proposed devices would be linked to relevant vehicle and insurance databases, allowing officers to verify whether a vehicle has valid cover without relying on physical insurance documents.
LONGER INSURANCE COVER FOR NEW VEHICLES
The court has also proposed extending the mandatory third-party insurance period for newly purchased vehicles.
For new private cars, the compulsory third-party insurance period would increase from three years to four years.
For new two-wheelers, the period would rise from five years to six years.
The move is aimed at reducing the number of vehicles that become uninsured after their initial insurance period expires.
WHY THE COURT IS PUSHING FOR TIGHTER CHECKS
The court has taken a wider view of the problem of uninsured vehicles, with the proposed measures aimed at ensuring that mandatory third-party insurance requirements are actually followed.
The proposed fuel check, ANPR integration and police verification system would create multiple points at which an uninsured vehicle could be identified.
The measures would also make it easier for authorities to track vehicles that continue to operate without the legally required insurance.

The Supreme Court's proposals are now to be worked out by the concerned authorities, with the pilot project expected to examine how the insurance verification system can be implemented without disrupting the functioning of fuel stations or legitimate vehicle use.

For now, the proposals signal a significant tightening of India's approach to uninsured vehicles, with the court looking beyond conventional roadside enforcement towards technology and everyday services such as fuel purchases to improve compliance.

India to exchange territory with Myanmar? MEA says proposal under discussion

India and Myanmar are discussing a possible territorial exchange to resolve a long-pending border demarcation issue in Manipur, with the MEA confirming that talks are underway. The reported proposal, however, has triggered opposition from civil society groups in the state over concerns about territorial integrity.

India and Myanmar are reportedly exploring a possible territorial exchange to settle a decades-old undemarcated section of their shared border along Manipur. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi on Tuesday, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, "There are certain areas on the border which are yet to be settled. Discussions on those sectors are ongoing."

Jaiswal was responding to a question about reports suggesting that India was considering a land swap with Myanmar along the Manipur border. While he stopped short of confirming the reports, he acknowledged that discussions were underway to resolve unsettled stretches of the boundary.

His remarks came weeks after US-based magazine The Diplomat reported that New Delhi was actively considering such a proposal. In a July 17 report citing an "official document", the magazine said the Indian government was examining a "proposal" to complete the demarcation of the boundary between border pillars 65 and 68 along Manipur's border with Myanmar by exchanging around 1.4 square miles of territory. The distance between pillars 65 and 68 is approximately 2.8 km in length.

The proposed area for exchange lies in Manipur's Chandel district, adjoining Myanmar's Kabaw Valley in the Sagaing Region. According to the "official document", dated May 26, 2026, the demarcation exercise was expected to be completed within three months, meaning around August.

India and Myanmar share a 1,643-km-long international boundary that runs through Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram before entering Myanmar's Sagaing Region and Chin State. Much of the frontier is mountainous, forested and porous, cutting across ethnic communities that have historically lived on both sides.

According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, around 1,472 km of the border has been demarcated through boundary pillars, while nearly 171 km remains unresolved, mainly in Arunachal Pradesh's Lohit sector and Manipur's Kabaw Valley.
WHY INDIA MIGHT BE CONSIDERING A TERRITORIAL SWAP WITH MYANMAR

According to The Diplomat, the primary rationale behind a possible territorial exchange is to expedite the demarcation of an unresolved stretch of the India-Myanmar border, enabling New Delhi to fence the frontier to curb illegal immigration, insurgent movement and other cross-border crimes.

In 2024, India had announced a plan to fence the entire 1,643-km-long international boundary while also scrapping the India-Myanmar border Free Movement Regime that had been in place since 2018 and allowed tribal communities living near the border to travel up to 16 km into each other's territory without a visa using a border pass.

The current India-Myanmar boundary was defined under a 1967 bilateral agreement, but parts of it remain unsettled. In 2018, the government informed Parliament that the remaining unresolved stretches would be demarcated through a bilateral boundary mechanism, including the identification and erection of nine boundary pillars.

The most sensitive stretches in Manipur include the Molcham sector between border pillars 64 and 68, the Moreh sector between pillars 75 and 79, and the Choro Khunou sector between pillars 88 and 95. India has consistently maintained that there is no broader border dispute with Myanmar, but only nine unresolved boundary pillars that are being addressed through bilateral mechanisms.

Citing an unnamed government official, The Diplomat reported that the issue was discussed during Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing's visit to India last month. According to the report, both sides considered erecting auxiliary and new boundary pillars in the Molcham sector between border pillars 65 and 68, while also examining a 2017 Ministry of External Affairs proposal on the alignment of the border in the area.

Territorial exchanges with neighbouring countries are not unprecedented. In 2015, India and Bangladesh ratified the Land Boundary Agreement, under which New Delhi transferred 111 enclaves within its territory to Dhaka and received 51 Bangladeshi enclaves in return, bringing an end to a 41-year-old boundary dispute.
TERRITORY EXCHANGE PROPOSAL SPARKS PUSHBACK IN MANIPUR

The reported proposal has already drawn opposition in Manipur. Following the publication of The Diplomat report, The Imphal Times reported that the Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI) was warning the Government of India against ceding even a small portion of the state's territory to Myanmar, saying it would launch a strong public response if such a proposal were implemented.

COCOMI, a joint body of Meitei civil society organisations formed in 2019 during the Centre's peace talks with Naga insurgent groups, said on July 27 (10 days after The Diplomat report was published), "If the contents of the report are true and the proposal is translated into action, COCOMI will not remain a silent spectator."

Describing Manipur's territorial integrity as non-negotiable, the organisation said the state's existing boundaries had been inherited from previous generations and defended over time. It argued that Manipur had already lost parts of its historical territory since its merger with the Indian Union in 1949 and warned that any further reduction in the state's geographical boundaries would be unacceptable, reported The Imphal Times.
The organisation further cautioned that New Delhi should not "play with fire" by taking any decision affecting Manipur's territorial integrity without the consent of its people.

Safe harbour under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act protects platforms from liability for third-party content, recognising that social media companies cannot practically monitor every post uploaded by billions of users. The protection applies as long as platforms remove unlawful content when directed by courts or authorised government agencies.

However, government officials argued that Meta does not fall within the definition of an intermediary because its algorithms determine who receives content, making safe harbour protection under the IT Act inapplicable.

"It was made clear to them that they are not covered under the definition of an intermediary. They select who receives the content. Therefore, the safe harbour protection under the IT Act is not applicable," sources said.

The discussions also covered Meta's business practices. According to sources, the company admitted spending significant sums to boost certain categories of content and expressed regret over those decisions.

Big change in UPI policy? Payments above ₹2,000 may carry a fee. What we know
The bill seeks to remove the provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging a fee, including MDR, on notified electronic payments.

A major policy change might be headed towards the free Unified Payments Interface (UPI), with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman introducing the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha.
UPI, one of the world's largest real-time payment interfaces, processed 23.6 billion transactions worth ₹29.9 trillion in July, as per official data.
The bill intends to further amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the Income-tax Act, 2025, and the Finance Act, 2026.
ALSO READ | HT Insight: India’s UPI revolution’s becoming a global export

While amendments have been proposed to different parts of the bill, the aim remains the same -- making India a more attractive and predictable place for global capital, manufacturing, and businesses to come to and remain in the nation, news agency PTI reported, citing finance ministry sources.
Regarding a policy change in UPI, the main focus among the proposed amendments is the amendment to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

The bill seeks to remove the existing legal provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging a fee, known as the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), on notified electronic payments.
MDR is a fee that merchants pay to banks and payment service providers for processing digital transactions.

Relevant changes have been sought in Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, and Section 269SU of the Income Tax Act, requiring large businesses with a turnover exceeding ₹50 crore to accept payments via specific electronic modes, including BHIM-UPI QR codes and RuPay debit cards.

So far, no bank or payment system provider has imposed any charge on anyone, either directly or indirectly, for using the electronic modes of payment prescribed under Section 269SU of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
The latest amendment bill, however, proposes to expand the scope of what could be notified under modes of payment that attract no charges.
While no charge on UPI payments would be imposed immediately, the bill does give the government the flexibility to introduce MDR at any time.

The proposed amendments may result in the Centre setting an MDR fee below 0.5 per cent, which would apply to transactions above ₹2,000, Moneycontrol reported, citing sources. But this charge may be valid for merchants with an annual turnover above ₹1.5 crore.
This means that consumers may not have to pay any additional charges, and small businesses may also continue to enjoy the UPI facility free of cost.
Another option is that an MDR would be determined based on transactions above a certain limit, Reuters reported.

However, no final decision has been made on the rate or the transactions that would be covered under this amendment.
Why was there no fee on UPI payments?

In December 2019, the Centre issued a circular to clarify that, based on Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007, no charges, including MDR, shall be applicable on or after January 1, 2020, on the payment made through prescribed electronic modes.
- Unified Payments Interface (UPI) (BHIM-UPI)
- Unified Payments Interface Quick Response Code (UPI QR Code) (BHIM-UPI QR Code)
According to a March 2026 report from the Standing Committee on Finance, the objective of zero MDR was to make digital transactions more affordable and widely accessible.

The committee was told by the Department of Financial Services that the policy aimed to encourage wider acceptance of UPI and RuPay payments, including by smaller businesses.

However, it noted that the absence of a fee was making the UPI ecosystem "financially unstable." The committee observed that a structural funding gap was impacting long-term infrastructural investment.
The committee observed that while government schemes are necessary to democratise digital payments in Tier 3-6 cities, it urged DFS to explore a self-reliant, tiered revenue model.

"The Committee would like to emphasise that establishing a viable revenue mechanism is critical to ensuring the UPI ecosystem achieves financial sustainability without perpetually straining the government exchequer," the report stated.

New Delhi: With the Congress slamming the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) almost on a daily basis, the possibility of its senior leader Shashi Tharoor sharing a stage with the Hindu organisation’s chief Mohan Bhagwat at an event in Mumbai was bound to raise eyebrows. “It is not RSS-led. It’s a student movement that invites educationists and thought leaders of all backgrounds to address students. Bhagwat is scheduled to interact with young participants on 6 August at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC) in Mumbai. The event marks the 15th anniversary of IIMUN and the opening of its annual Championship Conference, news agency ANI reported.

Bhagwat’s participation has also drawn political criticism from Opposition parties. Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray ) leader Aaditya Thackeray took a swipe at those seeking to engage with Gen Z and Gen Alpha, questioning where they were when young protesters were facing police action.

I trust Gen Z blindly, protesting doesn't make them anti-national: RSS chief
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat backed Gen Z and Gen Alpha, saying he would "trust Gen Z blindly" and that students have every democratic right to protest, question authority, and demand reforms.

Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Thursday strongly backed India's younger generation, saying he would "trust Gen Z blindly" and asserting that students taking part in protests should not be labelled anti-national.

Addressing around 2,000 Gen Z and Gen Alpha members at the 15th anniversary celebrations of India's International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN) in Mumbai, Bhagwat said the younger generation deserved to be heard through dialogue rather than judged for questioning authority.

"I want to make it clear that if Gen Z engages in any agitation, they are not anti-national. They are our own people; they are our next generation. A sense of belonging and mutual respect is needed for dialogue to take place. We need to recognise and respect each other. Only then can a meaningful dialogue happen, where we understand their concerns and they understand our perspective," Bhagwat said.

Describing today's youth as more honest than previous generations, he added, "I believe today's younger generation, Gen Z and Gen Alpha, is more honest than the existing generation. This generation should have honesty towards the nation, a spirit of patriotism, and a commitment to service."
Bhagwat reiterated his faith in young people even while acknowledging that he did not know the complete facts behind the recent confrontation between police and protesters.
"I will trust Gen Z blindly," he said. Referring to reports of the use of tear gas and pellet guns during the protests, Bhagwat said conclusions should not be drawn without verified information.

"If I had to believe, I will believe Gen Z. But we do not know the reality. Both of us are conversing on the basis of information available through reports. There have also been reports of some anti-social elements in this movement. But we cannot talk without authentic information," he said.
'WILL NEVER SAY GEN Z SHOULD NOT PROTEST'
Calling protest an integral part of democracy, Bhagwat said dialogue was essential to address genuine grievances.

"Protest is also one of the means of dialogue. Democracy is a way to make consensus after discussion. Grievance is genuine, and a lot has to be improved in our nation's education system. So dialogue is important," he said.
Drawing a contrast with previous generations, Bhagwat said today's youth are more willing to question authority.
"We never used to question authorities, but Gen Z and Gen Alpha question authority and want logical answers, that too with love," he said.

The RSS chief said he would never discourage young people from protesting. "I will never say that Gen Z should not protest, but there should also be a way given in democracy. We need to see that if youth is shouting, it is not for opposing but for improvement," he said.
He added that there were shortcomings in the system that needed to be rectified and that student protests seeking reforms should be viewed as a legitimate democratic exercise.
'A LEADER CREATES MORE LEADERS, DOESN'T SEEK THE SPOTLIGHT'

Bhagwat also outlined what he called the qualities of a true leader, saying leadership was not about delivering speeches, winning elections or standing in front of people, but about working quietly, sharing success and nurturing future leaders.

Referring to a Sanskrit verse, the RSS chief said an ideal leader should possess knowledge, recognise and appreciate the strengths of others, share success, fame and material gains with colleagues, and display courage like a warrior when faced with challenges.
"Real leaders are those who lead from behind. They work from within," Bhagwat said.

Rejecting the conventional notion of leadership, he added, "Leadership is not about standing before people, making speeches or winning elections. I do not see myself as a leader. I see myself as a worker."
Bhagwat said the ultimate purpose of leadership was not to build followers but to create more leaders.
"The purpose of leadership is to lead people towards light. The purpose of leadership is to create leaders. It is not to lead by myself. My leadership should create leaders," he said.
EDUCATION IS SOCIETY'S RESPONSIBILITY
The RSS chief devoted a significant part of his address to education, saying it should not become a commercial activity.

"Education is not a commercial business. Community help can improve the education system. The financial burden of education is huge. We need to be vigilant, active and assess the system regularly. We also need to train our teachers. It is not just the government's responsibility to educate, but a social responsibility," he said.
Backing a long-standing demand for greater public investment, Bhagwat said allocating six per cent of the national budget to education remained relevant.

"Demand for a 6% budget allocation for education is old. But only the government does not run schools. We as an organisation also strive hard for education and learning. There should be a social spirit awakening for education," he said.
LAW ALONE CAN'T FIX SOCIAL MEDIA
Bhagwat also spoke about the influence of social media, saying legislation alone could not solve the problem of misinformation.
"It is necessary to change the attitude. Only law enforcement is not enough. We need to change role models," he said.
He urged influencers with millions of followers to act responsibly and stressed the need to verify information through authentic sources.
"If something is banned, there will always be loopholes. So banning alone cannot be the solution," he said.

Questioning why violent content attracts greater engagement online, Bhagwat said, "Gen Z does not subscribe to violence, then why does violent content receive more likes? It needs to be thought about and analysed."
BHAGWAT ON TIES WITH PAKISTAN, CHINA
Speaking on national security and international conflicts, Bhagwat said citizens should support the government's decisions during crises while maintaining a humanitarian outlook.

"In times of conflict, we have to go with what the government does. Pakistan and China are two examples. The Indian solution is to hold back differences while dealing with conflicts. Permanent hatred is not the solution," he said.
"It is not that Pakistanis are wholeheartedly our enemies, and not even all Indians. Humanity has to be one," Bhagwat added.
ON LGBTQ, SAME-SEX COMPANIONSHIP
Bhagwat said members of the LGBTQ community were an integral part of society and deserved accommodation.
"They are also part of our society, and we have a tradition to accommodate them," he said.
However, he distinguished marriage from companionship, saying marriage was a social institution rather than merely an arrangement for two people to live together.

"Marriage is not a convenience to just live together, but it is a unit of society. Families create good citizens. We need to have some system first. If existing systems are disrupted without creating new systems, there will be consequences," he said.
Emphasising that social norms shape legislation, Bhagwat said, "Law does not dictate society, but society dictates law."
He added that while he did not support same-sex marriage, society should evolve a framework to recognise same-sex companionship.
"We have to devise a system where not same-sex marriage, but same-sex companionship should be accommodated," Bhagwat said.

Bhagwat's remarks come amid a wider debate over student-led protests, police action and the role of democratic dissent, with the RSS chief arguing that India's younger generation should be engaged through dialogue rather than suspicion.

France offers to build 94 of 114 Rafale jets in India under Rs 3.25-lakh crore deal

A key feature of the offer is the local production of 94 jets in partnership with Indian industry. The government is now examining the technical and commercial aspects of the bid, including indigenous weapons integration and technology transfer.

France has submitted its detailed technical and commercial proposal to India for the proposed acquisition of 114 Rafale multirole fighter aircraft, marking a key step forward in one of the country's biggest defence procurement programmes. Estimated to be worth around Rs 3.25 lakh crore, the government-to-government deal is currently being evaluated by the Ministry of Defence's Acquisition Wing and the Indian Air Force (IAF), defence sources said.
The proposal follows India's Letter of Request (LoR) sent to France in May this year and places strong emphasis on local manufacturing, technology transfer and greater indigenous content.

A major highlight of the French proposal is the plan to manufacture 94 of the 114 Rafale jets in India through a domestic industry partner. The production programme is expected to involve Dassault Aviation along with leading French defence firms MBDA, Safran and Thales.

The project is expected to significantly boost India's aerospace manufacturing ecosystem, with substantial opportunities for Indian companies such as Tata, Larsen & Toubro and other domestic defence manufacturers. Industry participation under the programme could generate business worth around Rs 1.6 lakh crore, according to sources.
INDIGENOUS WEAPONS, LOCAL CONTENT UNDER SCRUTINY

The Indian side is expected to closely examine the French proposal for provisions related to the integration of indigenous weapons systems, particularly variants of the Astra beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile, into the Rafale platform.

Officials will also assess the level of indigenisation offered under the deal, in line with the government's push to strengthen domestic defence manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported military equipment.
CRITICAL FOR IAF'S COMBAT STRENGTH

The acquisition is aimed at addressing the Indian Air Force's declining squadron strength, which has been affected by the phased retirement of ageing MiG fighter aircraft and delays in the induction of indigenous platforms such as the LCA Mk1A and the upcoming LCA Mk2.
The Rafale was selected by the Defence Ministry in 2012 after a lengthy global competition and has since emerged as one of the IAF's frontline combat aircraft.

The Defence Acquisition Council cleared the proposal for procuring 114 Rafale jets around five months ago, following a capability enhancement review initiated by Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh after he assumed office in 2024.
INDIA'S RAFALE FLEET SET TO GROW
The Indian Air Force and the Indian Navy have already placed orders for 62 Rafale aircraft. If the proposed acquisition goes through, India's Rafale fleet will increase to 176 aircraft.

The Indian Navy has also expressed its intent to induct 31 additional Rafale-M fighter jets for carrier-based operations, which could eventually take the total number of Rafales in Indian service to more than 200.
Tamil Nadu CM Vijay urges PM Modi to fast-track Godavari-Cauvery link

Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi to expedite the Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar river linking project. He said the project is vital for Tamil Nadu's water security and deserves national importance status.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to speed up the implementation of the Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar river linking project and declare it a project of national importance.
In a letter to the Prime Minister, he sought direct intervention to ensure long-term drinking water and irrigation security for southern India.
Vijay said Tamil Nadu has an inherent surface water deficit and depends on neighbouring states for more than 30 per cent of its water needs.
He said the proposed river link was the most significant long-term opportunity to increase the state's surface water resources and address the growing demand for drinking water and irrigation.

In his letter, the Chief Minister said, "Groundwater resources have also been exploited to critical levels, with several regions continuing to experience over-exploitation despite the sustained regulatory and conservation measures undertaken by the state government."

He added, "The Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar Link represents the most significant long term opportunity for augmenting Tamil Nadu's surface water resources. It is of vital importance to redress the growing needs of drinking water and irrigation for the population in Tamil Nadu."
He also said, "The southern districts of Tamil Nadu, particularly Pudukkottai, Sivagangai, Ramanathapuram and Virudhunagar, are chronically water-scarce and highly drought-prone".

Vijay said the most sustainable way to meet the growing water needs of these regions would be the implementation of the Godavari-Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar link project, which would allow the transfer of surplus floodwaters from water-surplus basins to water-deficit regions.
He said, "The National Water Development Agency (NWDA) has prepared the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Godavari-Pennar-Palar-Vellar Link as phase one of the larger project."

He added, "This component is envisaged to benefit Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu," but noted that "the alignment covered by the DPR presently terminates a few kilometres upstream of the Cauvery River".
Urging quick action, he said, "Therefore, may I request that the project of inter-linking of Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar rivers which is a project of national importance be taken up on a priority basis."

He added, "I am confident that this project can be achieved and differences between states can be resolved through constructive consultation and cooperative federalism, keeping in view the larger national interest and I request that, considering the strategic importance and far-reaching socio-economic benefits of the project, Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar Link Project be taken up on a fast-track basis and may be given the status of a project of national importance".

The Chief Minister also said a dedicated special purpose vehicle with the participation of the Centre and the beneficiary states could be considered to ensure coordinated implementation, assured funding and timely completion.

He said, "It's early execution would benefit the people and farming communities of Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka" and assured that the Tamil Nadu government would extend all necessary cooperation for the project's speedy and successful implementation.

In his closing appeal, Vijay asked the Prime Minister to direct the Ministry of Jal Shakti and the NWDA to speed up consultations with stakeholder states, help build an early consensus on pending issues, finalise the DPR for extending the link up to the Kattalai Barrage across the Cauvery, accord priority to the project, implement it as a national project on a fast-track basis, consider setting up a dedicated special purpose vehicle, and declare it a project of national importance.

New Delhi: Over four weeks after quitting the Trinamool Congress (TMC), the 20 rebel Members of Parliament (MPs) of the party who had merged with the Tripura-based Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) find themselves on a sticky wicket.

While they have gone on the warpath with Trinamool chairperson Mamata Banerjee at the cost of inviting brickbats from their own constituents for supporting the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the latter does not seem to be willing to fully embrace them.

Twenty of the 28 TMC parliamentarians had broken away from the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress in mid-June in the aftermath of the party’s humiliating defeat in the West Bengal Assembly elections. Even in the West Bengal Assembly, 60 of the 80 TMC legislators led by Ritabrata Banerjee split from the party and claimed to be the “real TMC.”

The rebel MPs led by Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on 14 June and sought recognition as a separate parliamentary group. The Mamata Banerjee camp also wrote to Birla on 10 June, urging him to not recognise any separate faction within the party, and pressed for the disqualification of the rebel MPs under the anti-defection law.

Nearly two months since both factions wrote to Birla, sources in the Lok Sabha Secretariat told ThePrint that the Speaker is yet to deliver a ruling. “No decision has been taken in the matter,” the source said. In fact, the Lok Sabha website still lists all 28 MPs, including the 20 rebels, as TMC MPs.
The Speaker’s delay in giving a ruling has led to an air of uncertainty in the rebel camp. Sources speak of the fear of some dissident MPs leaving if the air is not cleared about their status.
Though the rebel MPs have merged with NCPI, they support the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance. A majority of the rebel group also attends NDA parliamentary party meets.

Trouble seems to be brewing. At least three MPs from the rebel camp – Khalilur Rahaman from Jangipur, Yusuf Pathan from Baharampur and Abu Taher Khan from Murshidabad –vented their feelings by skipping the NDA meeting on 4 August. This was the second time in two months that the three MPs skipped the NDA meeting.

Speaking to reporters in Parliament on 4 August, Abu Taher Khan said that he will not join the BJP. ThePrint also reached out to six of the MPs from the rebel faction, including Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandopadhyay, Abu Taaher Khan, Yusuf Pathan and Khalilur Rahaman, but all refused comment.

While the rebel group merged with NCPI to avoid disqualification under the anti-defection law, several MPs from the camp have expressed their willingness to join the BJP. But resistance from its own leaders and party rank-and-file seems to be holding the BJP back.

On 4 June, days before he was appointed West Bengal’s Finance Minister, Swapan Dasgupta in a post on social media platform X, cautioned his party to be wary of “false friends”. “I shed no tears for the TMC’s self-destruction. My only hope is that the political culture of the vandals does not start contaminating the West Bengal BJP. We in the BJP have to be always wary of false friends who are today cosying up to us because they need to wash away their past sins. The detox of Bengal cannot be left incomplete.”

The rebel MPs are also facing heat in their constituency and outside for aligning with the BJP. On 7 July, when one of the rebel MP Sayani Ghosh went to Baruipur to meet the family of an 11-year-old rape and murder victim, she was greeted with chants of “traitor”.

Even the Election Commission of India (ECI) is silent on the matter of 60 MLAs who have split from the Mamata Banerjee-led party and claim to be the real TMC. Both factions have also met the election commissioner and submitted letters making competing claims. While the rebel camp has staked claim to the TMC’s name and symbol, the Mamata Banerjee faction has urged the ECI not to recognise the former. The ECI has also not given any decision in the matter yet.

Leaders from the Mamata Banerjee camp have urged the Election Commission multiple times – the last was four days back – to give a ruling. “They (ECI) seem to be under pressure,” a leader from the Mamata Banerjee camp told The Print on condition of anonymity.

A leader from the Mamata Banerjee camp told ThePrint that the rebel MPs and MLAs have not only violated the 10th schedule of the Constitution that deals with disqualification but also the TMC’s constitution that bars party leaders from electing the party’s chairperson till five years after they are elected.

“Mamata Banerjee was elected the TMC chairperson in 2022 by member delegates for a term of 5 years. How can the rebel MLAs elect Arup Roy as the chairperson when Mamata Banerjee continues to hold the position?” the leader, who did not want to be named, said.

NEW DELHI: Parliament proceedings remained disrupted on Thursday as opposition parties continued to demand the presence of Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against student protesters at Jantar Mantar. However, members of the Treasury benches objected, triggering a heated exchange between the ruling and opposition members.Kharge reiterated the opposition's demand that Amit Shah address the House on the police action against protesters and said the opposition was ready for a discussion."We only raise genuine questions concerning the country and its 140 crore people.

New Congress members not learning anything because their leadership not giving them a chance", Rijiju told Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge in Rajya Sabha.Following the exchange, the Rajya Sabha Chairman directed Rijiju to convey the sentiments of the opposition to the home minister."Now i request you to consider his request. Why they are not present is still unknown. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha told the Parliamentary affairs minister that the home minister should come to the House and speak on this incident. Rijiju alone does not have the authority to resolve the issue.

He only conveys the matter, and then the issue fizzles out," Kharge said."When I raise a point of order, I am not allowed to speak. We want the House to run peacefully, and for that, the Home Minister should make a statement in the House. Instead of asking students to seek forgiveness, the government should apologise to the students and their families," he added.Asked whether the opposition would continue its protest, Kharge said the next course of action would depend on the government's response.

"It depends on when the Home Minister comes to the House and what statement he makes. Even the Prime Minister should come to the House and apologise. New Delhi: Gen Z should not be branded as anti-national if they participate in an agitation, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat said Thursday while addressing a youth conference in Mumbai, adding that protesting is a way of building consensus.

Responding to a question about concerns that protesters may be labelled “anti-national”, Bhagwat said he does not endorse the term. “I want to make it clear that if Gen Z engages in any agitation, they are not anti-national. They are our own people; they are our next generation. Gen Z vagerah aise hee mai toh ye baatein nahi maanta…A sense of belonging and mutual respect is needed for dialogue to take place. We need to recognise and respect each other. Only then can meaningful dialogue happen, where we understand their concerns and they understand our perspective.”

“I believe today’s younger generation, Gen Z and Gen Alpha, is more honest than the existing generation and honest appeal of patriotism and service works with them,” he added, as he addressed Gen Z and Gen Alpha attendees at a conference on ‘The Role of Youth in Uniting the World, the Indian Way’, organised by India’s International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN) in Mumbai.
“If I had to choose one generation to trust, I would place my trust in Gen Z,” he further said.

The RSS chief’s remarks come days after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protests—which originated in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar and spread across the country—ended on 25 July after former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan submitted his resignation, which was the protesters’ key demand in connection with the NEET paper leak and subsequent student suicides.

The BJP has also embarked on an outreach programme to connect with Gen Z across states, conducting small-scale programmes that are being addressed by local leaders. The outreach was initiated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself, when he began posting reels addressed to the youth while the Jantar Mantar protest was still ongoing.

Asked if he agreed that if dialogue had started earlier, the matter wouldn’t have escalated, Bhagwat said: “When something happens that shouldn’t happen, it means there was a lapse somewhere. Whose fault it is or what happened is a separate matter, but there certainly was a shortcoming. It will be corrected; it should be corrected. That’s what I believe.”
Bhagwat’s comments also come at a time when the Modi government has faced intense criticism over use of force against protesting students, especially at Jantar Mantar and in Bihar.

Specifically asked about the lathi-charge and pellet gun firing, he said, “We need to first understand what happened and why it happened. We need to examine the reasons behind it. I do not have all the information required to give a complete opinion on this issue, and I do not think you have the complete details either. We need to look into where exactly the problem lies.

He added: “At this moment, I cannot say what happened or who was right or wrong, because I do not have complete information. You are sharing what you have read, and I am also going by what I have read…However, if I am asked to place my faith in someone, I would place my faith in Gen Z.”
‘Gen Z’s grievance is genuine’

“A protest is also a way of dialogue. We are sitting here and discussing, and if we understand each other’s perspectives, that is good. Otherwise, a debate will continue. If you or I are facing a difficulty and the solution is in your hands or mine, but it is not being resolved, then I may raise my voice and say that I will bring you there and ask you to resolve it because it is urgent,” Bhagwat said.

The RSS chief further said that in a democracy, protests are also a way of building consensus. “Lots of views come together, and consensus evolves after discussions. That discussion may happen through dialogue. However, due to various reasons, if a concern is not heard, one may move towards agitation. But all these steps should be taken to evolve a consensus, not to create divisions.”

Bhagwat added that Gen Z’s grievances are genuine. “As far as Gen Z is concerned, what happened recently, their grievance is genuine. A lot needs to be done in India’s education system, and it is not being done.”

“…when we were their age, we were habituated to accepting whatever the elders said, we never questioned them. Now, Gen Z and Gen Alpha questions, they want logical answers and love…In democracy, this is the method. They call it ‘debate’ in English, we call it ‘shastrarth’. There is no debate there but there are two sides—‘poorv’ and ‘uttar’. We look at all aspects and everyone has their own perspective, so a new dimension comes to light in every subject. So, we get so many opinions and counter-opinions, they together form a total view of the truth. This should indeed happen,” he further said.

Bhagwat said that he won’t say that Gen Z should not protest, but there are methods to how and what is to be done in a democracy. “Those who drafted the Constitution, the speeches of Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar, have indications on the same. This should be looked at. We too should see that Gen Z is not raising its voice to oppose, they are doing this because they have some issues and that should be rectified. Agitation should not be against me or you, but for system correction…”

A total of ₹557.51 crore has been spent on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visits to 77 countries since 2021, including ₹74.59 crore on trips to 12 nations this year, according to information provided by the government in Parliament on Thursday.

The highest expenditure during this period was recorded in 2025, when the PM’s visits to 23 countries cost ₹187.83 crore, figures provided by minister of state for external affairs Pabitra Margherita in the Rajya Sabha showed. He was responding to a question from Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh and CPI MP V Sivadasan.

According to details provided by Margherita in a written response, the figures for 2026 did not include expenses incurred on a visit to France in June for the PM to attend an outreach session of the G20 Summit and hold bilateral meetings, as the “compilation of bills is still underway”.
Margherita noted in response to questions from the MPs that the total foreign direct investment (FDI) received by India between April 2021 and December 2025 was $381.8 billion.

He said the PM’s trips between 2021 and 2026 resulted in the signing of 316 agreements — including government-to-government pacts and MoUs between government institutions, research bodies, and universities — in fields such as defence, trade, investment, nuclear energy research and development, healthcare, renewable energy, space, sports, and culture.

Of all the trips this year, the PM’s visit to Norway in May for a bilateral meeting and to attend the India-Nordic Summit was the most expensive, costing the exchequer ₹17.46 crore. This was followed by visits to Israel in February ( ₹11.92 crore), Seychelles in June ( ₹8.22 crore), and Sweden in May ( ₹6.32 crore).

Expenditure on other trips this year included ₹5.57 crore for a visit to Malaysia in February, ₹1.97 crore for a visit to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), ₹3.6 crore for a visit to the Netherlands, ₹4.23 crore for a visit to Italy (all in May), ₹4.77 crore for a visit to the Slovak Republic in June, ₹3.87 crore for a visit to Indonesia, ₹1.18 crore for a visit to Australia, and ₹5.43 crore for a visit to New Zealand (all in July).

“High level visits by the Prime Minister are established means of fostering closer relations with foreign countries and promoting India’s engagements at bilateral, regional and global levels,” Margherita said in his reply.

“These visits, and the understandings and agreements concluded therein, facilitate the strengthening of partnerships across a wide range of sectors, including technology, innovation, trade and investment, defence and energy cooperation, and resilient supply chains, among others.”
Of the visits to 23 countries in 2025, the five most expensive were to France ( ₹25.59 crore), Brazil ( ₹17.72 crore), the US ( ₹16.54 crore), Saudi Arabia ( ₹15.54 crore), and China ( ₹10.6 crore).

The PM visited 17 countries in 2024 at a total cost of ₹109.51 crore, with the five most expensive trips being to the US ( ₹15.33 crore), Italy ( ₹14.36 crore), Russia ( ₹10.75 crore), Poland ( ₹10.1 crore), and Singapore ( ₹7.75 crore).

There were visits to 11 countries in 2023 that cost a total of ₹93.63 crore, with the most expensive trips being to the US ( ₹22.89 crore), Japan ( ₹17.19 crore), France ( ₹13.74 crore), and Papua New Guinea ( ₹8.58 crore).

The PM’s visits to 10 countries in 2022 cost a total of ₹55.83 crore, with the most expensive trips being to Germany ( ₹14.47 crore), another visit to Germany ( ₹9.44 crore), and Japan ( ₹8.68 crore).
The PM visited four countries in 2021, resulting in total expenditure of ₹36.12 crore. This included a visit to the US that cost ₹19.63 crore and a trip to the UK that cost ₹8.57 crore.

Margherita’s response also provided figures on expenditure for the PM’s visits under the previous UPA government for reference and noted that ₹10.74 crore was spent on a visit to the US in 2011, ₹8.33 crore on a visit to France in 2011, ₹9.95 crore on a visit to Russia in 2013, and ₹6.02 crore on a trip to Germany in 2013.
“These figures show actual expenditure without adjusting for inflation or currency fluctuations,” he said.

Bombay high court convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, overturns acquittal
Edited by: Ayush Pandey / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 06, 2026, 13:22 IST
Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, overturns acquittal (PTI image)

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Thursday convicted former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal in the 2013 rape case filed by his former junior colleague, overturning his acquittal by a Goa trial court.The verdict came nearly 13 years after the alleged incident during the ThinkFest event in Goa, where Tejpal was accused of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator. The high court had reserved its judgment last week after hearing arguments from both sides.

Arguments on the quantum of sentence are currently underway, and the court is scheduled to pronounce its order on sentencing at around 2.30 pm.The Goa government had challenged Tejpal's acquittal after a sessions court cleared him of all charges in May 2021. The appeal was heard by Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar of the Bombay high court's Goa bench, which had directed Tejpal to remain present for the pronouncement of the verdict.Appearing for the Goa government, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta had argued that the trial court committed a serious error by evaluating the complainant's conduct based on preconceived notions of how a survivor of sexual assault should behave.

He submitted that there is no universal standard governing the reaction of a sexual assault survivor, as responses vary depending on an individual's education, personality, social background and circumstances.Tejpal, who was present in court, sought leniency, claiming that he was a "political victim" and the father of two daughters.Mehta also argued that the trial court placed undue emphasis on minor inconsistencies in the complainant's statements instead of examining whether her core allegations remained consistent.Referring to an email sent by Tejpal to the complainant after the alleged incident, the Solicitor General argued that the accused had apologised for his "lapse of judgment", expressed shame and stated that he believed the encounter had been consensual.
According to the prosecution, those statements amounted to an admission that an encounter had taken place.

The defence, led by senior advocate Abad Ponda, argued that the prosecution had misread the apology emails as admissions of a sexual encounter.Ponda submitted that none of the emails contained any admission of a consensual physical or sexual encounter and that the references related only to a consensual verbal conversation of a sexual nature.The defence also questioned the complainant's credibility, arguing that her conduct before and after the alleged incident, along with emails, WhatsApp messages and documentary evidence, contradicted the prosecution's case.The high court's conviction reverses the trial court's acquittal, with sentencing to be decided after hearing arguments on the quantum of punishment.

Air India turbulence lasted 5 minutes, crew members suffered spinal injuries: Minister
An Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi encountered severe mid-air turbulence, briefly losing around 300 feet in altitude and leaving 17 people injured on Thursday.

The mid-air turbulence that hit an Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi on Tuesday lasted nearly five minutes, leaving some crew members with spinal and neck injuries, Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu said as he shared fresh details about the incident.

The Airbus A320neo, operating as flight AI2379, experienced a sudden loss of around 300 feet in altitude while cruising on Tuesday. The aircraft, carrying 137 passengers and eight crew members, continued its journey and landed safely at Delhi airport at 11.07 am.
Speaking at a briefing in New Delhi, Naidu said the turbulence lasted around four to five minutes and praised the cabin crew for continuing to assist passengers despite suffering injuries themselves.

"The plane had to travel for one more hour and even through that hour, the crew members provided all the assistance required. It was very brave... I would like to thank them for the bravery they have shown," Naidu said.
When asked about the extent of the injuries, the minister said a couple of crew members suffered spinal injuries, including injuries near the tailbone and neck, and had been advised rest by doctors.

A total of 13 passengers and four cabin crew members were taken to hospital following the incident. Air India said on Wednesday that all 13 passengers had since been discharged, while the four crew members remained under medical care.

"As of Wednesday evening, all 13 passengers who were admitted to hospital following the incident involving Air India flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi on August 4 have been discharged. Four crew members remain under medical care and continue to receive treatment," the airline said in a statement.
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has launched an investigation into the incident, with the aircraft's Flight Data Recorder and Cockpit Voice Recorder secured for detailed examination.
According to a senior DGCA official, the pilot reported a severe injury to one cabin crew member, an injury to another and minor injuries to some passengers following the sudden loss of altitude.
"Air India A320 aircraft VT-EXO operating flight AI2379 (Phuket-Delhi) experienced loss of approximately 300 feet in altitude during the flight," the official said.
Air India had earlier said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss of altitude during cruise but continued to operate normally after the "momentary event" and landed safely in Delhi.
Following the incident, Naidu, Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha and DGCA Director General Vir Vikram Yadav visited Fortis Hospital in Delhi to enquire about the condition of those injured.

The aircraft has since been moved to a hangar as investigators examine the circumstances surrounding the sudden altitude loss. Air India has said it is cooperating with the investigation and has also informed the aircraft manufacturer.

JP Nadda and Himanta Biswa Sarma inspect flood-ravaged Assam (PTI)

As the Narendra Modi government explores the possibility of bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill to carry out a fresh delimitation exercise, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) may consider extending support if the government revises the legislation bringing in three essential changes to the Bill that reached the Lok Sabha in April.

There is a freeze on seats based on the 1971 Census which ends after the latest Census that is expected to be completed in 2027. The DMK wants this constitutional freeze to remain for another 25 years, while amending the Constitution to introduce a 50% blanket increase in the Lok Sabha seats for all States, which was verbally promised by Home Minister Amit Shah when the legislative package aimed at bringing about delimitation was brought in Parliament in April.

Additionally, the party wants a Schedule of the number of seats that each State will have in the legislative package, as per sources in the DMK. A top DMK leader said that the government has not yet approached them on the issue either “formally or informally”. The party maintains that it will take a final call only once the form and substance of Bills are known.

These conditions come amid renewed efforts from the government to reach out to the Opposition, with Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju speaking to Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi again on Thursday. “I had a productive conversation with Rahul Gandhi. I have made a request on a few specific issues and also discussed other matters. We expect continuous communication and coordinated action with the Congress and other Opposition parties,” Mr. Rijiju said.

The Parliamentary Affairs Minister had also met Mr. Gandhi at the latter’s office in Parliament on Wednesday, during which the Congress leaders are also said to have reiterated their opposition to any constitutional amendment to carry out the delimitation exercise.

Though the government doesn’t have the two-thirds majority yet to push through a constitutional amendment, the political situation has changed since April 17, when the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated on the floor of the House. The numerical strength of the INDIA bloc has since vastly changed.

In the present 540-member Lok Sabha, the two-thirds majority mark is 360, and if 22 Lok Sabha members of the DMK vote for the Bill, the government’s strength would go up to 346. While the government would still be short of 14 MPs, the threshold changes if there are abstentions during the proceedings. If the government brings the Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it will find it easier to reach the two-thirds majority mark. In the Rajya Sabha, if all 244 members are present during voting, the government needs 164 votes. The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance currently has 158 MPs.

Mr. Shah had earlier said that once it is assured of the numbers, the government would once again bring the constitutional amendment Bill to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 seats in order to implement the 33% reservation for women after fresh delimitation.

Since April, the government has secured the support of 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs, who are now part of the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) and six Shiv Sena MPs who had switched sides from the Uddhav Thackeray faction to the Eknath Shinde-led faction.
On Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be hosting the NCPI and Shiv Sena MPs for a breakfast meeting.

In anticipation of the delimitation and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bills coming up next week, the Congress is all set to issue a three-line whip, asking its members to be present in Parliament next week.
Meanwhile, the Lok Sabha continued to be disrupted over the Opposition protests regarding police action against students.
Speaker Om Birla started the proceedings in the morning by commemorating the anniversaries of the bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and members stood in silence to pay tribute to the victims.

Thereafter, Opposition MPs began raising slogans, demanding the presence of Mr. Shah in the House over the police action against student protesters on July 20. Some members were also seen displaying placards.
