Karnataka Council chair row: Basavaraj Horatti says Shivakumar asked him to resign
Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti said Chief Minister D K Shivakumar asked him to resign. He said only the House can decide the post, sharpening a fresh constitutional row.

Karnataka Legislative Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti on Tuesday said Chief Minister D K Shivakumar had called him and asked him to resign from the post. Horatti said he would discuss the matter with BJP and JD(S) leaders before taking a decision.

He also said the chairman of the Legislative Council and the Speaker of the Assembly can be chosen only by the House, and not by the high command of a political party. His remarks came after the Congress high command approved Saleem Ahmed as its nominee for chairman of the state Legislative Council and Umashree for deputy chairperson.

The approvals were conveyed in a letter sent to Shivakumar on Monday, along with the list of ministers who were sworn in the same day. The party also cleared the names of G S Patil as its nominee for the post of Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and A S Ponnanna for deputy speaker.

"The chief minister called me and requested that I resign and cooperate to prevent embarrassment, as the party has sent the name (for the new chairman).... I will discuss this with opposition leaders and decide," Horatti told reporters. Horatti, an eight-time MLC, has his current term till July 2028.

Questioning the announcement by the party, Horatti said, "This is probably for the first time I have seen a party declaring the chairperson of the legislative council. I'm not sure how they are doing it. It is not good in democracy." He said the chairman of the council and the speaker of the assembly could only be elected by the House.

Explaining the process for his removal, Horatti said, "To remove the chairman, ten members must give 14 days' advance notice, to move the no-confidence motion. Based on the discussion in the House the matter will be decided," and added that the decision of the House was supreme in the matter.
He also said no chairperson had been made to resign since 1956 and that all had completed their terms. According to Horatti, there were no grounds to remove him.

In the 75-member Legislative Council, the Congress has 38 members, the BJP 24 and the JD(S) 6. There is one Independent member and one chairman, while five seats are vacant. The row over Horatti's continuation has come after the Congress named its candidates for the top posts in both Houses.

A US lawmaker on Tuesday criticised the amendments proposed to India's foreign funding law, alleging that they could allow the government to take over churches and religious charities and warning that the issue could affect India-US ties.US Congressman Riley Moore said the proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) amounted to "a clear attack against Christians" and urged India not to proceed with the legislation in its current form.In a post on X, the Republican Congressman from West Virginia said Christianity had a long history in India dating back to the arrival of St Thomas the Apostle on the Malabar Coast."But despite this long Christian history, India's Parliament is considering amending Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment (FCRA) rules to permit government takeovers of churches and religious charities," Moore wrote."This is a clear attack against Christians.

If this bill proceeds in this way, it would be a point of major concern in our bilateral relationship with India," he added.The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 proposes the creation of a Designated Authority that would take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such funds if an organisation's FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or lapses after not being renewed.

The Bill specifies that where such assets include a place of worship, the Designated Authority must ensure that its religious character is preserved.It also proposes reducing the maximum punishment for violations of the Act from five years' imprisonment to one year.The FCRA regulates the receipt and utilisation of foreign contributions by NGOs, charitable trusts, educational institutions, religious bodies and other associations. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju met Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) in an effort to break the parliamentary deadlock, with the two sides discussing the proposed delimitation Bill and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill, 2026.

Amid speculation that the government could convene a three-day session after Independence Day to push through the women’s reservation Bill and the delimitation Bill, Mr. Rijiju told The Hindu that “there is no such proposal”.

Sources said Mr. Rijiju did not raise any proposal to extend the ongoing Monsoon Session or convene a Special Session during the nearly 50-minute meeting with Mr. Gandhi. Instead, he sought the Congress leader’s views on the party’s stand on delimitation, they said.

According to sources, Mr. Gandhi conveyed to Mr. Rijiju that a statement by Home Minister Amit Shah on the police action against students who protested against the NEET paper leak and a discussion on the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya were non-negotiable if the House was to function.
The Congress leaders also reiterated their opposition to any constitutional amendment to carry out the delimitation exercise, sources added.

The meeting, held in Mr. Gandhi’s Parliament office, was attended by Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal, deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.
The government’s outreach came on a day when Opposition MPs held a symbolic march within the Parliament complex, questioning Mr. Shah’s continued absence from the House.
Both Houses witnessed repeated disruptions before being adjourned for the day.

The Wednesday (August 3) meeting was the second between Mr. Rijiju and Mr. Gandhi in the past 10 days. The Parliamentary Affairs Minister had also spoken to the Congress leader over the telephone on Tuesday (August 4) night as part of the government’s efforts to secure Opposition cooperation during the remainder of the Monsoon Session.

Sources said Mr. Shah was expected to reply to the debate when the FCRA Bill comes up for discussion and passage. “The LoP has made it very clear that they cannot bring the FCRA Bill in this form,” Mr. Venugopal told reporters after the meeting.

“Now you see, the mood of Narendra Modi will change within a minute. If the Indian Opposition says something, he will not listen, but this kind of diktat is coming from foreign country, they will now...,” he added, when asked about U.S. Congressman Riley M. Moore’s social media post criticising the FCRA.

The Bill is considered contentious because it empowers a government-appointed authority to take over foreign-funded assets of organisations whose FCRA registration ceases, a provision that the Opposition says gives the Centre sweeping powers over NGOs and religious institutions.

However, there was no clarity on whether the delimitation Bill would be introduced during the current session, which is scheduled to conclude on August 13. Sources also ruled out, for now, the possibility of a Special Session immediately after Independence Day.

The government is understood to be assessing the political support available for reviving the delimitation Bill, a Constitution amendment Bill requiring a two-thirds majority in Parliament. It could not muster the required numbers when it attempted to move the legislation during the Budget Session.

Since the Monsoon Session began on July 20, the Lok Sabha has failed to transact Question Hour even once because of repeated disruptions. Five Bills have been passed without debate as the Opposition has pressed for discussions on the NEET paper leak, the police action against protesting students and the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, while demanding statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Shah.

Chandigarh: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi Friday to discuss the possible revival of an alliance between his party and the BJP for next year’s assembly elections in Punjab.
Akali Dal sources confirmed to ThePrint that a possible coming back together of the former partners was the agenda of the meeting. However, details of the discussion have not yet been made public.

A one-on-one meeting between the two leaders has happened after several years. The Akalis and the BJP remained political partners for over three decades before parting ways in 2020 following the controversy over the three central farm laws.

Sources further said that Badal was called for a meeting by the PM within days of the former having met Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini regarding a possible pre-poll alliance. Badal, along with senior Akali leaders Daljit Singh Cheema and Balwinder Singh Bhundar, had met Saini some days ago asking him to take up the matter—as in-charge of the BJP in Punjab—with the party leadership.
Saini, sources added, was instrumental in getting Badal an audience with the PM on the matter.
In March this year, Union Home Minister Amit Shah had during his rally in Moga ruled out the possibility of any bonding with the Akalis.

Moreover, PM Modi had during his visit to Jalandhar last month attacked the Akalis, along with other opposition parties in his speech. The negative reference to the Akali Dal had almost ruled out the possibility of the two parties coming together before the elections.
‘Anyone can go meet PM, We will contest all seats alone’

Reacting to the meeting, state BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon said that as far as the Punjab BJP is concerned, it is making preparations to contest all 117 assembly seats in the state and there was no possibility of a tie-up. “Anyone can go and meet the PM. We are going to contest alone on all seats,” he told mediapersons Friday.

On the other hand, some senior BJP leaders including former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh and former state party chief Sunil Jakhar had made it clear that the BJP will benefit electorally if it were to come back with SAD.
During a recent visit to Punjab, BJP president Nitin Nabin had said that a decision regarding the alliance would be taken at an appropriate time.

The seat sharing formula followed before the break-up had the Akalis in the dominant position. For the Lok Sabha elections, Akalis fought 10 of the 13 seats while the BJP fought on 3. In the assembly elections, the BJP fought on 23 seats while the Akalis fought on 94 seats.

After breaking away in 2021, the two parties contested the 2022 Punjab assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections independently. In the assembly elections, the Akalis won three seats and the BJP won two. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP failed to win any seats in the state, while the Akali Dal managed to secure only one.

Sources in the BJP told ThePrint that the state leadership was divided over the decision regarding a tie-up. However, everybody was on the same page that in case the two parties come together for the elections, the BJP will not be the junior partner. Sources added that the Akalis will have to give more or an equal number of seats to the BJP.

Akali Dal sources told ThePrint that issues related to the division of seats would come up only after an in-principle decision of a tie-up is agreed to by the Prime Minister. They said that the question of seat-sharing depended on the winnability of candidates but the Akalis are ready to give almost 35 seats to the BJP for the assembly elections.
AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal reacted to the meeting quoting a popular Bollywood number of the yesteryears. “Na na karte pyaar tumhi se kar baithe…(we kept saying no, no but finally we fell in love).”
“Are the chanda chor (temple donation thief) and beadbi (sacrilege) parties coming together?” he posted on X.

India maps 27 key Arunachal locations after China's repeated renaming attempts
The exercise was carried out in consultation with the Arunachal Pradesh government and is intended to ensure accurate identification of these places and improve public awareness, a statement said.

India on Friday formally marked 27 locations and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh on the official maps of the Survey of India, a move that comes amid repeated attempts by China to rename places in the border state.

According to an official statement, the exercise was carried out in consultation with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and is intended to ensure accurate identification of these places and improve public awareness.

"The Government of India, in consultation with the State Government of Arunachal Pradesh, has marked a total of twenty-seven (27) locations/geographical features situated in Arunachal Pradesh on the official maps of the Survey of India, along with their standard names," a Home Ministry statement said.

"The objective of formally marking these on the Survey of India's map of Arunachal Pradesh is to facilitate their precise identification and foster greater awareness among the general public," it added.
The development comes against the backdrop of China periodically releasing lists of so-called standardised names for places in Arunachal Pradesh, which Beijing refers to as Zangnan.
New Delhi has consistently rejected these exercises, maintaining that they have no bearing on India's sovereignty over the state.

India has repeatedly described the Chinese renaming exercise as "vain and preposterous" and asserted that it will not change the "undeniable" reality that Arunachal Pradesh "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of India.

Among the places formally identified on the Survey of India map is Longju, located along the Line of Actual Control. Longju was one of the earliest flashpoints in India-China border tensions when Chinese forces entered the area in 1959. Nearby Maja village in Upper Subansiri district has also been included.

The notified locations include several strategically important high-altitude passes such as Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La. Thag La, where one of the opening battles of the 1962 India-China war took place, has also been formally marked on the official map.
Jairampur in Changlang district, an important logistics hub that supports movement of security forces towards eastern Arunachal Pradesh and the Myanmar frontier, is among the identified locations.

Other places listed include Sambho Sarovar, a high-altitude lake, Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun, Dhan Bari, Pritnagar, Teritnagar, Ramnagar and Jaswant Garh, which houses the memorial of 1962 war hero Jaswant Singh Rawat on the Tawang road. Villages such as Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar and Baisakhi have also been marked.
The list further includes Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, which commemorates 1962 war hero Trilok Singh Thapa, along with Chhota Ropuk, Bara Ropuk, Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura, Kamlang Nagar and Buddhamandir.
| 22 | Sher-e-Thapa Memorial |
The government said the formal marking of these places has been done along with their standard names and locations on the official Survey of India map.

New Delhi has maintained that Chinese efforts to assign what it calls fictitious names to Indian territory are aimed at creating "baseless narratives" and cannot alter the situation on the ground. India has also warned that such actions could undermine efforts to improve bilateral relations.
China first released a list of six renamed places in Arunachal Pradesh in 2017. A second list covering 15 places followed in 2021, and another list containing 11 names was issued in 2023.

India has consistently reiterated that Arunachal Pradesh is an inseparable part of the country and that administrative or cartographic measures taken by China do not affect India's legal and territorial position.
Exclusive: DMK clears stance on delimitation bill amid buzz as Vijay calls MPs' meet

Amid strong buzz that the DMK has softened its stance on the delimitation bill, much to the unease of the INDIA alliance, Udhayanidhi Stalin clarified that the party had opposed the exercise from the very start.

At a time when the Centre has signalled its intention to reintroduce the delimitation bill, which it has linked to the implementation of women's reservation, the issue has become the latest flashpoint in Tamil Nadu. Amid buzz that the DMK has softened its stance on the bill much to the unease of the INDIA bloc, Udhayanidhi Stalin clarified to India Today that the party had opposed delimitation from the very beginning and "will continue to do so".

With differing voices emerging on the key issue, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay has called a meeting with state MPs to discuss the proposed delimitation exercise. So far, the DMK had not presented a stern stance on the bill amid talks of its revival. It had led to unease in the opposition, especially the Congress.
Rahul Gandhi, in a veiled swipe at the DMK, described the supporters of the bill as "21st-century Ettappans" - a term used in Tamil Nadu as a metaphor for a traitor.
DMK CLARIFIES ON DELIMITATION AMID BUZZ
A united opposition had defeated the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in April, which proposed lifting the freeze on expanding the number of Lok Sabha seats.

However, much water has flown down the Cauvery since DMK supremo MK Stalin burnt a copy of the bill as a symbolic protest. The DMK exited the INDIA bloc at the national level after the Congress ditched the party to support Vijay's TVK in Tamil Nadu.
The delimitation bill seeks to redraw constituencies based on the 2011 Census. It will see the total number of Lok Sabha seats rising from 543 to 850.
Clearing the DMK's stance on the bill, Udhayanidhi said, "The DMK has always opposed delimitation. We will continue to oppose it in the future."
"This is not a new issue. The Centre is presenting it as if it has surfaced for the first time," the Leader of the Opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly told India Today.

Significantly, the clarification came hours after a report in The Hindu claimed the DMK has indicated it might support the delimitation bill if three changes were incorporated. With 22 MPs in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha, the DMK is the fifth-largest constituent in Parliament.
The DMK has demanded that the 1971 Census and not the 2011 exercise should remain the basis for delimitation of the Lok Sabha for the next 25 years.
The party has also sought a blanket 50% increase in the Lok Sabha seats for all states. This was verbally promised by Union Home Minister Amit Shah when the bill was brought in Parliament in April.
Thirdly, according to the report, the DMK wants the bill to include a state-wise list showing how many seats each state will have following the proposed delimitation exercise.
Udhayanidhi's clarification on the DMK's position comes against the backdrop of the report.
THE DELIMITATION MUDDLE FOR TAMIL NADU
Now, why is Tamil Nadu opposed to the delimitation exercise?

The key argument of parties in Tamil Nadu and southern states is that linking the delimitation exercise to population would unfairly benefit the North, where population growth has been higher. The southern states have historically performed better in population control.

The South fears it will lead to a smaller increase in seats than the northern states, where the BJP wields influence. This will not only result in the South losing its voice in Parliament, but it may also lose out on tax devolution.
The five southern states - Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Telangana - account for around 24% of the population.
Now, let's understand the math.

Presently, Tamil Nadu has 39 Lok Sabha seats. Its share in Parliament is 7.2%. If the strength of each state is increased by 50%, as demanded by the DMK and other parties, Tamil Nadu will have 59 seats.
WHY UNIFORM INCREASE WON'T SOLVE PROBLEM
Even then, a uniform increase in Lok Sabha seats will substantially enhance the political weight of larger states, most of which are in the north.
This was very well portrayed by Kerala MP Shashi Tharoor via a salary analogy on X in his reply to Andhra Pradesh MP Chandrababu Naidu.

"Say your salary is Rs 2 lakh, and your driver's is Rs 20,000. A 50% increase will take your salary to Rs 3 lakh and that of your driver's to Rs 30,000. The percentage increase is the same - but aren't you much better off than your driver?" Tharoor said in a post in June.

Now, let's apply the same logic to Lok Sabha seats. A 50% increase will take Uttar Pradesh's representation from 80 MPs to 120. But a similar increase will take the number of MPs from Kerala to 30 from 20. This, in fact, takes the gap in MPs between UP and a southern state like Kerala from 60 to 90.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister Vijay will hold a meeting with MPs from the state on Saturday to discuss the proposed delimitation bill and its potential impact on the state. Vijay had previously called the Centre's delimitation exercise a "biased move" and vehemently opposed it.

The meeting will be attended by both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs from Tamil Nadu. The move by Vijay to engage with parties across the political spectrum earned praise from Congress MP Manickam Tagore.

"Over the past 12 years, I have seen five chief ministers as MPs. However, this is the first time I have seen a Tamil Nadu Chief Minister take the step of personally inviting MPs from all parties for a consultation, without any political differences," Tagore tweeted.
"Everyone must stand together so that Tamil Nadu speaks with one voice in Delhi against the oppression of the BJP-led Centre," he further said.
Congress MP and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has already conveyed to Union Minister Kiren Rijiju that the delimitation bill was "not acceptable" to the opposition.

The timing of the meeting is crucial, with the DMK and the TVK being at loggerheads recently. The dramatic arrest of Udhayanidhi earlier this week over alleged vulgar remarks against actor Trisha, a close friend of Vijay, further added to the bad blood.
With the DMK having the largest number of MPs from the state, it is expected that the party would influence the outcome of the meeting.

New Delhi: A day after Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat endorsed the role of Gen Z in the recent Cockroach Janta Party-led protests, BJP MP and actor Kangana Ranaut sought to make amends, calling them India’s ‘biggest strength’.

Her latest remarks marked a sharp climbdown days after the Member of Parliament from Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi referred to “young Hindu women” who took part in the CJP protests as “generation gutter”. Some wanted to imitate independent career women without earning their freedom or accepting accountability, she had said.

On Friday, Kangana said it was wrong to judge an entire generation based on the actions of a few individuals. “Gen Z is a part of the government. Our government has been in power for so long due to the mandate of Gen Z. “Today, the students sitting and protesting in Jharkhand are conducting themselves peacefully and responsibly. Akal Takht panel seeks Punjab compliance report before anti-sacrilege talks

The Akal Takht-appointed expert panel has asked the Punjab government to file a compliance report before any talks on the anti-sacrilege law. It says the state's reply ignored core objections and no discussion should proceed without Panthic consensus.

The Akal Takht-appointed expert panel has asked the Punjab government to first submit a compliance report on the objections raised by the Sikh temporal seat before any further discussion can take place on the proposed anti-sacrilege legislation.
The panel, formed to deliberate with the state government on issues related to the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026, held its first meeting on Thursday.
It said the government's July 29 response did not address the Akal Takht's basic objections, particularly on provisions seen as interference in Sikh religious matters.
On June 29, Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Kuldip Singh Gargajj had directed the Punjab government to address his objections to the anti-sacrilege law within a month.

In a statement issued on Friday, the Akal Takht Secretariat said, "The response of the Punjab government, received on the penultimate day of the one-month deadline, is clearly an obfuscation of facts and an attempt to skirt the issue. The concerns of the 'Khalsa Panth' have been clearly communicated to the Speaker, Punjab Legislative Assembly and members of the Punjab cabinet on July 31, 2026."

It further said, "The government's conduct so far has not been constructive towards finding a resolution to the grave and sensitive issue of sacrilege. Despite substantial time afforded by the Akal Takht, the Punjab government has not yet constituted its panel to deliberate on the issue."

More than a week ago, Gargajj had rejected the Punjab government's response on the anti-sacrilege law as "unsatisfactory" and announced a five-member expert committee to engage with the Aam Aadmi Party government on the matter.
The expert panel comprises Justice (Retd) Rupinder Singh Sodhi, Justice (Retd) Mohinder Mohan Singh Bedi, senior advocate Puran Singh Hundal, and Sikh scholars Dr Kehar Singh and Prof Jagmohan Singh.

Under the Jathedar's directions, separate letters were recently sent to Punjab Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh, Sikh MLAs and Punjab government ministers, stating that no further discussion or amendment to the anti-sacrilege law should take place without 'Panthic' consensus.

Gargajj had also directed all Sikh MLAs and Cabinet ministers to ensure that during the Assembly session beginning on August 3, no discussion takes place on the anti-sacrilege law until consensus is reached with the Akal Takht and the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, and not to give consent to any further amendments to the law.

The Jathedar's remarks had come a day after AAP MLA Inderbir Singh Nijjar submitted the Punjab government's response to objections raised by the Akal Takht on the proposed anti-sacrilege legislation. The latest stand of the expert panel underlines that the state government must first address those objections before talks can move forward.
Oppn may press for statement by Shah as govt set to table FCRA bill

A large section of the Opposition is set to continue to press for Union home minister Amit Shah’s statement on allegations of police excess during student protests in Jantar Mantar and stick to their demand even if the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill is introduced in Parliament next week

A large section of the Opposition is set to continue to press for Union home minister Amit Shah’s statement on allegations of police excess during student protests in Jantar Mantar and stick to their demand even if the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill is introduced in Parliament next week.

The controversial bill, tabled during the budget session, might be taken up for debate and approval of the Lok Sabha next week. On Thursday, Manipur chief minister Lalduhoma said the debate was likely on August 12.

Congress chief whip in the Rajya Sabha, Jairam Ramesh, told HT, “The Opposition parties have decided to continue to demand a statement first from home minister Amit Shah on police brutalities on protesting youth and students especially on July 20.”

On Friday, opposition parties held a short meeting to reconfirm that they would stick to their key demand — Shah’s statement. In the meeting, the leaders were also briefed about the sentiments of various stakeholders and a section of the international community for the proposed changes to FCRA.

“The Opposition parties have been very clear in our focus and commitment to run Parliament. The ball is squarely in the court of the home minister. Come, make a statement on the floor of Parliament on the police excess on students. If he does not, he would be responsible for the disruptions. Not us. This is Parliament. Not the Gujarat Gymkhana. And if they try any stunts and bring FCRA, it won’t cut. First: HM statement. Then all else,” Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha floor leader Derek O’Brien told HT.

The bill provides for the cessation of the FCRA certificate of an organisation upon expiry, non-renewal or refusal of renewal by the government. The amendments also establish a designated authority for “a comprehensive framework for vesting, supervision, management and disposal of foreign contribution and assets, including provisional and permanent vesting.” A provision stated that the government can appoint a “designated authority” to take over, manage, or sell assets created from foreign funds by an non-governmental organisation whose licence under FCRA was cancelled, suspended, or simply not renewed.
To be sure, a section of the Opposition want to participate in the debate and have argued that the bill was too important bill to be passed in din.

“I don’t know about any decision. As far as my party is concerned, we want to join the debate. We have to register our objections to the bill. The bill is not only against the Christians but against all sections of the society,” said Communist Party of India (Marxist)’s Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas. He added, “The Opposition has a duty to oppose this piece of legislation. It dents the fundamental rights.”
A senior Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam leader said, “We want a debate on the bill. The Congress wants diversions. We will not follow the Congress’s path.”

Brittasalso pointed out that the Opposition hardly got any opportunity to participate in the debate during the ongoing session. According to PRS Legislative Research data, The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 was the only bill passed after a full debate in this session. He said that during the British era, because the Pardhi community took part in the freedom struggle, the entire community was branded as a criminal tribe, which caused it to fall far behind in development. The new US legislation seeks to punish Russia and key buyers of its petroleum products, including India and China.

After the US Senate passed sweeping Russia sanctions bill which could lead to the imposing of up to 100 per cent tariff on India, questions arose over the impact of this decision on the ongoing India-US trade deal.

White House National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett said it was up to the negotiators to determine if the new US legislation which targets Russian oil buyers will affects trade talks with India. "That's upto the negotiators. I can't give you insight into the ongoing (talks)," Hassett was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.

The US Senate on Friday voted 86-11 to pass the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' which seeks to punish Russia and key buyers of its petroleum products, including India and China. Approving the legislation, the US claimed that such trade helps fuel the Ukraine war.

The new law allows US President Donald Trump to impose 100 per cent tariffs on goods from countries that are top five importers of Russian oil and gas. Among these are China, India, Azerbaijan, Hungary and Slovakia.

India has emerged as the second-largest importer of Russian crude. The reliance on Russia further increased as the West Asia war led to the closure of Strait of Hormuz, blocking supply from the Gulf. Russian oil, which is offered at discounted price, has helped Indian refiners manage costs and ensure stable fuel supplies.
Russian leaders and officials, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, oligarchs and financial institutions, could also face sanctions under this legislation.
The bill further extended the expiration date of the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996, to 2031. This act allows US to impose penalties on companies that invest in Iran's energy sector.

Centre appoints 30 judges to four High Courts, Madras gets highest share
The Centre has notified the appointment of 30 judges across four High Courts. The move is aimed at filling vacancies and easing the burden of pending cases.

The Centre on Saturday notified the appointment of 30 judges across four High Courts, with the Madras High Court receiving the largest share of new appointees as part of an effort to strengthen judicial capacity and reduce case pendency.

According to a notification issued by the Ministry of Law and Justice, the appointments include 20 advocates and 10 judicial officers. Of the total, 15 judges have been appointed to the Madras High Court, eight to the Calcutta High Court, six to the Karnataka High Court and one to the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The appointments were made by the President in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Supreme Court Collegium.
MADRAS HIGH COURT GETS 15 JUDGES
The Madras High Court received the highest number of appointments, including five permanent judges and ten additional judges.

The newly appointed permanent judges are advocates Krishnaswamy Govindarajan, Rajnish Pathiyil, Natarajan Ramesh, GK Muthukumaar and Ramakrishnan Rajesh Vivekananthan. Additional judges appointed from the Bar include Sankaranarayanan Raveekumar, Nagarajan Dilip Kumar and Ellappan Manoharan.
Among judicial officers elevated as additional judges are Dr. P Murugan, MD Sumathi, S Alli, C Thirumagal Chandrasekar, Shanmugam Karthikeyan, Baluchamy Murugesan and N. Gunasekaran.
EIGHT JUDGES APPOINTED TO CALCUTTA HIGH COURT

The eight new additional judges appointed to the Calcutta High Court are advocates Aryak Dutta, Atarup Banerjee, Sandeep Kumar Dey, Partha Pratim Roy, Sudip Deb, Anuj Singh, Arjun Ray Mukherjee and Rishad Medora.
SIX NEW JUDGES FOR KARNATAKA HIGH COURT

The Karnataka High Court has received six additional judges from the Bar. They are Raghavendra S Srivatsa, Hema Kulkarni, Subramanya Rangarao, Tadagavadi Prakash Vivekananda, Pramod Bakkeshwar and Shanti Bhushan Hombegowda.
ONE APPOINTMENT TO MADHYA PRADESH HIGH COURT
Senior advocate Amit Lahoti has been appointed as an additional judge of the Madhya Pradesh High Court.

The newly appointed judges are expected to take oath and assume office in the coming days. The appointments are expected to help fill vacancies in the four High Courts and improve the disposal of pending cases.
Jharkhand govt, protesting students to hold fresh talks at noon after no headway
The decision came after five rounds of discussions over Friday and Saturday, including a meeting with the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, which has been leading the protest.

The Jharkhand government has announced another round of talks with protesting job aspirants after a series of meetings with student groups failed to end a 15-day agitation over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The fresh meeting with student representatives is scheduled for 12 pm on Sunday.

The decision came after five rounds of discussions over Friday and Saturday, including a meeting with the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, which has been leading the protest. Soon after the announcement, the group accused the government of "political manoeuvring" and said the move was aimed at dividing students and shifting attention from their main demands.

On Saturday, the Hemant Soren government held four rounds of talks with different student organisations, including the Congress-backed NSUI, Jharkhand Chhatra Morcha and Adivasi Chhatra Sangh. The government had held talks with the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch on Friday.

After a four-hour meeting between the government panel and Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Saturday evening, Rural Development Minister Dipika Pandey Singh said the panel had informed the chief minister about the demands and concerns raised by student delegations. "It was decided in the meeting with the chief minister that a final round of talks with the protesting students will take place at 12 pm on Sunday," she said.

The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch strongly objected to the fresh engagement with other student bodies. Ravindra Paswan, a leader of the group, said the government was trying to weaken the agitation by holding talks with organisations that had "played no role in the ongoing protest."

"This is political manoeuvring by the government. It is trying to create a divide among students and divert attention. But they should know that all students are united," Paswan said at a press conference at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where students have been protesting since July 25. He said the Manch had already placed all its demands before the five-member government panel during a detailed meeting on Friday night.

The government panel, comprising ministers Dipika Pandey Singh, Sudivya Kumar, Chamra Linda and Sanjay Prasad Yadav, first met the faction of protesters led by Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader Devendra Nath Mahto, whose fast entered its seventh day. It later met the NSUI, ACS and JCM separately and sought their charters of demand. The JCM submitted five demands, including cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination.

The NSUI submitted six demands, including a CID probe within 90 days into all JPSC and JSSC examinations under suspicion and the setting up of a Jharkhand Testing Agency on the lines of the National Testing Agency. ACS leader Kartik Oraon demanded that tribal and regional languages be included as qualifying papers in recruitment examinations and that tests in which irregularities were found be cancelled.

The government said the discussions were held in a positive atmosphere and that it was considering the concerns raised by the protesting aspirants. Minister Sanjay Prasad Yadav said the government would continue talks with the agitators seeking comprehensive reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission. Higher and Technical Education Minister Sudivya Kumar said the government had issued an email ID to seek suggestions from aspirants on reforms in the recruitment process.

Despite the talks, the protesters said their agitation would continue until all their demands were met. They also announced a march to the Assembly on August 10 if the government failed to meet their demands by Sunday. Meanwhile, the All India Students' Association set up a separate platform at the stadium on Saturday, though its leaders said this should not be seen as a separate agitation.

AISA national president Neha Bora, who was attacked with ink during Friday's Assembly march near Birsa Chowk, briefly joined the protest and raised slogans demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC and JSSC-CGL examinations. Ranchi unit chief Vijay Kumar said the organisation had the same demands as the larger agitation and that its members would join the August 10 march without carrying the AISA banner.

The agitation has also seen protests by the ABVP. On Friday, its members scuffled with police while trying to breach barricades near the chief minister's residence. Deputy Superintendent of Police Ajay Aryan said around eight to 10 ABVP protesters were detained during the march and later released. The ABVP has announced a separate Vidhan Sabha march on August 11.

Amid the protests, students and job aspirants also observed martyr Nirmal Mahto's death anniversary by marching from the protest site to Albert Ekka Chowk and holding a flashlight procession. So far, 19 people have been arrested in connection with alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations, while former panel chairperson L Khiangte has been questioned four times since July 28. With the deadlock still unresolved, all eyes are now on Sunday's talks between the government and the protesting aspirants.

Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal in 2013 rape case, sentences him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment

PANAJI: Thirteen years after the arrest of a high profile editor-in-chief of Tehelka magazine, Tarun Tejpal, for rape in an elevator of a starred hotel, the Bombay high court on Thursday found him guilty of rape and sentenced him to ten years Rigorous imprisonment.The HC has granted him two weeks time to surrender.The sentence was pronounced in the State's challenge to Tejpal's acquittal by the trial court in 2021.

After the court found him guilty, senior advocate Aabad Ponda representing Tejpal sought lenient sentence for him on the grounds that he is a senior citizen today, aged 62 and that the case is a 13 year old one.Tejpal addressing the division bench of Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar said he is a "political victim" and is 62 years old and a father of two with a wife and sought a lenient sentence.He said that there is so much evidence in favour of him that he can be acquitted ten times.Solicitor general of India representing Goa Government Tushar Mehta however argued for maximum sentence for Tejpal.

He urged the court to consider that Tejpal was old enough to be in a parental position vis-a vis the survivor and argued that the sentence should set a precedent and have a strong deterrent effect.Mehta said that this was not some "misunderstanding or some banter" and pointed out that Tejpal had no remorse after the incident and alleged that he repeated the same thing on the next day.

He said Tejpal was brazen despite resistance and despite the survivor saying no.He further argued that the survivor's mature conduct after the incident had been wrongly portrayed as that of someone who had enjoyed the molestation."It is high time the highest constitutional court of the state gives him the maximum sentence. No means No. You may be whosoever you are but when a girl says no it means no. That deterrent message may be considered," Mehta told the court while arguing on maximum sentence for him.

Mehta during the hearings seeking Tejpal's conviction argued that the survivor was a stellar witness and stood by her case and that Tejpal's apology to her was proof of what he had done. He also argued that there was no reason for a man of her father's age to send her such her the 'the fingertips' text message after midnight and that it could not reasonably have an innocent meaning. Ponda had countered that saying the 'fingertips' text message had a different context and did not prove charge of rape.He had argued that the survivor had a "propensity to lie" and that her behaviour after the alleged incident was not commensurate with someone who had been raped and traumatised.

The flight was carrying 137 passengers. Several passengers and crew members were injured during the incident.
The occurrence has now been classified as a “Serious Incident” and will be investigated by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), the DGCA said.
Pending the confirmatory test and completion of the investigation, the DGCA has taken both flight crew members off the roster.
The regulator said further action would be taken based on the outcome of the AAIB investigation and the confirmatory test.

The DGCA's statement comes after sources had earlier told India Today that one of the pilots had undergone additional testing following the mandatory post-flight screening. Both pilots had been taken off flying duties pending the outcome of the tests and investigation.
AI2379 LOST 300 FEET OF ALTITUDE DURING CRUISE

Air India flight AI2379, operated by an Airbus A320 aircraft with registration VT-EXO, was flying from Phuket to Delhi on August 4 when it experienced a sudden loss of approximately 300 feet in altitude during cruise.
The aircraft subsequently stabilised and landed safely in Delhi.
The flight was carrying 137 passengers, including three infants, and eight crew members - two pilots and six cabin crew.
Several passengers and crew members were injured during the occurrence. The incident left at least 17 people injured, including four cabin crew members, according to the information provided.
Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu had earlier said the turbulence lasted around five minutes, with some crew members suffering spinal and neck injuries requiring medical attention.
PIC’S TEST REQUIRES CONFIRMATION
Following the occurrence, both pilots underwent the prescribed psychoactive substance screening as part of standard operating procedure.
“The screening test in respect of the Pilot-in-Command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing,” the DGCA said.
The PIC’s sample has consequently been sent to a designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis. The final report is awaited.
The wording means the initial screening has produced a result that requires further testing; it does not by itself establish that the pilot tested positive for drug use.
Pending completion of the confirmatory test and the AAIB investigation, the DGCA has taken both flight crew members off the roster.
Further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation and the confirmatory test results, the regulator said.
AIR INDIA SAYS IT CONDUCTS REGULAR DRUG TESTS
Air India had earlier confirmed that post-flight psychoactive substance screening had been conducted on the pilots, but said it had not received the results from the authorities.

“We are aware that a post-flight screening test was conducted on the pilots in accordance with applicable protocols. However, the results of the test have not been shared with Air India, and we are therefore not in a position to comment on any findings,” an airline spokesperson said.
The airline also said it conducts regular drug testing of crew members in compliance with civil aviation regulations and would continue to cooperate with the authorities.
AAIB TO PROBE SERIOUS INCIDENT
The DGCA has classified the AI2379 occurrence as a “Serious Incident”, bringing it under investigation by the AAIB.
The Ministry of Civil Aviation and the DGCA said the incident would be thoroughly investigated and appropriate action would be taken in accordance with prescribed regulations and procedures.
PASSENGERS RECALL MOMENTS OF TURBULENCE
Passenger Shrikant Jha, speaking in Jaipur, claimed that passengers had raised concerns about the pilot’s behaviour even before the turbulence.
“We actually had strong suspicions about this because of the pilot’s demeanour and appearance,” Jha said, alleging that the pilot’s gait and manner of speaking appeared unusual.
Jha said passengers had lodged a complaint with Ravishankar Gaur, the head of Terminal 3, urging authorities to conduct dope and blood tests.
Another passenger, Renu Raniwala, said she became particularly worried about children on board when the aircraft began dropping.
“When the flight started dropping, I was most worried about the children,” she said.

Raniwala said her grandson was sitting next to her and that she grabbed him and fastened his seatbelt. She claimed the force of the incident caused the handle to dig into her body, injuring two of her ribs.
She also claimed that a three-year-old girl was thrown towards the back of the aircraft during the incident.
Raniwala further alleged that passengers did not receive adequate assistance after landing, saying, “There was no care shown even after we landed.”

The passengers’ allegations about the pilot’s behaviour and the response after landing have not been independently established in the DGCA statement. The regulator’s investigation and confirmatory laboratory test are pending.

The collegium, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising justices Vikram Nath and BV Nagarathna, has decided to re-recommend Delhi high court judge justice V Kameswar Rao as chief justice of the Patna high court.

It has also decided to re-recommend two acting chief justices for appointment as full-time chief justices of their respective high courts — justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra for the Punjab and Haryana high court and justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma for the Rajasthan high court.

The collegium has further decided to recommended Allahabad high court judge justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi as chief justice of the Bombay high court and Bombay high court’s acting chief justice justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge as full-time chief justice of the Calcutta high court.
The signed recommendations are expected to be sent to the Union government shortly, people familiar with the matter said.
No decision has, however, been taken so far on appointing full-time chief justices for the Madhya Pradesh high court and the high court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

Rahul Navin will remain at the helm of India's financial crime agency for another year, extending his tenure beyond retirement as the ED continues several high-profile money laundering and financial investigations.

The Centre has extended Enforcement Directorate Director Rahul Navin’s tenure by another year, keeping him at the helm of the federal anti-money laundering agency until August 13, 2027, beyond his scheduled retirement.

Navin was made the acting director of the agency in September 2023 before taking over as its full-time chief the following year.

Russia to India by train? Moscow floats rail route to Indian Ocean
The proposal comes amid escalating maritime disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz following armed hostilities involving the US, Israel and Iran.

Russia is considering an ambitious railway route linking Russia to the Indian Ocean and potentially India, as Moscow explores alternative trade corridors amid risks surrounding key maritime chokepoints, including the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said the feasibility of such a rail link should be examined, suggesting that a possible route could pass through Turkmenistan, Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan before reaching the Indian Ocean.

Khusnullin, according to ANI citing Russian news agency TASS, said, “A rail link to the Indian Ocean should also be explored. Risks related to the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz might require alternative routes: through Turkmenistan, Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan. Any options providing access to India are acceptable.”
Why Russia is looking at alternative routes
The proposal comes amid escalating maritime disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz following armed hostilities involving the US, Israel and Iran.

On February 28, joint military strikes were launched against Iran, targeting key urban centres, including Tehran. In response, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) initiated retaliatory missile and drone operations against Israeli positions and US military bases across Bahrain, Jordan, Iraq, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE and Saudi Arabia.
Tehran subsequently announced a maritime blockade of the Strait of Hormuz against vessels affiliated with the US, Israel and allied nations involved in the operations against Iran.
The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global energy route, accounting for approximately 25 per cent of global oil trade and nearly 20 per cent of worldwide liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments.

Against this backdrop, Russia's proposed rail corridor could offer an alternative overland route for freight to reach the Indian Ocean and, potentially, India. Khusnullin said any route that provides connectivity to India would be considered viable.
Russia seeks bigger construction investment
In the same interview, Khusnullin also spoke about Russia's domestic construction sector, saying the industry needs sustained, long-term financial backing.
He said the country's construction industry currently has the capacity to absorb an additional one trillion rubles annually.

"The construction industry is already capable of handling an additional one trillion rubles annually. However, if such a volume is secured for the next five years, it would be possible to expand capacity and build even more," he added.

AIADMK's boycott clouds CM Vijay's bid for united Tamil Nadu front on delimitation

The AIADMK and the DMK will not attend Chief Minister Vijay's all-party meeting on delimitation in Tamil Nadu. Their absence exposes divisions over the Centre's proposed seat redraw linked to the 2011 Census.

The AIADMK has decided not to participate in Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay's all-party meeting on delimitation scheduled for Saturday, dealing a setback to efforts to present a united political front against the Centre's proposed constituency redrawing exercise.
The DMK has also decided to boycott the meeting, further exposing divisions among the state's major political parties over the issue.

The meeting was convened by Chief Minister Vijay to bring together Members of Parliament from Tamil Nadu and discuss a common strategy against the Centre's proposed delimitation exercise, which has emerged as a major political flashpoint in the state.
The latest development comes amid growing political debate over reports that the Centre is considering reintroducing the delimitation bill alongside the implementation of women's reservation.
The proposed legislation seeks to redraw parliamentary constituencies based on the 2011 Census and increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the current 543 seats to around 850.
WHY SOUTH INDIAN STATES OPPOSE DELIMITATION BILL?
Political parties across southern India, particularly in Tamil Nadu, have consistently opposed such an exercise if it is linked to population figures.

They argue that states which successfully implemented population control measures would be penalised with relatively fewer parliamentary seats, while northern states with higher population growth would gain a larger share of representation.
The issue had already triggered friction within the Opposition alliance after speculation that the DMK had softened its stand on the proposed legislation.
However, Tamil Nadu's Leader of Opposition, Udhayanidhi Stalin recently clarified that the DMK had opposed delimitation "from the very beginning" and would continue to do so.

The Congress had also expressed concern over the reported shift, with Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi taking a veiled swipe at supporters of the proposed legislation by referring to them as "21st-century Ettappans"—a term commonly used in Tamil Nadu to describe a traitor.
The proposed delimitation bill had earlier failed to secure passage after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in Parliament in April.
'DELIMITATION MIGHT REDUCE SOUTH INFLUENCE'

Opponents argue that delimitation based on the 2011 Census would disproportionately increase parliamentary representation for northern states while reducing the political influence of southern states, which have recorded lower population growth over the past decades.

They also contend that a reduced share of Lok Sabha seats could eventually weaken the South's bargaining power in Parliament and affect issues such as tax devolution and allocation of central resources.

With both the AIADMK and the DMK staying away, Vijay's meeting is set to proceed without the participation of two of Tamil Nadu's largest political parties, underscoring the complex political equations surrounding the contentious delimitation debate.
Abhishek Banerjee moves SC over bar on foreign travel for eye treatment

Abhishek Banerjee has approached the Supreme Court after the Calcutta High Court denied him permission to travel abroad for eye treatment. The dispute has turned on his refusal to appear before a medical board while an election-related investigation continues.
Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee has moved the Supreme Court against a Calcutta High Court order that refused him permission to travel abroad for eye treatment.

The high court had dismissed his plea on August 5, saying he was unwilling to appear before a medical board at the state-run SSKM Hospital in Kolkata for an assessment of his condition. The travel request is linked to conditions imposed in a case over alleged comments made at a public meeting during the West Bengal Assembly polls.

While dismissing the application, the high court said, "In view of submission made on behalf of the applicant (Banerjee) that applicant will not appear before the medical board at SSKM Hospital, Kolkata, this court finds the issue which is agitated before this court by filing application... ought not to be kept pending further."
The court said that if Banerjee had appeared before the medical board, the opinion of the medical experts could have been considered to examine whether he needed to go abroad for treatment.

On August 3, the Supreme Court had asked the Calcutta High Court to take up within a week Banerjee's plea seeking permission to travel abroad for eye treatment. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Banerjee, had told the top court that the plea sought modification of the high court order to allow the MP to travel for medical treatment.

The high court had earlier extended till October 6 Banerjee's interim protection from coercive action in a case related to alleged comments against leaders and workers of a rival party at a public meeting on April 27 in the run-up to the second phase of the West Bengal Assembly polls.

While granting relief, the high court had directed Banerjee to cooperate with the investigation and not travel abroad without the court's permission, as previously ordered. It had extended the interim protection till October 6, or until further orders, whichever was earlier, and said his plea for modification of the conditions would be heard in August, though no date was fixed.

The high court had also said earlier that it was not inclined to allow the petitioner to travel abroad while the investigation was underway, and noted that there were several reputed eye clinics in Kolkata. Banerjee has also sought quashing of the FIR against him.

With his latest move, Banerjee has now approached the Supreme Court after the Calcutta High Court refused to let him travel abroad for eye treatment and cited his unwillingness to appear before a medical board.

SC allows TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee to travel abroad for eye surgery

The Supreme Court on Monday pulled up the West Bengal government for opposing Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Abhishek Banerjee’s request to travel overseas for an eye surgery, asserting that every individual has a right to travel abroad and choose their medical treatment

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it saw “no serious impediment” to Banerjee travelling abroad for three weeks for the treatment and allowed him to do so, subject to conditions aimed at ensuring his availability to the investigating agency.
“Every individual has a right to go abroad. Every individual has a right to choose the medical treatment of their choice,” said the bench during the hearing.
The court also emphasised Banerjee’s right to privacy regarding his medical condition, observing that an individual cannot be expected to put his health records in the public domain.
“It is also a right to privacy to not bring your health records in public domain,” it observed.

The state opposed the plea, with additional solicitor general SV Raju submitting that there were at least 15 cases against Banerjee and arguing that his propensity to not return to India was greater because criminal cases were pending against him.

The bench, however, questioned the nature of the allegations in the case where the restriction on foreign travel had been imposed. “We are on to the nature of allegations. This is about a lecture given by him…there is no injunction against him in any other case,” it observed.
The court also pointed out that Banerjee had previously been permitted to travel abroad in matters involving more serious allegations.

“The State, we are certain, is weighed down with much serious investigations…He was allowed to travel before in cases with much more serious charges. What is the FIR in your case here? This is ultimately about some comments in a public meeting,” the bench said.

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Banerjee, submitted that the TMC MP was willing to comply with any reasonable condition and would travel on his diplomatic passport, which would enable embassies to track his movements.
The bench ultimately concluded that permitting Banerjee to travel would not prejudice the pending investigation.
“We feel no serious impediment will be caused to the pending investigation if the petitioner is allowed to travel abroad for three weeks for an eye-surgery,” the court said in its order.
The bench directed Banerjee to give an undertaking that he possessed no passport other than his diplomatic passport and to provide details of his itinerary, hospital and flights.

The dispute arose from a case relating to alleged comments made by Banerjee at a public meeting during the West Bengal assembly elections. The Calcutta High Court had earlier imposed a condition restraining him from travelling abroad without its permission while extending his interim protection from coercive action in the case.
Banerjee, nephew of former state chief minister Mamata Banerjee, had approached the Supreme Court after the high court on August 5 declined to permit him to travel abroad for eye treatment.
The high court had taken note of Banerjee’s refusal to appear before a medical board at the state-run SSKM Hospital in Kolkata for an assessment of his condition.

The travel restriction was earlier imposed while directing Banerjee to cooperate with the investigation. The high court had also noted that several reputed eye clinics were available in Kolkata and had previously indicated that it was not inclined to permit overseas travel while the investigation was pending.
The state told the high court that there was no medical emergency requiring Banerjee to seek treatment abroad and that his travel could affect ongoing investigations in cases against him.

Banerjee’s counsel, however, submitted that the criminal cases pending against him carried a maximum punishment of three years and were mostly bailable offences. It was also pointed out that Banerjee had previously been permitted to travel abroad during proceedings initiated by the Enforcement Directorate and had returned to India after overseas travel in 2023 and 2025.

Bombay HC judge recuses from plea challenging Maharashtra public security law

A Bombay High Court judge recused himself from hearing petitions against Maharashtra's Special Public Security Act, 2025. The challenge centres on claims that the law gives sweeping powers that could curb lawful dissent.

A Bombay High Court judge on Monday recused himself from hearing a challenge to the constitutional validity of the Maharashtra Special Public Security Act, 2025, which gives the state powers to declare certain organisations unlawful and take action against them.

Justice Gautam A Ankhad withdrew from the case when the petition filed by the Indian National Congress and the Communist Party of India came up before a bench also comprising Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge. The reason for the recusal was not stated in the court proceedings.

The petitions challenge several provisions of the law, arguing that they give the government broad and arbitrary powers to declare organisations unlawful, attach their properties and initiate criminal proceedings.

The Act aims to prevent what it describes as unlawful activities by Left Wing Extremist organisations and similar groups. The Maharashtra Assembly passed the Bill on July 10, 2025, followed by the Legislative Council on July 11. It received the President's assent on December 15, 2025.

The Congress and CPI have argued that the law allows organisations to be declared unlawful without adequate notice, a proper opportunity to present their case or access to the material on which the government's decision is based.
They have also questioned the advisory board set up under the Act, arguing that it is not an independent judicial body because its members are appointed by the government.
The petitioners have asked the High Court to stop the authorities from enforcing the law or taking coercive action under it while their challenge is pending.
CONCERNS OVER DISSENT AND EXISTING LAWS

The parties have also argued that the Act overlaps with existing legislation, including the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), and in some areas goes beyond them.
They have expressed concern that the law could potentially be used against political parties, civil society organisations, trade unions and other groups involved in lawful dissent.

The petitioners have further challenged provisions that they claim could make even association with an organisation later declared unlawful a criminal offence. They have also objected to references to a person's alleged “tendency” towards unlawful activity.

According to the petition, some provisions do not require authorities to establish criminal intent or a direct link between the alleged conduct and actual violence or public disorder. The petitioners argue that this could discourage people from exercising their rights to free speech, peaceful assembly and association.

Targeting those opposing ethanol-blended petrol during an event at Rewa Airport, Mishra said there are protests claiming ethanol won’t work and only ‘pure’ petrol should be used. “Desh mein jab shuddh petrol hai hi nahin to kya tumhare baap ke yahan se aaega (there’s no pure petrol in the country, so will it come from your father’s house?” he remarked, addressing critics of the policy.

Mishra went on to say that the whole world is trying to destabilise the prime minister at a time when he is working towards developing the nation.

Defending the ethanol blending policy, the MP said that India produces only 20 percent of its crude oil, and the rest has to be imported. “As for gas and oil, only 20 percent of the oil we use is produced domestically. We have to import 80 per cent from abroad. A war has broken out. The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and oil is being transported to the country via an 18,000-km detour,” he said.

“Yet, when PM Modi says that 20 percent ethanol will have to be blended into petrol, protests erupt, with people saying, ‘Ethanol won’t do—bring us only pure petrol.’ Will pure petrol come from your father’s house? When pure petrol isn’t even available in the country, where will it come from?”

Mishra then cited examples from other countries, including Brazil, where vehicles run on 100 per cent ethanol. “Brazil is the world’s largest producer of ethanol. Vehicles there run on 100 per cent ethanol without facing any issues. Mishra is no stranger to controversy. In November 2022, he had hit the headlines when he told a water conservation workshop in Rewa: “Lands are running dry of water, it must be saved… Drink alcohol, chew tobacco, smoke weed or smell thinner and solution but understand the importance of water.” Earlier the same year, he was filmed cleaning a toilet at a school with his bare hands.

Sharing the video clip of Mishra’s latest comments, senior Congress leader Supriya Shrinate said: “This is BJP MP Janardan Mishra from Rewa, Madhya Pradesh. People’s vehicles are getting ruined due to E20, but listen to his arrogance.”

The Opposition has been critical of the Modi government over the ethanol policy, with even the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) initiating a series of nationwide town hall meets against E20 fuel, in a bid to interact with vehicle owners and gather feedback on issues arising from ethanol-blended petrol.

Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan began a four-day official visit to Mauritius on Monday. This is his first visit to the island nation after assuming charge as Navy chief. India seeks to deepen bilateral maritime cooperation and strengthen defence ties with a key partner in the Indian Ocean Region.

During his visit from August 10 to 13, Admiral Swaminathan will interact with senior Mauritian Government leadership and hold discussions on maritime security, defence cooperation, capacity building and military collaboration.
The visit is aimed at strengthening operational-level linkages between the two countries and consolidating their strategic maritime partnership, the Navy said.

India and Mauritius share a longstanding maritime partnership, with the Indian Navy regularly engaging with the Mauritius National Coast Guard through training exchanges, operational interactions, including joint Exclusive Economic Zone surveillance, port visits and hydrographic surveys.

Mauritius has also been a regular participant in major Indian Navy-led multilateral and regional initiatives, including the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS), MILAN, the International Fleet Review, the Goa Maritime Conclave, IOS SAGAR and Exercise AIKEYME.

The engagements reflect the shared vision of MAHASAGAR — Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions – and India’s emphasis on strengthening maritime security and cooperation across the Indian Ocean.

Admiral Swaminathan’s visit comes as India continues to expand its engagement with maritime partners in the region through capacity building, information sharing, training and coordinated surveillance.

The Navy said the visit underscores the priority accorded by India to its close and enduring friendship with Mauritius, anchored in mutual respect, trust and a shared commitment to maritime security, regional cooperation and stability in the Indian Ocean Region.

Video: Uttarakhand flashflood rips apart bridge, sweeps away vehicle and driver
A bridge collapse cut off the border area and around a dozen villages, with rescue teams deployed to search for the missing BRO driver.

A sudden surge of floodwaters triggered by cloudbursts and intense monsoon rains turned the Tamak drain in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli into a raging torrent, sweeping away a Bailey bridge, a vehicle and a Border Roads Organisation (BRO) driver.

The bridge on the Malari-Niti National Highway connects Jyotirmath to the border area and the collapse snapped road connectivity to around a dozen villages, including Jumma and Niti and cut off the frontier.
A BRO driver, Pankaj, a resident of Pithoragarh district, was swept away by the powerful current as he was watching the floodwaters when the bridge suddenly collapsed. He remained missing.
A vehicle was also swept away as the floodwaters surged through the drain.
Rescue teams were quickly mobilised, with personnel from the district administration, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) dispatched to the site.

Following the bridge collapse, authorities suspended traffic on nearby roads as well. Officials said administrative teams were assessing the damage, while the BRO began work on alternative arrangements. Traffic is expected to be restored within a day or two, Chamoli District Disaster Management Officer NK Joshi added.
Over the past several years, floods and landslides in the Tamak drain have disrupted the Joshimath-Niti road, while flood debris has repeatedly choked the nearby Dhauli Ganga.
Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami directed officials to intensify relief and rescue operations and take precautionary measures in the lower areas following the flooding.
Dhami also directed officials to ensure that supplies of ration, food, medicines and other essential commodities to villages in the surrounding areas are not affected by the bridge collapse.

The Congress MP also urged the Centre to engage in constructive dialogue with the protesters. “I respectfully urge the government to reach out and engage in the dialogue our democracy owes its young citizens. That is not weakness; that is statesmanship,” he wrote.

Tricolour aboard ISS as Russian cosmonauts greet India on Independence Day
With India set to mark its 80th Independence Day, the cosmonauts reflected on the history of cooperation between India and Russia.

Russian cosmonauts aboard the International Space Station (ISS) have extended Independence Day wishes to India, marking the occasion with the Indian tricolour and a message celebrating the close ties between the two countries in space exploration.

With India set to mark its 80th Independence Day, the cosmonauts reflected on the history of cooperation between India and Russia, particularly their decades-long partnership in space missions and human spaceflight.
Also Read | Joint Russia-US crew returns to Earth after 241-day mission on ISS
‘Path of self-reliance and prosperity’
“Dear friends, today the Republic of India is celebrating its 80th Independence Day,” cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov said, extending wishes for peace and prosperity to the Indian people.
“India broke free from colonial rule and embarked on a path of self-reliance and prosperity,” Dubrov added.

The message also highlighted the connection between India's Independence Day and another significant milestone in space history. This year marks 65 years since Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human to travel into space.

Gagarin's visit to India in November 1961 further strengthened the bond between the Soviet Union and India. During the visit, he became an important symbol of the friendship developing between the two countries.
Recalling Gagarin's impressions of India, the cosmonauts said he had described the country as beautiful when viewed from space, but even more beautiful on Earth because it was home to “true friends.”

India and Russia's cooperation in space has spanned several decades. In 1975, the Soviet Union launched Aryabhata, India's first satellite, marking an important early milestone in the partnership. Nearly a decade later, in 1984, Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian to travel into space when he flew aboard the Soviet Soyuz T-11 spacecraft.
India's Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme

According to cosmonaut Anna Kikina, the partnership continues to evolve through India's Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme. Indian astronauts, known as Gaganyatris, have trained at the Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre in Russia ahead of India's first crewed space mission.

The cosmonauts also referred to a joint competition organised by Roscosmos, its representative office in India and ISRO to celebrate the two countries' cooperation in space. Entries selected as winners were presented alongside the Independence Day message.
The message concluded with the cosmonauts wishing India peace, prosperity and further achievements in space exploration.
“Long live India-Russia friendship,” cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev said, holding the Indian flag aboard the space station.

President Murmu gives assent to Vande Mataram Bill, grants it same legal protection as National Anthem
The Parliament had passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amending the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.
President Droupadi Murmu on Tuesday gave assent to the Vande Mataram Bill, granting the National Song the same legal protection as the national anthem.

The Parliament passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, last month, amending the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971. The legislation seeks to give Vande Mataram the same statutory protection as the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.
With the president's assent, the bill has become a law. Now, such offences are punishable with imprisonment up to three years, a fine, or both.

Earlier, the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act prohibited intentionally preventing the singing of the national anthem (Jana Gana Mana) or causing disturbance to any assembly engaged in such singing.

These offences were punishable by up to three years' imprisonment, a fine, or both, while a second and every subsequent conviction attracted a minimum of one year's imprisonment. The erstwhile law did not accord the same protection for the national song.

"Presently, there is no specific legal provision to prevent insults to the singing of 'Vande Mataram', which is honoured as the national song. Therefore, in order to prohibit any person from intentionally preventing the singing of the national song or causing disturbance to any assembly engaged in such singing, it is proposed to amend Section 3 of the said Act to include the national song also within its ambit, so as to make such acts punishable," the Bill had said.

The president of the Constituent Assembly, Dr Rajendra Prasad, on January 24, 1950, stated that the song 'Vande Mataram' composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, which played a historic role in the Indian freedom struggle, shall be honoured equally with the national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' and shall have equal status with it, the Bill further said.
Home ministry's Vande Mataram order
The Union home ministry said on Monday that for the first time at the Independence Day function, Vande Mataram will be sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort this year.
Earlier this year, the Union Home Ministry directed that all six stanzas of 'Vande Mataram' shall be sung first when the national song and the national anthem are played together.

In an order dated January 28, the home ministry gave the first set of protocols for singing the national song, directing that six stanzas of it, having a duration of 3 minutes and 10 seconds, shall be sung at official functions such as the arrival of the president, unfurling of the national flag, and speeches of governors.
"When the national song and the national anthem are sung or played, the national song will be sung or played first," the order read.
The assembly where the national song is sung shall stand in attention, it said.
The order, which carried several directives, said that in all schools, the day's work shall begin with community singing of the national song.
