90 porn videos found on ex-JDS MP Prajwal Revanna's phone seized from prison cell

A fresh FIR has been filed after a phone allegedly used by Prajwal Revanna was seized from his prison cell. The recovery has widened scrutiny of prison security even as his conviction and legal challenges continue.

Former Janata Dal (Secular) MP Prajwal Revanna, currently lodged in Bengaluru’s Parappana Agrahara Central Prison in a rape case, has come under fresh scrutiny after investigators allegedly found dozens of pornographic videos on a mobile phone recovered from his jail cell during a recent search operation, Central Crime Branch (CCB) sources told India Today.
Sources said the phone was seized during a raid conducted inside the prison as part of a drive targeting high-profile inmates.
During the subsequent examination of the device, investigators reportedly found between 80 and 90 downloaded pornographic videos.
Most of the content was allegedly Indian pornographic material. Police sources also said that newspaper clippings featuring women in revealing clothes were stored on the phone.

The recovered phone is now being subjected to detailed forensic analysis. Investigators are examining all video files, images and other digital data stored on the device to determine their origin, date of download and possible relevance to ongoing criminal proceedings involving Revanna.

The seizure has already led to administrative action within the prison. The Assistant Superintendent of the jail has been suspended, while a show-cause notice has been issued to the Superintendent of Bengaluru Central Prison.
Besides the mobile phone, officials recovered a pen drive and a charger from the cell. Authorities said no other prohibited items were found during the four-to-five-hour search operation.
Following the recovery, a fresh FIR has been registered. An undertrial prisoner, identified as Pratap Rai, who was lodged in the same prison, has also been named in the case.

The development comes days after the Karnataka High Court rejected Revanna’s plea seeking suspension of his life sentence and interim bail in the first rape case registered against him in Hassan district.

The High Court observed that the gravity of the offence and the pendency of multiple sexual abuse cases weighed against granting him relief. The court also expressed concern that his release could affect witnesses and pending trials.
Revanna was convicted in August 2025 by a special court and sentenced to life imprisonment for repeated sexual assault, voyeurism and destruction of evidence.

The case had drawn national attention after explicit videos allegedly involving him surfaced ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Revanna has consistently denied the allegations and has claimed that the videos were morphed.

His legal team has since approached the Supreme Court seeking transfer of one of the cases to another judge, alleging bias, while his appeal against conviction remains pending before the Karnataka High Court.

With the latest recovery from the prison cell, investigators are expected to focus on the source and use of the mobile phone, the digital material found on it and any possible violations of prison rules.
The forensic examination is likely to play a key role in determining the next course of action in the fresh case registered against Revanna.

Bengaluru: When DK Shivakumar faced his first legislature session as the chief minister of Karnataka on Thursday, there was no woman member in his 33-member cabinet. People aware of the development say different factions of the ruling Congress have been jostling to push their own candidate for the lone ministerial vacancy.

Shivakumar took over the charge of the state from his party colleague on 3 June, with 13 ministers taking oath alongside him. The cabinet expansion took place on 3 August, when 19 new ministers took oath out of 20 initially cleared. Gayatri Shanthegowda did not take oath. Later, it was said her inclusion in the list was a “typing error”.
Shivakumar has stated that the cabinet berth is reserved for a woman.

Although the All India Congress Committee (AICC) was able to reach a consensus on portfolio allocations for the 19 newly inducted ministers, a decision has not yet been reached on which woman legislator will fill the lone remaining seat in Shivakumar cabinet.
“It will take its own time. Now that the (legislature) session is on, we will take a decision after this,” said a senior Congress leader, requesting anonymity.
The Monsoon Session of the state legislature will continue till 27 August.
The leader added that appointing a woman Cabinet member without holding more deliberations will “create more problems”. Every leader, he said, is “naturally pushing for their own candidates”.
Another member, considered close to the chief minister, said there was “no urgency” in filling up the spot.

One of the reasons for the deadlock, it is learnt, is that Shivakumar, Siddaramaiah and national Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge are each pushing for their own candidate to fill the lone vacant cabinet berth.
Meanwhile, Shivakumar’s two-month-old government has come under sharp criticism over the issue.
Nayana Motamma (46), a first-time Congress legislator and MLA from Mudigere in Chikmagaluru district, said the delay in appointing a woman minister is sending out the wrong message.

“Even though I am a legislator who can be considered as an aspirant, I believe that the issue is bigger than me. From a larger picture about women empowerment, reservation, I think it’s really unfortunate and I hope that they (high command) do something about this as soon as possible. Otherwise, this reflects very badly on the party and the message it is giving out,” she told ThePrint.

Data shows that women significantly backed the Congress in the 2023 assembly elections, and the Congress centered its flagship programmes around them—Gruha Lakshmi (Rs 2,000 per month for woman head of household), Gruha Shakthi (free power), Shakthi (free public bus rides for women), Anna Bhagya (free rice scheme), and Yuva Nidhi (financial assistance to job seekers).
The Congress under Rahul Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi have supported reservation for women in state and national assemblies, as well as policies to empower women.

Siddaramaiah has been pushing for the nomination of Basavaraj Neelappa Shivannanavar for the lone remaining berth in the Cabinet, according to people aware of the development.
“We do not have any (woman) candidate. Our demand was to induct Shivannanavar,” said one person from the Siddaramaiah camp, requesting anonymity.
It is believed that earlier Siddaramaiah backed Shanthegowda, who, like himself and Shivakumar, comes from the Kuruba community.
Congress leaders ThePrint spoke to said if some leaders have their way, it could remain an “all-male cabinet”.

Shivakumar backs former women & child development minister Lakshmi Hebbalkar, while some other candidates have been trying to get the attention of the high-command, and the leaders of the respective warring factions.

Apart from facing criticism over no woman member in the Cabinet, the Shivakumar government is also battling public expression of dissent by several leaders, including M. Krishnappa, Tanveer Sait, H.C.Mahadevappa, M.C.Sudhakar, Narayanswamy and several others.

A.S. Ponnanna, the first-time MLA from Virajpet in Kodagu, was nominated as deputy speaker of the assembly, but was later appointed the political secretary to the chief minister. He has served as legal advisor to Siddaramaiah.
Certain communities have also aired their angst over the Cabinet expansion.

Brahmins, for instance, are protesting their exclusion for the first time in the state’s history. Several other smaller communities remain conspicuously absent when it comes to political representation.
When Siddaramaiah was the chief minister, he doled out nearly 150 cabinet ranks to Congress legislators and others to placate dissenting voices. Shivakumar appears to be following suit.
Veteran Congress leader R.V.Deshpande has been appointed the chairman of the reforms committee. Deshpande has been accorded a cabinet rank, as has Ponnanna.
‘Shrinking space for women in cabinet’
The situation is no different in other political parties and in states.

According to an analysis by Business Standard, only one in 10 ministers across Indian states is a woman, reflecting the stark reality of political parties whose platforms–elections and policy–are centred around women empowerment. Out of 608 ministers in 28 states and three Union Territories, only 30 are women.
In Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 72-member council of ministers, only two of
28 cabinet ministers are women: Nirmala Sitharaman and Annapurna Devi.
Out of the 39 ministers who hold minister of state rank, only five are women.

In most states, women are often allocated the Women and Child Development portfolio, with notable exceptions like Vangalapudi Anitha who holds Andhra Pradesh’s home department while S. Keerthana and Santana Chakma, who hold the industries portfolio in Tamil Nadu and Tripura respectively. Gupta and Kumari head the finance departments of their respective states.
According to Business Standard, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Puducherry and Karnataka have no women representation in the Cabinet.
Even within the Congress in Karnataka, most of the front-runners—Lakshmi Hebbalkar, Nayana Motamma, Kaneez Fathima from Kalaburagi, and Annapurana Tukaram—are dynasts, ThePrint reported earlier.
The party has four women legislators—Umashree, Aarthi Krishna, Bilkis Banu and Gayatri Shanthegowda–in the upper house of the state legislature.
Umashree, who was nominated as the deputy chairperson of the legislative council, has made it clear that she prefers a Cabinet role instead.

7 killed, 14 injured after tunnel collapse in Uttarakhand's Chamoli; 1 trapped
A tunnel under construction at the THDC project in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district collapsed, trapping several workers after debris and water entered the site.

Seven workers have died and 14 others were injured after debris and water entered an under-construction hydro tunnel at the THDC project in Mayapur (Pipalkoti) in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Thursday evening. One worker remain trapped inside the tunnel, while 21 of the 22 workers who were inside have been accounted for.
The incident occurred around 6.45 pm when a large volume of debris and water suddenly entered the tunnel being constructed by HCC. Workers from the shift on duty were trapped inside.

Rescue operations were launched immediately after the accident, with teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and other agencies deployed at the site.
Rescue teams are continuing efforts to reach the worker still trapped inside. Machinery is being used to clear debris and drain water from the tunnel.
The injured workers were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment. Officials said those with serious injuries would be shifted to higher medical centres, while others were being treated at Gopeshwar.

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami is monitoring the rescue operation. Earlier, he said several workers had been rescued and that all available resources were being deployed to evacuate those still trapped. He also said he had spoken to the Chief Ministers of Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh regarding the incident.
Chamoli District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar said the incident occurred at the under-construction tunnel of a THDC hydropower project and that rescue teams were working to evacuate the remaining workers.
The administration has mobilised all available machinery and personnel at the site as the rescue operation continues.
A search and rescue operation was launched immediately after the incident.

Rescue teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) are using improvised drum boats to reach them, as the workers are stranded due to debris and water that entered the tunnel. Rescue operations are continuing.
Previously, Chamoli District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar said that 16 workers had been rescued safely until 9 PM, while efforts were continuing to evacuate the remaining people trapped inside the tunnel.

"This is a tunnel under construction for a hydropower project belonging to THDC. Around 6:30 or 6:45 PM, a large volume of debris and water surged into the tunnel. Workers from the shift on duty got trapped inside. NDRF and SDRF teams, along with all our machinery, are currently engaged in operations for the remaining individuals, and we are hopeful that we will be able to rescue everyone within the next few hours," said Kumar.
Given the seriousness of the situation, teams of the Army, Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) were rushed to the site.
Rescue operations are currently being carried out by personnel from the District Incident Response Force (DIRF), local police and the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF).
UTTARAKHAND CM OVERSEES RESCUE ACT
Following the incident, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami had expressed concern and directed authorities to carry out rescue operations on a war footing.

In a statement, the Chief Minister said teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) had been rushed to the site in view of the seriousness of the incident.
He also instructed the district administration and all concerned departments to work in coordination to ensure a swift rescue operation.
Dhami said he was personally monitoring the situation and remained in constant touch with senior officials, receiving regular updates on the rescue efforts.

"The government's top priority is to ensure the safe evacuation of every person trapped inside the tunnel. All necessary resources have been deployed for the rescue operation," the Chief Minister said.
He also directed officials to ensure there was no delay or lapse in the ongoing rescue work and asked the administration to extend all possible assistance to the affected workers and their families.
Authorities are yet to ascertain the cause of the collapse.
Seven workers killed, 14 injured after landslide, water seepage in Chamoli tunnel
The incident occurred around 7 pm inside a tunnel of the Tehri Hydro Development Corporation (THDC)-owned Vishnugad-Pipalkoti Hydroelectric Project.

Dehradun: Seven workers were killed and 14 others injured after a landslide and heavy water seepage triggered a partial collapse inside an under-construction THDC tunnel at Mayapur near Pipalkoti in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district on Thursday evening.

The incident occurred around 7 pm inside a tunnel of the Tehri Hydro Development Corporation (THDC)-owned Vishnugad-Pipalkoti Hydroelectric Project, where construction work was being carried out by HCC, according to officials.
According to State Emergency Operations Centre (SEOC) officials, 22 workers were trapped inside the tunnel following the sudden landslide and water seepage.

A large-scale multi-agency rescue operation was launched immediately. By 11 pm, 21 workers were evacuated from the tunnel. Seven of them were declared dead, while 14 others were injured and shifted for medical treatment, officials said.

The rescue operation is being undertaken by 57 personnel from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), 42 from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), 21 from the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), 22 from local police stations and outposts, nine fire service personnel and four personnel from the District Disaster Response Force (DDRF).
Senior officials are at the site and supervising the relief and rescue operation. HCC machinery and specialised equipment were also deployed to clear debris and assist the rescue teams.

The injured workers were initially taken to the district hospital in Gopeshwar for treatment. The administration also placed Base Hospital Srinagar and AIIMS Rishikesh on alert to deal with any critically injured workers who might require advanced medical care.

With hours left, Parliament heads for a tense Monsoon Session finish

Amit Shah offered a marathon debate on the student protests, but Rahul Gandhi demanded a direct answer on who ordered the police action, leaving Parliament deadlocked as the Monsoon Session entered its final day.

Parliament’s Monsoon Session will enter its final day on Thursday with the government and Opposition still locked in a standoff over the student protests, after Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s offer of an extended debate failed to break the deadlock in the Lok Sabha.

Shah offered to participate in a detailed discussion on the protests and allegations of police action against students. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, however, rejected the proposal, saying the Opposition wanted a direct answer on who ordered the use of pellet guns and force against protesters rather than a “lecture” from the Home Minister.
The Lok Sabha was eventually adjourned for the day amid sloganeering despite repeated appeals from the government to allow the discussion.
AMIT SHAH OFFERS EXTENDED DEBATE
The confrontation began soon after the Lok Sabha assembled at 11 am on Wednesday.
Shah said the government was ready to discuss all issues concerning the student protests and asked the Opposition to submit a written request to Speaker Om Birla.
He offered to begin the discussion at 3 pm on Wednesday and continue it until 3 pm on Thursday.
“Even today, I say that they should submit a letter to the Speaker by 2 pm. We are ready for all kinds of discussions from 3 pm today until 3 pm tomorrow,” Shah said.
He later wrote to the Speaker, saying he was prepared to remain present throughout the debate and respond to questions raised by the Opposition.
Shah said dialogue and discussion were the only ways to resolve issues in a democracy and maintained that the government had nothing to hide.
The Opposition, however, did not accept the offer.
‘IF HE ORDERED IT, HE SHOULD RESIGN’
Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition was not interested in listening to what he described as Shah’s “imagination” or a lengthy lecture.
He said young people wanted to know who ordered the use of pellet guns, lathi charges and other force against protesting students.
“If Mr Amit Shah gave the order to shoot our children, he should resign because he is culpable, and if he did not, he should resign because he is incompetent,” Gandhi said.
He argued that the Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force come under the Home Ministry and questioned Shah’s responsibility for the alleged police action.
Gandhi later posted a video of his remarks on X, saying Shah’s silence amounted to a “confession”.
Congress deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi also questioned why the Home Minister had not participated in an earlier proposed discussion on education and student protests.
He said Shah should make a statement in Parliament on the police action against protesters and allegations surrounding the use of AK-47s in Bihar.
GOVERNMENT ACCUSES OPPOSITION OF AVOIDING DEBATE
The government, in turn, accused the Opposition of refusing the very discussion it had been demanding.

When the Lok Sabha met again at 3 pm after two adjournments, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the government was ready to begin the debate immediately and pointed out that Shah had already written to the Speaker.
He urged the Opposition not to “run away” when the Home Minister was prepared to answer its questions.
Presiding officer Jagdambika Pal also repeatedly appealed to Opposition members to allow proceedings to continue, but protests and sloganeering persisted.
The House was eventually adjourned for the day.
Rijiju later called it “unthinkable and incomprehensible” that the Opposition was refusing a discussion when the government had agreed to one.
WHY THE STUDENT ROW HAS DOMINATED THE SESSION
The student protests have emerged as one of the main flashpoints of the Monsoon Session.
The Opposition has demanded accountability over police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak, including allegations of pellet gun use, lathi charges and tear gas at Jantar Mantar.
Congress has also repeatedly sought statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Shah.
The government has maintained that it is willing to discuss the issue, but disagreement over the scope and nature of the debate has repeatedly disrupted proceedings.
With the session ending on Thursday, there has been no breakthrough so far.
Even as the student row kept Parliament on edge, the government managed to move ahead on several pieces of legislative business.

The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday adopted a motion referring the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee. The Lok Sabha had already approved the referral.
The JPC will comprise 21 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha and has been asked to submit its report by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session.

Introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25, the Bill proposes tighter oversight of foreign contributions received by NGOs and other organisations. It also provides for a designated authority to manage and dispose of assets if an organisation loses its FCRA licence.
The Opposition has opposed the legislation, alleging that some provisions could affect legitimate foreign funding for Christian NGOs and minority-run social welfare and educational institutions.
The government has rejected the charge, saying the Bill is not religion-specific and is aimed at regulating foreign contributions.

Congress MP KC Venugopal demanded that the legislation be withdrawn, while Rijiju pointed out that Opposition parties had themselves sought its examination by a parliamentary committee and urged them to raise their objections before the JPC.
Parliament also cleared legislation to officially change Kerala’s name to Keralam.
The Rajya Sabha passed the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, by voice vote on Wednesday, a day after it was cleared by the Lok Sabha.
The move follows a resolution passed by the Kerala Assembly in 2024 urging the Centre to change the state’s name.
The Bill provides for the alteration of the name and consequential amendments to the Constitution, including the First Schedule.
RAJYA SABHA CLEARS NCDC AMENDMENT BILL
The Rajya Sabha also passed the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, a day after it cleared the Lok Sabha.
The legislation expands the powers of the National Cooperative Development Corporation, allowing it to provide loans and grants directly to cooperative societies.

The NCDC, a statutory organisation under the Ministry of Cooperation, will also be allowed, with prior approval from the Centre, to participate in the share capital of cooperatives and other entities involved in cooperative development.
The changes are aimed at widening the channels through which financial assistance can reach the cooperative sector.
FINAL DAY, STUDENT PROTEST ROW STILL UNRESOLVED

The Monsoon Session began with the Opposition raising the NEET paper leak and alleged irregularities involving donations to the Ram temple in Ayodhya, before the political focus shifted sharply to police action against protesting students.
The issue has since dominated proceedings and contributed to repeated adjournments.
The government’s last-minute offer of an extended discussion on Wednesday failed to end the impasse.
The Lok Sabha will meet again at 11 am on Thursday for the final scheduled day of the session, leaving only a narrow window for the two sides to find common ground.

For now, the government says it is ready to debate. The Opposition says it first wants a direct answer on accountability. That divide remains unresolved as the Monsoon Session heads into its final day.

Former MP Prajwal Revanna, serving a life sentence in a rape case, lived apart from the ordinary prison population at Parappana Agrahara Central Jail in Bengaluru for two years. That cosy arrangement has been snapped.

The arrangement was not for a separate category of criminals entitled to such privileges; rather, allegations of preferential treatment have repeatedly centred on influential inmates living in the so-called “VIP cell”.

The move means Revanna will now live alongside 20 other prisoners and share a single toilet. He has also been ordered to wear the prescribed prison uniform and report for work in the jail library, according to a senior home department official.

“His earlier accommodation was shared with undertrial prisoner Pratap Roy, arrested in a POCSO case. Roy was described as being like an assistant to Revanna,” the officer, who asked not to be named, said.

“Despite all this security, how did a mobile phone get into the jail? We will investigate whether the officials were involved in this. If the officials were involved, who brought the phone to Prajwal Revanna? How long has he been using the mobile phone? We have also been instructed to find out who is involved in this,” Alok Kumar said.

DGP says Revanna was warned earlier

The DGP said authorities had previously warned Revanna about prison rules. He also said a search of actor Darshan’s cell had found no mobile phone or other devices. “We had warned Prajwal Revanna in advance. We also searched actor Darshan’s cell and no mobile or other devices were found,” he said.

The phone discovery has raised questions about security inside Parappana Agrahara, where jammers have been installed around the prison. Alok Kumar said mobile SIM cards, including Airtel cards issued in Andhra Pradesh, had nevertheless been found inside the jail.

“Airtel company SIMs are being used inside the jail. Especially, Airtel SIMs from Andhra Pradesh have been found, despite many warnings about this, the SIMs are being found. Therefore, an investigation has been conducted into this matter and a report has been submitted,” he said.

Priyank Kharge promises action

Home minister Priyank Kharge said the investigation would determine who was responsible and that action would not depend on an officer’s rank. “Whoever the officer is, action will be taken against him. Whether he is a PC, PSI or ADG, there is no difference,” Kharge said.

“Action should be taken when inappropriate activities take place in prisons. The viral Prajwal video is a bit old, so it is not possible to say who did it, who gave it, or what it was given. But action will be taken against anyone who cooperated,” Kharge said, adding: “No one, from constables to IPS, will be protected in my time.”
HD Revanna puts responsibility on Home Department

Prajwal’s farther and JD(S) leader, H.D. Revanna, asked about the discovery outside Vidhana Soudha, put the responsibility on the state Home Department. “The responsibility of the Home Department lies with Priyank Kharge. His party is in power. Let him conduct the investigation himself,” he said.

Revanna, 36, represented Hassan in the Lok Sabha from 2019 to 2023. He was convicted in August 2025 by the Special Court for People’s Representatives for raping a dometic worker at a farmhouse in Holenarasipura, Hassan district.

“It will be conducted concurrently with training at the Gurugram academy, post flight at our Flight Briefing Centres / Air India Offices, or at locations provided by your respective bases,” the internal communication added.
Full pilot screening begins across Air India group
Air India and Air India Express together have around 5,000 pilots.

The move follows an August 4 incident involving Air India flight AI2379, an Airbus A320neo flying from Phuket to Delhi, which suddenly lost about 300 feet in altitude during cruise. While the case is being investigated by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), the pilot-in-command tested positive for marijuana in an initial, and a second confirmatory, test early this week. A preliminary defect report prepared by the pilots suggested the incident was preceded by multiple technical glitches, including an autopilot disconnection.
Also read: Air India pilot who tested positive for marijuana slept 30-35 minutes during Phuket-Delhi flight
Government weighs stricter drug-testing rules

Meanwhile, people aware of the matter said the government is planning to amend the drug-testing rules for aviation personnel. “The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) will review the existing civil aviation requirements (CAR) on testing for psychoactive substances, with a possible increase in random testing and stronger penalties under the revised framework,” one of the people said, requesting anonymity.

The current CAR, effective since January 2022, requires scheduled commercial airlines, air traffic controllers, flight training organisations and air navigation service providers to conduct random drug tests covering at least 10% of employees annually. The rules also provide for removal from safety-sensitive duties following a non-negative screening result.

India mandates pilots to undergo breath analyser test for alcohol before and after the flight. “The government may look at similar rules for drug testing. The random testing module can also be increased,” a second person said. “While the discussions have just begun, the amendments to the CAR may also look at placing greater responsibility on airlines for ensuring compliance with drug-testing requirements.”

New Delhi: At least half of the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) office-bearers, including those in its national working committee, have had some past association with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). Asked by ThePrint about his past association with the AAP, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said he was a part of the party but has no connection with it anymore.

Dipke’s AAP link has now come back into focus after the CJP released the list of its national working committee. Of the 12 members inducted into the CJP’s core team, six were either directly associated with the AAP or supported it publicly.

AAP spokesperson Sanjeev Jha acknowledged that some of those associated with the CJP had links with the party in the past, but maintained that they had since moved on, and there had been no recent contact. “Yes, there was a link, but no more. They were with the AAP, but recently there was no contact. They went their own ways to find jobs or study.”
ThePrint tracks the CJP core team’s past association with the AAP.
Also Read: Abhijeet Dipke launches new CJP campaign—‘School Thik Karo’ for ‘neglected’ govt schools
Abhijeet Dipke (CJP founder): In 2020, Dipke joined the Aam Aadmi Party’s social media team, where he said he developed a style of political messaging built around memes, humour and satire.
His experience with the AAP also gave Dipke early grounding in using social media as a political communication tool—something that later became central to the CJP.

In 2023, Dipke moved to the United States to pursue a master’s degree in public relations in Boston, but continued to follow Indian politics closely. He launched the CJP in May this year and returned to India.

The familiarity between Arvind Kejriwal and Dipke was visible when the former Delhi chief minister visited the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar. The two hugged when they met. AAP sources, however, said the party had extended support to the CJP agitation beyond what was publicly visible, including through volunteers, food and other basic amenities.

Ashutosh Ranka (CJP co-convener): Ranka was an AAP volunteer in Rajasthan. He wrote opinion pieces, participated in TV debates wearing the AAP cap. He has maintained that he was never officially a spokesperson of the party, but said he was volunteering for the AAP and had communicated to the party that he was no longer associated with it.

He met Deepak Baliyan, another member of the CJP’s national working committee, while the latter was organising a protest in Jaipur. In March 2026, Ranka wrote an editorial for ThePrint titled ‘AAP liquor case points to what is missing in India: Accountability’.

Ajinkya Shinde (CJP organisation in-charge): Shinde’s appointment as the CJP’s organisation in-charge raised questions, as his social media pages continue to carry his past affiliation with the AAP, listing him as ‘Ex-Convener – AAP Youth Wing (AYW), Maharashtra’ and ‘Sah Prabhari AAP, Goa’.
His Instagram profile, @ajinkyashinde_aap, is now unavailable. His Facebook page has also been deactivated.
BJP leader Amit Malviya also took a swipe at Shinde’s appointment, posting his photograph with Kejriwal.

Vijay Reddy Malangi (media lead and South zone head): In an interview with local YouTube channel Kranthi TV in November 2025, Malangi was introduced as a spokesperson and leader of the Aam Aadmi Party from Telangana. When ThePrint went through his Facebook profile, it found several posts shared by him in support of the AAP.
In some of them, he was seen wearing the AAP sash and the ‘Anna topi (cap)’.

Malangi also shared a statement criticising Raghav Chadha and the other six AAP parliamentarians who switched to the BJP. He did not comment on his affiliation when reached out via call and text message.

Ankit Bhardwaj (in charge, East and Northeast zones): A 12 May 2017 report in the Hindustan Times identified Bhardwaj as an AAP volunteer associated with the party since 2014, and that he had put his chartered accountancy work on the backburner to work for the party. According to news reports from 2017, he had allegedly attacked Kapil Mishra while the politician, by then sacked as a minister by Kejriwal, was sitting on dharna.

A video available on YouTube, titled “Ankit Bhardwaj ke 2 shabd Kapil Mishra jaise dokhebaazon ke liye (Ankit Bhardwaj’s comments on traitors like Kapil Mishra)”, shows him speaking in support of the Aam Aadmi Party. In the video, he addresses AAP volunteers and says: “Main apne Aam Aadmi Party ke saathiyon ko ek baat kehna chahta hoon; niraash mat hona, hum aaj bhi vohi party hai jo 3 saal pehle thi, ye party bauhat aage jaayegi.”
(I want to tell my fellow Aam Aadmi Party members one thing: do not be disappointed. We are still the same party that we were three years ago, and this party will go very far.)

According to the Delhi Police, as reported by Hindustan Times, Bhardwaj had gone to meet Mishra to question him over his criticism of the AAP and Arvind Kejriwal. Mishra and his supporters alleged that Bhardwaj had attacked him. Bhardwaj, however, told the police that he had only been gesturing with his hands during the argument and denied hitting Mishra.
Saurav Das (co-convener): Das is an investigative journalist who frequently tweeted and retweeted content in support of the Aam Aadmi Party and its leaders.
His admiration for Arvind Kejriwal and several AAP leaders was visible through his social media activity, leading to questions about his political leanings.
Also Read: Abhijeet Dipke launches new CJP campaign—‘School Thik Karo’ for ‘neglected’ govt schools
As of now, the CJP calls itself a pressure group and has continued to reiterate that it does not intend to enter electoral politics.

Political analyst and Delhi University professor of political science Chandrachud Singh told ThePrint that the overlap between the two organisations was not surprising given the similarity in their style of politics and Dipke’s own past association with the AAP.

“The fact of the matter is that the Aam Aadmi Party is also kind of something which does this kind of educational politics, right? And agitation politics and the politics of the street, in the way that was done during the Anna movement. AAP is known for this,” he said.

Adding, “The fact that Dipke himself came from that party means that he must be having some connects and some contacts in the party. So there would be people who might be sulking in the AAP or may not be in the mainstream of its organisation. Therefore, Dipke will offer them some chances, and they will be happy to grab those opportunities.”

Singh also said, “It is very clear that the CJP did get support, and you would see that some of the early political leaders who went and met him, I think Kejriwal was one of those, isn’t it? And not only Kejriwal, but I think other members of his party were also there.”

“The bonhomie between the Aam Aadmi Party and the leadership of CJP — the CJP in itself, the organisational part, is quite closer to the AAP and therefore there would be a movement to and fro. I don’t see that not happening,” he added.
Former AAP spokesperson Ashutosh, meanwhile, said the members who had previously been associated with the party should be seen as having made a break with it.

“Since they have decided to form CJP and become its office-bearers, that means they are having a clean break from the AAP and are not happy with the way the AAP is working. They may have had some idealism and hope in the AAP, but over a period of time they felt disillusioned with the party and the political establishment. However, it would be wrong to understand CJP as being launched or propelled by the AAP,” he told ThePrint.
AAP spokesperson Sanjeev Jha, too, acknowledged that some CJP members had previously been associated with the party, but said they had since moved on.
“Yes, there was a link, but no more. They were with the AAP, but recently there was no contact. They went their own ways to find jobs or study,” Jha said.
The other members of the CJP’s 12-member core team come from varied professional and activist backgrounds.

Deepak Baliyan (organisation co-in charge and North zone head): A political science post-graduate from Alwar, Rajasthan, and has been involved in agrarian movements. He was also involved in organising the CJP’s Jaipur protest and had met Ashutosh Ranka while organising a protest in the city.
Aafreen Nawaz (national secretary): A Bengaluru-based entrepreneur with an MBA who left the corporate sector to work on issues concerning students and young people.
Ratna Singh (legal affairs): A lawyer from Lucknow who has been one of the CJP’s more visible faces, particularly on legal issues involving protesters.

Vaishnavi Gaur (research & policy lead): A lawyer from Dehradun who has emerged as one of the CJP’s prominent spokespersons, regularly speaking about the organisation’s demands and responding to criticism of the movement.
Rohan Deshpande (technology lead): Based in Mumbai, he has a background in hotel management from IHM Mumbai. He has also written on political and social issues.

India and Bangladesh are in talks for an early bilateral visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to New Delhi, preferably before the end of this month or the first week of September, to help in full normalisation of relations. Officials hoped that the early visit would pave the way for the renewal of the Ganga waters treaty, energy deals and removal of the trade restrictions that were imposed in May 2025 on Bangladesh.

Diplomatic sources expressed cautious optimism, saying that “positive developments” can take place quickly in the coming few days. Sources in Dhaka expressed satisfaction over the ongoing exchanges between the two sides but cautioned that continued activities by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina or her party Awami League from India have the potential to cast a shadow on fresh initiatives. Sources here also said normalisation will have to be achieved as soon as possible as the diplomatic window may close soon because of other visits and commitments that are being scheduled for the Indian leadership in the remaining four months of the year.

The exchanges between the Indian and Bangladeshi sides began last Monday (August 10, 2026) when High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi called on Mr. Rahman at the Secretariat in Dhaka. The meeting took place against the backdrop of tension generated by the virtual press conference that was addressed by Ms. Hasina and her son Sajeeb Wazed Joy at the Foreign Correspondents Club in New Delhi on August 5, 2026. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bangladesh said it was “outraged” by Ms. Hasina’s press conference and described the event as an “afront” to the “sovereignty of Bangladesh”.

A day earlier on August 9, Bangladesh hosted a delegation led by Parag Jain, Secretary, Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW), the external intelligence wing of the Government of India. In response to Bangladesh’s remarks, the Ministry of External Affairs distanced itself from Ms. Hasina’s event and said India did not “endorse” the remarks that were made at the event against the “duly constituted government of Bangladesh”. The Ministry’s Official Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal further clarified that alongside the invite to Mr. Rahman for the BRICS meeting, India had extended an invite for a bilateral visit on February 17, 2026. This bilateral invite was further acknowledged by Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman on August 10, 2026 after Mr. Trivedi met Mr. Rahman.

Subsequently, Mr. Trivedi visited Delhi and briefed Prime Minister Narendra Modi during Tuesday evening. It has been learnt by The Hindu that the Indian side has conveyed that an “early bilateral visit preferably before the end of the month” will ensure full normalisation of India-Bangladesh ties, including “addressing the water-related issue, energy agreements, visa facilities, and lifting of restrictive measures that were imposed on the textile and food processing sectors of Bangladesh in May 2025”.

It was also communicated to the Rahman government that “if you get stuck with Hasina, you will miss the bus.” It is understood that there has been greater interest of Bangladesh in a bilateral visit for Mr. Rahman and not so much for a participation in the BRICS summit as Bangladesh is not a member of the BRICS and as a result, Mr. Rahman is unlikely to feature in the main round table meet of the leaders of the member countries. Diplomatic sources, however, cautioned that a fresh meeting by members of Ms. Hasina’s Awami League is also being planned by the end of this month in Delhi and suggested that it could hurt positive trend in the talks.

Bangladesh, one of the largest trading partners of India in the neighbourhood, has had a prolonged spell of cold relation with India since the fall of the Hasina government on August 5, 2024. India had reached out to Mr. Rahman on February 17 when he was sworn in after winning the February 12 election with a landslide majority. Subsequently, Mr. Rahman has remained occupied domestically with a worsening energy situation that coincided with the Gulf crisis, a measles crisis that has killed hundreds of infants, and tough challenge from the Jamaat-e-Islami that is leading the Opposition bloc in the Parliament in Dhaka. Bangladesh will elect a new President on August 20 and seniormost Cabinet member Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, the choice of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party, is expected to be the new President. Mr. Rahman is likely to have a few days after that during which a visit could be scheduled.

Sonam Wangchuk seeks 'peaceful revolution' to reshape India's politics
Sonam Wangchuk has called for a peaceful revolution in how India chooses its political leaders. He said the shift is necessary if India is to emerge as a developed nation by 2047.

Climate activist and education reformer Sonam Wangchuk has called for a “peaceful revolution” in India, arguing that the country needs a fundamental change in the way it chooses its political leaders if it is to emerge as a developed nation by 2047.

In a video message posted ahead of Independence Day, Wangchuk said he had been reflecting on India’s future and was increasingly disappointed by India’s progress compared with several countries in the region.
“Fifty years ago, countries that were behind us or at par with us are today miles ahead of us,” he said, citing Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh in terms of per capita GDP.
Wangchuk warned that if the current trajectory continued, India could struggle to hold its place in the global economy by 2047, the centenary of its Independence.

He also praised people who had recently taken to the streets demanding change, saying their protests had already resulted in the resignation of the education minister. However, he said the appointment of a new education minister had not yet brought any visible transformation.
“As long as education remains backward, the future of the country will also remain backward,” Wangchuk said.
NOT ABOUT ANY ONE POLITICAL PARTY

Wangchuk said the problem extended beyond any particular political party. Referring to protests and government action in different states, he argued that governments across the political spectrum had been accused of silencing voices raised against injustice.
He recalled the anti-corruption movement of 2012-13, which led to a change in government in Delhi, but said corruption and injustice had returned in a different form.
“Now, 12 years later, corruption and injustice have changed their route, but are staring at us, frightening us, in a form two or three times bigger,” he said.
Wangchuk said India therefore needed a “very big change”, which he described as a “peaceful revolution”.
FOCUS ON HOW POLITICAL LEADERS ARE CHOSEN
The activist said the biggest weakness in India’s political system was the way leaders were selected.
“If the leaders are not right, the whole country goes in the wrong direction,” he said.

Wangchuk acknowledged that there were politicians who followed principles and worked with honesty, saying he saluted such leaders. But he questioned how India could become a developed country when many lawmakers face criminal cases.

He claimed that nearly half of India’s MPs face criminal cases and around a third face serious allegations, including murder, rape and kidnapping. He stressed that he was not targeting any particular party or the ruling or opposition camp, but was speaking about the country as a whole.
SEEKS NAMES OF SELFLESS INDIANS
Wangchuk said he now wanted to bring together some of the country’s “best minds” to seek ideas and advice on how India could move towards a new political system.
But he said he was not looking merely for intellectuals.
“I want to meet people who are selfless, who have character and who follow principles,” he said.
Wangchuk, who is currently in Ladakh, appealed to people across India to suggest names of individuals they believe possess these qualities and could help create a “new map” for the country’s future.
He also said he wanted to travel to different states and cities to seek suggestions directly from people.
Wangchuk ended his message by wishing people on Independence Day and appealing for their help in building what he described as a peaceful transformation of India.
“Give me the best gift this Independence Day by suggesting such names,” he said.

Netflix, Instagram, WhatsApp and Prime Video were among applications found on a mobile phone seized from former MP Prajwal Revanna during a Central Crime Branch raid at Parappana Agrahara Central Prison, where he is serving a life sentence.

The applications were installed on a light blue Redmi 5G handset recovered from Room 4 on the first floor of Security Section 3 during a search conducted between 2 pm and 9 pm on Tuesday. He said similar searches would be conducted across the state. “Whether it is Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Bengaluru or any other prison, we will take strict action. We will keep doing this,” said the minister.

He said officials continuing to follow “old practices” would be identified and face legal action. If any official was found involved in criminal activity, the government would consider dismissal from service.

as India enters its 80th year as an independent nation, what does the world think of it?

Kenya and the United Kingdom rank alongside Sri Lanka among the countries most positive towards India, with roughly seven in 10 adults expressing favourable views.Majorities in Germany, Israel, Italy, Sweden, Japan and Thailand also see India positively.In contrast, Latin American publics express mixed-to-negative views, alongside substantial shares of respondents who offer no opinion.The findings suggest that India's global image is not simply a reflection of its diplomatic alliances.Economic ties, strategic partnerships, cultural familiarity and perceptions of India's growing global role all appear to shape how people view the country.
The bigger story is perhaps not where India stands today, but how its image has changed.In most countries surveyed, opinions have remained relatively stable since Pew last asked the question.

But in 10 countries, the change has been statistically significant â and in seven of them, India's favourability has fallen.Turkey and Nigeria have recorded the sharpest declines since 2025, with the share of people expressing a favourable opinion of India falling by 10 percentage points in both countries.India has also lost ground in the United States, Indonesia, South Africa and Mexico.The decline is particularly striking in Bangladesh.Pew's previous survey there was conducted in 2024.

Since then, the share of Bangladeshis with a favourable opinion of India has fallen by 15 percentage points, leaving fewer than half with a positive view.At the same time, the number of Bangladeshis who do not express an opinion has also fallen sharply, from 24% to just 7%.

In other words, more Bangladeshis now appear to have a defined opinion of India â and that opinion has become considerably less favourable.The trend is not uniformly negative, however.India's image has improved significantly in Germany, Britain and Sri Lanka.The share of Britons with a favourable opinion of India has risen 11 points since 2025, while Germany has recorded a six-point increase.

Sri Lanka has seen an even bigger jump, with favourability rising 14 points since 2024.Looking further back to 2023 reveals another interesting divide.Across several European countries, India's image has strengthened substantially since the first post-pandemic survey. In Germany, for example, only 47% had a favourable opinion of India in 2023. That figure has now climbed to 63%.France has followed a similar trajectory. India's favourability there has risen from 39% in 2023 to 50% today.Outside Europe, however, the picture is less encouraging.South Korea is one example.

In 2023, 59% of South Koreans viewed India favourably. Today, that figure has dropped to 44%.Latin America also tends to lean more negative, although large numbers of people in several European and Latin American countries do not express an opinion at all.

India's global image is also shaped by domestic political ideology in some countries.The United States and Canada show a striking pattern: people on the political left are more likely than conservatives to view India favourably.In the US, 54% of liberals express a positive opinion of India, compared with 40% of conservatives. What have I done?: Jinnah reportedly struck his forehead after seeing refugees

Kuldip Nayar recounts a reported moment when Muhammad Ali Jinnah saw Partition's refugee columns from the air. The anecdote and Nayar's own memories highlight the scale of loss, fear and displacement in 1947.

As Partition tore through the subcontinent in 1947, millions were forced to flee across a newly drawn border amid communal violence, killings and looting. It was in this backdrop that Pakistan founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah, after reportedly seeing streams of people moving across a divided Punjab from the air, struck his forehead and said in despair, "What have I done?"

The episode is recounted by journalist and author Kuldip Nayar in his autobiography Beyond the Lines. Nayar also records his own memories of violence and fear while leaving his ancestral home in Sialkot for Delhi, offering another account of the upheaval that accompanied Partition.

Nayar writes that when Jinnah was in Lahore, Pakistan's rehabilitation minister Iftikhar-ud-din and Pakistan Times editor Mazhar Ali Khan flew him in a Dakota aircraft over the divided Punjab. "When he saw streams of people pouring into Pakistan or fleeing it, he struck his hand on the forehead and said despairingly: 'What have I done?'" Nayar wrote. According to the author, both Iftikhar and Mazhar had vowed not to repeat the remark. Nayar says Mazhar later confided in his wife Tahira, who in turn told Nayar about Jinnah's comment long after her husband's death.

Nayar says the remark came at a time when the scale of the human tragedy linked to Partition was becoming increasingly visible. He writes that Jinnah had initially not believed reports that thousands of people were migrating from both sides of the border. Both the Congress and the Muslim League had rejected the proposal for an exchange of population and had insisted that Muslims and non-Muslims remain in their homes. However, escalating violence led to a massive movement of people across the newly carved borders at Wagah and Attari.

Recalling his own journey, Nayar writes of the devastation he saw while approaching Wagah. "I saw corpses lying on both sides of the road and empty suitcases and bags which bore testimony to the looting that had taken place either before or after the killing," he says. He also remembered the fear as they neared the border, writing, "There was nervousness as we neared Wagah."

Together, the two accounts recorded by Nayar — Jinnah seeing displaced people from the air and Nayar witnessing bodies and abandoned belongings on the road — underline the scale of suffering during Partition. August 14 is observed in India as Partition Horrors Remembrance Day to remember the loss of lives, displacement and suffering caused by Partition and the communal violence that accompanied the division of the subcontinent.
‘What have I done?’: When Jinnah confronted Partition’s horrors from the skies over Punjab
As India marks its 80th Independence Day, the story of Partition remains inseparable from the birth of India & Pakistan -- and the crores displaced by violence.

From thousands of feet above the fractured landscape of Punjab, Muhammad Ali Jinnah saw the human cost of Partition unfold beneath him. In August 1947, from the window of a Dakota aircraft, he reportedly watched endless columns of men, women and children making their way along dusty roads.
Some were fleeing west, others east. Along the routes lay unburied bodies, abandoned trunks, broken carts and the remains of homes destroyed in communal violence.

The sight deeply affected Jinnah, according to an account recorded by veteran journalist and author Kuldip Nayar in his autobiography Beyond the Lines. “What have I done?” the Pakistan founder reportedly struck his forehead and said in despair as he looked down at the streams of displaced people.

Nayar wrote that Jinnah was flown over divided Punjab by Pakistan's rehabilitation minister Iftikhar-ud-din and Pakistan Times editor Mazhar Ali Khan. Both reportedly decided not to repeat Jinnah's words. Mazhar later told his wife, Tahira, who eventually shared the account with Nayar.
“When he saw streams of people pouring into Pakistan or fleeing it, he struck his hand on the forehead and said despairingly: 'What have I done?'” Nayar wrote.
Estimates of those killed during Partition range from several lakh to around 10 lakh, while more than 1.5 crore people were displaced in one of the largest mass migrations in modern history.

Nayar himself was among those caught in the upheaval. Travelling from his ancestral home in Sialkot towards Delhi, he recalled seeing corpses along the road and abandoned luggage left behind after looting.

“I saw corpses lying on both sides of the road and empty suitcases and bags which bore testimony to the looting that had taken place either before or after the killing,” he wrote. “There was nervousness as we neared Wagah.”
How British-India broke into two

The Partition of British India was not caused by one decision or one leader. It followed decades of political disagreements, British policies, communal tensions and the growing rivalry between the Indian National Congress and the All-India Muslim League.

At the centre of the demand for Pakistan stood Jinnah, the leader of the Muslim League. But Jinnah had not always demanded a separate country. Jinnah initially supported Hindu-Muslim cooperation and worked with both Congress and the Muslim League.

The political environment, though, changed considerably during the first half of the 20th century. British constitutional reforms introduced separate electorates for different communities, helping institutionalise communal political representation. The Muslim League, founded in 1906, increasingly presented itself as the principal political organisation representing Muslim interests.
There were also periods of cooperation. The 1916 Lucknow Pact brought Congress and the Muslim League together on constitutional demands.

That did not last. The provincial elections of 1937 became an important turning point. Congress was the dominant political force in several provinces, while the Muslim League did not perform as strongly as Jinnah expected.

Jinnah increasingly feared that Muslims could become politically vulnerable in a united India dominated by a strong central government. By the 1940s, he moved towards the demand that Muslims be treated as a separate political nation.
At its Lahore session in March 1940, the Muslim League adopted the Lahore Resolution, calling for independent political units in Muslim-majority areas of north-western and eastern India.
The resolution did not use the word “Pakistan”, but it turned the idea of a separate Muslim homeland into the League's central political demand.
The 1945-46 elections then gave support Jinnah's position. The Muslim League won most of the Muslim seats, allowing Jinnah to claim that the League had a mandate to speak for Muslim voters.
The last attempt to keep India united
Britain's Cabinet Mission arrived in 1946 with a plan to keep India united while giving provinces considerable autonomy.
Congress and the Muslim League initially accepted the proposal but disagreed over how the provinces would be grouped and how much power the central government would have.
The compromise collapsed and the political crisis soon spilled into the streets.
The Muslim League called August 16, 1946, Direct Action Day. Calcutta witnessed days of communal violence, followed by violence in Noakhali, Bihar and Punjab.
By 1947, the political dispute had become inseparable from communal violence.

When Lord Louis Mountbatten became Viceroy in 1947, Britain decided to accelerate its withdrawal.
On June 3, Mountbatten announced a plan to transfer power to two new Dominions - India and Pakistan.
Punjab and Bengal, both divided between large Muslim and non-Muslim populations, would themselves be partitioned.

British lawyer Sir Cyril Radcliffe was given only weeks to draw the new boundaries. The Radcliffe Line divided Punjab and Bengal, but the borders were publicly announced only on August 17, two days after India's independence. For many people, independence came before they knew which country their homes would belong to.
Pakistan became independent on August 14, 1947, with Jinnah as its first Governor-General.
India became independent on August 15, with Jawaharlal Nehru as its first Prime Minister.

But independence came with a massive humanitarian crisis. Millions of Hindus and Sikhs moved from areas that became Pakistan towards India, while millions of Muslims moved in the opposite direction. Villages were emptied, homes were abandoned and families were separated.

The violence included killings, looting, abductions and sexual violence. Estimates of the death toll vary, with some historical estimates reaching around 10 lakhs. The number of displaced people ran into crores.
Punjab suffered some of the worst violence. Refugee trains crossed the new border as people fled in search of safety.
Jinnah got Pakistan, but not the Pakistan he wanted
Jinnah achieved his primary objective: Pakistan was created. But the country was not formed as he had envisioned.

Punjab and Bengal were divided, despite Jinnah's opposition to their partition. Pakistan also then sorted itself into two geographically separate wings -- West Pakistan and East Pakistan, with over 2,000 km of Indian territory between them.
East Pakistan later became Bangladesh in 1971.

Cockroaches, expired food: Maharashtra FDA suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 14, 2026, 22:56 IST
Inspections uncovered violations ranging from cockroach infestation and expired food to poor hygiene and storage practices.

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 14 food business establishments linked to quick-commerce platforms Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after a statewide inspection drive uncovered multiple food safety and hygiene violations.The August 13 drive covered 86 establishments across Maharashtra involved in the storage, sale and delivery of food through online platforms.

The FDA issued 60 improvement notices and ordered one facility to temporarily halt operations, news agency PTI reported.Of the 14 suspended licences, five were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto, two to Instamart, while one each belonged to Bhagwati Stores and Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd.The inspections focused on storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest management, personal hygiene of food handlers, food safety records, display of licences and compliance with inventory practices such as First In, First Out (FIFO) and First Expired, First Out (FEFO).In Pune, the FDA suspended the licence of a Zepto outlet in Lohegaon after inspectors found food items stored beyond their declared "use by" dates.

The regulator also flagged unhygienic storage conditions, inadequate pest control and lapses in personal hygiene, adding that the company's response during the hearing was unsatisfactory.Another Pune facility operated by Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd was found to have a cockroach infestation, inadequate cold-chain maintenance for frozen products and deficiencies in hygiene and pest-control practices.In Mumbai, a Blinkit facility in Malad (West) was found to be operating with chiller temperatures above the prescribed limit.

Inspectors also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone mandatory medical examinations and that records were unavailable.The FDA said several workers were not using protective gear such as gloves, aprons and head coverings. Inspectors also found damaged storage racks, poor organisation and inadequate segregation of different categories of food products.At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, officials flagged shortcomings in drainage, waste disposal, temperature control and housekeeping.

The outlet was classified as non-compliant after scoring 46 per cent during the inspection.Inspections at Zepto facilities in Mulund and Goregaon revealed deficiencies related to food storage, temperature management, cleanliness and licence display.

At an Instamart outlet in Andheri, inspectors found food packets stored directly on the floor. The FDA also reported inadequate storage space, overcrowding and deficiencies in hygiene and temperature control.The inspection drive also covered delivery operations.At a Blinkit store in Karad in Satara district, officials checked 125 delivery riders and found that they lacked identity cards and medical fitness records.

The regulator also found that the outlet's FSSAI licence was not displayed on delivery bags and boxes.The FDA directed the company to suspend two-wheeler delivery operations at the outlet until the deficiencies were addressed.The regulator said the action was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and urged all food businesses operating through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed food safety, hygiene and storage standards.

India says Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of the country, while urging the world to focus on Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and cross-border terrorism.

India responds to White House report on Chinese goods transshipment
India says it is studying a White House report that flags the country among major hubs for transshipment of Chinese goods to evade US tariffs.

India on Friday said it is examining a White House report that places the country in the top tier of nations allegedly being used for transshipment of Chinese goods to evade US tariffs, while defending the national framework of laws and regulations to prevent such practices.

The report by the White House’s Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy, seen as part of efforts to prevent Chinese products from circumventing US tariffs through third countries, listed India among more than 40 countries that are perceived to be exposed to China-linked transshipment risks. The report listed India among “China’s biggest enablers”.

“We have seen some reports on this particular matter. We would like to study the findings and the methodology that has been adopted in detail,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a regular media briefing when he was asked about the White House report.
“We have robust laws and procedures governing customs, rules of origin and exports, and any instances of violation that may be there are dealt with in accordance with law,” he said.

Jaiswal noted that the government had learnt of the US report on Friday morning and is still studying its findings and methodology. “Beyond that, I don’t have, at present, anything specific to add to what I’ve already said,” he said.

The report placed India, along with Canada, the European Union, Israel, Japan, Mexico, South Korea and Taiwan, in Tier 1 of “countries and trading blocs that account for large absolute volumes of China-linked goods while maintaining diversified industrial bases and major US-bound export platforms”.
The report contended that in these jurisdictions, “illegal transshipment risk is embedded within broad legitimate trade flows”.

“The countries that comprise China’s Shadow Transshipment Network include many of America’s largest trading partners. China’s biggest enablers range from Mexico and Canada on US land borders to the European Union, India, Japan and South Korea,” the report said.

The White House also estimated that “approximately $67 billion in US-bound goods were transshipped from China through the top hubs — Mexico, India and Vietnam — in 2025, producing an estimated $28 billion in lost tariff revenue”.

Jaiswal also dismissed speculation that the government referred a bill proposing changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) to a joint parliamentary committee because of pressure from the US.

“As I have informed you earlier and let me reiterate again that legislative matters concerning India are our own internal matters on which the Parliament of India is there to decide, and only the Parliament of India is there to decide,” he said in response to another question.
“I would also urge you that you should disregard mischievous and misleading reports on this particular issue,” he said.

Reports had suggested that US Vice President JD Vance had spoken on the phone with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US ambassador Sergio Gor had met Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval regarding the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 after several American lawmakers expressed concerns about its impact on Christian organisations and charities.

CJI Surya Kant says remarks were misused, warns of social media misleading youth
CJI Surya Kant said his Supreme Court remarks were taken out of context and circulated misleadingly online. He said transparency would continue, but misuse and monetisation of court clips must stop.

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has said his oral remarks in a Supreme Court hearing were misquoted and misused with "malicious intent", as he voiced concern over clips of court proceedings being circulated on social media without adequate context. In an interview with DD News, he said such material was being used to mislead the youth of the country and urged responsible reporting of judicial proceedings.

He also said the judiciary was committed to transparency, including through live-streaming of Supreme Court proceedings, but stressed that such access should not lead to misuse or commercial exploitation of court footage. Referring to his recent order, he said unauthorised dissemination, reposting, uploading and monetisation of audio and video recordings of judicial proceedings on social media and other digital platforms should not be allowed.

On May 15, 2026, while hearing a case in the Supreme Court, the CJI had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees to "cockroaches" who become social media or RTI activists to attack the system. The remark triggered widespread youth backlash and inspired the satirical online movement "Cockroach Janta Party" or CJP.

CJI Kant said what happened afterwards was unfortunate and clarified that he could never imagine such things regarding the people involved. "My comment was misquoted and misused. What was not said is presented as though it was said. This is extremely unfortunate. Particularly, it is a major malicious attempt to mislead the youth of the country," he said.

Asking the media to report responsibly on judicial proceedings, he said every citizen had a duty to maintain harmony in society. "You are on social media, print media or any form of media or you are simply a citizen. All of us have rights and constitutional duty and responsibilities. When we speak of rights, we must also possess the capacity to fulfil our obligations. Therefore, I would urge them to keep their responsibilities in mind; we must all make tireless efforts to ensure that harmony prevails in society," he said.

The over-a-month-long CJP-led protests at Jantar Mantar against the NEET-UG paper leak later led to a clash between agitators and police on July 20, leaving several individuals on both sides injured. The protests also resulted in the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as the Union education minister.

The 53rd CJI said transparency in judicial proceedings was necessary, but it should not result in commercial exploitation. "We are committed to bringing transparency into the judiciary. There should be transparency. As a further step in this direction, we started live streaming in the Supreme Court. But live-streaming should not be misused. Particularly, it should not be misused commercially. People misuse small clips for their personal gain, for commercial gain. That should stop," he said.

In sum, the CJI said his remarks had been taken out of context, called for responsible handling of court proceedings in the media, and reiterated that while judicial transparency would continue, misuse and commercial use of court clips must be stopped.
Gorakhpur teen fakes own kidnapping, uses AI to extort father for online gaming

A Gorakhpur teenager allegedly staged his own kidnapping and sent AI-generated images to demand Rs 1 lakh from his father. Police said the false ransom plot was aimed at raising money for online gaming and involved no real kidnappers.

In a bizarre case from Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur district, a teenager allegedly staged his own kidnapping and used AI-generated images to demand Rs 1 lakh from his father to fund his online gaming activities.

The incident came to light in the Sikriganj police station area when a man informed the police that his nephew had left home and failed to return. Around the same time, several images were sent from the boy's mobile phone to his father's phone, accompanied by a demand for Rs 1 lakh.
Treating the matter as a suspected kidnapping, police immediately registered a case and launched an investigation.
Using call detail records (CDR) and CCTV footage, police teams traced the boy and recovered him safely within two hours. He was later handed over to his family.

During questioning, police uncovered an unexpected twist. According to investigators, the boy, who was allegedly addicted to online gaming, had fabricated the kidnapping story himself to obtain money for use in online games.

To make the plan appear genuine, he allegedly sent AI-generated images portraying himself as a kidnapping victim and demanded Rs 1 lakh from his father. Police said no actual kidnappers were involved and the ransom demand had been orchestrated by the boy himself.
According to information gathered during the probe, the AI-generated images were reportedly created with the help of the boy's girlfriend, who lives in Delhi.
Khajani Circle Officer Deepanshi Rathore said police acted immediately after receiving the complaint and traced the boy within two hours with the help of technical surveillance and CCTV footage.

She said the investigation revealed that the boy had staged the kidnapping and sent AI-generated photographs to support the false claim, with the sole aim of raising money for online gaming. Police confirmed that no third party had demanded money in the case.

Indians, Pakistanis see each other as greatest geopolitical threat: Pew survey
Despite some positive sentiments from Indian Muslims, mutual distrust persists between the nuclear-armed neighbours eight decades post-independence.

Most people in India and Pakistan view each other as their greatest geopolitical threat, a testimony to the "continued animosity" between the nuclear-armed neighbours nearly 80 years after their independence from British rule, according to a new survey by US-based think tank Pew Research Center.
Over half of Indians (54%) surveyed named Pakistan as their country’s greatest threat, while 43% of Pakistanis identified India.

Majority Indians view Pakistan as threat

The report revealed that 78% of the Indians surveyed held an unfavourable view of Pakistan, including 65% with a very unfavourable opinion. "Muslims in the Hindu-majority country are somewhat more favourable toward Pakistan (21%) than Hindus are (6%)," the report said.

Sharing data on Pakistani's take on the issue, the report said, "Roughly nine-in-ten Pakistanis have an unfavourable view of India, with about three-quarters (73%) saying their view is very unfavourable. This sentiment is shared broadly across demographic groups in Pakistan."

Bilateral relations hit a new low after terrorists killed 26 Indians, mostly tourists, in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam on April 22 last year. India responded with Operation Sindoor, targeting terrorists deep inside Pakistan, and successfully thwarted Islamabad's drone attacks before hitting several Pakistani airbases.'

The government also put the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 in abeyance, saying Pakistan should "credibly and irrevocably" abjure its support for cross-border terrorism first. The move has far-reaching consequences for Pakistan, a country heavily dependent on the Indus river system for 80% of its 16 million hectares of agricultural land and 93% of its total water use.

'Skeptical of govts' commitment to maintain ties'

According to the Pew survey, respondents in both India and Pakistan—which have fought four major wars—"are skeptical of how committed the other country’s government and people are to good bilateral relations".

The report involved 3,566 people in India and 1,039 people in Pakistan, alongside respondents in other countries included in the surveys, which were conducted in India from February 8 to April 27, 2026, and in Pakistan from April 8 to May 7, 2026.

The survey found that a majority of Indian adults think the Indian people and government are committed to good bilateral relations. But a majority of Pakistani adults said the Indian people and government are not committed.

Similarly, a majority of Pakistani adults said "their country’s people and government are committed to good bilateral relations", even though Indians thought that the Pakistani people and government were not committed.

The report said there are differences in how Hindu and Muslim respondents view Pakistan, with Indian Muslims generally expressing more favourable opinions than Indian Hindus. Pew Research Center estimates from 2020 put the Muslim population in India at about 15%.

Among the global players, Indians see China as a top threat (named by 21%). Pakistanis see Israel (24%) and the US (24%) as their next-greatest threats, according to the findings.
