Indian Muslims are somewhat more favorable toward Pakistan (21%) than Indian Hindus (6%), and they are also less likely to name Pakistan as their top threat (34% vs 57% among Hindus).
The numbers on bilateral perceptions are stark.

Pew's polling also shows that this is not a temporary shift in sentiment.Indian views of Pakistan have remained overwhelmingly negative for more than a decade, with the share expressing a favourable opinion never rising above 20% since 2013.Historical Pew surveys also show that Pakistanis have long held predominantly negative views of India. Pakistani respondents expressing favourable views of India have generally ranged from single digits to around one-third.

The survey further suggests that hostility is not simply about how Indians and Pakistanis perceive each other. It also extends to whether they believe the other side genuinely wants better relations.A clear pattern emerges: people tend to believe that their own government and population are committed to good bilateral relations, while doubting the intentions of the other side.
When asked whether the Indian and Pakistani governments and people are committed to good relations with each other, the clear pattern is that people only have faith in their own country

A majority of Indians believe both the Indian government and Indian people are committed to maintaining good relations with Pakistan. But a majority of Pakistanis reject that assessment, saying the Indian government and people are not committed to good relations.The mirror image appears in Pakistan.
Beneath the geopolitical differences lies a more fundamental problem: the absence of trust.

A majority of Pakistanis say their government and people want good relations with India.Most Indians, however, believe Pakistan's government and people are not committed to improving ties. About a quarter of Indian respondents were unsure.This mutual lack of trust creates a difficult cycle: each side sees itself as willing to improve relations while viewing the other as unwilling to reciprocate.Indian Muslims again stand apart to some degree. Around a third say the Pakistani government and people are committed to good relations, significantly higher than the corresponding share among Indian Hindus.
How Bangladesh, Sri Lanka view the rivals

The Pew findings become even more revealing when India and Pakistan are placed alongside Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.Of the four South Asian countries surveyed, Sri Lanka is the only country that receives more positive than negative ratings from respondents in all three of the others.
The India-Pakistan divide extends beyond bilateral relations.

India, meanwhile, has the widest range of perceptions.Sri Lankans are overwhelmingly positive toward India, with 79% expressing a favourable opinion. In Bangladesh, 42% view India favourably. In Pakistan, however, the figure plunges to just 7%.India is also seen as Sri Lanka's most important ally by a clear majority: 63% of Sri Lankan respondents name India.The picture is very different in Bangladesh and Pakistan, where India is most often identified as the greatest threat.Views of Prime Minister Narendra Modi follow a broadly similar pattern.

Seventy percent of Sri Lankans express confidence in PM Modi to do the right thing in world affairs, compared with 42% in Bangladesh and 4% in Pakistan.The survey also finds that Pakistan is not universally viewed negatively across South Asia.Fifty-seven percent of Sri Lankans and 54% of Bangladeshis have a favourable opinion of Pakistan, compared with only 8% of Indians.Bangladesh itself receives broadly positive views in Pakistan and Sri Lanka: 66% of Pakistanis and 56% of Sri Lankans express favourable opinions of Bangladesh.

Only about a quarter of Indians do so.Sri Lanka emerges as the region's relative outlier. Around half or more of respondents in India, Pakistan and Bangladesh view the island nation positively, while significantly fewer hold negative views.

The India-Pakistan divide extends beyond bilateral relations to the way each country views the global order.For Indians, Russia remains a particularly important and popular partner. Thirty-six percent identify Russia as India's most important ally, while 16% name the United States.Russia's favourable image in India is particularly striking.

Fifty-eight percent of Indians have a favourable opinion of Russia, while 51% express confidence in Russian President Vladimir Putin.Pakistanis are considerably less positive: 39% have a favourable view of Russia and only 32% express confidence in Putin.India's relationship with the United States is also reflected in public opinion.

Indians are substantially more favourable toward the US than Pakistanis are and are more likely to express confidence in US President Donald Trump.The picture is almost completely reversed when it comes to China.An overwhelming 90% of Pakistanis have a favourable view of China, while 83% express confidence in Chinese President Xi Jinping. Three-quarters of Pakistanis identify China as their country's most important ally.Saudi Arabia is a distant second, named by 12%.In India, however, only around a quarter of respondents view China or Xi positively.
Even Indian Muslims, who are more favourable toward China than Indian Hindus, remain negative toward both China and its president on balance.

Nearly 80 years after Partition, the survey suggests that the India-Pakistan rivalry remains deeply embedded not only in government policy and military strategy, but also in public perceptions.The most striking finding may therefore not be that Indians and Pakistanis dislike each other.

It is that both overwhelmingly believe the other side sees them as the problem.That mutual conviction â reinforced by decades of conflict, competing national narratives and geopolitical rivalry â remains one of the biggest barriers to changing the relationship between the two nuclear-armed neighbours.Yet beneath these geopolitical differences lies a more fundamental problem: the absence of trust.Both populations believe their own side is committed to better relations, while doubting the intentions of the other.

Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Thursday (August 13, 2026) flagged concerns over the misuse of live-streamed court proceedings and the circulation of clips on social media without adequate context. Cockroaches, expired food: Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart face Maharashtra FDA crackdown

Maharashtra's FDA has suspended 14 licences after statewide inspections found food safety lapses at quick-commerce facilities and other establishments. The drive also triggered notices, seizures, FIRs and a warning to food businesses to meet prescribed hygiene and storage standards.

Maharashtra’s Food and Drug Administration has launched a major crackdown on food businesses after a statewide inspection drive uncovered serious hygiene, storage and food safety violations at quick-commerce facilities, hotels, restaurants and other establishments.

The FDA inspected 86 establishments linked to online food delivery platforms on August 13, suspending 14 food business licences with immediate effect. Five licences were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto, two to Instamart, while one each belonged to Bhagwati Store and Swinsta ENT Pvt Ltd.

The action came after inspectors found expired food products, poor temperature control, pest infestations, unhygienic storage, inadequate waste disposal and serious lapses in personal hygiene at several facilities.
14 LICENCES SUSPENDED AFTER STATEWIDE INSPECTIONS
Alongside the licence suspensions, the FDA issued 60 improvement notices and ordered one establishment to immediately halt business operations.
The inspections examined storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, hygiene of food handlers, FIFO and FEFO practices, food safety records and the display of FSSAI licences.
Officials said suspension action was taken against establishments where serious non-compliance was detected.
EXPIRED FOOD, COCKROACHES AND COLD-CHAIN FAILURES

At a Zepto facility in Pune’s Lohegaon area, inspectors found food products stored beyond their declared “Use By” dates. The facility also failed to follow FIFO and FEFO practices and had unhygienic storage, inadequate pest control and serious personal hygiene deficiencies.
The FDA said the company’s response during the hearing was unsatisfactory.

At Swinsta ENT Pvt Ltd in Warje Jakat Naka, Pune, inspectors reported cockroach infestation, inadequate cold-chain maintenance for frozen products, temperature-control problems and serious hygiene and pest-control deficiencies.
BLINKIT FACILITIES FLAGGED IN MUMBAI
A Blinkit facility in Malad West was found operating with a chiller-room temperature of 6 degrees Celsius, above the prescribed level.

The FDA also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone medical examinations and that the required records were unavailable. Several workers were reportedly not wearing headgear, aprons or gloves.

Inspectors further flagged disorganised storage, damaged and rusted racks, inadequate segregation of vegetarian, non-vegetarian, cooked and dairy products, along with shortcomings in training and food safety supervision.

At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, inspectors found inadequate drainage and waste-disposal arrangements, poor temperature control for frozen products and unprotected lighting fixtures in an unpacked-food storage area.
The establishment scored just 34 out of 74 marks, or 46 per cent, and was declared non-compliant.
ZEPTO, INSTAMART UNITS ALSO FOUND NON-COMPLIANT

At Zepto’s Mulund facility, inspectors reported inadequate waste disposal, temperature-control failures, lighting problems, poor cleanliness and inadequate separate storage facilities. The FSSAI licence was also not prominently displayed.
The facility scored 81 out of 180 marks, or 45 per cent, and was declared non-compliant.

A reinspection of Zepto’s Gola Unit in Goregaon also found deficiencies in temperature control, lighting, food storage, personal hygiene facilities and cleanliness. Despite scoring 98 out of 142 marks, or 70 per cent, the unit was still classified as non-compliant.

At an Instamart facility in Andheri, food packets were found stored directly on the floor. Inspectors reported inadequate storage space, congestion, temperature-control deficiencies and problems with lighting, cleanliness and personal hygiene.
The facility scored 76 out of 140 marks, or 55 per cent, and was declared non-compliant.

At Zepto’s Lokhandwala facility, the FDA additionally found inadequate temperature control for perishable food, no ante-room for frozen products, poor warehouse layout and improper segregation of food, non-food items and hazardous substances. The facility scored 65 out of 140 marks, or 47 per cent.
DELIVERY RIDERS ALSO UNDER FDA SCANNER
The crackdown extended beyond warehouses and stores to delivery operations.
At a Blinkit store in Karad, Satara district, officials checked 125 two-wheeler delivery riders and found that they lacked identity cards and medical fitness records.

The FDA also found that the principal food business’s FSSAI licence was not displayed on delivery carts, bags or boxes. The firm was directed to stop business activity involving two-wheeler deliveries until the deficiencies were rectified.
MILK PRODUCTS, BAKERY ITEMS SEIZED
The statewide drive also resulted in significant seizures of food products.

The FDA seized 698 kg of milk and milk products valued at around Rs 34,302. Another 1,270 kg of food items, including milk products, bakery products and edible oil, valued at approximately Rs 1,29,762, was seized.
The regulator said the total value of seized goods involving other food items and banned products stood at around Rs 46,89,603.

The drive also led to 10 FIRs over the sale, distribution and transportation of banned products such as pan masala and gutkha. Nine people were arrested and banned stock worth Rs 46,76,631 was seized.
109 HOTELS, RESTAURANTS AND DHABAS INSPECTED
The FDA also inspected 109 hotels, restaurants and dhabas as part of the wider crackdown.
Officials issued 49 improvement notices and suspended four food establishment licences. A total of 15 raids were conducted during the special drive.
BOLLYWOOD CAFE FACES ACTION OVER HYGIENE LAPSES
The FDA also conducted a special inspection at Bollywood Cafe, Studio Number 13, located in Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari, Film City, Goregaon.
Inspectors found serious shortcomings in cleanliness and food safety standards. The condition of utensils and the premises was found unsatisfactory, while a large-scale fly infestation was reported.
The kitchen was found with dirty water, accumulated dirt and food residue. Officials also found food being prepared on rusty and unhygienic food-contact surfaces.
The department directed the cafe management to immediately rectify the violations and strictly comply with prescribed food safety and hygiene standards.
The FDA said penal action was being initiated under Section 69 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

The Maharashtra FDA said the action against quick-commerce establishments and other food businesses was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the rules and regulations framed under it.

The regulator has warned food business operators involved in selling and delivering food through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed standards for food safety, hygiene, storage and handling.

Karnataka says releasing 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu difficult
Karnataka has said it will be difficult to release 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water daily to Tamil Nadu. The state will place its objections before the Supreme Court as protests gather pace.

Karnataka Minister Ramalinga Reddy on Wednesday said the state would find it difficult to release 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water a day to Tamil Nadu, as directed by the Cauvery Water Management Authority.

He said the state government would decide its next course of action after a Supreme Court hearing on Thursday on Tamil Nadu's petition, and added that it would ensure that no injustice was done to Karnataka.

The Cauvery Water Regulation Committee, which met in New Delhi on Tuesday, directed Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days from August 12. The Cauvery Water Management Authority later upheld the decision.

Reddy said discussions had been held with Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and officials. “I have held discussions with the Chief Minister (D K Shivakumar) and officials. The CM spoke to our Advocate General and advocates in Delhi. Tamil Nadu's petition is coming up before the Supreme Court tomorrow; it has been listed. We will have an opportunity there, and our advocates will file our objections. Let's see what the Supreme Court says. Thereafter, we will have further options,” he said.

Speaking to reporters, the State Water Resources Minister said the government's future course of action would depend on the outcome of the hearing. “Tamil Nadu has filed a petition, and we have been served a notice. We will have an opportunity to present our case there. Based on the outcome, we will decide whether further legal action is required. This is based on the suggestions given by the advocates,” he added.

The Tamil Nadu government had earlier this month moved the Supreme Court over the Cauvery dispute with Karnataka, saying that the quantum of water directed by the CWRC, as well as the water released by Karnataka, was insufficient.

Earlier, on July 28, the CWRC had directed Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. Karnataka had initially said it could not release water because of poor storage in its reservoirs. However, after heavy rain in the Cauvery catchment areas in the state, it began releasing water under the earlier 3,500-cusec direction.

Reddy said Karnataka had complied with that earlier order and had, in fact, released more water to Tamil Nadu. “When the Kabini dam filled due to rains in the catchment area, the water flowed downstream as there was no scope to store it further. About 10 TMC of water has flown,” he said.

He said Karnataka had about 76 TMC of water in its reservoirs, of which 36 TMC would be needed every year for drinking water, apart from losses due to evaporation and the requirement for rivers and crops. “We have about 76 TMC of water (in our dams), out of which we will need 36 TMC a year for drinking water. There will also be evaporation, and we will have to release water to rivers and for crops. Asking Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs for 15 days is inappropriate,” he said.

Reddy said the earlier direction to release 3,500 cusecs a day was somewhat acceptable, but the latest order to release 12,000 cusecs daily for 15 days, amounting to about 16 TMC, was “too costly” for Karnataka. He said the state would not have faced difficulty if it had been asked to release a smaller quantity. “This is too high a quantity,” he said.

He also said the monsoon had not been satisfactory in Karnataka's old Mysuru region and claimed that Tamil Nadu had enough water in its reservoirs. He said Tamil Nadu receives most of its rainfall during the northeast monsoon from October to December and has a better water table than Karnataka. “Our water table is too low here. Even if we go 800-1,000 feet, we don't get water, while they get water at much higher levels. Despite our Additional Chief Secretary, advocates, and experts effectively putting forward our case with all these facts, the order has come. It will be difficult for us to release 16 TMC of water in 15 days. We have discussed it. We will decide what to do,” he said.
“The CM has spoken to advocates in New Delhi and experts. We will ensure that no injustice happens to the state,” he added.

Meanwhile, farmers have staged sporadic protests in Cauvery basin districts, including Mandya and Mysuru, against the water release order. Some pro-Kannada organisations have called for a Karnataka bandh on Thursday in protest against the directive, while others have opposed the bandh call. Overall, the state government has said it will place its objections before the Supreme Court and decide its next steps after the hearing.
With hours left, Parliament heads for a tense Monsoon Session finish

Amit Shah offered a marathon debate on the student protests, but Rahul Gandhi demanded a direct answer on who ordered the police action, leaving Parliament deadlocked as the Monsoon Session entered its final day.

Parliament’s Monsoon Session will enter its final day on Thursday with the government and Opposition still locked in a standoff over the student protests, after Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s offer of an extended debate failed to break the deadlock in the Lok Sabha.

Shah offered to participate in a detailed discussion on the protests and allegations of police action against students. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, however, rejected the proposal, saying the Opposition wanted a direct answer on who ordered the use of pellet guns and force against protesters rather than a “lecture” from the Home Minister.
The Lok Sabha was eventually adjourned for the day amid sloganeering despite repeated appeals from the government to allow the discussion.
AMIT SHAH OFFERS EXTENDED DEBATE
The confrontation began soon after the Lok Sabha assembled at 11 am on Wednesday.
Shah said the government was ready to discuss all issues concerning the student protests and asked the Opposition to submit a written request to Speaker Om Birla.
He offered to begin the discussion at 3 pm on Wednesday and continue it until 3 pm on Thursday.
“Even today, I say that they should submit a letter to the Speaker by 2 pm. We are ready for all kinds of discussions from 3 pm today until 3 pm tomorrow,” Shah said.
He later wrote to the Speaker, saying he was prepared to remain present throughout the debate and respond to questions raised by the Opposition.
Shah said dialogue and discussion were the only ways to resolve issues in a democracy and maintained that the government had nothing to hide.
The Opposition, however, did not accept the offer.
‘IF HE ORDERED IT, HE SHOULD RESIGN’
Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition was not interested in listening to what he described as Shah’s “imagination” or a lengthy lecture.
He said young people wanted to know who ordered the use of pellet guns, lathi charges and other force against protesting students.
“If Mr Amit Shah gave the order to shoot our children, he should resign because he is culpable, and if he did not, he should resign because he is incompetent,” Gandhi said.
He argued that the Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force come under the Home Ministry and questioned Shah’s responsibility for the alleged police action.
Gandhi later posted a video of his remarks on X, saying Shah’s silence amounted to a “confession”.
Congress deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi also questioned why the Home Minister had not participated in an earlier proposed discussion on education and student protests.
He said Shah should make a statement in Parliament on the police action against protesters and allegations surrounding the use of AK-47s in Bihar.
GOVERNMENT ACCUSES OPPOSITION OF AVOIDING DEBATE
The government, in turn, accused the Opposition of refusing the very discussion it had been demanding.

When the Lok Sabha met again at 3 pm after two adjournments, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the government was ready to begin the debate immediately and pointed out that Shah had already written to the Speaker.
He urged the Opposition not to “run away” when the Home Minister was prepared to answer its questions.
Presiding officer Jagdambika Pal also repeatedly appealed to Opposition members to allow proceedings to continue, but protests and sloganeering persisted.
The House was eventually adjourned for the day.
Rijiju later called it “unthinkable and incomprehensible” that the Opposition was refusing a discussion when the government had agreed to one.
WHY THE STUDENT ROW HAS DOMINATED THE SESSION
The student protests have emerged as one of the main flashpoints of the Monsoon Session.
The Opposition has demanded accountability over police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak, including allegations of pellet gun use, lathi charges and tear gas at Jantar Mantar.
Congress has also repeatedly sought statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Shah.
The government has maintained that it is willing to discuss the issue, but disagreement over the scope and nature of the debate has repeatedly disrupted proceedings.
With the session ending on Thursday, there has been no breakthrough so far.
Even as the student row kept Parliament on edge, the government managed to move ahead on several pieces of legislative business.

The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday adopted a motion referring the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee. The Lok Sabha had already approved the referral.
The JPC will comprise 21 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha and has been asked to submit its report by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session.

Introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25, the Bill proposes tighter oversight of foreign contributions received by NGOs and other organisations. It also provides for a designated authority to manage and dispose of assets if an organisation loses its FCRA licence.
The Opposition has opposed the legislation, alleging that some provisions could affect legitimate foreign funding for Christian NGOs and minority-run social welfare and educational institutions.
The government has rejected the charge, saying the Bill is not religion-specific and is aimed at regulating foreign contributions.

Congress MP KC Venugopal demanded that the legislation be withdrawn, while Rijiju pointed out that Opposition parties had themselves sought its examination by a parliamentary committee and urged them to raise their objections before the JPC.
Parliament also cleared legislation to officially change Kerala’s name to Keralam.
The Rajya Sabha passed the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, by voice vote on Wednesday, a day after it was cleared by the Lok Sabha.
The move follows a resolution passed by the Kerala Assembly in 2024 urging the Centre to change the state’s name.
The Bill provides for the alteration of the name and consequential amendments to the Constitution, including the First Schedule.
RAJYA SABHA CLEARS NCDC AMENDMENT BILL
The Rajya Sabha also passed the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, a day after it cleared the Lok Sabha.
The legislation expands the powers of the National Cooperative Development Corporation, allowing it to provide loans and grants directly to cooperative societies.

The NCDC, a statutory organisation under the Ministry of Cooperation, will also be allowed, with prior approval from the Centre, to participate in the share capital of cooperatives and other entities involved in cooperative development.
The changes are aimed at widening the channels through which financial assistance can reach the cooperative sector.
FINAL DAY, STUDENT PROTEST ROW STILL UNRESOLVED

The Monsoon Session began with the Opposition raising the NEET paper leak and alleged irregularities involving donations to the Ram temple in Ayodhya, before the political focus shifted sharply to police action against protesting students.
The issue has since dominated proceedings and contributed to repeated adjournments.
The government’s last-minute offer of an extended discussion on Wednesday failed to end the impasse.
The Lok Sabha will meet again at 11 am on Thursday for the final scheduled day of the session, leaving only a narrow window for the two sides to find common ground.

For now, the government says it is ready to debate. The Opposition says it first wants a direct answer on accountability. That divide remains unresolved as the Monsoon Session heads into its final day.

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) on Thursday assured the Supreme Court that it will not convene a meeting to finalise the selection of Director General of Police for the State of Odisha till the next apex court hearing on August 18.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant intervened in a petition, represented by senior advocate P. Chidambaram, alleging that the Odisha DGP selection process was in violation of the apex court’s Prakash Singh judgment. It alleged that the Odisha government was trying to include a junior officer in the list of candidates.
A submission was made before the Bench that the UPSC meeting was scheduled to be held later in the day (August 13).
Mr. Chidambaram alleged that an officer was given promotion just a day back, preempting the Supreme Court hearing, so that he could be included in the list of candidates for the DGP post.
The Bench had also sought assistance from senior advocate Raju Ramachandran, the amicus curiae in the Prakash Singh matter.
The court, in a 2006 judgment in the Prakash Singh case, had made it clear that the office of DGP should be divorced from political or other external pressures.

It had invoked its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to direct that DGPs must be selected by State governments from among the three seniormost and meritorious officers empanelled by the UPSC. The court had thrown out the “concept” of acting DGPs. It had held that State police chiefs should have a minimum fixed tenure of two years.

Subsequent apex court orders in July 2018 and March 2019 detailed the appointments mechanism, which included the State concerned sending a proposal to the UPSC three months ahead of the retirement of the incumbent DGP. The UPSC would prepare a panel of suitable officers. The State would appoint one of the empanelled officers as DGP “immediately”.

Sonam Wangchuk seeks 'peaceful revolution' to reshape India's politics
Sonam Wangchuk has called for a peaceful revolution in how India chooses its political leaders. He said the shift is necessary if India is to emerge as a developed nation by 2047.

Climate activist and education reformer Sonam Wangchuk has called for a “peaceful revolution” in India, arguing that the country needs a fundamental change in the way it chooses its political leaders if it is to emerge as a developed nation by 2047.

In a video message posted ahead of Independence Day, Wangchuk said he had been reflecting on India’s future and was increasingly disappointed by India’s progress compared with several countries in the region.
“Fifty years ago, countries that were behind us or at par with us are today miles ahead of us,” he said, citing Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh in terms of per capita GDP.
Wangchuk warned that if the current trajectory continued, India could struggle to hold its place in the global economy by 2047, the centenary of its Independence.

He also praised people who had recently taken to the streets demanding change, saying their protests had already resulted in the resignation of the education minister. However, he said the appointment of a new education minister had not yet brought any visible transformation.
“As long as education remains backward, the future of the country will also remain backward,” Wangchuk said.
NOT ABOUT ANY ONE POLITICAL PARTY

Wangchuk said the problem extended beyond any particular political party. Referring to protests and government action in different states, he argued that governments across the political spectrum had been accused of silencing voices raised against injustice.
He recalled the anti-corruption movement of 2012-13, which led to a change in government in Delhi, but said corruption and injustice had returned in a different form.
“Now, 12 years later, corruption and injustice have changed their route, but are staring at us, frightening us, in a form two or three times bigger,” he said.
Wangchuk said India therefore needed a “very big change”, which he described as a “peaceful revolution”.
FOCUS ON HOW POLITICAL LEADERS ARE CHOSEN
The activist said the biggest weakness in India’s political system was the way leaders were selected.
“If the leaders are not right, the whole country goes in the wrong direction,” he said.

Wangchuk acknowledged that there were politicians who followed principles and worked with honesty, saying he saluted such leaders. But he questioned how India could become a developed country when many lawmakers face criminal cases.

He claimed that nearly half of India’s MPs face criminal cases and around a third face serious allegations, including murder, rape and kidnapping. He stressed that he was not targeting any particular party or the ruling or opposition camp, but was speaking about the country as a whole.
SEEKS NAMES OF SELFLESS INDIANS
Wangchuk said he now wanted to bring together some of the country’s “best minds” to seek ideas and advice on how India could move towards a new political system.
But he said he was not looking merely for intellectuals.
“I want to meet people who are selfless, who have character and who follow principles,” he said.
Wangchuk, who is currently in Ladakh, appealed to people across India to suggest names of individuals they believe possess these qualities and could help create a “new map” for the country’s future.
He also said he wanted to travel to different states and cities to seek suggestions directly from people.
Wangchuk ended his message by wishing people on Independence Day and appealing for their help in building what he described as a peaceful transformation of India.
“Give me the best gift this Independence Day by suggesting such names,” he said.

Addressing the nation from the ramparts of Red Fort on its 80th Independence Day, just days after massive youth protests rocked the capital, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s speech included a seven-point economic reform plan and an outreach to Gen Z youth, promising AI skilling programmes and free online coaching in an attempt to address post-globalisation anxieties. He also warned the country about the threat of “dimagi Naxals” — intellectual or ideological Naxals — in society, even after the eradication of armed left wing extremism.

At the first Independence Day that saw Vande Mataram preceding the national anthem, the Prime Minister directly addressed challenges facing the youth, from employment worries to the incursion of of Artificial Intelligence in everyday life.

More than one crore youth will be provided AI skills in a “mission mode” drive over the coming year, he said. India’s digital public infrastructure will be used to provide free online coaching to students wishing to take various competitive exams, and there will be a nationwide sports talent hunt among children between five and 15 years of age ahead of the 2036 Olympic Games, he added.

Mr. Modi recalled that, when he had first promoted his ‘Make in India’ initiative, advocates of globalisation had reacted as though it was heresy. In the current global economy, however, every country is thinking for itself, he pointed out.
‘Identify, isolate intellectual Naxals’
This acknowledgement of GenZ anxieties that spilled over into the recent Jantar Mantar protests was, however, spiked by a warning about “intellectual Naxals”.

“For years, people with a Maoist ideology had established themselves in the corridors of power and influenced policymaking, including as advisors on government committees. We have succeeded in eliminating armed Naxalites from the forests and freeing the country from that grave threat, but these ideological Naxalites are waiting for opportunities,” Mr. Modi said. “They are trying to revive the paths of violence and anarchy, and are making various attempts to drag society in the wrong direction. We must identify these ideological Naxalites and isolate them. At the same time, we must connect the country’s young generation with the mainstream effort to build a developed nation,” he added.
Freedom’s Progress Through the Years

He announced a full review and restructuring of civil defence infrastructure. “The nature of warfare is changing. We had announced Mission Sudarshan Chakra, [a multi-layered defence infrastructure system, with AI and cybersecurity components] last year, and work on it is going on rapidly,” he added.

NEW DELHI: More than 75 years of the Constitution coming into force, the derogatory practice of witch-hunting that targets defenceless women due to prejudice, suspicion, superstition and irrational fear, continues in the country, the Supreme Court lamented while upholding life term for two who murdered a woman in a tribal village of Odisha in Feb 1998.A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria said the facets of the case had a disturbing impact on the court as a defenceless woman was branded a practitioner of witchcraft and was brutally assaulted in front of her daughter.

âWhat effect it must have had on the daughter of the deceased who had to witness her mother being killed in the most brutal way,â the bench wondered.Writing the judgment, Justice Mishra said the malady of with-hunting continues to plague sections of our society, where prejudice, superstition, and irrational dear supersede the rule of law and constitutional morality.âThe brutality associated with witch-hunting extends far beyond the act of killing; where victims mostly women are subjected to torture, beatings, sexual violence and social ostracization.

In such a situation, superstitious beliefs or fears are given precedence leading to vulnerable women becoming victims of collective hostility,â he said.IN Feb 1998, in the remote village of tribal inhabited Sundergarh district, one Manobodha Naikâs daughter died, and family members claimed that she died because of witchcraft practice of one Puni Naik.

Hearing this Udai Oram dragged Puni Naik to Naikâs house and with his associate, mercilessly assaulted her with sticks leading to her death. The trial court had convicted the duo in 2002, but the Orissa HC took two decades to uphold the conviction and life sentence.

Justices Mishra and Anjaria said, âSometimes in the most difficult situations, it often becomes an easy escape to blame a woman for the acts she did not commit, thus reflecting a deeply rooted social prejudice that often seeks scapegoats rather than solutions. In such situations, what can be given an ascendency is âreasonâ for reason is the only virtue that stands as a bulwark against collective irrationality.âSC said the Constitution guarantees equality, promotes fraternity and envisages citizens to adopt scientific temperament to rid the society of derogatory practices against women.

âDespite this, practices such as witch-hunting continue to persist within a few sections of our society. A Constitutional democracy such as ours cannot survive; wherein such derogatory practices continue to elude the principles of rule of law and Constitutional morality,â it said.
IPS Nupur Prasad, who led Sushant Singh Rajput CBI probe, to get President's Medal

Senior IPS officer Nupur Prasad has been selected for the President's Medal for Distinguished Service. The honour highlights her high-profile CBI tenure, including supervision of the Sushant Singh Rajput death probe.

Senior IPS officer Nupur Prasad, who supervised the CBI investigation into the death of actor Sushant Singh Rajput, has been selected for the prestigious President’s Medal for Distinguished Service this year.

Prasad, a 2007-batch AGMUT-cadre IPS officer, recently completed her tenure with the Central Bureau of Investigation and returned to the Delhi Police. She is currently serving as Joint Commissioner of Police in the Economic Offences Wing.

The award citation describes Prasad as an “accomplished officer” and a leader known for “versatility, integrity and institutional vision”. It highlights her work across the Delhi Police, CBI, West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh, including several high-profile investigations and major policing initiatives.
ROLE IN SUSHANT SINGH RAJPUT DEATH PROBE
Prasad’s role in the Sushant Singh Rajput investigation was among the most prominent assignments of her CBI tenure.

Rajput, 34, was found dead at his Bandra residence in Mumbai on June 14, 2020. The Mumbai Police initially registered an accidental death case and investigated the circumstances surrounding his death.
The case took a major turn after Rajput’s father, K K Singh, filed an FIR in Patna against actress Rhea Chakraborty and others, alleging abetment to suicide, financial wrongdoing and harassment.
Following the legal and political controversy surrounding the jurisdiction of the investigation, the CBI took over the case in August 2020.

The investigation continued for nearly five years and involved examination of witnesses, scrutiny of medical and forensic evidence and investigation of allegations of murder, abetment to suicide and other suspected wrongdoing.
The case generated intense public and media scrutiny, with several theories circulating on social media and television, including allegations of poisoning and strangulation.

In March 2025, the CBI filed closure reports before courts in Mumbai and Patna, stating that its investigation had found no evidence of foul play, abetment to suicide or criminal conspiracy in Rajput’s death.
The President’s Medal citation highlights Prasad’s work across several challenging assignments.

As the first DCP of Shahdara, she was tasked with establishing the district’s policing framework from the ground up. During her tenure, she led action against drug networks and gambling operations and worked to make Anand Vihar a “snatching-free zone”.
As DCP, North District, Prasad oversaw security arrangements for major events, including Delhi University elections and Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort.

She also spearheaded community-oriented initiatives, including women’s self-defence training, hygiene camps in collaboration with the Ladli Foundation, youth skill-development programmes and drug de-addiction initiatives with SPYM.
Her career also includes significant assignments outside Delhi. In West Bengal, she handled security arrangements during the 2011 Assembly elections and the Ganga Sagar Mela.
As Superintendent of Police in Arunachal Pradesh, she worked to restore inter-tribal peace and dismantle extortion networks.
CONTRIBUTIONS TO POLICING REFORMS
During her CBI tenure, Prasad supervised some of the agency’s significant cases, including the AgustaWestland investigation and the Sushant Singh Rajput death case.
She also contributed to the CBI Crime Manual 2020 and the agency’s Vision Document. She was associated with preparations for the Interpol General Assembly 2022 and the G20 Cyber Conference.
After returning to the Delhi Police, Prasad introduced the MyKase software for trial monitoring while serving in the Economic Offences Wing.
She also contributed to the Bureau of Police Research and Development’s National Police Mission, Micro Mission.
PRESIDENT’S MEDAL FOR DISTINGUISHED SERVICE
The President’s Medal for Distinguished Service is among the highest service honours conferred on police personnel.

Prasad’s selection recognises a career spanning investigation, law-and-order policing, community outreach, institutional reform and assignments in some of the country’s most challenging security environments.

Her supervision of the Sushant Singh Rajput investigation remains one of the most high-profile assignments of her CBI tenure, with the agency ultimately concluding that there was no evidence of foul play in the actor’s death.

Gurugram: Union Minister of State Rao Inderjit Singh turned an official Partition Horrors Remembrance Day event in Gurugram into a stage for his grievances Friday, publicly asking BJP national president Nitin Nabin on the dais why he (Rao) had even bothered to show up if he, as the local MP, could not be included among the speakers.
The gathering included Union Minister Manohar Lal Khattar and Haryana BJP chief Dr Archana Gupta.

Rao pointed to Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Bhatia, who was seated on the dais, and asked whether a similar programme in Panipat would have gone ahead without inviting Bhatia, or one in Karnal without Khattar. Panipat is Bhatia’s hometown while Khattar represents Karnal in the Lok Sabha.
The MoS said his name did not figure anywhere in the speeches at the event, and added that, had it not been a party president’s programme, he would not have been called at all.
Khattar was seated on the dais as Rao made these remarks, a moment made sharper by the two leaders’ long history of uneasy relations.
Rao also took aim at the organisers’ outreach to Gurugram’s Punjabi community, the primary audience for the day’s commemoration of Partition refugees.

He said most of the families affected by Partition had settled in Haryana rather than Punjab, and that Haryana had welcomed them, before adding, in a pointed remark to the organisers, that “taali do haath se bajti hai (it takes two to tango)”.

He noted that Haryana was the first state to have given the country a Punjabi chief minister, twice over, referring to Khattar and his successor Nayab Singh Saini, and that two of Independent India’s Army chiefs, Dalbir Singh Suhag and General Deepak Kapoor, had hailed from the state.
“People sitting here may say one of them was Haryanvi while the other was a Punjabi. But don’t forget, both Suhag and Kapoor hailed from Haryana,” he added.
He said that Dharamvir Gaba, Gurugram’s first Punjabi MLA, had won only because communities across the constituency backed him and not on the strength of the Punjabi vote alone.

Rao further said the party must bear in mind that if a Punjabi, referring to Khattar, could become the chief minister twice and another Punjabi, Gaba, could become MLA from Gurugram on four occasions, it was not solely because of the Punjabi community, but also because of the contributions of other communities.
“However, you don’t even consider inviting people like me to address the party event,” Rao said.

Nabin, in his remarks at the event, said the Nehru family had partitioned the country for power and was now working to partition society. He also questioned why the Congress had never “apologised” to Partition’s victims.
A decade of friction with Haryana’s BJP leadership
Friday’s outburst fits a pattern that has defined Rao Inderjit Singh’s relationship with the state’s BJP leadership since Manohar Lal Khattar became chief minister in 2014.
A six-time MP and Ahirwal strongman, Rao has repeatedly taken digs at Khattar, accusing him of trying to erode his hold over south Haryana.

After the BJP’s win in the 2024 assembly election, Rao said at his Rewari residence that a former chief minister, without naming Khattar, had tried to divide his camp and introduce rival leaders for a decade. He described it as an attempt to undercut 40 years of his own political work.
Party insiders have said the fight over ticket distribution in seats such as Bawal, where Khattar backed a rival candidate over a Rao loyalist, was one of several such flashpoints.
The friction did not ease after Khattar moved to the Centre and Nayab Singh Saini took over as chief minister, though Rao’s daughter Arti Singh Rao is a minister in the latter’s cabinet.

At a rally in Rewari last year, Rao told Saini directly that the BJP’s Ahirwal MLAs had helped bring the government to power and had a rightful claim on it, and that the previous chief minister had never visited the region.
Saini responded by saying his government belonged to all 2.75 crore people of the state, not any one community.
However, days after the event, Rao and his daughter Arti Singh hosted a dinner for Saini and his wife.

Rao has separately criticised Khattar’s tenure as chief minister, arguing that despite spreading development projects across the state, Khattar never became a mass leader and failed to win over the state’s Jat voters.

He has also alleged that officials from Khattar’s chief ministerial office continue to hold sway in the state administration even after Khattar became a Cabinet minister in the Narendra Modi government.

The rivalry has also spilled into policy. Earlier this year, Rao publicly opposed the Panchgram smart cities corridor project, first conceived during Khattar’s tenure, warning that farmers’ land in the Rewari-Gurugram belt could be exploited. He said he would take his objections directly to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

In January this year, Rao wrote to CM Nayab Singh Saini, flagging environmental concerns in the Aravalli region, pointing out that public anxiety was high in Gurugram, Nuh, Rewari and Faridabad over these issues.

New Delhi: In his shortest Independence Day address in the past four years, Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a major outreach to the youth, stressing that the greatest beneficiaries of ‘Viksit Bharat (Developed India)’ will be the country’s youth.

The Prime Minister’s outreach to the young generation, including Gen Z, was amply clear as he mentioned the words ‘youth’, ‘young’ and ‘younger’ 43 times in his 75-minute speech. He used the term ‘youth’ 20 times, ‘young’ 22 and ‘younger’ once in his speech.

“When I speak of a ‘Viksit Bharat’, when I speak of taking the country forward at a rapid pace, who is the greatest beneficiary of all these efforts? Who is the greatest force driving these efforts? If there is one, it is the youth of my country, the youth power of the country,” the PM said Saturday.

His speech packed with announcements for the young generation assumes significance, especially against the backdrop of the protest that took place across the country, particularly in New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak and concerns about the integrity of other competitive exams.

The BJP and the Modi government faced flak over the condition of India’s overall education system and the lack of job opportunities for the youth. The protest finally concluded with the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July, but it also led to growing concerns within the party about its inability to connect with the aspirations of the youth.

In fact, the party had faced criticism from several quarters including from RSS ideologues such as Ratan Sharda, who severely criticised the BJP’s media team, including its IT cell, over its handling of the protests in New Delhi, pointing out that they had no idea about youth anger because they are not in touch with ground realities.

For the BJP that came to power riding high on the success of social media and WhatsApp, advice came from the PM himself as he directed his Cabinet ministers to become more active on Instagram, post reels, and use interactive sessions to connect with the youth—something he did himself to reach out to the protesting youth.

The PM, in his Independence Day speech, announced free online coaching classes for competitive examinations, showcasing it as a way to ease financial burden on poor and middle class families. In another outreach to the youth, Modi announced a programme to train one crore young people in AI skills over the next year.
Moving beyond Gen-Z, the PM extended his outreach to even children from Gen Alpha and announced a nationwide talent hunt for identifying sports talent.
It comes as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which spearheaded the Jantar Mantar protest, has taken the shape of a pressure group and has launched the ‘School Thik Karo” campaign.

The campaign was launched after scores of Gen Alpha students across several states launched protests demanding better school infrastructure including clean water, functional toilets, roads, teachers among others.
Experts point out that the youth outreach announced by Modi shows that the government is thinking seriously about the growing youth discontent.

“The fundamental offerings and youth outreach announced by Prime Minister Modi in his Independence Day speech show one thing quite clearly: the government is thinking seriously about growing youth discontent,” said Sayantan Ghosh, political analyst and author.
He called the emphasis on AI infrastructure, online tuition for competitive examinations and job creation as important.

“The problem is that these themes have appeared repeatedly in election manifestos, government budgets and policy promises across states. Employment, education infrastructure, online learning and, increasingly, AI have become recurring features of political messaging. The real question is not what is being promised, but how much of it is actually being implemented,” he added, pointing out that the speech did not sufficiently address the question of accountability.

“The larger question is whether youth discontent will be viewed merely as an issue of jobs, education and technology, or whether the government is willing to understand it as a deeper demand for accountability and responsiveness.”
However, many like Yashwant Deshmukh, founding director of CVoter,
pointed out that it will also depend on whether these announcements help generate employment, something which has been a major concern for the youth.
The announcements, he said, were expected especially after the Jantar Mantar protest.

“The kind of anger the youth had expressed as long as these announcements practically result in generating jobs, and new opportunities, it will definitely have some impact. However, if it remains rhetorical and on papers, then the issues will remain the same and so will be the concerns of the youth,” Deshmukh said.
The Mood of the Nation tracker has been highlighting that inflation and unemployment are major concerns and need to be resolved, he said.
“If every year these issues are coming up, then surely there is something wrong,” he added.

Social scientist and political analyst Badri Narayan pointed out that PM Modi doesn’t want to leave any room for uncertainty amongst the youth and is reaching out to even the section that was questioning the party.

“This is a positive step and we must welcome it. The BJP’s core support has traditionally come from the youth, and there has been some confusion among the young people, rather amongst a section, that the party is now trying to address which is what his speech indicates,” Narayan said.
He further said that while Modi’s popularity among the youth remains strong, he is also reaching out to the segment that had begun to question the party.

“We should welcome this effort, as it aims to rebuild trust and dispel the doubts that had arisen. A certain narrative has been created, and he does not want to leave any room for uncertainty among young voters about the BJP.”
However, Congress leader Pawn Khera termed the announcements as “too little, too late and too desperate”.

“Today’s grand announcements are just another Modi-era pipe dream with no real implementation plan. This is a desperate attempt to recover the government’s lost legitimacy by dangling fancy announcements before the youth,” he said.

“Free online coaching and AI sound impressive. But this government has a terrible record of last-mile delivery. During COVID, millions of students were left behind because they lacked smartphones, devices, electricity or reliable internet needed for online classes.”

Khera said these same students — those from marginalised backgrounds who most need support to complete their education in an increasingly extractive and exploitative system — are likely to be left behind again under this fresh push for online coaching and AI.
“In reality, BJP is a party of the rich, for the rich. It neither understands nor cares about the interests of the poor and marginalised,” he said.
Author and researcher Chandrachur Ghose said the PM’s address to the youth had two components.
“Firstly, reiteration of all the policies and programmes of the past decade to emphasise how these have opened new horizons in terms of productive opportunities,” he said.

“The second component was to present to the youth a picture of a whole new world of opportunities-expansion of infrastructure, focus on spotting talent in specific areas and providing training and development with definite goals. These opportunities would be in the form of integration with the new economy, deployment of new technologies and involvement in national service.”

Ghose pointed out that a few words on addressing systemic weaknesses would have given the picture of a promising future, a more solid grounding, but perhaps the speech from the Red Fort was not quite the occasion for it.

“The promises were finely balanced not to appear as an effort to counter the grievances of a section of students and youth, but to portray that despite the problem areas a promising future is waiting for them,” he said.

A Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) event meant to commemorate the horrors of Partition turned into an unexpected display of the party’s internal fault lines in Gurugram on Friday, with Union Minister of State for Planning and MP Rao Inderjit Singh publicly objecting to the programme being projected as a “community-specific” event and questioning why local leaders had not been invited.

The State-level Vibhajan Vibhishika Smriti Diwas programme at Sector 29 brought together BJP national president Nitin Nabin, Union Minister Manohar Lal and Haryana BJP president Archana Gupta. But the spotlight soon shifted from Partition remembrance to the politics within the Haryana BJP.

Taking the microphone, Mr. Singh made it clear that he was unhappy with the way the event had been organised. “People from various parts have come to this event. I think local people have not been invited today. I object to this,” he said, before thanking Ms. Gupta for inviting Mr. Nabin and turning the programme into a party event rather than allowing it to remain, in his words, a programme of a “specific community”.

Mr. Singh then directly addressed Mr. Nabin, welcoming him, while pointedly questioning whether he himself would have been invited had the national president not attended. The Gurugram MP drew comparisons with other BJP leaders. If such a programme were held in Panipat, he asked, would Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Bhatia not be invited? And if it were held in Karnal, would local MP Manohar Lal not be invited?

He also took a swipe at Mr. Lal, recalling that Haryana had been the first State to have a Punjabi Chief Minister and stressing that Mr. Lal had become the Chief Minister with the support of people from all communities.
Invoking Gurugram’s political history, Mr. Singh recalled that Dharambir Gaba, the city’s first Punjabi MLA, had won four times – not merely on Punjabi votes, but with support across communities.

“Most of those unsettled from Pakistan came to Haryana, and the people of Haryana welcomed them,” Mr. Singh said, underlining that Partition’s legacy belonged to the people of the entire State rather than any one community.
However, Mr. Singh’s address was stopped midway.

Sources in Mr. Singh’s office said the Minister had not received a formal invitation from the organisers, the Vibhajan Vibhishika Smriti Nyas. According to the sources, when the Chief Minister’s Office contacted Mr. Singh on Thursday afternoon to confirm his participation, his staff pointed out that no formal invitation had been received. The issue reportedly prompted administrative intervention. Ms. Gupta subsequently called Mr. Singh, informed him about Mr. Nabin’s presence and invited him to the programme.

An invitation letter issued by the organisers and shared by Mr. Singh’s office did not list the local MP’s name. An invitation issued by the local administration, however, did mention him as a guest of honour.
Convenor Bodhraj Sikri told The Hindu that the invitation letter from the district administration was forwarded to Mr. Singh on Thursday evening.

IPS Nupur Prasad, who led Sushant Singh Rajput CBI probe, to get President's Medal

Senior IPS officer Nupur Prasad has been selected for the President's Medal for Distinguished Service. The honour highlights her high-profile CBI tenure, including supervision of the Sushant Singh Rajput death probe.

Senior IPS officer Nupur Prasad, who supervised the CBI investigation into the death of actor Sushant Singh Rajput, has been selected for the prestigious President’s Medal for Distinguished Service this year.

Prasad, a 2007-batch AGMUT-cadre IPS officer, recently completed her tenure with the Central Bureau of Investigation and returned to the Delhi Police. She is currently serving as Joint Commissioner of Police in the Economic Offences Wing.

The award citation describes Prasad as an “accomplished officer” and a leader known for “versatility, integrity and institutional vision”. It highlights her work across the Delhi Police, CBI, West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh, including several high-profile investigations and major policing initiatives.
ROLE IN SUSHANT SINGH RAJPUT DEATH PROBE
Prasad’s role in the Sushant Singh Rajput investigation was among the most prominent assignments of her CBI tenure.

Rajput, 34, was found dead at his Bandra residence in Mumbai on June 14, 2020. The Mumbai Police initially registered an accidental death case and investigated the circumstances surrounding his death.
The case took a major turn after Rajput’s father, K K Singh, filed an FIR in Patna against actress Rhea Chakraborty and others, alleging abetment to suicide, financial wrongdoing and harassment.
Following the legal and political controversy surrounding the jurisdiction of the investigation, the CBI took over the case in August 2020.

The investigation continued for nearly five years and involved examination of witnesses, scrutiny of medical and forensic evidence and investigation of allegations of murder, abetment to suicide and other suspected wrongdoing.
The case generated intense public and media scrutiny, with several theories circulating on social media and television, including allegations of poisoning and strangulation.

In March 2025, the CBI filed closure reports before courts in Mumbai and Patna, stating that its investigation had found no evidence of foul play, abetment to suicide or criminal conspiracy in Rajput’s death.
The President’s Medal citation highlights Prasad’s work across several challenging assignments.

As the first DCP of Shahdara, she was tasked with establishing the district’s policing framework from the ground up. During her tenure, she led action against drug networks and gambling operations and worked to make Anand Vihar a “snatching-free zone”.
As DCP, North District, Prasad oversaw security arrangements for major events, including Delhi University elections and Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort.

She also spearheaded community-oriented initiatives, including women’s self-defence training, hygiene camps in collaboration with the Ladli Foundation, youth skill-development programmes and drug de-addiction initiatives with SPYM.
Her career also includes significant assignments outside Delhi. In West Bengal, she handled security arrangements during the 2011 Assembly elections and the Ganga Sagar Mela.
As Superintendent of Police in Arunachal Pradesh, she worked to restore inter-tribal peace and dismantle extortion networks.
CONTRIBUTIONS TO POLICING REFORMS
During her CBI tenure, Prasad supervised some of the agency’s significant cases, including the AgustaWestland investigation and the Sushant Singh Rajput death case.
She also contributed to the CBI Crime Manual 2020 and the agency’s Vision Document. She was associated with preparations for the Interpol General Assembly 2022 and the G20 Cyber Conference.
After returning to the Delhi Police, Prasad introduced the MyKase software for trial monitoring while serving in the Economic Offences Wing.
She also contributed to the Bureau of Police Research and Development’s National Police Mission, Micro Mission.
PRESIDENT’S MEDAL FOR DISTINGUISHED SERVICE
The President’s Medal for Distinguished Service is among the highest service honours conferred on police personnel.

Prasad’s selection recognises a career spanning investigation, law-and-order policing, community outreach, institutional reform and assignments in some of the country’s most challenging security environments.

Her supervision of the Sushant Singh Rajput investigation remains one of the most high-profile assignments of her CBI tenure, with the agency ultimately concluding that there was no evidence of foul play in the actor’s death.

The controversy surrounding Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s alleged objection to the singing of the entire Vande Mataram song during the party’s Independence day celebrations snowballed into a full-blown political feud on Sunday, with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) staging protests across the country and registering complaints against the senior opposition leader.

On Sunday, Union home minister Amit Shah said the Vande Mataram song was sung at the Red Fort and all other places where flag hoisting was held after 80 years of Independence.

"Thousands of people faced bullets and lathis and were jailed for singing Vande Mataram," he said, referring to the use of the revolutionary slogan during the freedom struggle. 20 Blackbucks rewilded in Banni Grasslands on Indiaâs 80th Independence Day by Anant Ambaniâs Vantara

On Indiaâs 80th Independence Day, the Gujarat Forest Department, with technical support from Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre (GZRRC), Vantara, released 20 blackbucks also known as antilope cervicapra, into the Banni Grasslands of Kutch, marking an important milestone in the restoration of native wildlife and the ecological character of this unique grassland landscape.The release comprised five male and 15 female blackbucks, transferred from Vantara, Jamnagar, following the requisite approvals of the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, and the Central Zoo Authority (CZA).

The transfer was undertaken in accordance with prescribed protocols covering veterinary examination, health screening, quarantine, disease surveillance, safe and humane transportation and release. Vantara complied with all the necessary requirements.

The significance of the initiative extends beyond the release of 20 animals. Restoring native herbivores is an important part of rebuilding the ecological fabric of Banni, strengthening its native herbivore community, supporting natural predator prey relationships and contributing to the recovery of a more resilient grassland ecosystem.Banni is a vast grassland landscape supporting pastoral communities and diverse native wildlife. Blackbuck, chinkara, nilgai and wild boar have historically formed part of its herbivore assemblage.

Their recovery, alongside habitat conservation and scientific grassland management, can help restore the ecological character and biodiversity of the landscape.The initiative reflects the broader national commitment to the revival of Indiaâs native species and restoration of its grassland ecosystems, a conservation direction strongly championed under the leadership of the Honâble Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi.

Dr Jaipal Singh, IFS, Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, said, âRestoring native wildlife is fundamental to restoring healthy landscapes. The release of these 20 blackbucks into Banni on Indiaâs Independence Day is an important milestone in our continuing effort to recover the ecological character and biodiversity of this unique grasslands.

20 blackbucks released in Gujarat’s Banni grasslands on Independence Day
Gujarat Forest Department, Vantara release 20 blackbucks in Banni grasslands to boost native wildlife.

Twenty blackbucks were released into Gujarat’s Banni Grasslands on Sunday as part of an initiative to restore native herbivore populations and strengthen the ecosystem of one of India’s largest grassland landscapes.
The Gujarat Forest Department, with technical support from the Greens Zoological Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre (GZRRC), Vantara, released the animals on India’s 80th Independence Day.
Also Read | Vantara a lawful global hub of conservation excellence: UN wildlife trade body
The group comprised five males and 15 females and was transferred from Vantara in Jamnagar after obtaining approvals from the Chief Wildlife Warden, Gujarat, and the Central Zoo Authority.

The animals underwent veterinary examinations, health screening, quarantine and disease surveillance before being transported and released in accordance with prescribed wildlife translocation protocols.
Increase number of blackbucks, restore grassland's native herbivore community

Officials said the initiative is aimed not merely at increasing the number of blackbucks in Banni but at restoring the grassland’s native herbivore community. Blackbuck, chinkara, nilgai and wild boar have historically been part of Banni’s herbivore assemblage.

“Restoring native wildlife is fundamental to restoring healthy landscapes,” Gujarat Chief Wildlife Warden Dr Jaipal Singh, IFS, said. He described the release as an important step in efforts to recover Banni’s ecological character and biodiversity, adding that such restoration requires scientific management, sustained efforts and collaboration.

Banni is a vast grassland landscape that supports pastoral communities as well as a range of native wildlife. Conservationists have emphasised the importance of maintaining healthy herbivore populations in sustaining natural predator-prey relationships and strengthening the resilience of grassland ecosystems.

The release is also part of a wider Gujarat programme for the conservation and translocation of native herbivores. The Central government, through the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, has approved the translocation of 500 blackbucks and 100 chinkaras in Gujarat.

Some components of the broader programme are intended to augment prey populations in connection with the planned cheetah reintroduction programme. However, the Banni release has an additional objective of restoring populations of species native to the grassland.

The Banni Grassland Forest Division has sought Vantara’s technical assistance for the wider translocation programme. This includes specialised vehicles for transporting herbivores, portable boma systems, veterinary expertise and support for the safe handling and transportation of animals.
Vantara has previously supported the Gujarat Forest Department in the rewilding of nearly 80 spotted deer in Barda Wildlife Sanctuary, following approval from the Chief Wildlife Warden.

Ajit Kulkarni, Special Director, Compliance and Due Diligence, Vantara, said successful species restoration involves more than releasing animals and requires an understanding of habitat conditions, animal health, population planning and the participation of local communities.

The Banni initiative brings together the Gujarat Forest Department’s conservation efforts and Vantara’s technical expertise in veterinary care, wildlife management, translocation and post-release monitoring.

The release of the 20 blackbucks marks another step towards restoring native wildlife populations in Banni, with officials stressing that long-term habitat management and sustained monitoring will be crucial to ensuring the success of the programme.

The Congress on Sunday (August 16, 2026) strongly rebutted Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s charge that the party had insulted the National Song Vande Mataram, asserting that it has always respected the song and accusing the BJP of trying to manufacture a political controversy.

He said thousands of freedom fighters had faced bullets, lathis and imprisonment for raising the slogan during the freedom struggle.
Responding to the charge, Congress general secretary (organisation) K. C. Venugopal dismissed the allegation and maintained that the party’s commitment to Vande Mataram was beyond doubt.

Congress General Secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh also launched a sharp attack on the Home Minister, accusing him of attempting to divert attention from more pressing issues.

Chatterjee alleged that there was “discomfort” and repeated attempts to stop the singing of the full version of “Vande Mataram” during the event. He described the alleged incident as “not merely unfortunate but a shameless repetition of a historical mistake”, news agency PTI reported.

In a letter to Gandhi, the BJP MLA from Naihati said he was writing as an ordinary citizen, a patriot and a direct descendant of Bankim Chandra, expressing “deep pain, emptiness, and anger” over the episode.

A video from the Congress event shows Gandhi speaking to party president Mallikarjun Kharge while “Vande Mataram” is being played. Gandhi and Kharge can subsequently be seen allegedly gesturing to stop the song.
The Congress, however, denied that there was any attempt to stop the singing of the full version of “Vande Mataram”. The party said Gandhi was only asking for a chair for Kharge.

Invoking Sri Aurobindo's description of “Vande Mataram” as a mantra that initiated the nation into the “religion of patriotism”, Chatterjee said any reluctance to recite the full song on the soil of free India was an insult to the sacrifices of freedom fighters such as Khudiram Bose.

Chatterjee highlighted the song's role in India's freedom movement, referring to Rabindranath Tagore's rendition of “Vande Mataram” at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress and Sarala Devi Chaudhurani's recitation at the 1905 Benares Congress session.

He also recalled supporters of Bal Gangadhar Tilak singing the song during his 1909 sedition trial and nationalist students at Hyderabad's Osmania University using it as a rallying cry in 1938 despite restrictions imposed by the Nizam.

The BJP MLA alleged that the Congress's “so-called dual policy” towards the song was not new. He referred to the party's decision in 1937 to truncate “Vande Mataram” after objections from Mohammad Ali Jinnah, saying the shadow of that “compromise” was visible again in the party's conduct.

Chatterjee also pointed to the Congress's West Bengal student wing, Chhatra Parishad, which uses the slogan “Mantra moder sanjeevan – Vande Mataram”, and questioned why the party's top leadership would be uncomfortable with the song.

He said “Vande Mataram” was not the property of any political party but part of India's collective memory and Bankim Chandra's legacy. He added that the song was a national symbol earned through the sacrifices of freedom fighters and that respecting it was equivalent to respecting the country's freedom struggle.
Warning that “history forgives no one”, Chatterjee said any leadership that failed to respect its own “mantra of freedom” would eventually be pushed into “the darkness of oblivion”.

He said the alleged incident had deeply hurt the sentiments of people in West Bengal and appealed to Gandhi to introspect and tender an unconditional apology to the country, particularly the people of the state.

At least 7 killed in stampede at Bihar's Ashokdham Temple, CM announces ₹4 lakh ex-gratia for kin of victims
Bihar stampede: Witnesses blamed the lack of crowd management for the stampede.

At least seven devotees were killed and 12 injured in a stampede during the entry of devotees into a temple in Bihar's Lakhisarai district on the auspicious occasion of the third sombari of the Shravan month of the Hindu calendar on Monday. Most of those killed in the stampede were women.

Officials said crowds of devotees became uncontrollable as they attempted to enter the Indramaneshwar Temple in Ashokdham, one of the oldest Shiva temples in Bihar, leading to the stampede after barricades the police had erected for crowd control were broken.
What caused the Bihar stampede?

Lakhisarai district magistrate Shailendra Kumar said the incident took place around 6:40am when some youngsters tried to force their way through a queue, breaking barricades. "Women in the queue fell on each other,” he said, as he rushed to Lakhisarai Sadar Hospital.

Kumar said that security personnel were managing the heavy rush of devotees, and that the situation was under control. “Those said to be injured had actually fallen sick because of extreme humidity and suffocation caused by overcrowded surroundings. They were being treated at the hospital, and their condition is out of danger."
Witnesses blame crowd management

Witnesses blamed the lack of crowd management for the stampede. An estimated 50,000 people gathered at the temple. Eyewitnesses said rumours of an electric current in a pole spread panic among the devotees, as they started running. Locals and devotees tried to pull the trapped people.

A police officer said the crowd grew restless, and many began to jostle. "The situation was soon brought under control." A second police officer said the crowd had started pouring into the temple since Sunday night. “The queue stretched for over six kilometres. It took an average of four hours for a pilgrim to get inside the temple.”
Chief minister Samrat Choudhary expressed grief over the stampede, describing the incident as heart wrenching. He announced ₹4 lakh ex-gratia for families of the deceased.
The CM also said directives have been issued for immediate medical treatment of those injured in the stampede.

“The incident at Ashok Dham in Lakhisarai is extremely tragic and heart-wrenching,” he wrote on X. “The news of the deaths of devotees in the accident has left my heart deeply distressed. My deepest condolences go out to the bereaved families. Necessary instructions have been issued to the administration for the proper and expeditious treatment of the injured. May God grant peace to the departed souls and a swift recovery to the injured.”

The Bihar temple stampede is the latest in a series of such stampedes. It came days after a devotee was killed and over 100 others fell ill during a temporary crowd surge at the annual Jagannath Rath Yatra in Odisha. In January 2025, at least 30 people were killed in a stampede at the 2025 Prayag Kumbh Mela at the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers in Prayagraj. This is the sixth stampede during the Kumbh Mela in 70 years. In the same month, at least six people were killed and 35 injured in a stampede near Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple (Tirupati) in Andhra Pradesh as devotees assembled there to secure free visit passes.

In July 2024, around 121 people died after thousands of devotees rushed to get a closer glimpse of a preacher in Uttar Pradesh's Hathras district. At least 12 people died in a stampede at the Vaishno Devi temple in Jammu and Kashmir after a crowd of devotees tried to enter the shrine in January 2022.

In March, a stampede at Sheetla Mata Temple in Bihar’s Nalanda left eight people dead and 12 others injured amid heavy crowds. The temple was packed with devotees, with witnesses saying barricades broke and people fell and were trampled.

Ashokdham, also known as Indradamneshwar Mahadev Temple, is a prominent Lord Shiva shrine in Bihar’s Lakhisarai district. The temple complex has the main Indradamneshwar Mahadev shrine at its centre, along with temples dedicated to Goddess Parvati, Nandi and Goddess Durga. The temple is particularly crowded during Sawan and Shivratri, when large numbers of devotees visit to offer prayers to Lord Shiva.
