'Deal with China confidently': Jaishankar on India strategy; lays out 3Cs, 4Ds global outlook
Edited by: Vijaya Srivastava / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 22, 2026, 19:37 IST
On China, Jaishankar said India should continue doing business with Beijing while developing the domestic strength needed to compete with it

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Saturday offered a candid assessment of a rapidly changing global landscape, warning that growing geopolitical and economic tensions are creating new challenges for countries and businesses. He also stressed that India must remain engaged with the world's major economies while strengthening its own industrial and economic capabilities.Speaking at the Economic Times World Leaders Forum 2026, Jaishankar said the emerging global environment required countries to reduce vulnerabilities, broaden their economic options and prepare for disruptions rather than rely on assumptions of stability.

He framed his assessment around three defining features of the present world order: competition, conflict and the growing use of economic and strategic leverage. To navigate these pressures, he proposed a four-part approach centred on reducing risks, diversifying partnerships and sources, addressing market distortions and maintaining a margin of safety.On China, Jaishankar said India should continue doing business with Beijing while developing the domestic strength needed to compete with it. He said greater self-reliance, industrialisation and manufacturing capacity would allow India to engage China more confidently rather than disengage from it.

"We have to do business with the entire world. That includes China too. But it is important we deal with them confidently."Jaishankar said India-China relations had gone through a difficult period between 2020 and 2024 because of the border situation, but both countries had an interest in maintaining stable ties. He also said India needed to make up for decades of shortcomings in building its manufacturing and industrial base."So I think a stronger, more self-reliant India, a more industrialised India, a more manufacturing India will be able to actually compete with China as it will with other major countries of the world."
Jaishankar's 3Cs view of the world

"It's not a very comforting answer I'm going to give," Jaishankar said while describing how he sees the world today.He said the world had become increasingly competitive, with countries and policymakers pursuing their interests to a point where competition could turn into conflict."I think what we've seen particularly in the last year or so, but I would really describe it as a growing trend.

It looks increasingly competitive," he said, adding that countries and policymakers were pushing their interests "to a point where you actually have conflicts."He pointed to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the conflict in West Asia as major examples, noting that one had entered its fifth year while there was still no clear "light at the end of the tunnel" for the other.Jaishankar said competition was no longer confined to traditional geopolitical rivalry, with economic and strategic tools increasingly being "weaponised"."This is a world increasingly characterised by choke points," he said, explaining that such a choke point emerges when "a country or a set of countries have established dominance" in a particular field and are prepared to use that dominance to exert pressure.According to Jaishankar, such leverage can "inflict pain" on others, while countries exercising it may believe they are sufficiently insulated from the consequences.

Jaishankar then outlined what he described as a response to these challenges."If I declare the problems in terms of Cs, maybe I move an alphabet beyond," he said, presenting derisking as his first and "biggest mantra"."Derisking will be my biggest mantra," Jaishankar said, stressing that the principle applied not only to businesses but also to politics and strategy.His second D was diversification."The more partners, the more sources that you have, clearly extending that you derisk," he said, arguing that countries and businesses should avoid excessive dependence on a small number of partners or sources.The third was dealing with distortions.

Jaishankar pointed to disruptions in energy, fertiliser and shipping markets linked to conflicts and the emergence of choke points.For his final point, he urged businesses and policymakers to move beyond the traditional principle of "Trust and Verify"."Today I say 'Distrust and Diversify'," he said, arguing that planning should take into account the possibility that "things may not go right".He also warned against excessive reliance on just-in-time supply chains and the assumption that the lowest cost should always determine economic decisions."Don't let your supply chain really be just in time anymore; don't assume that your lowest cost will be the determinant," he said, stressing the importance of building a "margin of safety".
India-China ties need stability

Turning to China, Jaishankar said India's engagement with Beijing should ultimately help modernise the Indian economy and strengthen domestic capabilities, even as trade and other economic interactions continue."But for us, the interaction is the purpose of it is finally to modernise our economy and to develop our capabilities, but even as we do so, obviously there will be trade, there will be other economic interactions with them."He said India and China had experienced a particularly difficult phase between 2020 and 2024."I think we went through a particularly bad patch between the summer of 2020 and the autumn of 2024, and that was primarily an outcome of the situation in the border"However, he said both countries remained major economies and markets for each other, and that greater cooperation could be possible if relations remained stable and moved in a more cooperative direction.At the same time, Jaishankar said India had to address the weaknesses created by decades of inadequate industrialisation."We stand our ground as we have stood in the border.

We develop our strengths, which unfortunately, as I said, from the 1960s for half a century, we did not do.""We have to make up for the shortcomings and you know the the mistakes of the past, and and that is really what we are hoping to do."Jaishankar said building a stronger manufacturing base would be central to India's ability to compete with China and other major economies.

British commandos seized the oil tanker Smyrtos in the English Channel and charged its captain, Ajay Pant. The case has raised questions over sanctions enforcement and the vulnerability of seafarers.
The Indian captain of an oil tanker seized by British commandos in the English Channel has been made a scapegoat, his wife told AFP, as he awaits trial in Britain on sanctions-related charges.
Ajay Pant, 38, has been charged with sanctions offences carrying a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. His trial is scheduled to begin on December 15.
“My husband just became the scapegoat,” Ritu Pant, 36, told AFP in her first interview since his arrest in June. “He was at the wrong place at the wrong time.”
British commandos fast-roped from a helicopter on June 14 to intercept the sanctioned oil tanker Smyrtos, which was captained by Pant.

The vessel is allegedly part of Russia’s shadow fleet, a network of ships with opaque ownership and insurance arrangements that Moscow is accused of using to evade oil sanctions imposed after its invasion of Ukraine.

According to MarineTraffic, the Smyrtos sailed from Russia’s Ust-Luga port on June 5 and passed through the Baltic Sea, with Egypt’s Port Said listed as its destination. As it crossed the English Channel, British commandos intercepted the vessel. Then-prime minister Keir Starmer described the operation as “a blow to Russia”.
Pant’s wife said her husband was a victim of the circumstances and was struggling in custody after being denied bail.
“He was broken and he was just crying,” she told AFP, recalling their first phone call after his arrest. “He didn't know what had happened to him... He just said, ‘I am in jail, please take me out’.”

Prosecutors allege Pant was the “master of the ship” and knew about its cargo, which consisted of around 98,000 tonnes of oil. Pant’s lawyer told a court that the captain was “simply following orders” as an employee of the vessel’s owner. His wife has also maintained that his responsibility was to safely transport the cargo to its destination.
The case raises complex legal questions and could become an important test as European countries intensify action against Russia’s shadow fleet.
It is believed to be the first case in Europe in which sanctions-violation charges have been brought against a ship’s captain rather than only the vessel or its owners.

India’s Foreign Ministry has said its consular officials visited Pant to enquire about his wellbeing. Pant is the only sailor from the vessel to have been charged. Most of the other 24 crew members have since been repatriated.
The Smyrtos remains anchored off England’s southern coast.

The case has also raised concerns among seafarers about being caught between geopolitical powers, according to Steve Yandell, coordinator of the seafarers’ section of the International Transport Workers’ Federation.
India, with more than 320,000 seafarers, is a major contributor to the global merchant shipping workforce.

Manan Mishra's BCI tenure under SC challenge: Plea seeks removal, fresh elections and term limits.

NEW DELHI: A day after Bar Council of India (BCI) chairman Manan Kumar Mishra said he would not resign from the post, a petition has been filed in the Supreme Court challenging his decade-long tenure. The plea seeks his removal, fresh elections and reforms to the rules governing the Chairman's term.The plea, filed by advocate Yogamaya MG through advocate Deepak Prakash, challenges the legality of Mishra's prolonged tenure and contends that Rule 12(2) of the BCI Rules prescribes a two-year term for the Chairman and Vice-Chairman, or until cessation of membership, whichever is earlier.

The petitioner has also challenged an April 21, 2025 Gazette notification that purportedly extends Mishra's tenure until 2030, arguing that an administrative notification cannot override the statutory framework governing the BCI.The plea has urged the apex court to quash the notification and direct the BCI to withdraw or rescind it."Although Rule 12(2) prescribes a two-year tenure, no meaningful restriction exists upon repeated re-election. Consequently, the office has remained with the same individual for nearly twelve years," the petition stated.It further argued that such prolonged concentration was "prima facie inconsistent with the representative scheme embodied in Section 4(1)(c)", under which every State Bar Council contributes to the composition of the BCI.

"A national institution representing the entire legal profession should not permit its highest office to remain concentrated indefinitely in one individual or a narrow regional grouping," the petition stated.Among its reliefs, the plea seeks Mishra's removal, fresh elections within a time-bound period under independent supervision, and the introduction of a cumulative cap on the number of years a person can serve as BCI Chairman.The petitioner has also sought a cooling-off period and a transparent rotational mechanism to give representatives from different States and regions an opportunity to head the BCI.The plea further asks the Supreme Court to constitute an independent committee headed by a former Supreme Court judge or former Chief Justice of a High Court.

According to the petition, the committee could be assisted by an auditor nominated by the CAG, along with financial and technical experts.The petitioner has also raised concerns over the functioning and finances of the BCI Trust, "PEARL-FIRST", and the financial affairs of the All India Bar Examination. It has sought an independent inquiry and a time-bound audit of statutory funds, examination receipts, institutional receipts, Trust finances, vendor contracts and related party transactions.The petition traces Mishra's tenure as BCI Chairman to 2012.

It states that although he briefly demitted office in 2014, he returned as Chairman in November that year and has remained in the post since. Mishra was elected unopposed again in March 2025, which the petitioner claims was his seventh consecutive term.The plea also refers to Mishra becoming a Rajya Sabha member after being nominated by the BJP in 2024.

It clarifies that the petitioner does not contend that political affiliation, by itself, makes Mishra ineligible, but raises concerns about the perception of institutional neutrality."Petitioner does not seek the removal of any individual merely because of political affiliation or personal disagreement with any office bearer," the plea stated."The challenge is directed against structural illegality, alleged concentration of institutional control, prolonged concentration of statutory power, violation of mandatory statutory provisions governing tenure and elections, arbitrary exercise of regulatory authority, absence of transparency and accountability, and failure to preserve the representative democratic character contemplated under the Advocates Act, 1961," it added.

The petition comes a day after Mishra rejected calls for his resignation following a protest by lawyers outside the BCI office in New Delhi."I have served as the Chairman of the Bar Council of India for 12 to 14 years because I was elected. Manan Mishra represents 25 lakh lawyers; he will not step down simply," Mishra said.

He also defended the BCI's handling of the NALSAR University controversy, calling the students' boycott of the Chief Justice of India "deeply objectionable".Mishra said the BCI withdrew an order against the students within 15 minutes. He also said around 15 students had gathered outside the BCI office demanding his resignation.The controversy followed a BCI order on August 13 directing State Bar Councils not to enrol NALSAR University's 2026 graduating batch amid a student campaign linked to recent judicial developments and the invitation to CJI Surya Kant to their convocation.

After criticism, the BCI permitted enrolment and withdrew the proceedings, saying most students were innocent. CJI Kant later termed the order "absolutely unnecessary", upheld the students' right to protest and barred punitive action against NALSAR students or faculty.

His wife, however, said a captain's job is primarily to ensure that the cargo reaches its destination safely. “The master's responsibility in any vessel is to just get the cargo safely to its destination,” she said, AFP reported.
His defence has argued that he was acting on instructions from the vessel’s owner and had no role in determining the commercial arrangements surrounding the cargo.
Wife says ‘he was broken, crying’
Pant has remained in British custody after being denied bail. For his family back in India, the circumstances of his arrest have been difficult to comprehend.
Ritu said her husband sounded devastated when she first spoke to him after his arrest. “He was broken and he was just crying,” she said.
“He didn't know what had happened to him... He just said, ‘I am in jail, please take me out’," she was quoted as saying by AFP.
Just days before his arrest, he had spoken to her about the dangers at sea after Indian sailors were killed around the Strait of Hormuz amid the conflict in the Middle East.
“He said that the sea is becoming very difficult now,” Ritu said. “I was just praying, and telling him that, 'just be calm, be careful and just keep contacting us'.”
Now, his mother Deepa is appealing to the Indian government to intervene.

Pant is the only crew member from the ship to face charges. The other 24 sailors have largely been sent back to their home countries, while the Smyrtos remains anchored off the southern English coast.
His trial is due to begin on December 15.

Anwar Sadat of the Indian Society of International Law said the case presented “complex” legal issues. The prosecution is also being closely watched because it is believed to be the first instance in Europe of sanctions-related criminal charges being brought against a tanker captain rather than focusing only on the vessel or its owners.
David Hammond of Human Rights at Sea International said the outcome could have consequences beyond Pant himself.
“The case carries implications far beyond the fate of a single ship, its cargo or its master,” he wrote in an analysis for Lloyd's List Intelligence.
The issue carries particular weight for India, which has more than 3,20,000 seafarers working across the global merchant shipping industry.
The Indian government has been keeping a close watch on the case through the Indian High Commission in London, according to a statement released in June.
In a letter to Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, the High Commission shared an update on Pant’s case, according to an official release reported by news agency PTI.

Indian officials first established contact with Pant through the prison’s telephone system on June 19. During the conversation, Pant said he was in good health, had access to medical care and was regularly in touch with his wife.

Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks off Odisha coast, 2 survivors rescued, 22 missing
A Panama-flagged cargo ship carrying 24 crew members sank after communication was lost off Odisha, prompting a major Coast Guard-Navy rescue operation as the search for survivors continues.

A Panama-flagged bulk carrier carrying 24 crew members sank in the Bay of Bengal, around 240 nautical miles from Odisha's Paradip coast, on Saturday, triggering a major search-and-rescue operation by the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) and Indian Navy.

The vessel, MV Ocean Winner (IMO 9145530), was carrying 20 Chinese, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi crew member, according to the ICG. Its last port of call was Paradip and its next scheduled port was Singapore.
The ICG has so far confirmed that two survivors have been rescued from two liferafts, while the search continues for the remaining 22 crew members.
COMMUNICATION LOST WITH MV OCEAN WINNER

The ICG's Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Sri Vijaya Puram received information at 11:48 am from a company associated with the vessel about the loss of communication with MV Ocean Winner.
The company also requested search-and-rescue assistance, the ICG said.
The bulk carrier was carrying iron ore from Odisha and was bound for Singapore.
Following the alert, the MRCC diverted MT Aisopos, a commercial vessel that was operating in the vicinity, to search for MV Ocean Winner or liferafts and render assistance.
MT Aisopos recovered two survivors from two liferafts at around 8 pm, according to the ICG.
The condition of the rescued crew members was not immediately available.
The Indian Coast Guard and Indian Navy have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation to locate the remaining crew members.
ICG ships Varad and Anmol have been deployed for the search, while Vijit has been sent from Sri Vijaya Puram to augment the operation.
Other vessels in the area are also being coordinated with as authorities continue efforts to locate survivors and liferafts.
MV Ocean Winner had 24 crew members on board when it sank — 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi national.
With two survivors rescued so far, the search continues for the remaining 22 crew members.

The exact circumstances that led to the sinking of the vessel have not yet been established. Further details about the ship's condition before it sank and the status of the missing crew members are awaited.

The much-awaited meeting between the chief ministers of neighbouring Karnataka and Tamil Nadu took place in Mahabalipuram near Chennai amid a rain-deficient year and a long-running dispute over Cauvery water sharing. The meeting was held as part of the 31st Southern Zonal Council, chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah and attended by chief ministers and deputy chief ministers from southern states.

The contentious issue of Karnataka's Mekedatu dam project in Ramanagaram district, around 100 km south of Bengaluru and near the point where the Cauvery enters Tamil Nadu, has now emerged as a major flashpoint in the drought-hit region. Turning up the heat on Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay on Thursday, the state's main opposition party, the DMK, alleged that he remained silent while his Karnataka counterpart, DK Shivakumar, spoke in favour of constructing the Mekedatu dam at the meeting of southern chief ministers.

Addressing a press conference, DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran said, "At the meeting of southern chief ministers held in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar openly spoke in favour of constructing the Mekedatu dam. However, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay, who was present there, remained silent without uttering a single word in opposition."

For his part, Vijay, without specifically mentioning the Mekedatu reservoir, pointed out while addressing the Southern Zonal Council meeting that any interventions by an upper riparian state that could affect the lower riparian state's fair share should proceed within a legal framework.

The Mekedatu project has remained a bone of contention for years, with Tamil Nadu arguing that any increase in water storage by Karnataka, the upper riparian state, could prove disastrous for the downstream state, especially during dry years.

In a letter to PM Modi earlier, Vijay highlighted Clause XI of the Cauvery Tribunal Award, which states: “Any upper riparian State shall not take any action so as to affect the scheduled deliveries of water to the lower riparian States. However, the States concerned can by mutual agreement and in consultation with the Regulatory Authority, make any amendment in the pattern of water deliveries.”

Ahead of Shivakumar's meeting with Vijay, a decision by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) directing Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days from July 29, amid deficient southwest monsoon rainfall and low reservoir levels, did not go down well with pro-Kannada groups. They took to the streets and called for a statewide bandh on August 13 to protest the CWRC's directive. The CWRC's decision was ratified by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) only two days later.

However, between July 29 and August 2, Karnataka released only a fraction of the mandated water, prompting the Vijay government to knock on the Supreme Court's doors on August 3 to enforce the CWMA's order and seek inspections of Karnataka's reservoirs every 10 days.

Meanwhile, Shivakumar on Thursday stressed that he had assured Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, that their interests would be safeguarded in the proposed Mekedatu dam project.

Shivakumar said five TMC had been set aside for drinking water, while the rest of the water stored in the proposed reservoir would go to Tamil Nadu. He said he had made it clear to Amit Shah that, apart from the five TMC meant for drinking water, all the remaining water from the Mekedatu dam would be released to Tamil Nadu, even if there was only a single drop. He added that Tamil Nadu and Puducherry should have confidence that the project was being planned for their benefit as well, and not solely for Karnataka.
At the Southern Zonal Council meeting earlier, Shivakumar admitted that the Mekedatu project was important for both Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

Referring to a conversation before the meeting, he said Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu had told him that the Cauvery dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu should be resolved. Shivakumar said every drop of water from the Mekedatu project would support farmers in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, and added, "Help us to help you."

Describing rivers such as the Cauvery, Krishna, Tungabhadra, Pennar and Palar as the lifelines of southern India, Shivakumar said the approach should shift from water sharing to water cooperation. He said rivers did not follow political boundaries and that water should unite states instead of becoming a cause of division.

Referring to the June 25 meeting involving Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, he said the three states had shown that interstate water disputes could be handled through talks. He said they had discussed resolving water-sharing issues amicably and had agreed to work towards a lasting solution to the water crisis with the involvement of Union Jal Shakti Minister CR Patil.
Shivakumar said Karnataka recognised that every riparian state had valid needs and that its stand was based on three principles: equity, transparency and cooperation.

At the same time, he said cooperation had to work both ways and that Karnataka's lawful share under tribunal awards, along with the timely completion of projects meant to benefit its farmers, must be protected. Calling the June meeting with Andhra Pradesh and Telangana a historic landmark in interstate water relations, he said Chandrababu Naidu and Revanth Reddy had joined him as partners rather than competitors, adding that this reflected Karnataka's approach.

Mekedatu is a multipurpose project proposed by Karnataka that involves the construction of a balancing reservoir near Kanakapura in Ramanagara district. Tamil Nadu has opposed the plan, saying it fears the state would be affected if it goes ahead.
Karnataka officials say the project is intended to supply 4.75 TMC of drinking water to Bengaluru and nearby areas, generate 400 MW of power, and is estimated to cost Rs 9,000 crore at 2019 rates.
TVK's Vijay hits 100 as Tamil Nadu CM, then goes on a hard-hitting spree with bills
If his first 100 days were about establishing the new TVK government, the days immediately after have offered a glimpse of a more assertive Vijay.

Century up, celebrations over, Vijay is already back at the crease. The Tamil Nadu CM's days after completing 100 days have been a whirlwind of announcements, political sparring and one particularly swift U-turn.

From raising Aavin's milk procurement price and expanding maternity leave to announcing vehicles and allowances for MLAs and threatening to open “corruption files” against the previous DMK government, Vijay's post-century phase has been anything but quiet.

If his first 100 days were about establishing the new TVK government, the days immediately after have offered a glimpse of a more assertive Vijay, willing to spend, reverse course and draw political battle lines.
A flurry of decisions after the century
One of the biggest bursts of announcements came in the Assembly, where Vijay unveiled measures covering milk producers, legislators, healthcare and women government employees.
The government raised Aavin's milk procurement price from ₹38 to ₹41 per litre, benefiting more than 3.16 lakh milk producers. The move will cost the state an additional ₹30 crore a month.

Vijay also announced that all MLAs would get government vehicles and a ₹1 lakh monthly package, comprising ₹75,000 towards fuel, maintenance and driver expenses and ₹25,000 for an assistant for office work. The government said the move was intended to help legislators travel through their constituencies and take up development work.
The decision has already triggered criticism from the DMK, which argued that MLAs who already own vehicles should be excluded from the scheme.

Alongside the political and administrative announcements came a significant expansion of healthcare cover. The state's chief minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme was expanded from ₹5 lakh to ₹25 lakh a year.
One year of maternity leave for a third child
The government also announced a major change to maternity leave for women government employees.

The maternity leave available for a third child will be increased from 12 weeks to 365 days. Until now, women government employees with fewer than two children were eligible for one year of maternity leave, while those with two or more children could get up to 12 weeks.
The decision puts women's welfare and empowerment alongside the government's recent welfare announcements and marks another expansion of benefits under the new administration.
From order to U-turn in minutes

The hectic pace was also accompanied by an administrative embarrassment. Tamil Nadu's College Education Department issued an order asking officials to take coordinated action to prevent students and youth from government arts and science colleges from joining protests organised by Left parties and the Tamil Nadu Cockroach Janata Party.
The directive described the matter as “very urgent” and asked officials to coordinate with other departments and district administrations.
The order was withdrawn within minutes, with the department rolling back its communication to college principals.
Vijay flashes the corruption files
If the student-protest order produced a quick retreat, Vijay's confrontation with the DMK went in the opposite direction.

The Assembly witnessed heated exchanges over alleged irregularities in a ₹5.54-crore tender linked to the proposed relocation of the chief minister's office. The issue was followed by another clash over alleged discrepancies in road-laying works.
Vijay responded with a warning that he had files relating to alleged corruption during the previous DMK regime.
“I will reveal the corruption files from the previous DMK regime at an appropriate time. I have two files on my desk. Don't force me to do it now,” he said.

The warning came after public works minister Aadhav Arjuna said the government would soon release a detailed White Paper, signalling that the TVK government's battle with its predecessor could become a defining feature of the next phase of its tenure.
The frantic pace of government business has also fed into the image Vijay's ministers are building around him.
Aadhav Arjuna has described Vijay as a “political monk”, saying the chief minister works for 18 to 20 hours a day and can begin calling ministers at 4am for updates on their departments.
According to Arjuna, Vijay spends much of his time at the Secretariat, asking what needs to be done next and looking for problems across departments, particularly corruption and financial leakages.
The description fits neatly with the government's attempt to present Vijay as a hands-on administrator rather than simply an actor-turned-politician occupying the chief minister's chair.
The first 100 days: Welfare, promises and plenty of questions

Vijay's first 100 days were dominated by a substantial welfare push. On his first day in office, he signed orders for 200 units of free electricity for eligible households, a dedicated women's safety force and anti-narcotics task forces.

The government subsequently announced a ₹6,220-crore cooperative farm-loan waiver, expanded the school breakfast programme, allocated funds for laptops for college students and rolled out welfare measures for women and newborns. It also announced the closure of 717 TASMAC liquor shops located near educational institutions, places of worship and transport points.

But the first century was not without turbulence. The government faced questions over the implementation of election promises, the Cauvery water dispute, law and order, the state's finances and allegations of corruption. The opposition also accused Vijay's government of putting its “stickers” on schemes introduced by the previous DMK administration.

The Karur stampede case, which dates to a TVK rally addressed by Vijay before he became chief minister, remained another major issue. Political clashes with the DMK also intensified, including over the Udhayanidhi Stalin-Trisha controversy.

The government's 100-day report, “100 Days of Governance – A Government for Generations”, presented the period as one of welfare expansion and administrative change. But the challenges facing the government suggest that the next phase will be judged less by the number of announcements and more by their implementation, finances and political consequences.

NEW DELHI: Punjab Congress leaders on Friday sought to distance the party's state unit from Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda's remarks describing former party MP and 1984 anti-Sikh riots convict Sajjan Kumar as a "role model nationwide".

The leaders said the party stood with those who were killed and affected by the violence and that it was Hooda's "personal views".The pushback from Punjab Congress came a day after Sajjan Singh Kumar, who was serving a life sentence in connection with the 1984 riots, died at the age of 84 at Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi.Hooda had described Kumar's death as an "irreparable loss" to the country's political landscape and said he had been a prominent figure whose connect with people was "exemplary".The remarks triggered sharp criticism from Sikh groups, opposition parties and families of riot victims, forcing Congress leaders in Punjab to clarify that Hooda's comments did not reflect their position.
'We stand with those who died'

Congress MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Kumar had committed "misdeeds", had been punished for them and could not be held up as a model for political leadership."Sajjan Kumar did misdeeds. He has been punished for his actions.

A leader does not lead in harming others. We stand with those who died due to him," Aujla said in Amritsar.Asked specifically about Hooda's remarks, Aujla said they should be viewed as the Haryana MP's personal opinion."It must be the personal opinion of Hooda ji but our view is that whatever happened and whoever it happened with, we stand with them, the victims," he said.Punjab Congress working president Raj Kumar Verka also sought to put the focus on the victims of the violence."Sajjan Kumar's life had been full of controversies.

This is a matter related to Punjab and Punjabis have been hurt. If Sajjan Kumar is being held responsible for it, we first stand in support of those innocent people; Sajjan Kumar comes only later," Verka said."I don't know who said what. We are Punjabis and we will continue to stand with Punjabis," he added.Congress MP Manish Tewari, however, declined to comment directly on Hooda's statement, saying he had not read it."I haven't read the statement, so it won't be correct to comment on it," Tewari said

Hooda's comments came after Kumar's death on Thursday.Speaking to ANI, Hooda described Kumar's death as a loss to the political landscape and praised his public connect."Today, the country's political landscape has suffered an irreparable loss... He is cited as a role model nationwide," Hooda had said.The remarks quickly became controversial given Kumar's conviction in cases related to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, which followed the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi by her Sikh bodyguards.Kumar was a three-time parliamentarian and had faced criminal proceedings over the violence for decades. His legal journey included both acquittals and convictions before higher courts.

The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal sharply criticised Hooda and questioned whether his remarks represented the Congress's broader position.BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu accused Kumar and his associates of systematically targeting Sikh families during the 1984 violence and alleged that the Congress leadership had protected him for years.Bittu called on the Punjab and Delhi Congress units to clarify their position on Hooda's comments.The Shiromani Akali Dal also demanded an apology from Hooda and the Congress.SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia condemned the statement and said Congress should apologise."How can a person like Jagdish Tytler, HKL Bhagat...and all those who killed our innocent Sikh brothers in broad daylight and are responsible for the murder of around 3,000 people during the 1984 riots, be called role models?" Majithia said.He also questioned whether Hooda would continue to remain in the Congress after making the remarks.SAD leader Daljeet Singh Cheema said Hooda should have considered the impact of his comments on families whose homes were destroyed and relatives killed during the violence."When you glorify the life of such people in public, it causes a great deal of hurt to the Sikh community," Cheema said.The president of the 1984 Anti-Sikh Riots Victim Welfare Society, Surjit Singh, also condemned Hooda's remarks, saying victims had still not received justice.
Victims' family react to Sajjan Kumar's death

The controversy unfolded alongside emotional reactions from families affected by the 1984 violence.Ganga Kaur, a member of a riot-affected family, said members of her family had been killed during the violence."Members of our family were burned alive in front of us. Sajjan Kumar died naturally, but we would have found greater peace if he had been executed," she told ANI.Another victim-family member, who identified himself as Surjit Singh, said seven members of his family were burned alive during the riots."It is very unfortunate that Deepender Hooda is siding a criminal.
He should be ashamed of praising a person who is responsible for the massacre of so many people," he said.Sajjan Kumar died at Safdarjung Hospital on Thursday at the age of 84.

Hospital authorities said he had a history of high blood pressure and Parkinson's disease and had been admitted after being brought to the hospital by police with altered sensorium.Kumar had been serving a life sentence after the Delhi high court in December 2018 overturned his acquittal in the Raj Nagar case, relating to the killing of five members of a Sikh family and the burning of a gurdwara during the 1984 violence.

He surrendered and was lodged in Tihar Jail in December 2018.In February 2025, a Delhi court sentenced Kumar to another life term in the Saraswati Vihar case over the killings of Jaswant Singh and his son Tarundeep Singh during the riots. The court spared him the death penalty, citing his age, medical condition and conduct while serving his earlier sentence.In another case relating to violence in Janakpuri and Vikaspuri, a Rouse Avenue court acquitted Kumar in January 2026 of charges linked to the killing of Sohan Singh and his son-in-law Avtar Singh and the burning of Gurcharan Singh. The Delhi high court subsequently issued notice on an appeal against the acquittal.(With agency inputs)

“Be loud, be proud and fight for your space in society,” he told the girl students at the AISSMS ground on Saturday (August 22, 2026) evening amid a rousing welcome. Speaking in Marathi, he said, “Pune mhanje prem [Pune means love],” drawing cheers from the youngsters.

His address, which lasted well over an hour, was interspersed with interactions with young women from different backgrounds who spoke of their concerns. He said the 70 crore women of India are more important than the 70 crore men of the country.

Calling the BJP leadership responsible for the “return of the Manusmriti”, he played a clip of Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressing shock at the foul language used by young girls during the Jantar Mantar protest, terming it a “cultural shock.”

“At Jantar Mantar, bad words were used by both boys and girls. And yet, the PM expressed cultural shock only about the girls. The message was that it is okay for the boys to use bad words, not the girls,” he said, adding that the BJP leaders believed that 80% of rapes happened because of women.

“We don’t want an India where it is believed that boys should get full freedom, but that girls should be kept in a cage at home. We want justice. We want that everyone should be respected. Ways of control, disguised as concern
Terming violence, disrespect, control and time as measures of exerting control over women, he cited statistics to illustrate their impact on women’s freedom and participation.

“Women are controlled through violence. Every six out of 100 women are raped in India. That is direct physical violence. He claimed that 60% of girls cannot go out of the house alone, and 45% drop out of school due to household responsibilities or marriage. He also said that only 8% of women in India own property independently.

Fear of disrespect was another way of controlling women, he said, with 99% of cases of sexual violence going unreported due to shame. “84% of women have to ask permission to work, and if you are a woman, you get paid 25% less than a man,” he said.
Speaking about how time is weaponised, he said girls have to face additional pressure at a young age, thereby limiting their opportunities.
The Manusmriti is back, he said, adding that girls should not have to bear an additional burden. He also asked tribal girls to invite him to the ongoing protest in Pune over tribal issues.

“The party should not claim that it has not left Hindutva,” the Shiv Sena said after issuing a cartoon on the incident. Earlier in the day, the police booked NSUI workers following a confrontation with ABVP workers at a college hostel in Pune.

Age limit, two-term cap: DMK passes nine resolutions for sweeping organisational overhaul
Edited by: Karan Manral / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 22, 2026, 14:53 IST
Stalin acknowledges that the changes would be âstringentâ and difficult for some to accept.

NEW DELHI: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) on Saturday unveiled a structural overhaul of its organisation following its defeat in the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections in April, when it lost power after a single term.DMKâs executive committee, headed by party supremo and former chief minister MK Stalin, met at Anna Arivalayam, the partyâs state headquarters in Chennai, and passed nine key resolutions aimed at radically restructuring the organisation.

Addressing the meeting, Stalin acknowleded that the changes would be "stringent" and even "difficult" for some to accept."The functioning of our party office-bearers is also one of the reasons for our defeat. We must first acknowledge our mistakes. We are going to make several changes in the partyâs organisational structure. They will certainly be stringent, and for some, they may even be difficult to accept,â the former chief minister said.âGoing forward, we are going to introduce age limits and terms of office for various organisational posts, according to the responsibilities involved. We are going to give a larger number of organisational responsibilities to newcomers.

We can regain political success only by restructuring the party. We must carry out the organisational reforms as quickly as possible,â he added.Under the new blueprint, the DMK leadership has introduced strict age limits, a mandatory two-term cap for all posts and a major expansion of organisational districts, with the aim of professionalising party operations and facilitating generational succession.The DMK will increase the number of organisational districts from 78 to 110, with each district broadly covering two assembly constituencies to ensure more localised administration.

Once Stalin formally releases the boundary maps for the 110 revamped districts, district executive committees will have to convene within 15 days under the supervision of the party headquarters to implement the transition.The standalone post of âcity secretaryâ in major urban centres such as Coimbatore and Tambaram has also been abolished. Instead, urban zones will be redrawn based on voter density, with Chennai Corporation Area Committees averaging 40,000 voters and those in other corporations averaging 30,000 voters per committee.

Following Stalinâs defeat in his Kolathur Assembly constituency in Chennai, the DMK is now being led in the Tamil Nadu assembly by his son and former deputy chief minister Udhayanidhi Stalin, who is now serving as the leader of the opposition.

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday held his first meeting with the party's newly appointed national office-bearers to discuss preparations for upcoming assembly elections and grassroots outreach, party sources said.The meeting at the BJP headquarters focused on poll preparations, grassroots mobilisation and communicating government initiatives to the public, according to news agency PTI.

Former Union minister Smriti Irani has been appointed one of the party's eight national general secretaries.B L Santhosh has been retained as national general secretary (organisation), while Vinod Tawde and Sunil Bansal have also retained their positions as general secretaries.The general secretary team also includes Biplab Kumar Deb, Gajendra Patel, Satish Poonia, Harish Dwivedi and Sanjay Bhatia.

Deepender Hooda makes U-turn after backlash over Sajjan Kumar 'role model' remark
Asked by reporters in Gurugram on Sunday whether he had called Sajjan Kumar a role model, Deepender Hooda said, “I did not use the words.”

Facing backlash over his alleged remarks describing former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar as a "role model", Rohtak Congress MP Deepender Hooda on Sunday denied using the phrase and expressed regret if his comments hurt anyone's feelings.
Kumar, a controversial former Congress MP who was serving two life sentences in connection with the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, died at the age of 80 on Thursday.
Also Read | Sajjan Kumar row: Punjab Congress distances itself from Hooda’s ‘irreparable loss’ remark
While condoling Kumar's death, Hooda had described it as a "loss to the country's political landscape" and praised the former MP's "connect with people and contribution to Delhi's development".

The remarks triggered criticism from within the Congress, with senior Haryana Congress leader Kuldeep Sharma writing to party president Mallikarjun Kharge and seeking Hooda's removal from the Congress Working Committee (CWC) for "extolling the virtues" of Sajjan Kumar.
Hooda's comments also drew sharp reactions in Punjab, where the SAD, BJP and AAP accused the Congress of having an "anti-Sikh mindset".
Asked by reporters in Gurugram on Sunday whether he had called Kumar a role model, Hooda said, "I did not use the words, nor did I harbour any such sentiment."

He added, "These words are being put in my mouth by those who wish to play politics by undermining the spirit of brotherhood. I had no intention of hurting anyone's feelings; those who know me are aware that I never harboured any intent to cause hurt to anyone."
Also Read | Punjab Congress distances itself from Deepender’s remarks on Sajjan
Statement being ‘distorted’: Hooda
Hooda later posted a video on X seeking to clarify his remarks on Sajjan Kumar.

"For the past two days, I have observed that my statement is being distorted and presented out of context. An English word – 'role model' – is being attributed to me, which I never uttered, nor did I ever intend to convey any such meaning.
"I had absolutely no intention of hurting anyone. And I could never even imagine causing hurt to our brothers in the Sikh community," Hooda said.
He added, "Nevertheless, the Sikh community is like family to us. If anyone's feelings have been hurt, I express my regret as your brother. My intention or objective was never to cause anyone pain."

Hooda, who ended the video with "Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh", called the Sikh community a glorious part of the nation and said, "I take pride in a community whose sacrifices for us can never be forgotten."

"Whether it is the defence of our borders or the struggle for Independence, we take pride in the sacrifices the Sikh community has made for the nation; we share a bond akin to family. Whenever the need arose, we always stood together like brothers – that is the nature of our relationship," he said.

"During the recent farmers' agitation (against the now repealed farm laws), when our farmer brothers arrived from Punjab, I was among the first to reach out and stand with them. We have always stood together in every struggle," Hooda said.
"On the events of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, we stand with the Sikh community in their fight for justice. They deserve justice, and no guilty person should be spared," Hooda said in the video.

The clarification came after AAP MLA from Punjab Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal on Saturday said the wounds of the 1984 anti-Sikh massacre remained alive in the hearts of Sikhs and described Hooda's remarks as deeply hurtful.

Three FIRs have been registered against 39 named people and more than 900 unidentified people following clashes during protests by job aspirants in Jharkhand’s Giridih and Hazaribag, officials said on Sunday.
The protests over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations turned violent when demonstrators attempted to burn effigies of Chief Minister Hemant Soren.
The cases come a day after Ranchi police registered three FIRs against 14 named and 200 unidentified people for allegedly obstructing government work and clashing with police.
In Hazaribag, Korra police registered an FIR against 18 named people and 700 unidentified people over violence during an attempt to burn Soren’s effigy on August 21.

The accused have been booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to assault on police personnel, obstruction of public servants and unlawful assembly.

Two FIRs were registered at Giridih Town police station over clashes on Friday and Saturday.

2 rescued, 22 missing after China-bound iron ore vessel sinks off Odisha coast
Two of the 24 crew members aboard the ship were rescued from life rafts, while an intensive search is underway for the remaining seafarers,

Twenty-two seafarers are missing in deep sea, while two have been rescued after a Panama-flagged cargo ship MV Ocean Winner carrying more than 72,000 tonnes of iron ore fines from Odisha to China sank in the Bay of Bengal, about 230 nautical miles off the eastern coast, officials said on Sunday.
Two of the 24 crew members aboard the ship were rescued from life rafts, while an intensive search is underway for the remaining seafarers, officials said.

The vessel left Paradip Port on Friday after loading iron ore fines and was bound for China. It reportedly sank in deep waters on Saturday after contact was lost. The crew comprised 20 Chinese nationals, three from Myanmar and one Bangladeshi national, officials said.
The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Sri Vijaya Puram (formerly Port Blair) activated a search-and-rescue operation after receiving a distress alert and losing contact with the vessel.
Indian Coast Guard ships and a Navy maritime surveillance aircraft have been deployed, while merchant vessels in the area have been alerted to assist in the search.

“MRCC Sri Vijaya Puram initiated a swift SAR effort following a distress alert and loss of contact with MV Ocean Winner, nearly 230 NM South East off Paradip,” Coast Guard spokesperson Commandant Amit Uniyal said. “Diverted via international safety net, MT AISOPOS successfully rescued two survivors from life rafts.”

The rescued crew members were being brought to the mainland for medical treatment. “We are yet to verify their nationalities,” said the spokesperson. He said rough sea conditions in the Bay of Bengal were hampering the search.

The cause of the sinking has not been established. Authorities are expected to examine whether adverse weather, sea conditions, problems involving the cargo, mechanical failure or other factors contributed to the incident. The loss of the vessel from tracking systems before it sank is also likely to form part of the investigation.

Ports, shipping and waterways minister Sarbananda Sonowal expressed concern over the incident, saying all agencies were coordinating the search and rescue efforts. “Deeply concerned by the unfortunate incident involving MV OCEAN WINNER off the coast of Odisha,” Sonowal said in a social media post.
The MV Ocean Winner, built in 1998, had a deadweight capacity of about 72,928 tonnes, according to available vessel details.
The incident occurred during the southwest monsoon, when rough seas and heavy weather can pose risks to vessels carrying bulk cargoes.

Paradip is one of India’s major ports for bulk commodities and handles large volumes of iron ore, coal and other mineral cargoes. Bulk carriers regularly sail from the port to international destinations across the Bay of Bengal.
The sinking recalls earlier accidents involving bulk carriers carrying iron ore from Indian ports.

In September 2009, the Mongolian-flagged MV Black Rose sank a few kilometres from Paradip after developing a hole in its hull. The vessel was carrying about 23,847 tonnes of iron ore and 920 tonnes of furnace oil.

In another incident that year, the Vietnam-flagged MV Vinalines Mighty developed a serious stability problem while carrying about 24,500 tonnes of iron ore from Paradip and sent an SOS after beginning to tilt. A major accident was eventually averted.
In 2009, during the monsoon, the MV Asian Forest capsized after loading iron ore fines at Mangalore Port on India’s west coast. The vessel sank after cargo liquefaction caused it to lose stability.

NSA Ajit Doval to visit China for border talks ahead of Xi Jinping’s India trip
Ajit Doval is expected to meet his counterpart for the Special Representatives mechanism, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi on Tuesday.

National security adviser Ajit Doval is expected to visit China on Monday for a meeting of the Special Representatives on the boundary issue, which is part of efforts by the two sides to normalise ties, people familiar with the matter said on Sunday.

Doval is expected to meet his counterpart for the Special Representatives mechanism, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi, on Tuesday, the people said on condition of anonymity. This will be the 25th round of talks under the mechanism, established in 2003 to work out a framework for resolving the dispute over the 3,488-km border.

Doval’s visit assumes greater significance as it comes ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s expected trip to India next month to participate in the BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Though both sides have not made an official announcement in this regard, Xi is expected to join the summit to be held during September 12-13, the people said.
This will be Xi’s first visit to India in seven years. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Xi last met in August 2025 on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in China.

Talks against recent Arunachal Pradesh standoff

The talks between the Special Representatives is being held against the backdrop of a recent standoff between Indian and Chinese troops in the Arunachal Pradesh sector of the Line of Actual Control (LAC). External affairs minister S Jaishankar reiterated at a media conclave on Saturday that the state of the border will determine the course of the overall India-China relationship.

“I think we went through a particularly bad patch between the summer of 2020 and the autumn of 2024, and that was primarily an outcome of the situation in the border areas,” Jaishankar said, referring to a military face-off in the Ladakh sector of the LAC that lasted more than four years and took bilateral ties to a six-decade low.

After the two sides reached an understanding on ending the face-off in Ladakh in October 2024, Xi and Modi met in Russia and agreed on measures to normalise ties and address the border dispute. Though the two sides have taken steps such as reviving the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, resuming direct flights and easing visa restrictions for Chinese nationals, there has been no forward movement on de-escalation on the LAC.

Last round of Special Representatives' talk

At the last round of Special Representatives’ talks in New Delhi a year ago, the two sides reiterated the “importance of maintaining peace and tranquillity” on the border to promote the overall development of ties.

According to an Indian readout issued at the time, the Special Representatives agreed on the need for a “political perspective” while working on a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable framework for settling the boundary question in line with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question of 2005.

They also agreed to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) on India-China Border Affairs to “explore early harvest in boundary delimitation”, and a working group under the WMCC to advance effective border management.
They further agreed to create general-level mechanisms in the eastern and middle sectors of the border, in addition to the existing general-level mechanism in the western sector.

Vijay made three key requests before Union home minister Amit Shah -- one on delimitation, another on NEET and a third on drug control, HT reported earlier.
Addressing the meeting, Vijay sought firm assurance from the Centre that no state would lose parliamentary representation as a result of the proposed Delimitation Bill, 2026.

"As the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census approaches its end and the Delimitation Bill, 2026, is considered, there is a genuine and shared concern across the Southern States that delimitation based predominantly on populations may diminish our collective voice in Parliament," the Tamil Nadu CM said.
He argued that with the delimitation bill, the southern states should not be penalised for their achievements in population stability, news agency ANI reported.
CM Vijay said the southern states have, from the forefront, achieved population stabilisation, human development, and economic growth.

"These achievements reflect the successful implementation of national priorities and should not result in a reduction of our representation. Public policy must not inadvertently penalise States for fulfilling national objectives," he added.

"I therefore urge the Union Government to provide a clear legislative assurance that no State will suffer a reduction in its percentage of representation in Parliament on account of its success in population stabilisation," Vijay said.

The Tamil Nadu CM said that such an approach would ensure the upholding of the principles of equity, the preservation of the federal balance envisioned by the Indian Constitution, and the reinforcement of the Confidence of all the states in the nation's democratic institutions.

Tamil Nadu, along with Kerala, has consistently voiced concerns about delimitation based on population metrics. This is because southern states have implemented national family planning and population control directives to a larger extent over the last five decades. As a result, their relative population share has grown at a slower pace than that of many northern states.

The draft electoral rolls for Karnataka was published on Monday as part of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter list. The draft rolls can be accessed at https://www.ceo.karnataka.gov.in.The names of 4.46 crore voters are expected to be in the draft electoral rolls.

About 1.08 crore voters in the current electors’ list will find themselves out of the draft electoral rolls as they remained in the Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others (ASDDO) list after the 49-day doo...door-to-door enumeration phase of the SIR that ended on August 17.The Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of Karnataka has appealed to all citizens to verify their details in the draft electoral rolls and ensure accuracy.

Here is what happens once the draft electoral rolls are published.Following the publication of the draft electoral rolls, the claims and objections phase of the SIR begins. This phase allows people to verify their details in the draft rolls, fix exclusions and ensure their names are in the final list that will be published on October 27.The window to file claims and objections will be open from August 24 to September 23.

If citizens need to fix their voter status, they must submit the correct form based on the specific situation.Form 6: Use this for the inclusion of a new voter registration (if you are a first-time voter or your name has been deleted from the rolls).Form 6A: Use this for the inclusion of an overseas voter registration (for non-resident Indians).Form 7: Use this for the deletion of a name (to report deceased or permanently relocated voters etc).Form 8: Use this for shifting of residence, correction of entries, replacement of EPIC, or marking of PWD (persons with disabilities).
.Karnataka SIR | Name listed in ASDDO?

Here is what voters should do.According to the Election Commission, here is the list of indicative documents that may be submitted with the forms:Any Identity card/Pension Payment Order issued to regular employee/pensioner of any Central government/State government/PSUAny identity card/certificate/document issued in India by the government/local authorities/banks/post office/LIC/PSUs prior to July 1, 1987.Birth certificate issued by the competent authorityPassportMatriculation/educational certificate issued by recognised boards/ universitiesPermanent Residence certificate issued by competent State authorityForest Right CertificateOBC/SC/ST or any caste certificate issued by the competent authorityNational Register of Citizens (wherever it exists)Family register maintained by government officials under any statute/administrative/regulationAny land/house allotment certificate by governmentAadhaar (refer Election Commission's directions issued on September 9, 2025) Notice and hearing phaseThe notice and hearing phase will be in force from August 24 to October 22.Once the claims and objections are submitted, the electoral registration officers (EROs) will issue a public notice regarding the received forms.

The EROs will then verify documents, hold hearings, and decide on all claims and objections during this window.Filing an appealIf a citizen's name or claim is excluded after the ERO holds the hearing, they have a legal right to appeal.First appeal can be filed with the District Magistrate/Deputy Commissioner within 15 days of the ERO's final order.The second appeal can be filed with the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) within 30 days of the date of the first appeal order.Final electoral rolls Once all corrections and appeal decisions are resolved, the final electoral rolls will be published on October 27, 2026.
It will be available at https://www.ceo.karnataka.gov.in.

With the removal of over 1.07 crore names, Karnataka’s electorate shrunk to 4.46 crore voters when the draft electoral rolls were published on Monday as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). An overwhelming number of the missing names were marked ‘absent, shifted, duplicate, dead, and others’ (ASDDO).

Announcing the figures at the end of the enumeration phase, Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) V. Anbu Kumar said the electorate comprised over 2.22 crore males, 2.24 crore females, and 2,871 others. Voters can check their names on the CEO’s official website at https://voters.eci.gov.in/download-eroll?stateCode=S10

The CEO said a special campaign will be conducted in areas reporting high ASDDO numbers, where voters will be assisted in filling Form 6 (for inclusion). The dates for the campaign are yet to be announced by the CEO’s office.

As many as 43.81 lakh notices will be served on voters whose enumeration forms contained logical discrepancies or those who could not be mapped. Notices may also be issued if a complaint is filed against a voter or if the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) has reason to suspect that a voter is ineligible.

With the enumeration phase ending, voters are likely to face the same problems they encountered with the ASDDO list. Just as people remained unaware that their names were in the ASDDO list until 12 days before the enumeration phase ended, they now have no way of knowing whether they will receive a notice until one is actually served. “We only have numbers on how many people will receive notices, and the names will not be known until the notice is generated,” the CEO said.

However, the entire process — from an ERO generating a notice to it being served — is to be completed within just seven days. This could become a major hurdle, especially for voters living in another district or city while remaining registered in their native constituency, as the voter must attend the hearing in person.
There is, so far, no online option to check whether a person is likely to receive a notice. The CEO reiterated that names will be known only after a notice is generated.

The process has now placed the burden of saving one’s vote squarely on the voter. Unlike the enumeration phase, when Booth Level Officers (BLOs) were instructed to hand over enumeration forms to voters and a family member above the age of 18 could fill them on the voter’s behalf, BLOs, during this stage, can serve notices on anyone available at the address. The notice will also carry a QR code to submit one of the 11 documents online, but the voter alone must appear for the hearing.
This could pose challenges for sections of voters such as senior citizens, single mothers, women in general, labourers and persons with disabilities, among others.
For instance, within Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) limits alone, 40,307 voters are above the age of 85, while 829 are above 100. More than 21,400 voters are persons with disabilities.

Following the enumeration phase, the number of polling stations across Karnataka increased after rationalisation. Each polling station will now have up to and not more than 1,200 voters, and where a polling station had more voters, they were shifted to another polling station within a two-kilometre radius, the CEO said. This has resulted in the addition of 1,873 polling stations across the State.

Voters unable to find their names in their current polling station or booth list have been advised to search using their EPIC details, where the updated polling station will be reflected if rationalisation has taken place. They may also check two polling stations before and after their current one.

Regarding notices on logical discrepancies and unmapped status, EROs have been vested with full powers to take a decision. If aggrieved by an ERO’s decision, a voter can appeal to the DEO/DC within 15 days. If the response remains unsatisfactory, the voter can appeal to the CEO, the final appellate authority, within 30 days of the first appeal.

While the draft electoral rolls were published at 12 p.m. on Monday, people struggled throughout the day to view and download the rolls, particularly the English versions. While voters were able to access the website, after downloading the rolls, files repeatedly threw up errors such as “error” and “file corrupted.”

Tarun Tejpal must surrender, seek exemption before appeal is heard: Goa tells SC
Senior advocate Kapil Sibal insisted that the requirement to surrender did not apply since the high court had given him four weeks to surrender

Former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal must surrender or secure an exemption from the Supreme Court before his appeal against his conviction and 10-year jail term in the 2013 sexual assault case can be heard, the Goa government told the Supreme Court on Monday.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, made the submission before justice Alok Aradhe, who was considering Tejpal’s appeal in the chamber list, where matters are taken up for preliminary or procedural consideration before being placed before a regular bench.

“The existence of the appeal is dependent on either filing a certificate that he has surrendered or, alternatively, he will have to pray to Your Lordships to allow an exemption from surrendering. These are the two options,” submitted Mehta, stressing the seriousness of the case.

Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Tejpal, opposed the state’s submission, arguing that the requirement to surrender did not apply in the present case as the Bombay High Court at Goa had granted him four weeks to surrender while declining to stay his conviction.
“This general rule does not apply because this is a case where stay has been granted by the high court, so there is no question of applying this rule,” contended Sibal.

He argued that Tejpal was still protected by the high court’s order and therefore there was no reason to insist that he surrender before his appeal was heard. “Why must I go to jail when I am protected?” asked Sibal, urging the court to list the appeal for hearing on August 31.
“If this court says no stay, I will have to go to jail. Allow me to argue the appeal and seek interim protection. If this court says we don’t think it is a case for bail, then I am inside,” he added.
Justice Aradhe, after hearing the submissions, said he would pass an appropriate order.

Tejpal approached the Supreme Court on August 20, challenging the August 6 judgment of the Bombay High Court at Goa that overturned his acquittal by the trial court and convicted him on two counts of aggravated rape. The high court sentenced him to 10 years’ imprisonment and imposed a fine of ₹10 lakh in all.

The high court, at Tejpal’s request, granted him four weeks to surrender before the jail authorities, although it rejected his plea to stay his conviction. He is therefore required to surrender in the first week of September.

The Goa government has separately approached the Supreme Court seeking enhancement of the sentence to life imprisonment. The state has not challenged the conviction but has argued that the 10-year sentence is grossly disproportionate to the gravity of the offences.

The government has also challenged the high court’s direction that the sentences for the two aggravated rape offences run concurrently, arguing that the alleged assaults took place on successive days and involved separate criminality.

Tejpal, in his appeal, has denied the allegations and challenged the high court’s findings that led to his conviction. He has argued, among other things, that the prosecution case was inconsistent with CCTV footage and questioned the circumstances in which the allegations emerged.

The case dates back to November 2013, when a junior female colleague accused Tejpal of sexually assaulting her twice in an elevator at a hotel in Goa during the Tehelka THiNK festival. Tejpal was arrested later that month and released on bail in July 2014.

The trial court acquitted him in May 2021 but high court reversed the acquittal on August 6 this year, holding that the trial court’s appreciation of the evidence was “not only unreasonable but perverse” and that the judge relied on preconceived notions while assessing the complainant’s testimony.

Tarun Tejpal must surrender before challenging rape conviction, Goa govt tells SC

Former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal challenged his 10-year rape conviction before the Supreme Court. Goa told the court his appeal depends on surrendering or seeking exemption from surrender. Kapil Sibal argued Tejpal need not surrender as the High Court's stay remains in force.

Former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal has challenged in the Supreme Court the Bombay High Court's verdict overturning his acquittal in the 2013 rape case and sentencing him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. During the hearing, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, argued that the maintainability of Tejpal's appeal depends on either him filing a certificate confirming his surrender or seeking an exemption from surrender before the court. “These are the two options,” Mehta said.
The arguments took place before a bench headed by Justice Alok Aradhe, with Tejpal's counsel Kapil Sibal and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, presenting opposing arguments.
Tejpal has challenged the Bombay High Court's verdict overturning the trial court's decision to acquit him and sentencing him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. The Supreme Court heard his plea.
Mehta urged the court to consider the maintainability of Tejpal's appeal in this context.

Kapil Sibal argued that the rule does not apply in this case because the High Court has already granted Tejpal relief from surrender. Therefore, he said, there was no question of applying the rule. The High Court had given Tejpal four weeks to surrender, until the first week of September.

Sibal said, "Suppose the court refuses to grant a stay, then I will have to go to jail. But when the High Court itself has granted a stay and that order is still in force, why should I surrender? In such a situation, what is the point of surrendering first and then filing an appeal?"

Referring to an earlier Supreme Court case, Mayuram Subramanian Srinivasan vs CBI, Tushar Mehta said the matter could also be viewed from another perspective. The special court had suspended the sentence and granted relief for a certain period. Whether or not that relief should be extended is a matter of the court's discretion. However, he said, in their view, it would be subject to the provisions of Order XXI Rule 13A of the Supreme Court Rules.
Mehta argued that the provisions of Section 389 of the CrPC and the Supreme Court Rules are independent provisions and must be considered on their own terms.
Sibal said, "Despite my request, submissions and arguments, if this court says that this is not a bail matter, I am ready to go to jail. This is my regular appeal and the relief is still in force."
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta interjected, saying, "You have been incorrectly briefed. This is not an SLP."
Sibal responded, "This is an extension of criminal appellate jurisdiction."
After hearing arguments from both sides, Justice Alok Aradhe said, "This is a criminal appeal. We will pass an order on it."
Sibal said that listing the matter for the 31st would cause no prejudice to anyone. He added that whatever the complainant had said did not match the CCTV footage.
"Justice should be done. We have said what we had to say. The court can now pass an order," Sibal said.

Manipur is awaiting a decision from New Delhi regarding the upcoming Census exercise, which remains in limbo in the State amid the demand by several Meitei and Naga civil society groups for a National Register of Citizens (NRC) to be compiled first. With the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) yet to spell out the future course of action, a government source said a review of the situation is likely to be held in the coming days.

On Monday (August 24, 2026), following a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by the Kangleipak Students Association (KSA), the High Court of Manipur constituted a Special Division Bench comprising Chief Justice M. Sundar and Justice A. Guneshwar Sharma to hear the matter on August 25 at 2 p.m. In a notification issued on Monday (August 24, 2026), the court said the Special Division Bench would sit exclusively to hear the PIL.
The first phase of the Population Census 2027, House Listing and Housing Census (HLO), is scheduled to be held in Manipur from September 1 to September 30.

The training of enumerators, mostly government school teachers, has been halted in the State due to opposition and protests by several civil society groups. Enumerators are required to visit each household for door-to-door enumeration and record details in a specific app on their personal phones.

The self-enumeration portal, which allows respondents to enter their details independently, was scheduled to go live on August 17, but is yet to become operational. “A decision from the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is awaited. The RGI office will assess the situation and there will be some clarity soon,” said a State government official.
In 2011, the Census exercise could not be carried out in at least 103 villages in Chhattisgarh and 260 villages in West Bengal due to violence associated with Left Wing Extremism (LWE).

Though the Census is not an exercise to determine citizenship and counts all individuals irrespective of nationality, there is anxiety among a section of people in Manipur that the next delimitation exercise, which will redraw the boundaries of electoral constituencies, may take into account the latest Census data in a manner that could disadvantage the Meiteis and small tribal communities. Manipur has three major communities: the Meiteis, the Nagas, and the Kuki-Zo people.

At least 14 civil society groups representing Meiteis, Pangals (Meitei Muslims), and the Kom and Rongmei tribes, among others, are in Delhi to seek an audience with the Union government. The group also has representation from those displaced from their homes as a result of the ethnic violence between the Kuki and Meitei communities that started on May 3, 2023.
The group met officials of the MHA, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju and BJP president Nitin Nabin.

Former Manipur Chief Minister N. Biren Singh, who met Union Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi last week, said people are apprehensive that the “presence of illegal immigrants in the State has affected demographic imbalance” and that while people are not against the Census, they want the NRC first.
The Congress party on August 20 sought the postponement of the Census exercise in Manipur, citing continuing violence and the displacement of thousands of people.
Kuki-Zo Council calls for Census

The Kuki-Zo Council (KZC), on the other hand, said that to rebut the “falsehoods and propaganda surrounding our population and demographic status during the Manipur conflict, an impartial Census is essential to establish facts and dispel unfounded claims”.

The KZC also welcomed delimitation to ensure fair representation based on verified demographic data. Regarding the NRC, the KZC said it was a national exercise and that there was no provision for any community or State government to unilaterally initiate or conduct a separate NRC in a particular State at its own discretion.

During the HLO phase, enumerators will collect information relating to housing conditions, household details, available amenities and assets possessed by households through a structured questionnaire comprising 33 notified questions. This phase of the Census forms an essential foundation for evidence-based planning and formulation of welfare and development programmes. The actual headcount will be done during the Population Enumeration phase, the second phase, which will be conducted in February 2027. In the second phase, for the first time, respondents will be asked to state their nationality along with their religion and the place and date of birth of both their parents.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday hit out at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on Manusmriti, accusing him of denouncing India's traditions and heritage and saying he had "ruined" his role as the Leader of Opposition.

Yogi Adityanath vs Rahul Gandhi
