Putin assures India of fuel, fertilisers amid disruptions over West Asia crisis
Jaishankar said PM Modi hopes that President Vladimir Putin would attend the Brics Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday assured India of supplies of energy and fertilisers amid disruptions caused by the West Asia conflict, even as external affairs minister S Jaishankar highlighted the need to address the growing imbalance in two-way trade that has soared to $50 billion.

Putin’s expected meetings with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Kyrgyzstan this month and on the sidelines of the Brics Summit in New Delhi in September figured in a meeting between the Russian leader and Jaishankar in Moscow. Jaishankar is in Russia to co-chair a meeting of the Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC).

Putin pointed out that bilateral trade has increased this year, after declining slightly in 2025, and said Russia is increasing fertiliser supplies to India. He noted that any important issues had figured in the IRIGC-TEC meeting and said: “One of these issues is not only energy – it is, of course, the supply of fertilisers…We are doing everything to resolve this issue for Indian farmers, for agriculture. We are increasing these supplies and are ready to do so further.”
Also Read | Russian President Vladimir Putin expresses hope to meet PM Modi soon as he hosts EAM S Jaishankar
The two sides are also making progress on cooperation in nuclear energy and high-tech, Putin said.

Jaishankar said Modi hopes Putin will attend the Brics Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13. “Prime Minister Modi looks forward to meeting you at the SCO Summit and also hopes that you will have the opportunity to come to the Brics Summit and host this annual summit,” Jaishankar was quoted as saying by state-run TASS news agency.

He also handed over a personal message from Modi to Putin. People familiar with the matter said Putin is expected to attend the Brics Summit, along with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. The summit is expected to focus on global economic and political challenges, and expanding multilateral cooperation among Brics member states.

While co-chairing the IRIGC-TEC meeting with Russia’s first deputy prime minister Denis Manturov, Jaishankar pointed out that a more than four-fold increase in bilateral trade in goods — from $13 billion in 2021-22 to nearly $60 billion in 2025-26 — had been “accompanied by a significant widening of the trade imbalance” from $6.6 billion to more than $50 billion.
Also Read | EAM Jaishankar to visit Russia, co-chair key trade and economic commission

“Addressing this imbalance is today one of our foremost priorities. Progress on market access, removal of tariff and non-tariff barriers, strengthening payment mechanisms and stronger business-to-business engagement will be critical for addressing this imbalance and achieving our shared objective of $100 billion in bilateral trade by 2030,” Jaishankar said at the start of the meeting.

Jaishankar made three proposals for the next phase of the India-Russia economic partnership – focusing on implementation and outcomes to prioritise deliverables and solving problems, strengthening engagement with businesses by aligning institutional mechanisms with industry priorities, identifying bottlenecks and improving policy responses, and exploring new possibilities to address the needs of de-risking and diversifying.

The discussions between Jaishankar and Manturov also encompassed cooperation in trade, investments, energy, fertilisers, nuclear energy, connectivity, technology, space and mobility of professionals. The two sides also reviewed the progress in discussions between India and the Eurasian Economic Union on a free trade agreement.

Manturov said Rosatom’s involvement in building the Kudankulam nuclear power plant in Tamil Nadu could be the basis for expanding cooperation in nuclear energy, including the “creation of new power generation facilities in India, including small-scale ones, as well as the localisation of equipment and nuclear fuel production”.

Russia also sees potential for new joint projects in the extraction and processing of non-ferrous and rare earth metals, Manturov said. Russia and India are also discussing cooperation in space exploration, including manned spaceflight, rocket propulsion and satellite navigation, he said.

The prototype of a high-speed electric train jointly produced by India and Russia will be assembled by the end of the year, after which serial production is expected to begin, Manturov announced at the meeting. “Within this framework, the flagship project in transport engineering — the development and production of the Vande Bharat electric trains — is systematically developing,” he said.
Also Read | Russia tests readiness for new round of military mobilization
In March 2023, a consortium led by Russia’s Transmashholding won a $6.5-billion tender for the development, production and 35-year service of 1,920 Vande Bharat electric train cars.

Manturov also prioritised cooperation in energy security, including the supply of oil, petroleum products and coal, as well as joint investment projects in hydrocarbon production and processing. Russia is currently among the top two suppliers of energy to India.

Russian energy minister Sergei Tsivilev described India as a key partner for the country’s fuel and energy sector, while deputy prime minister Alexander Novak noted that Moscow is interested in Indian investments in the Russian oil and gas sector, and developing a distribution network involving Russian companies in India.

Manturov also noted that tourist flows between Russia and India had increased by 8% in the first half of 2026, with more than 25,000 Indian tourists visiting Russia. Around 50,000 Russians also visited India, he said. Referring to labour migration, he said Russia and India are focusing on expanding the legal framework to create stable and transparent conditions for attracting workers.
The number of Indian students in Russia has also grown to almost 40,000, Manturov said. Support for talented children and youth can be a new vector of cooperation between the two countries, he added.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday said that hearings of applications for citizenship under the CAA will soon be over, and so far the state has issued certificates to 23,000 people out of 2.30 lakh applicants.

Addressing a press conference at the state secretariat 'Nabanna', Adhikari said the hearings related to citizenship under the CAA would be completed expeditiously, and certificates would be issued soon.

The CAA or the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, seeks to grant Indian citizenship to refugees belonging to six communities, who had sought shelter in India before December 31, 2014, due to religious persecution in three neighbouring countries - Pakistan, Bangladesh and Bangladesh. The six communities are Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians.

"We will complete the hearings quickly through the district magistrates. Out of the 2.30 lakh cases, 23,000 have received certificates and 2.07 lakh are still pending," Adhikari told a press conference.

He added that those who had not yet applied for citizenship under CAA would also be able to do so and stated that the process for Hindu refugees who came from Bangladesh, citing religious persecution, would be expedited.
"We will complete the hearings quickly and issue certificates to Hindu refugees who came from Bangladesh because of religious persecution," the chief minister said.
Adhikari also sought to reassure members of the Matua community and other Hindu refugees who had been waiting for CAA certificates for a long time that they will receive their certificates from him.
"The Government of India has entrusted this responsibility to me," the CM said.
Adhikari had said on August 1 that all pending applications for citizenship under the CAA in the state would be disposed of within the next six months.

The legislation, popularly referred to as the anti-goonda bill, was brought with the stated objective of curbing anti-social activities and strengthening preventive action by the police and administration.
"From today, a part of the anti-goonda law has come into effect in West Bengal. No one will be spared if government property is damaged," he said.

FDA suspends licenses of restaurants in Mumbai Cricket Association premises over 'hygiene' issues
The five MCA outlets facing the Maharashtra FDA action are the Permit Room, Pavilion, Mediterranean, Oriental Swing, and Clubway & Pastry Counter.

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the food licences of five outlets at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises over alleged hygiene issues, including violations of food safety norms, flagging deficiencies in food handling, storage, refrigeration, and sanitation.
The action comes as the FDA, under Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, intensifies inspections of food establishments across Maharashtra to ensure compliance with food safety and hygiene requirements.
As part of its statewide drive, the FDA has suspended the licences of 11 food establishments, including the five outlets at MCA, news agency PTI reported on Monday.
The FDA inspected 45 hotels, restaurants, eateries and dhabas during the drive, issued improvement notices to 33 establishments and conducted 25 raids, according to a press note.

The five MCA outlets facing action are the Permit Room, Pavilion, Mediterranean, Oriental Swing, and Clubway & Pastry Counter. The FDA inspected the outlets on August 20 and found various deficiencies related to hygiene, food handling, storage, refrigeration and sanitation.
What the FDA found at the MCA premises

According to the FDA release, inspectors found ice accumulation in a kitchen refrigerator at the Permit Room, along with an unclean, slippery floor near the kitchen entrance, inadequate temperature control, deteriorated raw materials, and deficiencies in food storage and handling.
The outlet also lacked food-grade conformity certificates for food-contact packaging material and did not conduct regular checks of cooking oil.

The Pavilion faced action after inspectors found ice accumulation, unclean refrigerator components, poor segregation of food items in cold storage, inadequate refrigeration calibration, improper thawing of frozen food, and shortcomings in cooling and storage practices.

At Mediterranean, the FDA found inadequate sanitisation of food equipment, improper cooling, poor portioning practices, inadequate thawing of frozen food, deficient temperature controls and shortcomings in the handling of raw materials and packaging.

The Oriental Swing outlet was found to have an improperly calibrated refrigeration system, an unclean kitchen floor, damaged plaster or paint on part of the kitchen ceiling, inadequate sanitisation and deficiencies in temperature control and oil-quality checks.

At the Clubway & Pastry Counter, the FDA found inadequate work space, improper storage of raw food, a lack of gloves for a food handler, and inadequate measures to prevent dust, dirt, and insects from entering the food preparation area.
Other eateries that faced action

Besides the five MCA outlets, the statewide action included Lenexis Foodworks in Mahim, CafÃ© Cadell in Shivaji Park, China Town Fast Food Centre in Mulund, Morya Misal in Warje and Saoji Upahar Gruh in Nagpur.

The FDA suspended the registration of China Town Fast Food Centre with immediate effect after finding excessive use of artificial colour and MSG, repeated use of highly oxidised cooking oil, cockroach infestation, unhygienic food storage, a risk of cross-contamination between vegetarian and non-vegetarian food and inadequate drainage.
The FDA also suspended the licence of Morya Misal in Pune after finding artificial colouring in food, and storage and use of expired food products.

NEW DELHI: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of five restaurants operating at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises in Mumbai over serious food safety and hygiene violations, officials said. The inspections uncovered rotten raw food, poor sanitation and improper temperature control.According to details released by the FDA, the action was taken against the Permit Room, Pavilion, Mediterranean, Oriental Swing, and Clubway & Pastry Counter at the MCA.

The establishments were found to have violated several food safety norms, including inadequate hygiene practices and improper handling and storage of food.During the inspections, officials found rotten raw food, poor general sanitation and improper freezing temperature control. Officials cited poor general hygiene and housekeeping, along with structural and sanitation-related deficiencies.

Manipur: 1 CRPF personnel injured, 2 houses burnt by unknown armed individuals
The gunfight broke out after two houses belonging to separate communities were set ablaze by an unidentified group of people

One Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel sustained a bullet injury during a gunfight between security forces and unidentified armed individuals in the Taphou area of Manipur’s Senapati district on Monday, officials said.

The gunfight broke out after two houses belonging to separate communities were set ablaze by an unidentified group of people, triggering tension in the area. One of the two houses belonged to a Kuki family while the other belonged to the Poumai community (a sub-community of the Naga community).

The CRPF personnel sustained a bullet injury to his leg during the exchange of gunfire and was evacuated to a nearby hospital for treatment. Officials said additional security forces have been deployed in the area to control the situation. A group of villagers have evacuated as well.
The reason for the attack was not immediately known.

According to a video clip circulating on social media, following the incident, locals from the area blocked National Highway 2 (Imphal-Dimapur) at Senapati headquarters. Protestors were seen blocking the highway with burning tyres and debris.
The Taphou Kuki Village Authority condemned the burning of a Kuki house and described the incident as “highly deplorable, inhuman and unacceptable”.

The village authority urged the district administration and police to take immediate and appropriate action to investigate the incident, identify those responsible and ensure that justice is delivered in accordance with the law.
The village authority has served a 24-hour deadline for the culprits involved in burning the Kuki house to claim responsibility and resolve the issue according to community law.

Tension between the Naga and Kuki communities has been simmering in the area since the twin ambush carried out at two different locations on May 13 -- one at Noney district and other at Kangpokpi district. Four persons including three church leaders and one Naga man was killed in the two incidents.

On the same day, 48 civilians belonging to Naga and Kuki-Zo were kidnapped by both the groups in retaliatory tension. Later, nearly after a month of captivity all the hostages were set free however. Six Naga men, however, were found dead near Kharam Vaiphei (Kuki village) in Kangpokpi district.

The case has been under investigation by National Investigating Agency (NIA) and as a part of the investigation four individuals including a couple have been arrested in the month of July on two separate occasions.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday (August 24, 2026) said that 23,000 certificates under the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), 2019 have been distributed out of the 2.30 lakh applications that have been made.

“Through the district magistrates, we will complete the hearings and grant the certificates. Now it is up to us to give certificates,” Mr. Adhikari said. The Chief Minister said that about 2.07 lakh applications are pending with the State government. He also urged people who have to come to India after facing religious persecution to apply to the State government for CAA certificates.

A few days ago, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) transferred the processing of pending citizenship applications under the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), 2019, from Empowered Committees to District Collectors in eight States and Union Territories.

During the campaign for the West Bengal Assembly elections 2026 Prime Minister Narendra Modi promised to fast-track and accelerate the implementation of the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) to grant legal citizenship rights to refugee communities like the Matuas and Namasudras.

Speaking to media persons at the State Secretariat, the Chief Minister said that the State’s Governor, R.N. Ravi, has given his nod for the new Act enabling the arrest of those attacking police, cost recovery for public property damage, and a notification was issued in this regard during the day.

Mr. Adhikari was referring to the West Bengal Maintenance of Public Order (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which imposes a payment of compensation on persons committing offences such as causing damage to public or private property. Another Bill passed by the State Assembly, the West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-Social Activities Bill, 2026, which empowers the government to detain a person for 12 months is awaiting the nod of the President.

Karnataka portfolios allocated, DK Shivakumar retains finance. Check full list here
After the August 3 expansion that inducted 19 ministers, the Shivakumar-led Karnataka cabinet strength rose to 33, with one vacancy remaining and no woman minister included.

Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Wednesday allocated portfolios to the newly inducted ministers, 10 days after expanding his cabinet. The reshuffle also included changes in the departments held by two ministers who had taken office earlier.

The allocation came a day before the Monsoon session of the state legislature. With the expansion on August 3, in which 19 ministers were inducted, the strength of the Shivakumar-led cabinet has gone up to 33, with one berth still vacant. There is no woman minister in the cabinet.

BZ Zameer Ahmed Khan has been given Housing, while Lakshman Savadi will handle Co-operation. Rudrappa Manappa Lamani, who was Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly until recently, has been assigned Sugar and Textiles.

The portfolios of two ministers were changed after they were unhappy with their earlier assignments. Ramalinga Reddy has been moved from Major Irrigation to Forest, Ecology and Environment, while KH Muniyappa has been shifted from Food and Civil Supplies to Social Welfare.

UT Khader has been given additional charge of Minority Welfare, Haj and Wakf. Shivaraj Tangadagi has been assigned Backward Classes Welfare and Kannada and Culture, while T Raghumurthy will handle ST Welfare.

Ajay Singh has been given Minor Irrigation and Science and Technology, Cheluvarayaswamy will handle Major and Medium Irrigation, Madhu Bangarappa has been assigned Primary and Secondary Education, Basavaraj Raya Reddy Higher Education, and Shivalinge Gowda Excise.

Puttaranga Shetty has been given Animal Husbandry and Sericulture, Vijayananda Kashappanavar Small Scale Industries and Public Enterprises, Santosh Lad Labour and Employment, KS Basvanthappa Muzrai, Fisheries, Ports and Inland Water, SS Mallikarjun Mines and Geology and Horticulture, Rizwan Arshad Food and Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Narendra Swamy Agriculture, HC Balakrishna Municipal Administration, and B Nagendra Planning and Statistics.
The portfolio allocation completed the distribution of departments after the cabinet expansion, with some changes made to accommodate ministerial preferences ahead of the Monsoon session.

New Delhi: An FIR is being filed in connection with pellet-gun injuries suffered by 19-year-old Sahil Lochab during the 20 July ‘Sansad Chalo’ protest march, according to Congress sources, hours after Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra along with other senior leaders, staged a dharna outside the Parliament Street DCP office demanding that a case be registered.

Gandhi initially reached the Connaught Place police station with Lochab and his mother earlier Friday, seeking registration of an FIR over the alleged use of pellet guns during the protest. He was later told that New Delhi DCP Sachin Sharma was at the Parliament Street police station, following which Gandhi went there and sought an update on the complaint before sitting on a dharna with Sahil’s family and other Congress leaders.
According to sources, the FIR is now being registered.
Rahul also took to social media platform X, seeking answers from Home Minister Amit Shah over the alleged use of force against protesters and calling the violence “a serious crime”.

“On July 20, the police attacked Sahil, who was peacefully protesting at Jantar Mantar, with a pellet gun. Severely injured by the pellets, Sahil’s vision in one eye is now at risk. Such brutality against a peaceful protest is not just illegal—it’s a serious crime. Neither has Home Minister Amit Shah offered any explanation to the students for this cruelty, nor has the Prime Minister apologised to them. Now, when Sahil wants to file a First Information Report (FIR) for justice, even that is not being allowed,” he posted. “In this way, the Constitution and constitutional rights are being trampled upon. Amit Shahji, why are you so scared of justice? This fear shows that you are admitting to your crime.”

He added, “The FIR will be filed. A judicial inquiry will take place. And action will be taken against everyone—from top to bottom—who is guilty of this brutality. We will ensure justice for Sahil, and every student victim like him.”

Gandhi had earlier accused Shah of being responsible for the violence during the protests, demanding that the home minister make a statement in Parliament. “We hold Amit Shah directly responsible for the violence… He authorised the shooting of our students,” Gandhi had said.

According to Congress sources, Lochab, accompanied by his lawyers, approached the Delhi Police on 14 August and submitted a written complaint. The police allegedly refused to provide an I/O number and did not give an acknowledgement.
The complaint was pursued again on 17 August through email and phone calls, but the family was again not given an I/O number or acknowledgement, Congress sources said.

The Congress has alleged that pellet guns were used by Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel during the 20 July ‘Sansad Chalo’ protest march, in which several students were injured. The Delhi Police has repeatedly denied using pellet guns, while the CRPF has not publicly addressed the allegation. This has led to a political slugfest with Congress leaders targeting the government and the BJP accusing Rahul Gandhi of politicising the incident.
The Congress has since held several protests inside Parliament, demanding an explanation from the government over the alleged violence and the injuries suffered by students.

Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal took to X to say: “The PM and HM, sitting on top constitutional posts, have no concern for the students and have still not cared to listen to their pain. On the other hand, they are deliberately stalling the LOP’s quest for justice, when he is out there on the streets, fighting for the students.
“Is it not a valid demand to ask for an FIR in such an egregious case, where Rahul ji has accompanied the victim whose body bears the evident of pellet guns?”

He added, “Without Home Minister Amit Shah’s orders, the Delhi Police would not dare to turn down Rahul ji when he has himself gone to the police station demanding an FIR. Is his demand unfair? Why has Amit Shah become such an enemy of our students and the youth?”
Congress leader Pawan Khera also targeted the BJP leadership.

“Nadda ji makes so much noise, without making any sense. Someone needs to tell him to be quiet, it’s funny how Modi ji keeps throwing one minister after another under the bus for Amit Shah – Ravi Shankar ji, Nadda ji, Rajnath ji, Kiren Rijiju ji.
“Always this ‘Ji’ or that ‘Ji’. But never the Relevant ‘Ji’,” Khera alleged.
He asked: “This is a Home Ministry matter—and it’s the Home Minister who is accountable. Why doesn’t he come forward? Is he a coward? Or is this silence an admission of guilt?”

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also backed Gandhi’s protest and again questioned the government over the alleged use of pellet guns. “Those shedding crocodile tears over nationalism are, in reality, the biggest enemies of the country’s youth! Amit Shah didn’t show up in Parliament for 19 days. The country wasn’t told who ordered the firing of pellet guns on students and why such brutality was even necessary against our youth? Now, Sahil, who was seriously injured by the pellets, and his mother are running around in circles with the Delhi Police to file an FIR. No Daily Diary Number, no Acknowledgment, no medico-legal report from Al India Institute of Medical Sciences,” he said.

“Today, Leader of Opposition Shri Rahul Gandhi himself has gone to the police station and then to the DCP’s office with Sahil and his mother. What exactly is Amit Shah hiding? There was a lathi charge on students, tear gas was fired, pellet guns were used. Many youth were seriously injured. Our daughters were groped, beaten with lathis and sticks. But Prime Minister Modi hasn’t uttered a single word to this day, and the home minister has kept dodging accountability,” Kharge said.

“Sahil is not alone. Shri Rahul Gandhi and the Congress Party stand with every affected youth. Their FIR will be registered, their voice will not be silenced, and the fight to deliver them justice will be waged with full force. The ‘Echo of Students’ will not fade,” Kharge said.
Union Minister J.P. Nadda hit back at the Congress, accusing it of trying to “ruin the future of children and students”.

“Now, the Congress party is bent on ruining the future of children and students as well…Rahul Gandhi must realize that the public has clearly recognized his ‘hit-and-run’ attitude and political hypocrisy. No matter how much drama he creates, the Congress cannot escape its sins or evade accountability. The people are demanding answers, and he will have to answer to them,” Nadda said.

New Delhi: Putting women’s rights and empowerment at the centre of his fourth ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ address in Pune Saturday, Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi called out what he described as the “Manusmriti mindset”, which, he said, keeps women under the control of men. He also took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on last month’s Cockroach Janta Party-led protest.

Referring to the PM’s video post on social media after the protests, where he “forgave” the ones who abused him, Gandhi said, “My question to you is that at Jantar Mantar, boys also abused and girls also abused. But the prime minister is saying that he felt a ‘cultural shock’ because the girls were also abusing. If boys abuse, there is no problem. For them, it is allowed. But if a girl abuses, it is a cultural shock. It doesn’t look good.”

Gandhi also cited remarks by RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and BJP leader Manohar Lal Khattar. “Mohan Bhagwat ji says that rape happens in India but does not happen in ‘Bharat’, Khattar ji says that 80 percent of rapes happen because of women.”

He went on to question why women were not treated as equals in society, saying that they had been reduced to three identities—“daughter, wife and mother”. He stressed on the need for women to be able to have independence and ambition without being controlled by men.

Referring to the Manusmriti, Gandhi said, “In childhood, a female must be subject to her father. In youth, she belongs to her husband. When her lord is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent.” He said that it is a “shame”, and that women should belong to no one but themselves.
He further called women India’s “biggest asset”, urging them to break the ceiling.

“People ask me, ‘What is India’s biggest strength?’ You get many answers. Somebody will say our economy, somebody will say our military, somebody will say our medical system, somebody might even say our people. But I am very clear on what is India’s biggest strength, our biggest asset, and that strength is 70 crore unique journeys, unique imaginations, unique dreams that the women of India are living,” he remarked.
“Women are by nature more sensitive, gentle, compassionate and forward-looking than men. That is why I believe India’s young and older women are its biggest asset.”

Gandhi then spoke about the different ways in which women are controlled by society, including violence, and restrictions on their opportunities and time. He said 4.5 lakh girls are killed every year before they are born, while 80 percent of women face harassment and 29 percent face physical violence. He added that six percent of women are raped and claimed that 99 percent of sexual violence cases go unreported because of social stigma.

He also said that safety concerns have a cascading effect on women’s education and employment. “Fifty percent of women are denied opportunities for education or employment in the name of safety… 84 percent of women need their family’s permission to take up employment. Women earn 25 percent less than men, and do not get promotions easily and only eight percent own land.”

Gandhi also spoke about how many girls are not allowed to step out of their homes on their own. “Sixty percent of our girls cannot go out of the house alone. If they have to go outside the house, they have to go with somebody.”
He also highlighted the unequal burden of household work, saying that women aged between 15 and 29 spend an average of 5.5 hours a day on household work, compared to around 30 minutes spent by men.
During the programme, several women students and competitive exam aspirants also shared their personal experiences with Gandhi, highlighting the pressures they face at home, in education and at work.

Tejwini, a fashion technology student from a small village, spoke about being pressured by her family to get married, instead of continuing her education. “I decided that no, I will work and study,” she said.

Gyaneshwari, who has completed her master’s degree from Jamia Millia Islamia, spoke about the pressure she faced over her education, career and her share in family property. “It’s not my right? It’s like, I am asking for the property.”

A tribal woman also raised concerns over the hunger strike by tribal students in Pune and the condition of tribal ashram schools, to which Rahul responded that he would join her in her agitation. “Call me there, I will come and sit with you,” he told her.
Concluding the programme, Gandhi called on women to challenge patriarchy and fight for their place in society.
“Patriarchy suppresses you, scares you, threatens you, controls you. Together, we have to finish this patriarchy. Be loud, be proud, and fight for your space in society,” he remarked.

Chennai: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay-led TVK government has decided to scrap the proposed greenfield airport project at Parandur in Kancheepuram district, planned by the previous DMK government as Chennai’s second airport. Vijay told the assembly Monday the decision has been taken to safeguard agricultural lands and the livelihoods of farmers and residents.

“I stand firmly with the people protesting against the airport to be established in Chennai’s Parandur and the surrounding villages. In order to safeguard the villages, the Parandur airport will be scrapped,” Vijay said in a statement in the House under Rule number 110.
Rule 110 allows ministers to make statements on matters of public importance in the assembly, with the Speaker’s consent, without an immediate debate on the statement.

DMK members staged a walkout after being denied an opportunity to speak on the announcement. Party leader and former chief minister MK Stalin, under whose term the project was approved. called the TVK government’s decision a “devastating blow to the employment dreams of Tamil Nadu’s youth”, saying it would hand a “jackpot” to competing states.

Vijay recalled visiting Ekanapuram and nearby villages on 20 January 2025, when he met the protesters. He had also voiced his disapproval of the project at his first public meeting in Vikravandi in October 2024.
“To fulfil the promise I made to the people to protect their lands, the steps taken to establish a new airport in Parandur will be abandoned by the TVK government,” he told the assembly,

The government will identify alternative sites around Chengalpattu and other areas in Kancheepuram, where impact on farmland and residential areas is minimal. The government will form expert teams to conduct technical feasibility studies to set up the new airport, he said.

Meanwhile, the existing Chennai airport in Meenambakkam will be expanded with a fifth terminal on the northwestern side. The expansion is expected to add significant passenger capacity to the current 30 million passengers per year.
The government remains committed to the Hosur airport project, subject to Defence Ministry clearance on airspace restrictions.

As per the TVK-led government’s instructions, land acquisition for Parandur has been stalled. and a decision is yet to be made on the already acquired land. Around 1,700 acres of land had already been acquired by March this year.
Stakeholders have emphasised the need for a second airport in Chennai due to growing passenger traffic, industrial expansion and capacity constraints at Meenambakkam.

While multiple sites were examined over the last 20 years, it was in 2022 that the then DMK government shortlisted four locations including Padalam, Thiruporur, Pannur and Parandur, after obtaining a feasibility report.
The Airports Authority of India narrowed it to Pannur and Parandur. In August 2022, Parandur was selected.

The project envisaged acquiring roughly 5,000–5,700 acres across 13 villages, with plans of dual parallel runways for simultaneous take off and landing, three terminals and handling up to 100 million passengers annually planned at an estimated cost of around Rs 27,400 crore. It was positioned to support the industrial corridor and improve connectivity.
However, the villagers opposed it.

The Civil Aviation Ministry granted in-principle approval in April 2025 and the state gave it special project status under the Tamil Nadu Land Consolidation for Special Projects Act to ease acquisition.
Residents of Ekanapuram began an indefinite agitation on 16 December 2022, which continued for over 1,000 days.
Vijay had also extended support and met the protesters in 2025.

The reasons for their objections included the displacement of more than 1,000 families, loss of fertile multi-crop agricultural land, impact on wetlands and water bodies, disruption of canal systems linked to Chennai’s flood management, and uncertain livelihoods.
After the TVK assumed power, ministers reiterated the party’s unchanged stand that a second airport is needed, but not at the cost of agricultural land and water bodies.
And Monday, Vijay formally announced the scrapping of the project. The decision drew sharp criticism from the opposition DMK.

‘Open-ended questions misleading’: Kharge, Rahul Gandhi write to PM Modi, flag caste census concerns
Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi said the same caste could have different names, sub-castes and spellings in different parts of India.

Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi have objected to the proposed method of collecting caste details in Census 2027. Their concerns were raised in a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The Population Census 2027 will include caste counting for the first time since Independence. Kharge, Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, and Rahul Gandhi, his Lok Sabha counterpart, said the government’s decision to use open-ended questions to record caste details could create confusion.

Reliable caste data was essential for framing social justice policies and assessing the socio-economic status of different communities, the leaders said. “Your government has chosen the method of recording caste information in the census using open-ended questions, which is misleading,” the letter read.
ALSO READ | Caste among 40 questions notified for the second phase of the Census 2027

The leaders said the same caste could have different names, sub-castes and spellings in different parts of India. If people from the same caste are recorded under different names, one caste could end up being counted as several different groups.
“This will result in millions of castes in the country, rendering the entire data obtained from the caste census useless,” the letter said.

Kharge and Rahul Gandhi said this could lead to incorrect estimates of the size of different communities. This could also affect decisions on education, jobs, government planning and social justice schemes, they said.
The proposed census would not give an accurate figure for the total OBC population because the questionnaire does not include the term “backward class”, the leaders wrote in the letter.
ALSO READ | SP turns to booth-level caste data ahead of 2027 assembly polls
Kharge, Rahul suggest caste list
The Congress leaders suggested using a fixed list of castes through a drop-down option instead of allowing people to enter caste names freely.
They said such a list could be prepared using existing government lists, including the Socially and Educationally Backward Classes list and information from the Anthropological Survey of India.

They cited the caste surveys conducted in Telangana and Bihar, saying both used caste lists. Copies of the caste lists from the Telangana Caste Survey-2024 and Bihar Caste Survey-2022 were attached to the letter.
“We do not accept this method of conducting a caste census,” Kharge and Rahul Gandhi said.
They asked the government to cancel the current questionnaire and prepare a new one after consulting political parties, experts and the public.
They said the new method should ensure that the number of people belonging to each caste and community is recorded correctly.
ALSO READ | How will the 2027 Census count caste? Number Theory

One of the most important parts of this Census is the caste enumeration, which will take place for the first time in independent India. Caste was counted during the British period but this practice was later stopped.

The Census has continued to separately count Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs). The population of other communities, including Other Backward Classes (OBCs), was not separately counted.
The demand for a caste census has mainly come from OBC groups and political leaders. So, how will the 2027 Census count caste apart from SCs and STs? Here is what we know so far.
The challenge of counting OBC sub-castes

A key question is whether the government has a complete list of all OBC sub-castes. There is no single nationwide list. There are 2,479 entries in the Central OBC list, while states have their own lists. The total number is therefore much higher.
For example, Tamil Nadu has 182 OBC entries on the Central list but 252 entries on its state list. The Mandal Commission identified 3,743 communities as OBCs.
Government surveys have already given broad estimates of India's caste composition. The NFHS 2019-21 estimated the population share of SCs, STs, OBCs and others at 22%, 9%, 42% and 27%.
The PLFS 2025 gave similar figures: 20%, 9%, 46% and 24%. The Bihar caste survey released in 2023 also broadly matched these estimates.

Did India hit Kirana Hills? Ex-CDS explains what happened during Op Sindoor
Former CDS General Anil Chauhan also revealed that India cleared further strikes on Pakistani military targets even after Islamabad reached out for talks, with Sargodha among them.

Former Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan has addressed speculation over whether India struck Kirana Hills near Pakistan's Sargodha during Operation Sindoor, saying a loitering munition searching for radars may have hit one of the hills after failing to find its intended target.

Kirana Hills, around 10 kilometres north of Sargodha, has long been associated with Pakistan's nuclear infrastructure. Questions over whether India had targeted the area emerged after Pakistani media showed images of smoke rising from the hills during the military confrontation.

"We had deployed loitering munitions around Sargodha ahead of India's strikes on Pakistani airbases to hunt for radars," the former CDS said at an event organised by the Vivekananda International Foundation.
Chauhan explained that such a munition could remain airborne for around two hours while searching for a target. If it failed to find one, it would eventually come down.
"It must have come and hit one of those hills. So that could be one of the reasons... even Pakistani media showed some kind of images in which there was smoke coming out of Kirana Hills," he said.
Chauhan's remarks suggest that any impact at Kirana Hills was not a deliberate strike on the area or its nuclear facilities.
LOWER AIRSPACE WAS PART OF INDIA'S STRATEGY
The use of loitering munitions around Sargodha was part of India's broader decision to exploit the lower airspace during Operation Sindoor.
Chauhan described this as a "third option", distinct from the land-based response after the Uri terror attack and the large air package used following Pulwama.

"During Operation Sindoor, we decided to use a third option, that is, to exploit the lower airspace. That means it would have kept the threshold of conflict low. It would have assured success and then there would have been an element of surprise," he said.
The lower air envelope can be used by drones, loitering munitions, attack helicopters and other low-level platforms.
SARGODHA STRIKE CLEARED EVEN AFTER PAK SOUGHT TALKS
Chauhan also revealed that India cleared further strikes on Pakistani military targets even after Islamabad reached out for talks, with Sargodha among them.
He said Pakistan contacted India seeking talks when the Air Chief asked him whether the Indian Air Force should strike Sargodha.
"Once the Pakistanis had picked up the phone and said they wanted to talk at about 10 AM, the Air Chief asked me whether he should strike Sargodha. I said, 'Go ahead'," Chauhan said.
He then asked the Air Chief to identify two more targets.

"I said, could you please identify two more targets? So, one of the targets he identified was Skardu. We gave a yes, but after some time, the weather there turned bad, and they had to change over to Bholari," he said.
Chauhan said India's escalation strategy ensured it would deliver the final strike. "The last strike or the winning note will always be delivered by us and not by the Pakistanis," he said.
The remarks shed light on India's escalation strategy during Operation Sindoor, including its decision to retain the option of further strikes even after Pakistan sought talks.
PAKISTAN 'BLIND' ABOUT RESULTS OF ITS STRIKES
Chauhan also said Pakistan did not know whether its strikes had hit their intended targets and tried to obtain commercial satellite imagery until around May 12 to find evidence of damage.
"They were actually after 10th also till about 12th they were trying their best to obtain images so that they have some evidence," he said.

Chauhan said commercial satellite imagery was available from both US and Chinese companies. Pakistan, he said, also tried other Chinese satellite sources but failed to find evidence that its strikes had hit targets.
"But since they are not able to hit any target, they got no evidence," he said.
Chauhan attributed India's success during Operation Sindoor to better situational awareness, battlefield transparency and coordination between the Army, Navy and Air Force.
"If I had to list out a couple of reasons for India's victory, I would say that we had better situational awareness, better battlefield transparency because we are better networked," he said.

He said the three services had access to a common operational picture, helping them make better decisions. They also worked on a unified plan instead of taking individual capability deficiencies before the political leadership.

"We have seen in the past, sometimes in front of political leadership, people bring out the kind of deficiencies that they have. This particular operation stands out... in which all three services and I, right from day one, did not bring any of these kinds of deficiencies," Chauhan said.

The former CDS also credited clear political direction for giving the military operational freedom. "The second thing I could attribute to victory was... clear political direction, which gave us a free hand to plan operations," he said.
India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people.
In the initial phase, the armed forces struck nine sites linked to terrorist groups in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.
The strikes used precision and standoff weapons, allowing Indian aircraft to engage targets without flying deep into Pakistani airspace.

The operation later expanded after Pakistan launched military actions against India, prompting the Indian Air Force to strike Pakistani military infrastructure, including airbases and radar facilities.
The confrontation ended through direct military-to-military communications via the Directors General of Military Operations after Pakistan reached out for a ceasefire on the morning of May 10, 2025.

The controversy also drew a response from actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut, who criticised Sanon’s look in the advertisement.

In a note shared on her Instagram Stories, she wrote: “Culture & Traditions are in her heart, not in her neckline! Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh walked out of the high-security Sunaria jail in Haryana’s Rohtak early Tuesday after being granted a 21-day furlough. This is his 17th temporary release since 2020.

The latest furlough comes less than two months after he returned to Sunaria jail on June 26 on completion of a 30-day parole.

The Dera chief was lodged in Sunaria jail in August 2017 after being convicted in the rape case involving two women followers. He was subsequently convicted in other cases, including the murder of Sirsa-based journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati.

With Tuesday's release, Ram Rahim has now been granted parole or furlough on 17 occasions during his imprisonment. His repeated temporary releases have frequently triggered questions and criticism, particularly over the frequency of the relief granted to a convict serving sentences in serious criminal cases.

Earlier this year, Ram Rahim was granted 40 days of parole in January. He was again released on a 30-day parole in May and returned to the Rohtak jail on June 26 after completing the period of his temporary release.

The latest 21-day furlough once again brings the controversial Dera chief out of jail. His repeated parole and furlough releases have remained a subject of public and political debate ever since his conviction nearly nine years ago.
Ram Rahim’s 17 temporary releases since 2020
According to official prison records for convict 8647/C, Ram Rahim has been granted 17 temporary releases since 2020, including his latest 21-day furlough:
1st release — October 2020: 1 day
2nd — May 2021: 12 hours to visit his mother
Why is he out of prison so often?
Ram Rahim’s repeated temporary releases are governed by the Haryana Good Conduct Prisoners (Temporary Release) Act, 2022.
Under the rules, eligible convicts can be granted up to 70 days of parole and 21 days of furlough in a calendar year, subject to the applicable conditions and approval by the competent authority.

India didn't target Pakistan's Kirana Hills; loitering munition hit it inadvertently: Ex-CDS Anil Chauhan
Ex-CDS Gen Anil Chauhan says Indian loitering munition likely hit Kirana Hills after failing to find a radar target near Sargodha within its loiter time.

Former Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan on Tuesday said that India did not target Pakistan's Kirana Hills nuclear facility during last year's Operation Sindoor, but an Indian loitering ammunition inadvertently hit it.

Chauhan explained that a lot of loitering munitions were sent at Sargodha, which is just 10 km north of Kirana Hills. He said one of those munitions must have come and hit the Kirana Hills nuclear facility after not finding a target.

"Before those strikes, we had sent a lot of loiter ammunition at Sargodha, and Kirana Hills is 10 km north of Sargodha. So the loiter ammunition was looking for radars, which were in and around Sargodha, and it has got a lifetime. It will loiter for about two hours, and if it doesn't find a target, it will come and hit somewhere. It must have come and hit one of those hills,'' General Chauhan was quoted by ANI as saying.

The Kirana Hills is a vast rocky mountain range and a designated area under the Pakistan ministry of defence in Sargodha district. Locally referred to as the “Black Mountains” due to its brownish terrain, it stretches between the township of Rabwah and the city of Sargodha.
Former Director General of Air Operations, Air Marshal AK Bharti, had said on May 12 last year that the Indian armed forces did not target the nuclear facility at Kirana Hills in Pakistan.

Responding to a query during a press conference at the time, Bharti said, “Thank you for telling us that Kirana Hills houses some nuclear installation. We did not know about it. And we have not hit Kirana Hills, whatever is there.”

Ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month, India and China held the 25th round of Special Representatives (SR) Dialogue on the Boundary Question, endorsing efforts to formalise the recent turnaround in the relationship on the back of border peace and discussing issues like de-escalation, boundary demarcation and border management.After the talks chaired by Special Representatives Ajit Doval and Wang Yi, while India said both sides agreed to work towards a political settlement of the boundary question in their long-term interests, Beijing also recalled a 2005 bilateral agreement to stress its proposal for a package solution.Doval was quoted as saying by the Chinese side that India and China are partners, not competitors, and developing a stable, predictable, and forward-looking India-China relationship carries great significance also for Asia and the world.âThe normalcy we have witnessed in our relationship has been a direct result of both sides maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas,â said Doval, stressing the significance of border peace for further progress in bilateral ties.

Wang, however, reiterated Chinaâs position that the border issue must be placed in an âappropriate positionâ in ties.According to a Chinese readout, Doval and Wang held "in-depth communications" on advancing boundary demarcation negotiations, improving border management and control and promoting cross-border cooperation, while reaffirming their commitment to the 2005 agreement on political parameters and guiding principles for a "fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable package settlement" to the boundary question.

'Will not step down': Manan Mishra reiterates stance as plea in SC seeks his removal as BCI chief
Edited by: Rajeev Singh / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 22, 2026, 15:20 IST
Manan Mishra also addressed the recent controversy involving students of NALSAR University of Law.

NEW DELHI: Bar Council of India (BCI) chairman and Rajya Sabha member Manan Kumar Mishra rejected demands for his resignation, saying he holds the position through an election and represents around 25 lakh lawyers across the country.Mishra made the remarks a day after a group of lawyers from different Bar Associations in Delhi staged a protest outside the BCI office in New Delhi.

The protesters raised several concerns, including Mishra's long tenure, the lack of welfare measures for advocates and the proposed increase in the enrolment fee for lawyers."I have served as the chairman of the Bar Council of India for 12 to 14 years because I was elected. Manan Mishra represents 25 lakh lawyers; he will not step down simply," Mishra said, responding to the protest.He further said: "I am an elected representative. I was neither selected nor nominated to the Bar Council of India. It is a statutory body established under the Advocates Act."The lawyers demanding his resignation also sought the implementation of an Advocate Protection Act and questioned the proposed increase in registration fees at State Bar Councils.
Supreme Court petition challenges Mishra's tenure
Amid the controversy, a petition has also been filed in the Supreme Court challenging Mishra's continuation as BCI chairman.

Filed by advocate Yogamaya MG through advocate Deepak Prakash, the plea alleges that his uninterrupted tenure for more than a decade is contrary to the rules governing the BCI.The petitioner has relied on Rule 12(2) of the BCI Rules, which provides for a two-year tenure for the chairman and vice-chairman, or until they cease to be members, whichever is earlier.The plea has also challenged an April 21, 2025 Gazette notification that allegedly extended Mishra's tenure until 2030.

It has asked the Supreme Court to quash the notification and direct the BCI to withdraw or rescind it.According to the petition, Mishra first became BCI chairman in 2012. Although he briefly left the post in 2014, he returned as chairman in November that year and has remained in the position since then.

The petitioner has claimed that his re-election in March 2025 was his seventh consecutive term.The plea has argued that the absence of a cumulative limit on repeated re-election allows the office to remain concentrated in one individual for an extended period."Although Rule 12(2) prescribes a two-year tenure, no meaningful restriction exists upon repeated re-election. Consequently, the office has remained with the same individual for nearly twelve years.

Such prolonged concentration is prima facie inconsistent with the representative scheme embodied in Section 4(1)(c), under which every State Bar Council contributes to the composition of the Bar Council of India. A national institution representing the entire legal profession should not permit its highest office to remain concentrated indefinitely in one individual or a narrow regional grouping," the petition stated.The petitioner has sought Mishra's removal and fresh elections within a time-bound period under independent supervision.

It has also asked for a cumulative cap on the number of years a person can serve as BCI chairman, along with a rotation system and cooling-off period to allow representatives from different states and regions to head the council.The plea has further sought an independent committee headed by a former Supreme Court judge or former chief justice of a high court.

The proposed committee would be assisted by an auditor nominated by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), along with financial and technical experts.The petition has also sought an independent inquiry into the functioning and finances of the BCI Trust, "PEARL-FIRST", and the financial affairs of the All India Bar Examination.It has called for a time-bound audit of statutory funds, All India Bar Examination receipts, institutional receipts, trust finances, vendor contracts and related party transactions.As an interim measure, the petitioner has proposed an independent administrative committee to oversee the BCI if the Supreme Court orders Mishra's removal.The plea has also referred to Mishra's political role.

It noted that he became a Rajya Sabha member after being nominated by the BJP in 2024.The petitioner has clarified that it is not claiming that Mishra's political affiliation alone makes him ineligible to remain BCI chairman. Instead, it has raised concerns about the combination of political office and leadership of the statutory body responsible for regulating the legal profession."Petitioner does not seek the removal of any individual merely because of political affiliation or personal disagreement with any office bearer.

Nor does the petitioner invite this Court to substitute its own opinion for that of the statutory authority. The challenge is directed against structural illegality, alleged concentration of institutional control, prolonged concentration of statutory power, violation of mandatory statutory provisions governing tenure and elections, arbitrary exercise of regulatory authority, absence of transparency and accountability, and failure to preserve the representative democratic character contemplated under the Advocates Act, 1961," added the PIL.
Mishra defends action over NALSAR student controversy

Mishra also addressed the recent controversy involving students of NALSAR University of Law in Hyderabad and the Chief Justice of India (CJI), who is also the university's chancellor."Lately, there has been a lot of irresponsible and absurd commentary circulating on social media.

Students from NALSAR University, Hyderabad, decided to boycott the Chief Justice of India - who is also their Chancellor - and refused to attend the convocation ceremony where he was to preside," Mishra said."As the Chairman of the Bar Council of India, I found this deeply objectionable," he added.According to Mishra, the BCI initially issued an order stating that the enrolment of the students involved would not be processed.

He said the decision was withdrawn within 15 minutes after their grievances were addressed."Within 15 minutes, that order was revoked, and the students' grievances were addressed," he said.Mishra alleged that the episode was later used by members of the Aam Aadmi Party and a group he described as the "CJP group" to demand his resignation."I have served as the Chairman of the Bar Council of India for 12 to 14 years because I was elected," he reiterated.He also said around 15 students had gathered outside the BCI office on Thursday night to demand that he step down."Yesterday, about 15 students came here at night demanding a resignation," Mishra said.Meanwhile, another group of lawyers gathered in support of Mishra and defended his position as an elected representative of the legal profession.Advocate Satyam Singh said protests alone could not remove the BCI chairman because he had been elected by members of the legal community."The BCI Chairman is an elected official who has been consistently voted into office.

He hasn't been appointed through a selection process or an exam where you can simply show up and demand his resignation," Singh said."He represents 2.5 million lawyers across the country, representing them successfully for years on end," he added.On the NALSAR controversy, Singh said the issue should be viewed in the context of respect for legal institutions."The CJI is the head of the Constitution--in a sense, its guardian--while NALSAR students are future lawyers and judges who will become part of this profession, whether on the Bar or the Bench.

If they do not respect or trust that institution, where does that leave us?" he said.Singh also defended Mishra's decision to issue the initial order, while acknowledging that it was subsequently withdrawn."He withdrew it and admitted it was issued in haste. However, it was necessary to send a message that one must trust and respect the institution; that was the intent behind the move," Singh said.
Lawyers raise welfare and fee concerns
The protest, however, was not limited to the demand for Mishra's resignation. Lawyers also raised broader concerns about welfare measures and working conditions within the profession.

Advocate Raman Sharma alleged that there had been no significant nationwide welfare scheme for lawyers despite Mishra's long tenure as BCI chairman.Advocate Umesh Kumar raised the issue of a national insurance scheme for lawyers and objected to the proposed increase in enrolment fees to Rs 22,500.Other protesters, including advocate Perdeep Nagar, called for greater scrutiny of lawyers' credentials and urged the BCI to give greater attention to the welfare of members of the legal profession.

Hyderabad: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy defended his plans to meet New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a proposed trip to the United States—to which the Centre denied political clearance last week.

Revanth Reddy returned from London early Monday after visiting Oxford and Cambridge universities, besides attending All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) legislator Akbaruddin Owaisi’s daughter’s wedding.

The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is developing a technology-driven command-and-control system for India’s land borders that will integrate surveillance inputs from the field through a network of command centres stretching from forward areas to New Delhi, according to a senior government official.

The initiative, part of a new border management policy, is aimed at strengthening monitoring and response capabilities in border regions where physical fencing is not feasible, such as the 3,488-km border with China, which remains un-demarcated at several points from Ladakh to Arunachal Pradesh. A pilot project will start soon from the Pakistan border, the official added.
Home Minister Amit Shah had earlier announced a four-pronged border security strategy, which involves border guarding forces, local population, State police and technological solutions.

“There will be several small command centres along the land borders that will be linked to the field headquarters and further to Delhi headquarters. The live feed will help the border guarding forces to monitor and also save the resources, reducing the need for physical patrolling,” said the official.

The “smart border” architecture for all of India’s land frontiers would integrate artificial intelligence, sensors, surveillance systems and unified command-and-control centres to strengthen border security and enable faster responses to threats, the official said.
India shares 15,106.7 km land border with seven countries.

“The proposed framework is designed to bring together surveillance inputs from multiple technologies, including cameras, sensors, image-processing tools, drones and other monitoring systems, to create a common operational picture for agencies deployed along India’s borders,” said the official.

The system was envisaged as an integrated platform where information gathered on the ground could be transmitted quickly to command-and-control centres, allowing authorities to respond more effectively to infiltration attempts, smuggling networks and other security challenges, said the official.
Addressing the growing threat from drones, particularly for smuggling and reconnaissance, has emerged as a major focus area, particularly along the Pakistan border.

According to the official, border-management technologies would be tailored to local conditions rather than deployed uniformly. India’s land borders traverse deserts, mountains, riverine stretches, forests and densely populated areas, requiring customised solutions for different terrains and operational requirements, the official added.

“No two borders are the same. Just like the China border, which cannot be fenced, there are riverine stretches along the Bangladesh border, which are flood-prone. No fence can be put there. We are moving towards a concept where physical presence is not always required,” said the official.

On July 9, Mr. Shah addressed the first ever Land Border Districts’ Superintendents of Police Conference–2026. The meeting was attended by Superintendents of Police (SPs) of 119 border districts of 17 States and Union Territories, which share land border with Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China and Myanmar.

At the meeting, States were asked to submit their suggestions by December and the quadrangular security grid, which involves border communities and the local police, will be finalised in the next 1.5 years.

In a cryptic Instagram story on Saturday, Ranaut posted caricatures of herself and an apparent Gandhi figure — with "Gandhi" declaring "Smash the patriarchy," and "Ranaut" cutting in with "Bro, wait. Bharat Mata ki Jay. Shuru karte hai," seemingly poking fun at performative feminism.
The Instagram story came hours after Gandhi backed Sanon who found herself in the crosshairs of the controversy over her Rakhi advertisement attire.

The 36-second video sent social media into a frenzy of debate, opening up questions of freedom of choice, what constitutes Indian culture and the nature of the brother-sister festival itself.

"It's a wonderful time to be a woman, our closets are full of variety of clothes, today's woman is a global woman, from cocktail dresses to lehenga cholis, jeans to saris, bikinis to salwar kameez.

India rejects ‘politically motivated, malicious references' in UN panel's rights report
Ministry of External Affairs, in a statement, said India had participated in the review in a “spirit of constructive engagement”.

India on Wednesday rejected what it called “politically motivated” and “highly malicious” references in a UN committee’s report on alleged racial discrimination in the country, saying the observations contained sweeping generalisations and unsubstantiated allegations.
“India rejects any politically motivated highly malicious references in the report with all the contempt that it deserves."

Responding to media queries on the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (UNCERD) press release following India’s 11th periodic review under the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ICERD), the Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement that India had participated in the review in a “spirit of constructive engagement” and reaffirmed its unwavering commitment to combating racial discrimination.
The statement added that India had highlighted its constitutional safeguards, legal framework, pluralism and efforts to protect disadvantaged communities during the review.
“During the review, we highlighted India’s constitutional safeguards, robust legal framework, pluralism and sustained efforts to protect disadvantaged communities.”

The ministry of external affairs stressed that the inter-ministerial delegation led by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta had already rejected the “sweeping generalisations, unsubstantiated allegations, or tendency to exceed the Convention’s mandate” during the review meeting.

"While we will respond to the Committee's observations through the established procedure, the inter-Ministerial delegation, which was led by the Solicitor General of India, Shri Tushar Mehta, had already rejected the sweeping generalisations, unsubstantiated allegations, or tendency to exceed the Convention's mandate during the review meeting," the MEA stated.
It added that India would respond to the committee’s observations through the established procedure. The Indian Mission in Geneva has also issued a detailed statement following the CERD review.
What prompted India's response

MEA’s response came after the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination raised concerns over reports of “large-scale violations” by law enforcement personnel against ethnic and ethno-religious communities, Indigenous and Tribal Peoples, including Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes, particularly Dalits, as well as non-citizens.

The recent review, held on August 11-12, covered India’s 12th and 21st combined periodic reports submitted to CERD in 2023. The discussions covered issues including the implementation of ICERD, progress among marginalised groups, and measures to address prejudice and intolerance, according to a statement by the Permanent Mission of India in Geneva, news agency ANI reported.

The Indian delegation highlighted the country’s diversity, constitutional safeguards, affirmative action, judicial remedies, democratic accountability and public policies aimed at promoting equality, dignity and opportunity for all citizens, the statement said.
In its statement, MEA stressed that India had played a leading role in negotiating and drafting ICERD in the 1960s.

Nadda distanced themselves from the ‘purification’ controversy related to Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally venue in Haldwani, Uttarakhand BJP president Mahendra Bhatt defended the ritual saying “the place was polluted with slogans”.

A ‘shuddhikaran’ (purification) ceremony was held at the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani after a rally was addressed by Kharge on 8 August that had not only created a political stir in Uttarakhand, but nationally too.
Nadda, while responding to Kharge in the Rajya Sabha, had condemned the ‘shuddhikaran’.

Bhatt, while speaking to reporters on the sidelines of a Rakshabandhan event in Mussoorie, said the criticism over the ritual was being exaggerated by the opposition Congress merely for petty political gain as they don’t have any issue to raise.
Bhatt, while explaining the incident, stressed that the sanctity of a religious and cultural venue should be respected by all.

“Those who have no real issues raise matters that only damage and divide society. Kharge-ji’s rally (was) held in Haldwani. The Ramlila Ground there was defiled. The BJP MP also accused the Congress of unnecessarily linking the controversy to Scheduled Caste politics.

“I can say that Congress members are making a mockery of their own leader; they have turned Kharge-ji into a subject of ridicule. Kharge-ji himself must surely realise that the incident which took place in Devbhoomi that day should not have happened,” he added.

A video of the ‘purification’ ceremony had gone viral on social media, with one of the organisers claiming that certain political slogans should not have been raised there. The ”purification’ ceremony was held at the site of the rally by members of the Shri Ram Sena a few days later.

“It is a matter of great regret for all of us that your sentiments were hurt,” Nadda said.

India not a ‘dharamshala’, says Amit Shah; cites threats from infiltrators
Amit Shah said only citizens had the right to live in the country and infiltrators posed a threat to India’s security, economy and demographics.

Union home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday reiterated that India was “not a dharamshala”, saying only citizens had the right to live in the country and that infiltrators posed a threat to India’s security, economy and demographics.

“This country is not a dharamshala (charitable rest house); only citizens of the country have the right to live here,” Shah said, speaking at the valedictory session of the National Security Strategy conference of the Intelligence Bureau (IB), attended by chiefs of central agencies and state police forces.
Shah's take on India's security policy

Stressing that infiltrators threatened the country’s “security, economy and demographics”, the home minister said: “Over the past eight months, after visiting all states sharing land borders, we have shared a document outlining a four-pronged approach to border security with the states. Our goal is to make the country free of infiltrators in a very short period.”

Shah said India’s security policy had to be framed against the backdrop of global instability, insecurity around energy and resources, supply-chain disruptions, rising radicalisation and the warfare of cyber misinformation. A strong internal security apparatus, he said, was a prerequisite for a developed India. “If India is to emerge at the forefront in every field, its internal security will have to be further strengthened.”
Also Read I Use trial in absentia for fugitives hiding abroad: Amit Shah at security brass meet

Over the two-day NSS conference, intelligence agencies and security forces discussed infiltration, real-time intelligence-sharing against terror groups, and the dismantling of their logistics and funding networks, among other national security matters.
Similar comments from the past

Shah made similar remarks in Lok Sabha on March 27 while replying to the debate on the Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025. On that occasion, he had said India was “not a dharamshala where anyone can come and stay for any purpose”, arguing that Parliament had the right to bar those who posed a threat to national security, and that sensitive locations and army establishments along the borders could not be left open to all. Those who came legally to contribute to India’s prosperity were welcome, he had said, but illegal entrants would be dealt with strictly.

The Supreme Court too used phrasing when on May 19, a bench of justices Dipankar Datta and K Vinod Chandran declined to intervene in the detention of a Sri Lankan Tamil national facing deportation after a seven-year sentence under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. “Is India to host refugees from all over the world? We are struggling with 140 crore. This is not a dharamshala that we can entertain foreign nationals from all over.”
Also Read I ‘Let panel work’: SC on plea seeking Amit Shah, Delhi Police chief’s role in protest case

Attacking previous governments, Shah on Tuesday said had they anticipated the problems of narcotics, Naxalism and insurgency in the northeast before they became enormous challenges, “the country would not have had to suffer their consequences for decades.” He said the challenges in the country’s three internal security hotspots had been eliminated, and credited state police forces, central agencies and the central armed police forces (CAPFs).

Asking officers to look for trends over the next 15 to 20 years, Shah said they should identify problems that might arise and work out strategies to prevent them. He also directed state police forces to implement the Narcotics Control Vision document 2026-2029 on the ground and work on the “three Ds — Detect, Disrupt and Destroy” — to achieve a drug-free India.

130+ Indians, 37 NRIs out of reach as Nepal floods toll mounts, Bihar, UP on alert: What is happening?
Around 133 Indian nationals and 37 NRIs are among the foreigners missing and out of contact after a flash flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Nepal's Rasuwa.

Nepal has been witnessing massive flash floods since morning, with 95 dead so far, hundreds more missing, homes, cars and other establishments swept away in districts near rivers, and people separated from families.

Around 133 Indian nationals and 37 NRIs are among the foreigners authorities are unable to get in touch with after a flash flood in the Bhote Koshi River in the Rasuwa district of Nepal. Follow live updates here.

"A preliminary agency-wise record received from tourism and travel companies has identified 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, who were reported missing from the affected areas," said Nepal Tourism Board, as quoted by news agency AFP.

As Nepal deals with the flood chaos, Indian states Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have also stepped up vigil, with the possibility of a sudden rise in the Gandak and Narayani rivers' water due to the flash floods in the neighbouring country.
100+ Indians, 37 NRIs out of reach

According to the Nepal Tourism Board, around 133 Indian nationals and 37 NRIs are among the foreigners out of contact amid the flash floods. At least 59 of the Indians were pilgrims for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra, PTI reported, citing Samrat Tours and Travel agency.
HT has learnt that the owner of a travel group has confirmed that 35 NRIs from a group of 47 people who left Kathmandu on Tuesday for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra are not reachable.

“They were staying at different hotels in Rasuwa. The 47 also include my staff and guests from Russia, Canada, US and UK. We spoke to them around 8 am today. We have lost touch after that. They were supposed to cross the Nepal-Tibet border today,” Sagar Pandey, owner of Himalayan Glacier Adventures said.
Also Read: Terrifying clips capture Nepal floods fury; buildings, people vanish in seconds

The 133 Indians are part of the 348 travellers out of contact since the flash floods hit Nepal. According to Reuters, 93 Nepalis, three US citizens, 17 Malaysian nationals, 12 British citizens, four South Africans, and one person each from Australia and the Netherlands. are also missing.
The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu has issued emergency numbers for assistance and information related to Indian nationals - 977 985 131 6807 or 977 970 910 7500.
Notably, at least 67 army personnel posted near the Nepal-China border are also among those with whom contact is yet to be established.
Why Nepal saw huge deluge today

Parts of Nepal and Tibet witnessed torrential floods on Wednesday morning. While roads, bridges, houses, and power projects were destroyed in Nepal, a mudslide hit Gyirong Port, a major land crossing with neighbouring Tibet.

According to Reuters, it is suspected that the floods were triggered by an earthquake striking the region and causing an ice-rock avalanche on the Lhende Khola river, which runs through both Nepal and Tibet.

Despite massive devastation in Nepal, the danger may not have passed yet. Authorities have reportedly warned that a second flood may occur since a blockage is still lodged upstream on the Lhende Khola river.
Parts of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are on alert amid raging floods in Nepal.

There is a possibility in a sudden rise in water levels of the river Gandak in Bihar, and six teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) are on standby in border villagers of Bihar, HT has learnt. Districts such as Muzaffarpur, Gopalganj, Motihari, West and East Champaran and Siwan are likely to be impacted depending on water level and its flow when it reaches Bihar.
"We are in touch with Nepal authorities and tracking the water flow to India," NDRF officials said.

In Uttar Pradesh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed the administrations of Maharajganj and Kushinagar districts to take all necessary measures to deal with any potential emergency. According to PTI, an official statement from Adityanath's office expressed concerns over the Nepal floods and said they could cause the water levels to surge in the Gandak and Narayani rivers in the neighbouring districts.
