In a first, sitting SC judge flags corruption charges against HC chief justice
SC Justice Sandeep Mehta seeks immediate transfer of Rajasthan HC acting CJ Sanjeev Prakash Sharma, citing corruption, nepotism and misuse of power.

Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta has made an extraordinary intervention seeking the immediate transfer of Rajasthan High Court acting chief justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma out of the state, accusing him of “corruption”, “nepotism”, “favouritism”, misuse of roster powers and administrative decisions that benefitted influential litigants and lawyers.
Justice Mehta writes three letters to CJI Surya Kant

In three successive letters to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on August 2, 10 and 17 , all seen by HT, Justice Mehta urged the Supreme Court collegium to appoint a chief justice from another high court to Rajasthan “with immediate effect”, warning that continued inaction was causing serious damage to the institution and that it was imperative “to save the Institution from further carnage”.
HT has contacted Justice Sharma for comment but has not yet received a response.
This is the first time that a sitting SC judge has written a letter flagging actions of a sitting high court judge.
Justice Mehta, who himself hails from the Rajasthan High Court, contended that Justice Sharma had been selectively withdrawing cases from other benches and shifting them to his own court.
Also Read | Rajasthan HC takes up Gen Z, Gen Alpha concerns, asks govt's response on slew of directions

In his August 2 letter, the top court judge said he had earlier brought several such instances to the CJI’s notice and was initially asked to provide a list of cases, but was subsequently told that there was no need to put the allegations in writing and that “suitable action” would be taken. “However, till date, the request to have a chief justice from another state in my parent high court has met no positive response,” Justice Mehta wrote.
Justice Mehta said he had received several complaints about Justice Sharma’s judicial functioning which, according to him, “prima facie, raise doubts on his integrity”.

In his second letter, dated August 10, Justice Mehta put forward two specific instances which he described as “living proof” of Justice Sharma’s “brazen misuse of power” and attempts to “hit longer sixes” before his retirement on September 26.

One concerns a batch of appeals over what Justice Mehta called “priceless land” in Udaipur. He alleged that the cases were moved to a bench headed by Justice Sharma at Jaipur despite an earlier judgment by Justice Sharma himself holding that matters falling within the jurisdiction of the Jodhpur principal seat could not be transferred to Jaipur.

Justice Mehta also highlighted the identity of a senior advocate appearing in the matter, Kamlakar Sharma, alleging that Justice Sharma was “espousing” the elevation of the lawyer’s daughter-in-law as a judge of the Rajasthan High Court.
The second case involved a mining magnate, Meghraj Singh, and an appeal challenging an order passed by a single judge in criminal jurisdiction under Section 482 of the CrPC.

Justice Mehta alleged that such an order was not appealable through a special appeal but the high court registry was nevertheless “manipulated” to register the matter as a special appeal writ and list it before Justice Sharma’s bench. This bench, he said, condoned a 457-day delay on the first day of hearing on August 6 this year, issued notice and stayed a direction in the single judge’s order.

Justice Mehta also pointed to the lawyer representing the mining magnate, Sandeep Singh Shekhawat, whom he alleged had been associated with Justice Sharma during his years in practice. “It is thus clear that Mr Justice SP Sharma has taken the events triggered by the letter dated 2nd August, 2026 to be a licence to go flat out for hitting longer sixes in cases involving influential and rich litigants,” Justice Mehta wrote. He went on to say that the instances “manifest brazen misuse of powers” to favour influential parties and “smack of corruption”.

The allegations came days after CJI Surya Kant, in an unrelated case, had spoken of a growing tendency among judges to pass orders for extraneous considerations as their retirement approaches and referred to judges attempting to “hit sixes” before retiring. Justice Sharma, who is due to retire on September 26, was described by Justice Mehta as appearing to have acquired a “licence to hit sixes” since taking over as acting chief justice.
Allegations include selective case transfers, administrative lapses and alleged vendetta

The Supreme Court judge went on to contend that “clear instances of corruption, nepotism and favouritism” were being overlooked despite what he called “damning evidence”, while efforts were being made to confirm Justice Sharma as the chief justice of Rajasthan. The August 17 letter added further allegations concerning the administration of the Rajasthan high court and the treatment of members of the subordinate judiciary on account of personal vendetta.

He referred to a message allegedly written by Rajasthan High Court judge Justice Uma Shankar Vyas to a group of sitting judges, expressing anguish over what Justice Mehta described as vindictive conduct by Justice Sharma towards Vyas’s wife, Nandini Vyas, a senior officer in the district judiciary. Justice Mehta said the allegation could be independently verified and questioned how Justice Sharma could continue at the helm of the high court despite such complaints. He also alleged administrative “apathy and incompetence” in relation to a new 40-court building of the Jodhpur District Court (Metro).

According to Justice Mehta, the building had been operationally complete for about a year but Justice Sharma, after visiting it, unilaterally put its inauguration on hold and ordered wholesale changes to an infrastructure that was already complete. The decision, he said, was particularly inexplicable because several courts in the Jodhpur Metro judgeship were functioning from rented premises.

Justice Mehta described the resulting loss to the institution as “unpardonable” and said the building was eventually inaugurated by CJI Surya Kant on August 15 following a request made by him and Justice Vijay Bishnoi.
The Supreme Court judge also questioned the functioning of the Rajasthan High Court during a three-day international conference in Jaipur from July 31 to August 2.

He alleged that all judges of the high court’s principal seat at Jodhpur were nominated to sit at Jaipur, leaving the Jodhpur seat without a single functional court for two working days. Around 20 to 22 district judges were also allegedly nominated, leaving their respective districts without their senior-most judicial officers.

Justice Mehta said the conference was primarily organised by two lawyers’ organisations and that the Rajasthan government had spent almost ₹80 lakh from the public exchequer on it. He described the decision to bring the functioning of the high court to a standstill for the event as “absolutely unacceptable”, particularly against the backdrop of the court’s heavy pendency.

The August 2 letter also contains allegations relating to the designation of senior advocates. Justice Mehta said a Full Court meeting on July 31 was convened in apparent violation of Supreme Court circulars concerning Full Court meetings on working days.

He alleged that the meeting was intended to push the designation of around 96 advocates as senior advocates without any prior discussion or uniform criteria. The proposal, he said, ultimately failed after other judges resisted what he described as an “autocratic attempt”.

Justice Mehta further alleged that judges of the Rajasthan High Court had complained to him about Justice Sharma’s conduct, including alleged threats of retaliatory transfers based on claims of proximity to the CJI.
He said Justice Sharma had a “seriously skewed and biased perception” against the Jodhpur principal seat and had been heard threatening to “destroy the very fabric” of the seat.

“The Rajasthan High Court is without a regularly appointed chief justice for the last more than 10 months,” Justice Mehta wrote in his first letter, arguing that the prolonged arrangement had enabled Justice Sharma to exercise extensive administrative powers without the institutional stability of a regular chief justice.
Justice Mehta also questioned the circumstances in which Justice Sharma returned to Rajasthan.

Justice Mehta has alleged that efforts are now underway to confirm Justice Sharma as the regular chief justice of Rajasthan . His final appeal to the collegium was therefore for an immediate intervention. “I, therefore, implore your goodself and the members of the collegium to take an early decision recommending a senior Judge from any other high court to be the chief justice of the Rajasthan High Court with immediate effect,” he wrote. In his August 10 letter, Justice Mehta went further, urging the CJI and collegium to “forthwith transfer” Justice Sharma out of Rajasthan “to save the Institution from further carnage”.

Nepal minister refuses to pick sides between India, China: 'Can't replace father with mother'
When asked about China's increased economic presence in Nepal, foreign minister Shisir Khanal said two-thirds of Nepal's entire trade is with India.

Nepal's foreign minister Shisir Khanal refused to pick sides when asked about how he sees the country's ties with China and India. The minister said that both relationships are significant from their own standpoints and he wouldn't want to choose one over the other.

"We do not want to supplement one with the other (relationships with China and India). He said that Nepal runs on an emotional side but views foreign policy more rationally, thus considering both India and China as important neighbours.
When asked about China's increased economic presence in Nepal, Khanal said: "Two-thirds of Nepal's entire trade is with India."

Notably, China also factors in in India and Nepal's border issues.

Ticking Chinese bomb near India: Experts flag China's monster dam after Nepal devastation

Over 100 have been killed and at least 750 are missing in Nepal after floods triggered by an avalanche in Tibet. The devastation has made experts raise a red flag over the 60,000-MW dam that China is building in the high seismic zone in Medog county, close to the border with Arunachal Pradesh.

It's young and growing, and restless too. And once in a while, it doesn't stop from showing its fury. The Himalayas are the world's most seismically active mountain range, and a flood resulting from an earthquake-triggered avalanche has killed over 100 people on the Nepal-Tibet border, with hundreds more unaccounted for. The devastation from the unstoppable wall of flowing water also made experts caution about a monster dam that China is building just next to the border with India.

The 60,000-megawatt (MW) Medog Dam that China is building on the Yarlung Tsangpo, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, is near Arunachal Pradesh. The dam, which Beijing is looking to operationalise by 2033, is located in China-occupied Tibet Autonomous Region's (TAR's) Medog or Medong. This is a zone that is prone to earthquakes, and such a massive dam has therefore been referred to as a "water bomb" by experts.

Houses, roads and power projects were swept away in Nepal, while officials in Tibet said they feared "major casualties" from the flood triggered by the avalanche in the TAR on Wednesday. The deluge of muddy water swept down from an estimated nearly 2,000 metres (6,560 feet) above sea level.
At least 341 foreign travellers, including more than 100 Indians, are missing. Most of them are Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims.

Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament on Wednesday that initial reports suggested that an earthquake could have triggered an avalanche and caused the floods in the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems.

Even a study by geologists affiliated with China's state-run geological survey had in July found that the under-construction Medog Hydropower Station on the Brahmaputra River in Tibet sits atop an active fault line.

"The Himalayas are the world's most seismically active major mountain range, with a record of triggering devastating earthquakes. How even a moderate seismic event can trigger massive cascading effects was illustrated today when a magnitude 4.4 quake along the Tibet-Nepal border unleashed a disaster, with flash floods washing away Nepali villages," wrote strategic expert Brahma Chellaney on X.

Reports also suggested that an ice avalanche could have triggered the deadly cascade. "A chunk of ice with a width of about 2,000 feet snapped cleanly off the glacier," The New York Times reported, quoting geologist Daniel Shugar.

Though it was too early to confirm the trigger, the devastation in Nepal made experts issue a stern warning over the mega-Medog Dam. The US Geological Survey on Thursday said that the seismic activity initially reported as an earthquake "was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow" that "caused subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream".

"China will be the death of everyone and everything downstream of it. Literally, and metaphorically," wrote Tunku Varadarajan, former editor of Newsweek Global and Newsweek International, while sharing a video of a half-built dam being washed away on Wednesday.
China has been building settlements and infrastructure projects in eco-sensitive border areas.
"This [the Nepal disaster] will renew global attention on China's folly in persisting with the construction of the world's largest dam in the middle of the Himalayan seismic zone," said Chellaney.
"The project, located next to the Indo-Tibetan border, is a water bomb in the making, which could drown India's northeast and wreak havoc farther downstream in Bangladesh," he added.
Former Indian ambassador and foreign affairs commentator Rajiv Dogra too warned the risk of a "much bigger devastation" to India's northeast because of the Chinese dam.
"A much bigger devastation could strike India's North-East if China goes to complete its 60,000 MW monster dam on Brahmaputra in seismologically sensitive zone," wrote Dogra on X.
In a post on August 19, Chellaney asked the Indian government to demand that "China lift the veil of opacity surrounding the super-dam project".

"The risks posed by the new super-dam are significant because it is being built in the Himalayan seismically active belt, where the Indian and Eurasian plates collide. The belt has produced some of Asia's strongest earthquakes, including the devastating 2025 Myanmar earthquake, whose tremors extended to Thailand, causing the collapse of a high-rise building under construction in Bangkok.
CONCERNS RAISED BY CHINESE EXPERTS OVER MEDOG DAM'S STRUCTURAL SAFETY

China began the construction of what is set to become the world's largest hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo river in Tibet, triggering concerns in India over water security, flooding, ecology and the future of communities living downstream.

The project, also known as the Motuo Hydropower Station, is estimated to cost around $167 billion. Once completed, the Medog Dam will surpass China's Three Gorges Dam, which is the world's largest, to become the largest hydroelectric project in size and could generate roughly three times as much electricity, according to the Sydney-based think tank, Lowy Institute.
Fresh concerns over the structural safety of the Medog Dam were raised in July after the study by geologists affiliated with China's state-run geological survey.

According to a report by the South China Morning Post (SCMP), citing a paper published in Mandarin in the journal Sedimentary Geology and Tethyan Geology under the supervision of the state-owned China Geological Survey, researchers identified the active Paizhen Fault directly beneath the Medog Dam site on the Yarlung Tsangpo.
WHY IS INDIA CONCERNED OVER CHINESE DAM ON YARLUNG TSANGPO?
The Yarlung Tsangpo flows from Tibet into Arunachal Pradesh, where it is known as the Siang, before becoming the Brahmaputra as it moves through Assam and eventually enters Bangladesh.

The Medog Dam that China is building is located in one of the most dramatic sections of the Yarlung Tsangpo, where the river makes a huge U-turn around Mount Namcha Barwa of Tibet. The river descends sharply through a deep canyon, creating enormous potential for hydropower generation. China plans to develop five cascading hydropower stations in the region.
The sheer scale and location of the project have raised concerns in India because China controls the upper reaches of a river that is crucial to communities, agriculture and ecosystems downstream.

A concern for India is China's ability to influence the flow of the Brahmaputra once the dam is fully constructed. Though the Brahmaputra gets most of the water from monsoon-fed tributaries in India, it is still a lower-riparian country. Any major alteration in the volume or timing of water released from Tibet could potentially affect Arunachal Pradesh and Assam.

During periods of heavy rainfall, a sudden release of water from reservoirs could increase the risk of flooding downstream. On the other hand, a prolonged reduction in releases during dry periods could affect water availability for agriculture, fisheries and local communities.

When India put the Indus Water Treaty (IWT) in abeyance against Pakistan's state-sponsored terror that killed 26 civilians in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam, Islamabad had hinted that China, being the upper riparian country, might be capable of controlling the flow of the Tsangpo-Brahmaputra river system.

Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu had in 2025 warned that the Siang and Brahmaputra could potentially see a major reduction in water flow. He has also described the project as an existential concern for tribal communities living along the Siang, particularly because of the possibility of sudden releases from a massive upstream reservoir.
INDIA'S MEGA PROJECT TO MANAGE CHINESE DAM'S THREAT
One of India's strategic concerns is that a mega dam could give Beijing greater leverage over a transboundary river.

India had raised concerns with China over large hydropower projects on the upper reaches of rivers shared by the two countries. The fear is not necessarily that China would deliberately cut off India's water supply, but that control over the tap of such a strategically important river could provide Beijing with significant influence over downstream water flows.
India has also been preparing for the possibility of increased water-flow fluctuations.

New Delhi is advancing a large 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project on the Siang river in Arunachal Pradesh to counter upstream Chinese dam construction so that the water flow can be controlled.
DIDN'T CHINA ISSUE AN EARLY WARNING TO NEPAL?

India's challenge is that it has limited control over developments taking place on the Tibetan side of the river. This makes information-sharing and real-time hydrological data particularly important. The similar situation was witnessed in Nepal on Wednesday.
Kathmandu-based journalist Parshuram Kaphle said Beijing didn't alert Nepal about the massive wall of water moving downstream.

"Nepal has been addressing the legitimate security concerns of our neighbors. However, it must be said with sadness that our northern neighbor has significantly undermined us. By failing to provide early warning of such a massive disaster, we suffered immense loss of human life," wrote Kaphle on X.
US-based Tibetan lawyer Tenzin Tsering said that Kathmandu, in all probability, wouldn't hold Beijing accountable for the disaster.

"But Nepal will likely never hold China accountable for this devastating flood. China is pursuing a similar strategy with India by constructing a massive dam in the southern Tibet region," Tsering wrote on X, commenting about the Medog Dam project.

The absence of a comprehensive water-sharing treaty between India and China, under which real-time hydrological information can be shared, adds another layer to the Medog Dam problem. The biggest concern, however, remains the massive size of the dam and it being situated in a quake-prone region.
Experts are pointing to the Medog Dam as a "water bomb", and the devastation in Nepal reveals the risk that China would be posing to India's northeast with the project.

Shashi Tharoor's vocab lesson amid flak over 'drama' remark on Nepal floods
A single word sparked backlash against Shashi Tharoor over his Nepal flood post. The Congress leader has now explained why he used "drama" and admitted he regretted the choice.

Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday clarified his use of the word "drama" in a post on the Nepal flash floods, saying he had used it in the sense of "a state, situation or series of events involving intensely clashing forces". He also said he regretted choosing a word that could be so easily "misinterpreted".

The clarification came a day after Tharoor faced criticism on social media for saying he had been "blissfully unaware of the drama that had taken place in the hills" while referring to the disaster in Nepal. Several users called the wording insensitive and questioned his choice of words.

In a post on X, the Thiruvananthapuram MP said, "For all those fulminating in outrage about my use of the word 'drama' in my first tweet from Nepal, the word does not only mean something theatrical. It is also defined as 'a state, situation or series of events involving intensely clashing forces'." He added, "That's the sense in which I intended it. But I do regret the choice of a word that could be so easily misinterpreted."

Tharoor's remarks came after his Thursday post on the Nepal flash floods drew sharp reactions online. In that post, he had said, "Took off for Kathmandu yesterday, blissfully unaware of the drama that had taken place in the hills and caused such catastrophic damage."

He also wrote, "A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal's Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise."

Tharoor had said he learnt on arrival about the loss of life and that some 2,000 or more people were estimated to be missing. He said raging floodwaters had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges, washed away roughly 40 kilometres of the Betrawati Rasuwagadhi highway, and heavily damaged eight operational hydropower projects.

He had also said, "I fully support the Indian government's immediate pledge of relief assistance. Nepal needs all the help it can get." In the same post, he added, "My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon."

Despite that broader message, many users focused on his wording. One user said, "Was nature's fury a 'drama'? How can you be so insensitive in your choice of words? What good is knowing the dictionary if you don't know what to say when? Your 'sympathy' seems like the drama here!"

Another wrote, "Sir, you are Shakespeare of Indian English. Is the usage of the word DRAMA in the second sentence of the first para appropriate?" A third user called it a "poor choice of words for someone with such a rich vocabulary".
Another post said, "Mr Exasperating Farrago -- Is this 'drama'?" while one more user wrote, "Drama?? You are a wordsmith, and this is what you came up with?"

Tharoor has now defended the intended meaning of the word while accepting that it could be misunderstood, after his post on the Nepal flash floods triggered a backlash and debate over his choice of language.

Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay moved from his designated chair and sat beside ministers in the Tamil Nadu Assembly. The unusual shift came amid a discussion on officials' presence in the House and broke with established seating practice.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay broke with a long-standing Assembly convention on Thursday when he moved away from his designated chair and sat alongside ministers in the front row during the afternoon session of the state Assembly.

Vijay's move drew attention as chief ministers traditionally occupy a separate chair positioned close to the Speaker's seat. Ministers sit separately in the front row alongside the Chief Minister, with their positions generally determined by seniority.
The Opposition occupies the row facing the treasury benches.

The Leader of the Opposition and leaders of various legislature parties are seated according to their numerical strength in the 234-member House, with members of their respective parties seated behind them.

During Thursday's afternoon proceedings, Vijay casually left his designated chair, located to the right of Speaker JCD Prabhakar, and took a seat between ministers KA Sengottaiyan, who is also the Leader of the House, and Aadhav Arjuna.
A source said it was unusual for a chief minister to move from the chair specifically designated for the post and sit in a seat meant for a minister.
While ministers and legislators occasionally change seats for brief conversations with colleagues, the source said such a move by a chief minister was perhaps unprecedented.

OPPOSITION RAISES ISSUE OF OFFICIALS' PRESENCE
Earlier on Thursday, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin raised concerns over the absence of department secretaries from the Assembly when members discussed important issues.

Udhayanidhi referred to discussions surrounding the Karur stampede and recalled that during the previous DMK government, former Chief Minister MK Stalin and senior bureaucrats, including the Chief Secretary and department secretaries, were present in the House when the issue was discussed.
He said the same level of administrative presence was missing during the current Assembly session.
Responding to the Opposition leader, Aadhav Arjuna said department secretaries were present in an adjoining "war room" and were taking notes from the speeches and issues raised by legislators.
Speaker JCD Prabhakar agreed with Udhayanidhi's suggestion and said senior officials would be asked to remain present in the Assembly during proceedings.
The exchange came amid discussions on the functioning of the House and the coordination between the political leadership and senior government officials.

Vijay's unusual seating shift later in the day, meanwhile, became one of the notable moments of Thursday's Assembly proceedings, departing from the traditional seating arrangement followed by successive chief ministers.

Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks off Odisha coast, 2 survivors rescued, 22 missing
A Panama-flagged cargo ship carrying 24 crew members sank after communication was lost off Odisha, prompting a major Coast Guard-Navy rescue operation as the search for survivors continues.

A Panama-flagged bulk carrier carrying 24 crew members sank in the Bay of Bengal, around 240 nautical miles from Odisha's Paradip coast, on Saturday, triggering a major search-and-rescue operation by the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) and Indian Navy.

The vessel, MV Ocean Winner (IMO 9145530), was carrying 20 Chinese, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi crew member, according to the ICG. Its last port of call was Paradip and its next scheduled port was Singapore.
The ICG has so far confirmed that two survivors have been rescued from two liferafts, while the search continues for the remaining 22 crew members.
COMMUNICATION LOST WITH MV OCEAN WINNER

The ICG's Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Sri Vijaya Puram received information at 11:48 am from a company associated with the vessel about the loss of communication with MV Ocean Winner.
The company also requested search-and-rescue assistance, the ICG said.
The bulk carrier was carrying iron ore from Odisha and was bound for Singapore.
Following the alert, the MRCC diverted MT Aisopos, a commercial vessel that was operating in the vicinity, to search for MV Ocean Winner or liferafts and render assistance.
MT Aisopos recovered two survivors from two liferafts at around 8 pm, according to the ICG.
The condition of the rescued crew members was not immediately available.
The Indian Coast Guard and Indian Navy have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation to locate the remaining crew members.
ICG ships Varad and Anmol have been deployed for the search, while Vijit has been sent from Sri Vijaya Puram to augment the operation.
Other vessels in the area are also being coordinated with as authorities continue efforts to locate survivors and liferafts.
MV Ocean Winner had 24 crew members on board when it sank — 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi national.
With two survivors rescued so far, the search continues for the remaining 22 crew members.

The exact circumstances that led to the sinking of the vessel have not yet been established. Further details about the ship's condition before it sank and the status of the missing crew members are awaited.

This comes after Maharashtra transport minister Pratap Sarnaik on August 12 notified the rule that drivers of passenger transport vehicles must have a working knowledge of Marathi to communicate effectively with commuters.

The petition by the cab drivers, which was filed through advocate Vivek Shukla, will be mentioned tomorrow (August 26) before the Chief Justice for urgent directions, Bar and Bench reported. It seeks an immediate stay on the government notification to prevent challenges to nearly 9.65 lakh drivers across Maharashtra.

The plea submitted by the four cab drivers argues that the rule regarding compulsory knowledge of Marathi violates their fundamental rights under Articles 14 (right to equality), 19 (freedom to carry on trade and profession) and 21 (right to life) of the Constitution.
It says that the rule is ultra vires the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which does not prescribe any language requirement for driving licences, according to the Bar and Bench report.

“The parent Act (Motor Vehicles Act) confers no power upon the State Government to prescribe working knowledge of any language as a qualification for a driver, as a condition of a badge, or as a condition of a permit, and confers no power to suspend or revoke a badge on such a ground,” the petition states. It argues that the language rule “manufactures a new disqualification and a new ground of suspension” which had not been enacted by the Parliament.

The ambush was carried out on Thursday between Makui Ashang and Thanamba Naga in Kangpokpi district while the Naga group was returning from Makui village to Senapati after attending a meeting.

On Friday, the funeral processesion was allowed to proceed towards Senapati on Friday morning amid deployment of local police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF). Post-mortem will be conducted at the Senapati district hospital, police said.

The remains were first received by civil society organisations at Thonglang Atongba, a Liangmei village, at around 8:30 am. The village authority presented four shawls in honour of the deceased during the reception. A large number of people gathered along the route and at the reception point to pay their last respects.
Meanwhile, Gaikamang Ringkangmai, 44, who sustained a bullet injury to his left forearm in the attack, is undergoing treatment at Senapati District Hospital.

Ringkangmai, said: “I could see the attackers. They were positioned in pairs of two. Some of them had long hairs and were wearing full camouflage uniforms. They had red ribbons tied on the top of their rifles from which they continued firing. They also pushed the vehicle into the gorge.”

Following the killings, the Naga People’s Organisation (NPO) called for an immediate shutdown of all shops and business establishments in Senapati district headquarters.

The United Naga Council (UNC) condemned the killings and demanded that those responsible be booked and brought to justice. The UNC further demanded the constitution of a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the attack.

The UNC announced the shutdown from 6 am to 6 pm on August 28 across Naga areas and district headquarters. During the observance, vehicle movement, shops and business establishments, as well as government and private schools and colleges, will remain closed.
The killings have heightened tension in parts of Kangpokpi and Senapati districts.

Since the May 13 twin ambush at two different places (Noney, a Naga -dominated district and Kangpokpi, Kuki-dominated district), in which four civilians including three church leaders and one Naga man were killed, tension has simmered between Naga and Kuki-Zo communities.

On the same day, 48 civilians belonging to Naga and Kuki-Zo were held captivated by both the groups in retaliatory tension. Later, nearly after a month of captivity all the hostages were set free however, 6 Naga men were found dead near Kharam Vaiphei (Kuki village) in Kangpokpi district.
Four persons including a couple were arrested, in two different raids in July, in connection with the killings by the national investigating agency (NIA).

Ethnic clashes have been reported in Manipur from May 3, 2023, between Kuki-Zo and Meitei communities. Clashes later spread between Naga and Kuki communities following the May 13 twin ambush incident.

Meanwhile, Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand on Thursday here in Imphal called for identifying individuals and leaders working against peace in the violence-hit state and taking action against them under the law, while stressing the need for dialogue and “trust diplomacy” to bridge the trust deficit between communities.
“There are people who don’t want peace. We have to identify them as soon as possible. As far as the law is concerned, we have to book them,” Khemchand said.

Khemchand said that a trust deficit exists in the state and said it cannot be addressed without direct communication between communities. Recalling his visits to Jiribam and meetings with people from different communities, including Kuki representatives, he said he had realised that peace efforts must begin with positive engagement.

“Without talking to each other, without dialogue, and without understanding each other’s fears, we cannot reduce the trust deficit through diplomacy,” he said.

The CM highlighted the role of security forces during the crisis, particularly in protecting civilians and helping displaced people return safely. He said more than 17,000 people from different communities were affected or displaced during the crisis.
The CM said vigilance and enforcement of law were necessary, but the ultimate goal must remain peace, reconciliation and a secure future for the children of Manipur.
Teary-eyed Karnataka minister B Nagendra resigns from cabinet, as MLA amid financial irregularity row
The opposition BJP had been mounting pressure on the DK Shivakumar government to seek B Nagendra's resignation.

Karnataka Minister B Nagendra announced his resignation from the state Cabinet led by chief minister DK Shivakumar, as well as from his MLA seat, on Friday, following allegations of his involvement in financial irregularities at the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribe Development Corporation.
In tears at a press conference, he said he had decided to “voluntarily step down” to avoid “embarrassment to the party”.

"I am resigning of my own will to avoid the embarrassment that may cost my party because of unnecessary allegations made by the opposition party against me," he said, adding that he was a victim of the BJP's “manuvadi” politics.

Nagendra's resignation came amid heightened political pressure on him and the Congress government over the alleged Valmiki Corporation scam. The BJP and JD(S) have been demanding the minister's resignation since his re-induction into the Cabinet on August 3, alleging that he was linked to the alleged diversion of funds from the state-run corporation.

The opposition staged repeated protests inside and outside the legislature during the recent monsoon session, which was curtailed by three days and adjourned sine die on August 24 amid the continued uproar.
The two parties had also planned a foot march from Raichur to Ballari, demanding Nagendra's resignation from September 1 to 10.
What is the Valmiki Cooperation scam?

The controversy around B Nagendra dates back to May 2024, when P Chandrasekharan, then an accounts superintendent with the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation, died by suicide and left a six-page note alleging irregularities and unauthorised transfers of corporation funds.

Subsequent investigations found that ₹89.63 crore had been transferred from a corporation account to a Union Bank of India account and subsequently moved to multiple other accounts, triggering a major political controversy.

B Nagendra, who was the tribal welfare minister when the controversy surfaced, had resigned from the Cabinet in June 2024. He was re-inducted on August 3, 2026, with the Planning and Statistics portfolio, prompting the Opposition to revive its demand for his removal.

After Nepal says no to foreign help, India to send tunnel rescue team ‘on request’
External affairs minister S Jaishankar said that NDRF personnel may be sent if Nepal requires it and that two planes of relief materials have already gone.

As India continues to extend helping hand to flood-ravaged Nepal, external affairs minister S Jaishankar on Friday said that a team of tunneling experts is being sent as nearly a hundred people are stranded in a hydropower tunnel. This comes amid Nepal government denying help from foreign countries saying that its security agencies are capable of handling the rescue operation.

Jaishankar was speaking to the media after meeting group of 21 people who returned to Delhi from flood-ravaged Nepal on Friday. The minister said that a team of NDRF personnel may also be sent if Nepal requires it, adding that two planes of relief materials have already gone and third one will be sent on later in the day.

“The main thing is that in one place where there is a hydroelectric project, there could be possibility of people who may be a tunnel. So, we are sending a team to help with the experts in tunneling. Also, they need some bailey bridges, so we are sending bridges. These are bridges that can be quickly put together along with a team. There may be some medical teams also going out there. If they require NDRF people to go, we will send them. We have given them that option. Two planes of relief supplies have already gone out there and third plane will be taking off today,” Jaishankar said.

While 85 Indians were rescued in Nepal on Friday, 315 still remain out of contact, Jaishankar noted. “We are still very much focused on contacting all the Indians who are there,” he said, adding that those who were evacuated and safely sent to India were thankful to Nepalese army.

Jaishankar further added that he spoke to Nepal's foreign minister on Friday morning as India remains focused on helping the flood-ravaged Nepal in the relief and rescue of people.

“We have given them a range of support offers, they are evaluating it. Whatever they feel is appropriate, they will pick up for their needs. Right now, the main thing is that in one place where there is a hydroelectric project, there could be possibility of people who may be a tunnel. So, we are sending a team to help with the experts in tunneling,” he said.

“Also, they need some bailey bridges, so we are sending bridges. These are bridges that can be quickly put together along with a team. There may be some medical teams also going out there. If they require NDRF people to go, we will send them. ”

The ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also said this earlier during the weekly MEA briefing. “As requested by the Nepal, we are preparing to send a Tunnel rescue team, for which a recce team is being flown in first to assess the equipment required etc. A medical team is also being sent. In addition, we have also offered Bailey bridges along with their associated technical teams so that connectivity can be restored quickly in the affected parts of Nepal. One Bailey bridge is already in Nepal and can be deployed for relief efforts," Jaiswal said.

Nepal has turned down offers from several countries to send search and rescue teams after devastating flash floods hit towns and villages near the China border. Nepal's Balen Shah-led government said on Friday that its security agencies are capable of handling the rescue operation.
At least 547 people have died and over 1,500 remain missing since Wednesday. Rescuers are searching through mud and debris, while newly formed barrier lakes raise fears of more flooding.

“The offer for help is natural. Our security agencies are doing the search and rescue operation. For now we don’t require such help,” Lok Bahadur Chhetri, spokesperson for Nepal’s foreign ministry, said, news agency Reuters reported.
The government has received requests from India, China, the US, UK, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh to allow their search and rescue teams to assist with the operation.

The official said the decision was influenced by Nepal’s experience during the 2015 earthquake, when the arrival of a large number of foreign rescue teams created coordination challenges. As many as 76 international urban search-and-rescue teams from 34 countries responded to the disaster, along with foreign medical and military teams.

The Defence Ministry has simplified export and licensing norms to help Indian defence manufacturers access global markets faster.

Under the revised Defence Export Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), stakeholder consultation [with Ministries and government agencies concerned] has been dispensed with for exports of non-lethal defence items to most destinations. Safeguards, however, will continue to apply to sensitive countries. The requirement has also been removed for exports of all items for international tenders and exhibitions, allowing Indian companies to participate in overseas opportunities more expeditiously.

The Ministry’s Department of Defence Production has also overhauled the Open General Export Licence (OGEL) framework, which provides eligible exporters a standing, one-time authorisation to self-generate export authorisations for multiple consignments of specified defence items without seeking separate approval for every shipment.
Three existing OGEL SOPs covering major platforms and equipment, parts and components, and intra-company transfer of technology have been consolidated into a single framework.

The validity of OGEL has been increased from two to three years, reducing the frequency of renewals and associated compliance requirements. Its country coverage has also been expanded from 41 to all countries, except negative and sensitive nations, and those subject to United Nations Security Council sanctions or arms embargoes.

A new provision has been introduced for Indian companies having long-term contracts or agreements with foreign original equipment manufacturers (FOEMs). An OGEL can be granted for eligible items for the particular FOEM, with validity aligned with the underlying contract or agreement, subject to prescribed conditions.

The range of items eligible for export under OGEL has also been expanded. The revised framework permits civil-end-use exports of specified parts and components of small-calibre arms and protective equipment, widening the scope for legitimate international business.

The reforms are intended to reduce routine procedural requirements while retaining safeguards for sensitive items, technologies, and destinations. The Ministry said the measures would particularly benefit Indian defence manufacturers, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), by helping them respond faster to international tenders and exhibitions, and reducing repetitive authorisation requirements.

The measures come amid a record growth in India’s defence manufacturing and exports. Defence production reached an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, while exports touched a record ₹38,424 crore during the financial year.

Hi5, smiles and more: PM Modi's day out with children on Raksha Bandhan

Narendra Modi celebrated Raksha Bandhan with schoolgirls and students at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg, where they tied rakhis and exchanged high-fives. The images and social media posts placed the festival interaction within a broader push for informal digital outreach to younger audiences.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Raksha Bandhan with schoolgirls and students at his official residence at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg, on Friday, sharing moments of interaction, smiles and high-fives with the young visitors.
In a post on Instagram, PM Modi shared glimpses of the celebrations and captioned them, “Hi5, smiles and more during today’s Raksha Bandhan celebrations at 7, LKM.”

The visuals showed the Prime Minister engaging with the students in an informal and relaxed setting as they marked the festival. The event featured young students in school uniforms, including some dressed in NCC cadet attire, tying rakhis around PM Modi’s wrist as a symbol of affection and protection.
PM Modi was seen seated among the students and interacting directly with them.
Traditional Raksha Bandhan items, including a ceremonial bowl, were also visible during the celebrations.
In several moments, the Prime Minister exchanged high-fives with the young participants and smiled as he interacted with them.
The interaction can be viewed as another avenue for PM Modi to connect with younger audiences, particularly GenZ, through informal and relatable engagements.

The use of candid interactions, high-fives and social media-friendly visuals also reflects how political communication is increasingly moving beyond formal public meetings and traditional political events.
The outreach comes amid a broader emphasis on engaging younger audiences through digital platforms and more informal interactions.

While the Prime Minister's post did not explicitly describe the Raksha Bandhan celebration as a GenZ outreach initiative, the participation of school students and the manner in which the interaction was presented online could contribute to building a more youthful and approachable public image.

Earlier, PM Modi extended his greetings to people on Raksha Bandhan, wishing them happiness, prosperity and success. In a post on X, he said he hoped the festival would preserve the bond of love, affection and mutual trust symbolised by Raksha Bandhan, and remain “forever unbreakable”.

Raksha Bandhan celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters traditionally tie colourful rakhis after applying tilak, while brothers offer gifts and reaffirm their support. The festival is observed on the full moon day of Shravana, generally in August, and is primarily celebrated in India and Nepal.

Madras HC issues notice to MK Stalin, DMK IT Wing over ₹1cr defamation suit
The Madras High Court issued notices to MK Stalin and the DMK IT Wing on Aadhav Arjuna’s ₹1 crore defamation suit over an X post linking him to a drug case.

The Madras High Court on Friday issued notices to former Tamil Nadu chief minister and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president MK Stalin and the party’s IT Wing on a ₹1 crore civil defamation suit filed by state minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) leader Aadhav Arjuna over an X post allegedly linking him to a narcotics case accused.

The notices issued by Justice K Govindarajan Thilakavadi, after hearing preliminary submissions from Arjuna’s counsel, are returnable by September 15. The judge also took note of senior counsel J. Ravindran entering appearance for Stalin and the DMK IT Wing.

Arjuna told the Court that the X post made by DMK’s IT Wing was “ex facie false” and highly defamatory. The post, shared by the DMK IT Wing’s official X handle, claimed that John Britto, an accused in a narcotics case involving the alleged smuggling of banned substances worth ₹258 crore, was related to Arjuna.
Arjuna has denied having any connection with the accused.
Also Read: Stalin moves high court over Kolathur election defeat, alleges VVPAT lapses

According to Arjuna’s suit, the John Britto referred to in the narcotics case was not his relative. His relative, P John Britto, had in fact approached the Greater Chennai Commissioner of Police and complained that he was being wrongly identified with the John Britto arrested in the narcotics case because of the similarity in their names.

Arjuna has asked the High Court to declare the June 8 post defamatory and direct Stalin and the DMK IT Wing to pay ₹1 crore as compensation for the alleged loss of reputation, personal injury and mental agony caused by the post.
He has also sought a permanent injunction restraining Stalin and the DMK IT Wing from making similar statements against him in future.

Arjuna has further sought directions to Stalin and the DMK IT Wing to issue unconditional apologies in both Tamil and English through their social media accounts, as well as widely circulated Tamil and English newspapers and television channels. He has sought that the apologies be given the same prominence as the allegedly defamatory post.

He has also asked the court to direct the deletion of the post and screenshots of it circulating on social media, and to surrender electronic records relating to its creation. He has sought reimbursement of the costs incurred in filing the suit.

Arjuna has alleged that the post was not an isolated statement by a social media functionary of the DMK, but was published on the instructions of Stalin, whom he described as exercising complete control over the affairs of the party.
In June this year, Arjuna had issued a legal notice to Stalin and the DMK IT Wing demanding a public apology within 48 hours over the allegations.
At the time, he had alleged that Stalin and the DMK were “wantonly and wilfully” tarnishing the Minister’s image by linking him to John Britto.

Arjuna had maintained that John Britto had no relationship with him and that the other John Britto had already approached the Chennai Police Commissioner to clarify that he was not the person arrested in the drug smuggling case.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Thursday announced that the government has decided to give autorickshaw and taxi drivers one year to learn “functional Marathi”.
The Chief Minister made the announcement after a delegation of representatives of autorickshaw and taxi drivers, led by Haji Arfat Shaikh, met him.

“They requested one year’s time. The State government has accepted their demand. No action will be taken against the during this period. Marathi classes will be organised and study material will be provided to help migrant drivers learn functional Marathi. They have come forward and are willing to learn. Therefore, it was necessary to give them time,” Mr. Fadnavis said.
The move comes days after the Transport Department headed by Shiv Sena Minister Pratap Sarnaik carried out a checking drive and issued notices to drivers who failed a Marathi test.

The State government faced backlash by a section of drivers, especially ahead of the 2027 Assembly election in Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled Uttar Pradesh. Maharashtra hosts a large workforce from U.P. across major economic hubs like Mumbai, Pune, and Nashik.

Mr. Fadnavis said the representatives shared the concerns of drivers. “They support the decision to learn functional Marathi, but said people of different age groups are in the profession. Many of them left studies years ago. In such a short span, it is difficult for them to learn the language. They have made an elaborate plan to learn functional Marathi in one year. So, the State government will help them learn it,” he said.

The government had announced in April that non-Marathi drivers must attain basic proficiency in the State’s official language and set August 15 as the deadline. Marathi classes were then organised for the drivers in the interim period.

Meanwhile, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde lauded Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik for the bid to bring and implement the decision. He said that 1.60 lakh non-Marathi people learnt the language because of this initiative. He also said that 15,000 to 20,000 auto and taxi drivers were certified in Mumbai alone.

Javelin missile explained: How anti-tank system India is buying uses ‘fire-and-forget’ tech to destroy armoured targets
The anti-tank missile system is currently used by the US Army and Marine Corps as well as several international customers.

India has signed the letter of offer and acceptance with the United States to purchase the Javelin anti-tank guided missile system through its foreign military sales process. This comes nine months after the US State Department approved the possible sale, reportedly worth $45.7 million, to the Indian Army following New Delhi’s request.

The missile system is produced by the Javelin Joint Venture, a partnership between RTX and Lockheed Martin, and is currently used by the US Army and Marine Corps as well as several international customers. It is designed to be used against a wide array of targets, including armoured vehicles and fortified positions.
US ambassador to India Sergio Gor hailed the move as one which would further deepen bilateral defence cooperation.
All you need to know about the Javelin system

The Javelin system is an advanced, medium-range, fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile. According to the Lockheed Martin website, it is one of the world's “premier” shoulder-fired anti-armor system.

The anti-tank missile system automatically guides itself to the target after launch, allowing the gunner to take cover and avoid counterfire, according to the manufacturer. The soldiers or marines using it can reposition immediately after firing, or reload to “engage another threat.”

The weapon uses an arched top-attack profile, climbing above its target for improved visibility, and then strikes where the armor is weakest, according to Lockheed Martin. To fire, the personnel has to place a cursor over the selected target, following which the Javelin command launch unit sends a lock-on-before-launch signal to the missile.
📌Key features and other details
• Javelin is a single man-portable fire-and-forget medium-range antitank weapon system designed to defeat all known and projected threat armor. It can be fired in top or direct attack modes.
• It was developed and produced for the US Army and Marine Corps by the Javelin Joint Venture between Lockheed Martin in Orlando, Florida and Raytheon in Tucson, Arizona.
• The highly lethal medium-range Javelin has been in full-rate production since 1994, and made its 50,000th delivery in 2021, according to the Lockheed Martin website.
• Lockheed Martin specified that the anti-tank missile system's fire-and-forget capability provides “superior survivability” by enabling the operator to immediately relocate after firing.

• The anti-tank weapon is a platform-employed precision weapon system, and can defeat “all known and projected armor on the battlefield”, including main battle tanks and softer targets. Its soft-launch design allows the system to be fired safely from enclosed structures, including buildings and bunkers.
What did US ambassador Gor say on the agreement?
US ambassador Sergio Gor on Friday said the agreement “reflects a defense partnership that is growing deeper, more capable, and more consequential.”

“The Javelin agreement demonstrates the depth of US support for the Indian Army and creates new opportunities for our defense industries to work together. We see tremendous potential for future cooperation that strengthens the defense industrial bases of both countries,” Gor added.

Gor made the announcement on X, saying the purchase, “highlighted by” US secretary of war Pete Hegseth at the May 2026 Shangri-La Dialogue, was a “great step forward in the US-India defense relationship and opens the door to co-production possibilities.” He further said that the engagement between Washington and New Delhi was “at record high levels.”

India sets sights on US Javelin anti-tank missile system. What is it?
One of the most famous anti-tank weapons in the world, the Javelin missile system uses fire-and-forget technology. It will be a potent addition to India's arsenal after last year's Operation Sindoor.

India plans to buy the US-made shoulder-fired Javelin anti-tank guided missile system (ATGM), US ambassador to India Sergio Gor announced on Friday, signalling further deepening of defence ties between Delhi and Washington. Calling it "big news", Gor asserted that it would open the door to co-production possibilities of Javelin missiles.

"Big news! India plans to buy the battle-tested Javelin anti-tank system... This is a great step forward in the US-India defence relationship and opens the door to co-production possibilities. The engagement between our two nations is at record-high levels," Gor tweeted.

The Indian army has signed a Letter of Offer and Acceptance (LOA) for the purchase of the Javelin missiles under emergency procurement. The development comes months after Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and his US counterpart Pete Hegseth signed a 10-year framework to deepen bilateral defence relations.
The deal, which will be through the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) route, will allow the armed forces to bypass the convoluted and long procurement process for contracts.

India's interest in the American FGM-148 Javelin system, however, is not new. Issues like technology transfer and local production have repeatedly stalled India's plans to procure one of the most famous anti-tank weapons in the world. In fact, talks have been ongoing since 2010.
WHAT IS JAVELIN ANTI-TANK MISSILE SYSTEM?
Jointly manufactured by Raytheon and Lockheed Martin, Javelin is a man-portable, fire-and-forget missile system. This means the operator does not have to manually guide the weapon to the target.
The missile system, which costs around $178,000, locks onto the target's heat signature before launch using its infrared seeker.

What makes the Javelin exceptional is its ability to strike tanks from above, where their armour is the weakest. Modern tanks are basically designed to survive frontal attacks. After being fired, the missile climbs to an altitude of 150 meters, and then dives onto the target from above.

Imagine a war scenario where battle tanks are pitted against Javelin missiles. A battle tank costs around $4 million. An infantry soldier carrying a Javelin system on his shoulder can destroy that tank in under 15 seconds.

Also consider the cost - the total Javelin system, including the command launch unit, costs a fraction of the target it's designed to kill. This is what makes the FGM-148 Javelin one of the most sought-after infantry weapons of the 21st century.
WHY IS IT KEY FOR INDIA'S ARMED FORCES?
When inducted, the Javelin missile system will undoubtedly be a potent addition to India's weaponry, especially following the hostilities with Pakistan last year.

In fact, the Indian Army's requirement for an advanced ATGM emerged in the early 2000s. Then, the Army was using the ageing French-origin Milan-2T and Soviet-era 9M113 Konkurs-M systems. While both were reliable, they were no match for third-generation ATGMs like Javelin.

The missile system was inducted by the US armed forces in the mid-1990s. Since then, it has evolved through several variants. While the base model has a maximum range of 2,500 metres, the more advanced FGM-148F system can fire missiles up to a range of 4,750 metres.
When the Indian forces ultimately acquire the Javelin system, it will bring to a close one of the longest-running defence procurement chapters in recent years.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear a petition on August 31 seeking a directive to the Centre and others to ensure mandatory and uniform labelling on every dispensing nozzle at petrol pumps, disclosing the exact percentage of ethanol in petrol.According to the apex court's causelist of August 31, the plea would come up for hearing before a bench comprising Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale.The petition, filed by Narendra Kumar Goswami, has also sought a direction that every fuel invoice should specifically and legibly state the percentage of ethanol in the petrol sold."Direct the respondents (Centre and others) to prepare and publish within a stipulated time an official, public, vehicle-wise compatibility database searchable by manufacturer, model, engine type and year of manufacture, indicating the suitability or otherwise of various ethanol blends for each vehicle," the plea said.It has also sought constitution of an independent expert committee comprising representatives from the ministries of petroleum and natural gas, road transport and highways, the Bureau of Indian Standards and others, including independent automobile engineers, to examine and submit a public report on real-world vehicle compatibility of E20 across the existing fleet.The plea said the committee should also submit a report on the impact on fuel efficiency, engine longevity and maintenance costs, warranty and insurance implications, the net environmental footprint, including tail-pipe emissions and water consumption associated with ethanol production, and food-security and feed-diversion concerns allegedly arising from the blending programme.

"Direct the respondents to frame a national consumer disclosure protocol for all ethanol-blended petrol, in consultation with the Central Consumer Protection Authority and the Bureau of Indian Standards," it said.It also sought directions to the concerned authorities to place before the apex court all policy files, technical studies, compatibility reports, safety standards, consumer advisories and records of public consultation that support the compulsory roll-out of E20.

Several students from at least two medical colleges and hospitals in Kolkata were summoned by the Swastha Bhawan (State Health Department Headquarters) in relation to a blood smuggling scam in West Bengal. The fourth-year medical students faced questioning on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) at the health department.

At least four students from the National Medical College and Nil Ratan Sircar Medical College appeared before a committee of the West Bengal health department for questioning in connection with the blood smuggling scam.

State Health Minister Dr. Sharadwat Mukherjee said that their officials are still investigating the irregularities. “In many places, there is a mismatch of documents. There is a case in court, so we will not comment more on this at the moment,” Dr. Mukherjee said.

According to sources, these medical students were disguised as doctors and were taken to medical and blood donation camps, which helped facilitate the scam. Reportedly, senior medical students had an arrangement with private blood banks to run this racket, for which they took a monetary commission.

Meanwhile, at least three laboratory technicians have also been arrested from Panskura, Purba Medinipur district by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) for their alleged involvement in the blood selling racket. Previously, the police had also arrested a tout who helped to operate this racket.

The tout used to buy the blood donor cards from local clubs for Rs 100-150 each and then collect free blood from blood banks and sell it to families of patients for ₹1,500-₹2,000 per unit. The collected money was distributed among all stakeholders in this racket, according to sources.

Two weeks back, the State health officials uncovered a blood selling scam in the State which led to at least six blood banks being under the scanner and at least 11 were asked to stop organising blood donation scams.
The sale of blood is prohibited under the National Blood Policy, which was introduced in 2002.

According to the health department officials, in multiple blood camps, especially in the districts, donors were offered incentives for donating blood. Which is illegal under the National Blood Policy.
Then several units of both blood and plasma were sold to states outside West Bengal. The authorities are now exploring a multi-state scam which is suspected to be worth crores.
Since then, several blood banks, including a few reputed organisations have been raided by the State health department officials.

The slugfest between the two Bihar leaders erupted earlier this week when Manjhi's HAM backed sub-quotas for SCs and STs within the existing reservation system. Manjhi's son and Bihar minister Santosh Kumar Suman said a review was needed to ensure that reservation benefits reach the most vulnerable and historically marginalised communities.
"We are not talking about ending reservation. We are talking about making reservation more just, effective and ensuring that it actually reaches those who are deprived," Suman said.
WHAT IS THE CONTROVERSY ABOUT?
Both Paswan's LJP (Ram Vilas) and HAM(S) are allies of the NDA in Bihar as well as at the Centre. Manjhi belongs to the Mushahar group, among the most backward Dalit groups.

The controversy has its roots in a 2024 Supreme Court judgment.
In a big verdict that year, the Supreme Court allowed states to sub-classify SCs and STs to ensure quota benefits to more backward castes in these groups.

Countering HAM, Chirag Paswan asserted that if the party wanted sub-quotas and a creamy layer within SC reservation, then Manjhi and Suman, both being ministers, should resign.

Paswan, whose party has always opposed sub-quotas, underlined that all communities within SCs have remained united. He said the Constitution does not provide for SC reservation to be determined on economic grounds.
Explaining his opposition, Paswan said introducing sub-quotas or a creamy layer within SC reservation could undermine the very purpose of social justice.

A day later, the NIA registered a case under section 16 and 18 of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and section 3 and 4 of the Explosive Substances Act.

An FIR has been registered against former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and organisers of the Trinamool Congress Chhatra Parishad (TMCP Mamata Banerjee faction) over alleged violation of a Calcutta High Court order during the student wing’s foundation day rally in Kolkata. The complaint said that Mamata Banerjee, along with TMCP organisers, entered into a “criminal conspiracy” and that supporters were provoked during the programme held on August 28.

The case was registered at Hastings Police Station on August 28 under Sections 61(2), 223, 125(a), 132 and 285 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The FIR was based on a complaint filed by Sub-Inspector Apu Baidya.

According to the complaint, the High Court had permitted the foundation day programme on one flank of Cathedral Road. However, the police alleged that TMC workers and supporters also occupied the other flank, causing an obstruction to vehicular movement.

The police further said that the crowd pushed aside barricades and jostled with personnel deployed to maintain law and order, leading to a chaotic situation on Cathedral Road. The complaint also alleged that the programme continued beyond the time permitted by the High Court.
Hundreds of TMC workers had gathered at Cathedral Road for the TMCP foundation day event, where Mamata Banerjee addressed the gathering.
The case has been registered as Hastings Police Station Case No. 112 dated August 28, 2026. The allegations in the FIR are yet to be established in court.

Meanwhile, the TMCP's 28th birth anniversary triggered a major political showdown between the two factions of the party, with both sides trading barbs at each other. The rival camps held separate programmes at different locations and launched attacks against one another.

The Mamata Banerjee-led faction targeted the camp led by Bengal's new LoP, Ritabrata Banerjee, accusing it of acting as a stooge of the ruling BJP. The Ritabrata Banerjee-led camp rejected the charge, claiming that it alone represents the "real" Trinamool Congress.

NEW DELHI: Zurich Airport has prepared itself for a longer takeoff roll at Noida Airport before the traffic here takes off. Multiple factors like the last-minute pullout by on of the three launch airlines; Delhi's IGI Airport operating way below its existing and still expandable capacity and Noida International Airport's (NIA) connectivity woes with Delhi have meant a much lower than originally expected air traffic at the new hub that stated operations on June 15.

Zurich Airport International AG is NIA's primary developer and concessionaire.Zurich Airport has said in its outlook for NIA: "Slower ramp up expected due to challenging geo political environment with near time performance remaining subject to elevated uncertainty. Route network will continue to expand with international services expected to follow. Strong confidence in the long term growth potential and attractive fundamentals of the Indian aviation market."It said NIA saw 104 flights and 25,000 passengers in June. This rose to 1,044 flights and 77,000 passengers in July.

The airport's HY 16 EBIDTA loss is estimated about $3 million.IndiGo is the biggest operator at NIA, with Akasa having a few flights. Air India Express, which was to be the third launch airlines, had pulled out due to mounting losses of AI group. Setting up a new base means incurring significant expense, something AI wanted to avoid at this time.

The going was never going to be easy for NIA, the first second airport to open in an Indian urban conglomerate without either the pre-existing hub operating to capacity (like Mumbai CSMIA); being constrained (like Goa Dabolim) or the older one shutting down (like Bengaluru HAL, Hyderabad Begumpet and Visakhapatnam when Bhogapuram opens in a couple of months). The new airports in Hyderabad and Bengaluru are almost as far as Delhiites find NIA to be but travellers simply didnât have any option but to trudge the distance.

Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida and Ghaziabad, however, have an option thatâs closer, better connected and more affordable multi modal transport.When it was coming up amid the boom post Covid boom in air travel, NIA was expected to have a tough time till 2030 when IGIA was to saturate by reaching its peak capacity of about 13-14 crore passengers annually (CPA). IGIA currently has a capacity of 11 CPA and handled less than 8 crore passengers last year.

Delhi Airport handles about 1,300 flights daily, way short of the 1,550 seen during the heady days of G20.So NIA would have to compete to get traffic with peak traffic hour slot availability being its USP to attract airlines. But it opened at a time when Indian carriers are reeling under the triple impact of finding lucrative western routes become unviable for them due to closure of Pakistan airspace for them since last April, US-Iran war sending oil prices flaring and the rupee weakening. As a result, they are cutting flights.

While we must navigate through them in daily life, the underlying reality remains, we are one. A 25‑year‑old woman died allegedly during her first delivery at Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital (GMH), in Rewa along with her unborn child, in a case that has triggered outrage after a disturbing video of the woman surfaced.

Hospital superintendent Dr Rahul Mishra said, “The woman’s condition was poor from the beginning. She had undergone check‑ups only twice during her pregnancy at a private hospital and may have suffered from high blood pressure, which caused panic.”
Kalpana’s father, Ramsharan Mishra, said, “The daughter was active until shortly before her death. She was neither in a coma nor on oxygen support. She died because of negligence in the treatment.”

Penguin Random House India on Friday said it had been “keen to publish” Sonia Gandhi’s memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love throughout “the relevant discussions” but said it was its “prerogative and responsibility” to fact-check authors.

"I must note that these are not infallible mechanisms. In each such instance, the judiciary has intervened to rectify the situation," he said.
Justice Kant referred to the apex court's verdict holding that grounds for arrest must be provided to the accused in writing, rather than merely read aloud.

"Furthermore, in Arvind Kejriwal versus Central Bureau of Investigation, a decision I had the opportunity to author, the court upheld the legality of the arrest but nonetheless granted bail, based on the principle that prolonged pre-trial detention should not be transformed into punishment under a different guise," he said.

The CJI said if global estimates on money laundering were even roughly accurate, the world launders enough money in a single year to buy every one of the eight billion people alive on the planet a modest laptop, and still have some change left over.
"And of that immense tide of illicit wealth, by the most generous reckoning, less than one unit in a hundred is ever recovered," he said.

The CJI said Indian statesman and teacher Kautilya had, back in the second century BC, written in his treatise on statecraft, the 'Arthashastra', about distinct ways in which an official of the State might siphon away its treasury.

"He then offers a line that every compliance officer present will recognise across twenty-three centuries: it is as impossible for an official to handle the king's revenue and take nothing from it as it is akin to holding honey or poison upon the tip of the tongue and taste neither," he said.
The CJI said the very nature of illicit wealth and economic crime was that neither honoured the sovereignty that otherwise shields our legal structures from foreign interference.
"Let this Symposium's answer be that vigilance, cooperation and the rule of law thwart fraudulence in equal and, I hope, escalating measure," he said.

"In closing, I would say this: the measure of this Symposium's success will not be the eloquence with which we described the problem this week, but the diligence with which each of us, returning to our own jurisdictions, endeavours to put an end to it," he said.
