He said he had taken the decision with a heavy heart to ensure that the party leadership was not embarrassed.Nagendra alleged that he was being targeted as part of a conspiracy and said the BJP could not intimidate him through central investigating agencies."They (BJP) can't scare me with ED, CBI," Nagendra said.He also alleged that "Manuwadis", in an apparent reference to the BJP, were targeting him because they did not want a tribal person in the country to grow."Manuwadis targeted me as they didn't want a tribal person in the country to grow," he alleged.

Nagendra also challenged the BJP to defeat him in Ballari in the "court of public opinion". He said he was prepared to resign as an MLA and face elections if the BJP was ready to take him on.The resignation marks the second time Nagendra has stepped down from the cabinet over the controversy. He had earlier resigned as tribal welfare minister in June 2024 when the issue first surfaced.
Pressure after cabinet re-induction
Nagendra was re-inducted into the Karnataka cabinet on August 3 and given the planning and statistics portfolio.

His return triggered fresh demands from the BJP and JD(S) for his removal over the alleged diversion of funds from the state-run corporation.Earlier on Friday, Nagendra had said he would meet chief minister D K Shivakumar and discuss the matter in detail."If a situation arises where my actions cause embarrassment to the party, then I will..." he had said, alleging that the developments were part of a "conspiracy".The opposition BJP and JD(S) had been protesting his re-induction into the cabinet and alleging his involvement in the alleged Rs 89 crore scam.The two parties had also staged repeated protests inside and outside the Karnataka legislature during the recent monsoon session, which was curtailed by three days and adjourned sine die on August 24 amid continued disruptions.The BJP and JD(S) had planned a foot march from Raichur to Ballari from September 1 to 10, demanding Nagendra's resignation.
What is the Valmiki Corporation case?

The controversy dates back to May 2024, when P Chandrasekharan, then an accounts superintendent with the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation, died by suicide and left behind a six-page note alleging irregularities and unauthorised transfers of corporation funds.

Subsequent investigations found that Rs 89.63 crore had been transferred from a corporation account to a Union Bank of India account and later moved to multiple other accounts, triggering a major political controversy.Nagendra, who was tribal welfare minister when the issue surfaced, resigned from the cabinet in June 2024.He had previously rejected reports that he would resign and maintained that the allegations against him were "politically motivated". Just two days ago, he had dismissed media reports claiming that he had offered to step down.His resignation on Friday came amid renewed political pressure on the Congress government over the alleged Valmiki Corporation scam.

New Delhi/Gurugram: Three BJP MPs were reprimanded by party chief Nitin Nabin for visiting the family of former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar, who was convicted in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, to offer their condolences on his death.
Kamaljeet Sehrawat, Ramvir Singh Bidhuri and Yogender Chandolia visited Kumar’s residence and met members of his family.

The BJP has found itself in a bind as the gesture is in sharp contrast over its long-held position on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. On Friday, it had termed the visit by the three leaders as a personal one.

Kumar was convicted in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots case and was serving two life terms for his role in the riots. He died on 20 August in New Delhi at the age of 80. With the Punjab elections all set to take place next year, the visit has the capacity to snowball into a major controversy, party leaders told ThePrint.
ThePrint reached out to Chandolia, Sehrawat and Bidhuri for a comment and the report will be updated once they respond.
According to sources, H.S.Phoolka, advocate and former Member of the Punjab Assembly, expressed his strong displeasure on the visit of the BJP MPs.

“Strongly condemn visit of 3 MP’s Kamaljeet Sehrawat, Ramvir Singh Bidhuri and Yogender Chandolia to mass murderer Sajjan Kumar’s residence to offer condolences on his death,” Phoolka had posted on X on August 28.

“This when #BJP has always supported our quest for justice against this culprits and supported us in ensuring that he stays in Jail. Sympathy should be reserved for victims and their families-many of whom live the horror of those days even till now. I call for the boycott of these 3 MPs.”

According to sources, the central leadership of the party is quite upset especially as it comes months before the Punjab elections. Sources within the party said that Nabin expressed displeasure over the visit.

“It seems like the three acted on their own without the party’s approval. With the Punjab elections just around the corner, this may snowball into a major issue. The party is mindful of that and which is why the three leaders were summoned,” said a senior party leader.

Phoolka reacted to the action taken by Nabin. “Greateful to @NitinNabin ji for taking a strong stance on the issue. This is what leadership should look like, as opposed to the hypocrisy of the Congress all these years. BJP has fought for this issue as their own for 40 years, starting from ……..#1984SikhGenocide,” he posted.
Kumar was a towering leader within the Jat community that has significant electoral and political power across rural Haryana as well as Delhi.

He represented the erstwhile Outer Delhi Lok Sabha constituency multiple times/ The South, West and North-West Delhi Parliamentary constituencies were carved out of this seat. “Naturally the BJP MPs felt the need to at least offer their condolences as it is culturally important for the segment,” said a leader.

The three BJP leaders who visited Kumar’s residence belong to these three constituencies. While Kamaljeet Sehrawat represent West Delhi parliamentary constituency, Bidhuri is the MP from South Delhi and Chandolia from North West Delhi.
After West Bengal, the BJP has set its eyes on Punjab where it will contest all 117 Assembly seats in the upcoming elections.
BJP general secretary (organisation) B.L.Santosh, who was on a two-day visit to the state to review organisation work, expressed confidence of BJP doing well.
Recently Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda’s remarks on Kumar’s death had put him in the middle of a controversy. The BJP MPs’ visit has added another layer to the row.
The three were present at Kumar’s final bhog ceremony.

“In our Haryanvi society, and the outer Delhi area shares the same culture, it is considered important for political leaders to visit a family whenever there is a death, to do ‘mokhan‘, to offer condolences,” the above-mentioned leader said.

“I remember people whose ‘mokhan‘ I missed telling me to my face that I did not even bother to come when someone in their family died. In our times, a political leader could skip a wedding in his constituency, but he did not dare skip a ‘mokhan‘.”
Hooda had also drawn sharp criticism from the Sikh community and from within his own party.

A senior political leader told The Print that there was no doubt Deepender’s father Bhupinder Singh Hooda had a close association with Sajjan Kumar, who was a frequent visitor to the senior Hooda’s Delhi residence during his years as Haryana chief minister.

The leader said that even after Sajjan Kumar could not contest elections because of his case, and his brother Ramesh Kumar became MP from the seat between 2009 and 2014, the family too enjoyed proximity with Hooda and with several other Jat leaders from Haryana.
It is this old association, and not any recent political calculation, that explains why the Hoodas found themselves under the scanner the moment Sajjan Kumar died, the leader said.
BJP national spokesperson and Sikh leader R.P.Singh said that the three MPs should have avoided the visit and that they have been reprimanded by the top brass is in line with the BJP’s ideology.

“Rajniti se badi samaaj niti hoti hai (Social policy is greater than politics). I had pointed out that they should not have gone in the first place. Kumar was convicted in the carnage which claimed thousands of lives. It is because of PM Modi that the SIT was formed in 2015 to reinvestigate the closed cases related to the riots,” he told ThePrint.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi order an FIR against those involved in the “shuddikaran” or purification of the Ramlila ground in Haldwani after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, a Dalit, addressed a public meeting there.

Calling it a fight between two ideologies — the Constitution versus the RSS-BJP’s views — Gandhi said his party president must get justice and urged the government to take action under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

New Delhi: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi Saturday stepped up his attack on the BJP and RSS over the ‘shuddhikaran’ performed at Haldwani’s Ramlila Maidan after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a rally there, calling it an act of untouchability and demanding an FIR under the SC/ST Act.
“This is a crime. According to the Constitution of India, this is a crime,” Gandhi said at a press conference Saturday afternoon.

Kharge had addressed the Congress’s ‘Vijay Shankhnaad’ rally at the Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani on 8 August. The Congress has objected to the purification ritual at the venue two days later. Gandhi also referred to remarks by Uttarakhand BJP president Mahendra Bhatt defending the exercise.
“Who does this? Only BJP and RSS people do this,” Gandhi said.

He said the Congress wanted those responsible to face legal action. “Our demand is that, as soon as possible, an FIR should be registered in Uttarakhand against the people who carried out the purification,” Gandhi said.
Gandhi said the incident should not be viewed merely as an issue concerning the Congress president, but as an example of the discrimination faced by Dalits.
“This is not Kharge ji’s issue. This is the issue of every Dalit person in India, from the smallest child to the oldest person,” he said.

He also referred to other instances involving Dalit leaders. “Here, our Rajasthan CLP people go to temples, BJP leaders carry out purification. And an example from their party—Bihar Chief Minister Manjhi ji, he goes to a temple, and there too purification takes place,” Gandhi said.

Rahul Gandhi linked the Haldwani episode to an alleged wider pattern of caste discrimination, citing the treatment of Dalit children in schools, restrictions on access to water and separate cups at tea stalls.
“Even today, in schools, Dalit children are made to clean toilets. They are made to sweep and mop. At wells, Dalits are not allowed to drink water,” he said.

“At tea shops, look at this, two kinds of cups are used. One is a glass cup, a reusable cup, which can be washed. And the other is a paper or plastic cup, which is thrown away,” Gandhi said. “The plastic one, the paper one is for Dalits, and the glass one is for other people.”
He also spoke about attacks on Dalits during wedding processions.

“And finally, on the wedding day, which should be a day of happiness, thousands of Dalits in India, when they ride horses and go in the wedding procession, they go wearing helmets. Stones are thrown at them, they are attacked, threatened, beaten,” he said.
“The louder the voice, the more successful the Dalit person is, the more strongly he is attacked,” Gandhi added.
Gandhi described the political contest in the country as a fight between two competing ideologies.

“Look, there is a fight going on in the country between two ideologies. One is the Constitution of India; Ambedkar ji’s Constitution, Gandhi ji’s, Jawaharlal Nehru ji’s, Sardar Patel ji’s Constitution. And the second is the ideology of the BJP and RSS,” he said.
He said the purification at Haldwani reflected what he described as the BJP-RSS mindset towards Dalits.
“They do not want Dalits of this country to progress. They do not want Dalits of this country to live with respect and be successful,” Gandhi said.

The controversy had already spilled into Parliament 13 August, when Kharge raised the Haldwani incident in the Rajya Sabha. Kharge said a ‘havan’ had been performed at the Ramlila Maidan after his rally and spoke of the pain and humiliation caused by the alleged ‘shuddhikaran’ of the venue.

BJP president J. P. Nadda, responding to Kharge, said the BJP did not support such practices and that the matter would be looked into, with action to follow if anyone was found responsible for the ‘shuddhikaran’.
The issue subsequently took a sharper political turn after Uttarakhand BJP president Mahendra Bhatt defended the ritual, saying the venue had been “defiled” by slogans.
Rahul Gandhi said the Congress would pursue action against those responsible for the ‘shuddhikaran’ even if the BJP did not act.
“Even if BJP doesn’t do it, we are going to get it. He is not going to escape. I guarantee you, the entire Congress Party is not going to let that man escape,” he said.
“We have taken a decision that we want our President to get justice in Uttarakhand,” he added
“Our issue is that the Congress President should get justice,” Gandhi reiterated.

Over 17 days after tribal students began a hunger strike in different parts of Maharashtra, the State Government on Saturday (August 29, 2026) accepted all their demands. A delegation of tribal students walked out of Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis’ residence, ‘Varsha,’ on Saturday (August 29) afternoon, stating that they were satisfied with the meeting after the government provided them with a time-bound schedule for implementing key demands, including the pending recruitment for 12,500 positions for tribals.

“We thank Rahul Gandhi, Rohit Pawar, Yashomati Thakur, and other leaders. This was the first time that the tribal students’ demands were heard on a national platform,” said tribal students’ leader Suraj Iccharam Kokani.

Tribal Affairs Minister Ashok Uike met with the protesting students late at night on Saturday (August 29) to present a copy of the written assurances. The students subsequently announced the suspension of their agitation, stating that they would resume it if their demands were not fulfilled within the given time frame. The Minister then offered juice to the protesting students.

Elaborating on the demands accepted by the government, he said that the students were assured that their demands would be fulfilled in three months. “As per the directions of the Supreme Court, we will complete the recruitment drive. In three months, the number of vacancies will be ascertained. In the next three months, recruitment to those positions will take place. The recruitment under PESA will also be done. For the safety and security of ashram shaalas (residential tribal schools), measures will be taken after the third party audit,” he said.

Government officials told The Hindu that an independent recruitment drive will be held if needed to adhere to the timeline of six months for filling up the positions. This was the main demand of the protesting students.

The meeting held by the Chief Minister was attended by seven student representatives from Nagpur, Pune, and Nandurbar. Students had been protesting for over 14 demands, including better infrastructure in tribal schools and hostels, the completion of pending recruitment drives, and the uploading of caste validity committees’ judgments on the website, among others. Officials stated that they had provided the students with written assurances, along with a timeline. The students said they received a copy of two new GRs regarding their demands.

The other key demand was action against bogus adivasis who had claimed government jobs on fake tribal certificates. The Chief Minister said that action against such bogus job-holders will start immediately. “As per the government rule, those selected for government jobs under the ST category have to submit their caste validity certificates within six months. But despite failure to do so, no action has been taken against them for 10 years,” said Mr. Kokani.

The government gave written assurance to the students about the safety and security measures in tribal residential schools to address the infrastructure gaps in them, starting hostel mess in the next three months and stopping the DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) allowance for food, a study of their demand for rise in fund allocation, plugging the loopholes in the central kitchen system and reviewing the existing schools under the scheme to draw tenders for clusters in a scientific way to avoid logistic challenges, new SOPs for the administration of the private aided ashram schools, expansion of SWAYAM scheme which will now be applicable for all courses for 11th standard students at taluka level too.
The government also said that it will ensure that candidates produce their caste validity certificates before receiving their final appointment letters in the future.

In the wake of the devastating flash flood that severely impacted Nepal’s power infrastructure, Kathmandu has asked India to give the requisite approvals for the transmission of electricity to Nepal earlier than usual, senior officials in the Union Power Ministry said on Saturday (August 29, 2026).

“Nepal has asked that India advance import approvals, starting from September this year, in view of the generation deficits caused by this disaster. The concerned authorities are processing the requests,” an official said. According to officials, India is willing to provide any additional power that Nepal may need.

Nepal usually imports electricity from India during the winter months, starting around October, as power generation is typically low in the Himalayan country during the freezing winter months. Conversely, the country exports its excess hydropower to India during the summer. According to official data, India imported 3,299 million units (MUs) of power from Nepal in fiscal year 2025-26 and exported 1,451 MUs to it.
Transmission of electricity across India’s borders requires mandatory clearances from the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), among others.
India ‘capable of absorbing shortfall’
According to an internal assessment, Nepal’s electricity generation capacity has declined by about 550 megawatts because of the infrastructural damage induced by the flood.

Officials said that this resulted in the cross-border power flow to India reducing by approximately 400 MW from earlier peaks of 950 MW to 1,000 MW. However, the officials assured that India was not foreseeing any requirement to make alternative arrangements to compensate for the shortfall.

“We do not foresee any requirement for exceptional emergency procurement or alternative arrangement to balance domestic demand,” an official said, adding, “India’s vast national grid capacity and robust generation reserve margins are capable of absorbing a temporary shortfall of 400 MW seamlessly without disrupting grid stability or retail supply."

The flash flood in the Nepal-Tibet border regions has killed about 675 people, authorities in Nepal said on Saturday. The country’s meteorology department has, meanwhile, warned of fresh rainfall and thunderstorms in the affected areas.

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman invited global investors to set up manufacturing bases, and technology and innovation centres in India, urging them to leverage talent and opportunity to build for the world.

Addressing a high-level Business Roundtable with leading investors and business leaders in Chicago on Friday (August 28, 2026), Ms. Sitharaman highlighted India’s broad-based growth, reform momentum and expanding opportunities for long-term investment.

Ms. Sitharaman emphasised that India’s investment proposition rests not on any single sector, but on the convergence of scale, growth, talent, infrastructure, technology, and sustained reform over the past decade.

“The policy environment is increasingly focused on enabling businesses to invest, manufacture, innovate and expand,” she said at the roundtable organised by India’s Consulate General in Chicago in association with U.S.-India Strategic Partnership Forum.
The Finance Minister invited global partners to co-develop, co-produce and build for global markets.

She urged them not to consider India merely as a market to serve, but as a platform from which to build for the world — whether as a manufacturing base, technology and innovation centre, consumer market or destination for long-term infrastructure investment — leveraging India’s engineering talent, manufacturing scale and technology ecosystem.

The focus of the meeting was “Manufacture in India — for India and for the world”, with opportunities across manufacturing, AI & digital, financial services, infrastructure, food processing, defence and advanced technologies.

“As global companies reassess supply chains and capital allocation, India offers not only scale as a market, but increasing depth as a long-term investment and operating platform,” Ms. Sitharaman said.
The Minister said India’s Digital Public Infrastructure such as Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, ONDC and India Stack, has created platforms at population scale.

“The next opportunity is to build higher-value businesses in AI, engineering, analytics, product development, semiconductors and electronics, with India’s Global Capability Centres increasingly becoming global innovation hubs,” she said.
Ms. Sitharaman said GIFT City was emerging as an international financial centre connecting global capital with Indian opportunities.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi thanked his "brother" President Shavkat Mirziyoyev for the honour, saying India and Uzbekistan will work together for the welfare of the Global South and humanity.

"Being conferred with Uzbekistan's highest award is a moment of immense pride for me. And you used a word with which the people of India are also very familiar--'Dostlik'," he said.

Just a chapter, not my entire life: Divya Mittal gets candid on why she quit IAS

Divya Mittal said her resignation from the IAS was a considered personal decision driven by family and priorities. Her remarks cast the move as a transition towards other interests while formal approval remains pending.

IAS officer Divya Mittal has broken her silence after voluntarily resigning from the Indian Administrative Service, saying the decision was carefully considered and was not prompted by pressure or any sudden “trigger moment”.
Speaking to India Today, Mittal said her decision was based on her priorities, interests and family. “The IAS job is merely one chapter of my life, not my entire existence,” she said.
The 2013-batch Uttar Pradesh cadre officer, who served as District Magistrate of Deoria, Mirzapur and Sant Kabir Nagar, is currently posted as Special Secretary in the Board of Revenue.

In a social media post announcing her resignation, Mittal described her 13 years in the IAS as an “unforgettable journey” and expressed gratitude for the experiences, colleagues and people she encountered during her career.
WHY DIVYA MITTAL RESIGNED FROM IAS
Mittal said her resignation was not a hurried decision. She said she had considered her priorities, interests and responsibilities towards her family before taking the step.

She is a mother of two daughters and said that, alongside her family responsibilities, she also wants to pursue some of her long-held interests. She indicated that her future could involve writing, teaching or social service, although she has not yet taken a final decision on what she will do next.
Reflecting on her decision, she said the IAS was an important part of her life, but not the entirety of it.
‘I WANTED TO REPAY MY DEBT TO THIS SOIL’
In her resignation post, Mittal recalled growing up in a modest environment and dreaming of a successful life. After studying at IIT Delhi and IIM Bangalore, she secured a job in London.

She worked at JP Morgan, while her husband, former IAS officer Gagandeep Singh Dhillon, worked at Citi Group. Despite having successful careers and lucrative salaries abroad, both eventually returned to India after feeling that something was incomplete.

She subsequently returned to India and joined the civil services. Mittal secured the IAS with an All India Rank of 68 in her second attempt in 2012, while Dhillon cleared the civil services examination in his first attempt.
During her tenure in Uttar Pradesh, Mittal served as District Magistrate in Deoria, Mirzapur and Sant Kabir Nagar.

She said her postings taught her lessons that went beyond administration. According to her, Deoria taught her that standing up for what is right is a duty, while Mirzapur taught her that “impossible” is not a fact but an opinion.
She also recalled her experiences at the feet of Goddess Vindhyavasini in Mirzapur, saying they taught her that true power comes not from a position but from divine grace and the trust of the people.
WHAT HAPPENS TO DIVYA MITTAL’S RESIGNATION?
The resignation submitted by Mittal is currently pending. The decision rests with the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, after a recommendation from the Uttar Pradesh government.

Meanwhile, her resignation has also brought renewed attention to her husband Gagandeep Singh Dhillon, a former IAS officer who resigned as Joint Director General in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry in 2022.
Both Mittal and Dhillon are alumni of IIT Delhi and IIM Bangalore.
For Mittal, however, her resignation marks the end of only one part of that journey, rather than the end of her larger ambitions.
India’s growth to stay at 7% despite global uncertainties: Nirmala Sitharaman
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said India’s economy will sustain 7% growth despite wars, tariff uncertainty and disruptions to global energy and fertiliser supplies.

India’s economy has been growing at 7% or more since the Covid-19 pandemic and is expected to maintain the momentum despite global uncertainties, Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said while addressing the Indian diaspora in Chicago.

Sitharaman said India had “recovered well” from the pandemic and continued to sustain growth at 7% or more, even as global uncertainties have multiplied due to wars, tariff issues and disruptions to energy and fertiliser supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. “We thought, we saw the worst when we went through Covid,” she said.

“This year too, our growth will be at that range,” she said, pointing to global uncertainties caused by two wars, tariff issues and the situation at the Strait of Hormuz, which is disrupting global supplies of energy, fertilisers and other essential commodities.

The finance minister’s statement came close on the heels of the Reserve Bank of India’s latest growth projection on August 5. According to the RBI, India’s real gross domestic product (GDP) growth for 2026-27 is projected at 6.7%.

The RBI increased its latest GDP growth rate projection by 10 basis points from its June estimate as the economy weathered the storm generated by a turbulent global geopolitical environment, trade-related uncertainties and an unpredictable monsoon in the first quarter of 2026-27.

Sitharaman said notwithstanding the breakdown of global energy and fertiliser supply chains, the government shielded its citizens. Despite the Hormuz crisis—which the finance minister termed a “big challenge”—India kept itself “well provisioned” to meet the fertiliser requirements of farmers without any additional cost, and energy was made available to every household.

India imported nearly 80% of the fertilisers it consumed through Hormuz, including urea, diammonium phosphate (DAP) and potash, she said. As a result, Indian farmers were left without fertilisers, which she recalled as an “unthinkable” situation. But the government arranged fertilisers through various routes and the country is “adequately” stocked.

While the crisis has been managed, the government paid a huge price to procure fertilisers for farmers from global suppliers, she said. The government continues to give urea at ₹300 per bag to Indian farmers, while its procurement cost is ₹3,000 per bag, she said. “So, ₹2,700 is the subsidy we give per bag of fertilizer,” she said, adding that “there is no shortage” of fertilizer for farmers and no burden of the cost is shifted to them.

The finance minister said irrespective of global uncertainties, India is marching on the reform path with its focus on bilateral trade and investment cooperation with several economies and accelerating the domestic engine of growth through capital investments for their multiplier effects. “So, reforms continue. We are also talking with several countries for bilateral investment treaty and also bilateral trade agreements because multilateral institutions are very slow…, she said.

Talking about fiscal management, she said, “We have set ourselves a certain target, which is to bring the borrowing down to the 50% level of GDP by 2030. Therefore, I will be working on that path. There are advanced economies whose debt is well over 200% of their GDP even now. We have given ourselves a fiscal discipline path on the fiscal deficit as well. We have fulfilled the trajectory. The last mile that had to be reached by 2025-26, we have reached,” she added.

“The world has witnessed the fiscal prudence of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi when he was Chief Minister of Gujarat and when he is the Prime Minister of the country. Our credit ratings are improving. But that’s not by cutting corners. That’s not by stopping the resources which have to go for social welfare. It is through proper management of the economy,” she said.

She said 2047 is the target year set for achieving Viksit Bharat. “It’s hardly 20 years from now. So, the speed and scale with which the reforms are happening require a lot more support. Lots more support from people who are talented and have exposure. Lots more support from people who can give ideas for us to carry it forward. And, above all, support in terms of capital, which is so required for a country to meet all its aspirations,” she added.

Union ministers Chirag Paswan, Jitan Ram Manjhi clash over SC/ST reservations, demand each other's resignations

Union minister and LJP(RV) chief Chirag Paswan on Saturday demanded resignations of Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) founder and Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi and his son, Bihar minister Santosh Kumar Suman, for advocating a review of scheduled caste (SC) reservation.

Speaking to reporters in Patna, Paswan underscored simmering differences within the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over the issue into an open confrontation. “If the father-son duo wanted such changes, they should first quit their ministerial posts—one at the Centre and one in the state—and then raise the matter in Parliament,” he said.
Reservation, he stressed, is not charity but a constitutional right rooted in historical untouchability and social discrimination, not an economic measure open to periodic review.
The flashpoint is the call for reviewing SC/ST quotas and introducing sub-categorisation.
“We are in favour...We are simply asking for a review of the SC/ST quotas. We want quota benefits to reach the least privileged among us,” Suman told reporters on Friday.
Manjhi has backed the line, framing it as social justice and citing the Supreme Court’s 2024 judgment permitting sub-classifications based on empirical data.

Paswan’s stance is in line with that of his late father Ram Vilas Paswan, who had fiercely opposed a separate “Mahadalit” category introduced in the state more than a decade ago by the then chief minister Nitish Kumar.

When Manjhi’s attention was drawn to Paswan’s latest retort, he said, “It is not us, but Chirag Paswan who should resign as he is unable to understand the point Santosh and I have been making in the broader interests of Dalits.” “It is a fact that among the Dalits, there are castes which are relatively more vulnerable and these deserve targeted welfare which can happen after introducing a sub-category...” the Gaya MP said.

New Delhi: Hindutva does not mean excluding Muslims, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat said Saturday, asserting that any Hindu who believes Muslims should have no place in India ceases to be a Hindu.
He was speaking at the ‘One World: One Humanity’ Faith Leaders Conference in New York, which brought together speakers from Christianity, Judaism, Hinduism and Islam.

“If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu. If you want to call yourself Hindu, you must believe that all paths are leading to the same goal and that every human has dignity. There is no difference between human beings,” the RSS Sarsanghchalak said at the event organised by the AHEAD (American Hindus for Engagement And Dialogue) Forum.

The RSS chief further said socio-religious organisations may want to influence and shape policies before they take effect, but politics itself has largely become a ‘game of self-interest’, and hence they need to begin their work with society first.

“We want to influence and shape policies before they take effect, and in the right way. We want to stop wars. Therefore, at some point, we have to engage with politics. But we cannot start there. My experience aligns with the traditional thought of Bharat, the underlying unity of humanity. Leaders throughout our history have emphasised this, and our Constitution reflects it as well. Yet, change is not happening through politics alone,” Bhagwat added.

“I am sorry to say, but politics has largely become a game of self-interest. As has been rightly said, wherever there is ‘me’ and ‘mine’, there is no solution; ‘We’ and ‘ours’ is the only solution. Our experience in Bharat has taught us that we must start with society itself. And we have already begun that work,” he said.

Bhagwat also recalled a 2018 speech he delivered in Delhi, and how many people reached out to him afterwards and invited him for a dialogue, following which the organisation initiated that dialogue, primarily with the Muslims and Christians of Bharat.

At his US event, he added, “In 2018, during my lecture series in Delhi, several Muslim brothers present there asked me, ‘You are a Hindu organisation. You speak of Hindu Rashtra. What about us Muslims? Will you drive us out?’ I told them, ‘No, that is not Hindutva. If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he ceases to be a Hindu.”
The RSS chief emphasised how the organisation believes in serving, and while doing so it “doesn’t see any discrimination”.

“We (RSS) are serving. While serving, we don’t see discrimination. Whoever is in need, we are serving. 1.30 lakh service projects are being run by our Swayamsevaks with the help of society. They served everywhere and served equally,” said Bhagwat.
He further cited the example of 1996 when two planes collided in Haryana’s Dadri and Swayamsevaks were the first to reach and help.

“Two planes collided in Dadri, Haryana (1996) – a state in India. Both planes were from Muslim countries. Most of the passengers were Muslims. After the collision, our Swayamsevaks reached there first. And they served. All passengers were dead. Our Swayamsevaks arranged the funeral, and when their relatives came, helped in identifying them. We don’t have the thought that they are Muslims,” he explained.
“Religious leaders have to impart this eternal wisdom from time to time, keeping in mind that in the present situation, it will be a laborious task,” he added.
Bhagwat said the organisation believes in serving and, while serving, “we don’t see discrimination”.
The RSS chief highlighted that while people may follow different religions, humanity remains one. “We live in a society where religions may be different, but humanity is one,” he said,
He also emphasised that in India, people of all religious denominations live, and “Bharat has given shelter to everybody” without discrimination.
“Those who could not find a safe place in the world came to Bharat, where they found their place.”
However, he did maintain that there does exist a baggage of the past that people “unnecessarily carry”.

“Somehow, it happened in the course of history. I cannot point to the moment. After that, our society and our country became targets of foreign invasions, and so many things were lost. But that tradition still exists, which teaches common people the same thing: one world, one humanity. But, like you said, there is baggage that people unnecessarily carry. In our Bharat, people of all denominations live together because, traditionally, Bharat has given shelter to everybody,” he said.
Bhagwat said where there is “me” and “mine,” there is no solution.

“We” and “ours” are the solution. Diversity is a decoration for our unity. It has to be accepted. It has to be respected. It has to be protected. As I protect my own specific nature, I have to protect others also,” he said.

Truth, he said, is one. “There are many religions. In today’s world, religious work is largely defined by rituals. And to bring in religious discipline, and to create that path to divinity, this discipline of rituals is also necessary.
Among the speakers was Cardinal John Olorunfemi Onaiyekan, the prominent Nigerian Catholic prelate who served as Archbishop of Abuja from 1994 to 2019.

Maharashtra agrees to tribal students’ demands; 17-day hunger strike ends

Under pressure from the Bombay high court and following an open letter by Rahul Gandhi urging CM Devendra Fadnavis to intervene, the state government on Saturday stepped in to resolve the indefinite hunger strike by tribal students. The students had begun the agitation on August 13 over changes to government tribal hostel rules. Their demands subsequently expanded to include hostel facilities and safety, tribal reservations, recruitment to vacant posts, appointments under the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, caste validity certificates and compensation for the families of three tribal girls who died of snakebite at an ashram school in Gadchiroli.

‘Do you feel you are a lord?’: Bombay HC rebukes Tukaram Mundhe-led FDA over crackdown on MCA eateries
Following the court’s remarks, the Maharashtra FDA on Saturday said it would withdraw its order suspending the licences of the five restaurants.

The Bombay High Court has warned Tukaram Mundhe-led Maharashtra Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) officials of contempt action and even jail after rebuking them for taking a “pedantic instead of pragmatic view” while suspending the licences of five restaurants operating on the Mumbai Cricket Association premises.
“Do you feel you are a lord and you can do anything,” the division bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad questioned the FDA, HT reported earlier.
Following the court’s remarks, the Maharashtra FDA on Saturday said it would withdraw its order suspending the licences of the five restaurants.

The court vacated the suspension after a fresh inspection report submitted by the FDA confirmed that the eateries located in the Bandra-Kurla Complex area were 88 per cent compliant with food safety rules, the report added.
The MCA had approached the high court challenging the FDA’s decision to suspend operations over alleged hygiene violations and third-party operational irregularities.

Although a fresh inspection carried out on Thursday showed 88 per cent compliance, the FDA had initially maintained the suspension because the eateries were being operated by M/s Shirke Infrastructure despite the licences being registered in the MCA’s name.
The FDA on Saturday informed the court that it would issue a fresh notice to the MCA, grant it a hearing on the issue of its contract with Shirke Infrastructure and then pass a reasoned order.
The court accepted this and said that since the eateries are now compliant with the rules, the order suspending their licences stands vacated and they can reopen their services.

“There is no provision in the law that prohibits the same,” the bench noted, pointing out that during the last hearing it had specifically asked FDA officials to apply their minds and take a pragmatic view of the situation.

“However, despite clearly saying this, the FDA has disobeyed our order and taken a pedantic view instead of a pragmatic view. We are tired of scolding the department and officers all the time. It is now time to pass stinging orders. We will issue contempt action against the concerned officers. Let them convince us or go to jail,” the court said.
The bench also questioned why the FDA was always in “undue haste” and passed orders without analysing the law.

“How many times should we try to convince and balance equities so that the department does not feel discouraged? Why do we say don't kill a mosquito with a sword? Do you feel you are a lord and you can do anything?” the HC questioned.
Pursuant to the court's remarks, additional government pleader P P Kakade submitted that the FDA would withdraw its order suspending the licences of the five eateries.

FIR against Rahul Gandhi for calling havan ritual in Haldwani ‘untouchability’
An FIR was lodged against Rahul Gandhi based on the complaint submitted by Amit Kumar, a member of the Scheduled Caste community.

A first information report (FIR) was registered on Sunday against leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi at Haldwani Kotwali police station in Uttarakhand’s Nainital district over his alleged remarks on a “purification ritual” conducted at the local Ramlila Ground.

Superintendent of Police (City) Haldwani Manoj Kumar Katyal confirmed the development, saying, “Based on the complaint submitted by Amit Kumar, a Jawahar Nagar Colony resident, an FIR has been registered against Rahul Gandhi under relevant sections, and a thorough investigation into the matter is currently underway.”
Kumar (26) identified himself as a member of the Scheduled Caste (Valmiki) community and an office-bearer of the local trust, Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas.
The case has been registered under sections of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and Sections 196 (promoting enmity between classes) and 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

2 accused in Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan's killing shot dead in UP encounter
Two shooters involved in Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan's murder were killed in an encounter with the UP STF. Police said four shooters and two recce suspects have so far emerged in the investigation.

Two shooters involved in the murder of Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan were killed in an encounter with Shamli Police and the SWAT team, officials said. The two men, identified as 24-year-old Sumit and 22-year-old Mohit, carried a reward of Rs 50,000 each.

According to police, Sumit and Mohit were among four shooters involved in Baliyan's killing, while two other suspects had conducted reconnaissance and identified the singer's location before the attack. Police said a total of six people have so far emerged as being involved in the case.
CCTV footage captured four armed assailants opening fire at Baliyan outside the gym, with the attackers reportedly firing around 12 rounds before fleeing the scene, triggering panic in the area.

Baliyan, a popular 35-year-old Haryanvi singer, was shot dead by four assailants outside a gym in Shamli, Uttar Pradesh. He was known for songs including Bhari Court Mein Goli Maarenge Meri Jaan, which had gained popularity in the region.
TWO RS 50,000-WANTED SHOOTERS KILLED IN ENCOUNTER
The encounter took place near an Indian Gas godown on Kairana Road in Shamli, where teams from Shamli Kotwali Police, Jhinjhana Police and the SWAT team were involved in the operation.

Police said both suspects were shot during retaliatory firing after they opened fire at police personnel. The two men were taken to the District Joint Hospital in Shamli, where doctors declared them dead during treatment.
Two SWAT team head constables, Harvinder and Pradeep, were also injured in the encounter, police said.

Police recovered two pistols, 10 live cartridges and nine spent cartridges of 30-bore ammunition from the encounter site. Another pistol, along with 16 live and six spent cartridges, was also recovered.
A Splendor motorcycle, a bag, a mobile phone and Rs 5,000 in cash were also seized from the spot.
TWO MEN RIDING BIKE OPENED FIRE: POLICE
Shamli SP Narendra Pratap Singh said police teams had been conducting intensive checks following Baliyan's murder, with the SWAT team, surveillance unit, SHOs, ASP and COs assigned to the case.
He said a blockade plan was implemented from midnight to 6 am to ensure that vehicles entering the district were checked.

According to Singh, at around 4 am, Hijana SHO Virendra Kasana spotted a motorcycle approaching from the Karnal side while conducting checks near his police station. When he tried to stop the motorcycle, the two men riding it opened fire.
Singh said Kasana narrowly escaped, although a bullet struck his vehicle. He immediately alerted other police teams over the wireless, following which the suspects fled towards Kairana.

When the motorcycle reached the area beneath the Manna Madra bridge, Kotwali SHO Dharmendra Gautam, who was conducting checks there, attempted to stop the suspects. They opened fire again, shattering the windshield of his vehicle.

The SHO then challenged the suspects, who turned left towards the city. However, by then, an alert had been circulated over the wireless network, prompting the SWAT team, surveillance unit, SHOs, CO City, ASP and CO Kairana to move towards the location.
Singh said the suspects subsequently swerved their motorcycle towards the area where the police teams had assembled, leading to the encounter.

Ankit Baliyan’s father, Satveer Singh Balyan, said the police encounter had brought his family “half justice”, but the remaining accused must also be brought to justice. He thanked Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the police for the action.
MOHIT HAD 14 CASES IN HARYANA: POLICE
Police said preliminary checks showed that Mohit had around 14 criminal cases registered against him in Haryana. One case was reportedly registered against Sumit in Haryana.
Authorities are checking their complete criminal histories and investigating their roles in Baliyan's killing.
GOGI GANG CLAIMED RESPONSIBILITY
Baliyan was fatally shot outside a gym in Shamli, where the attackers opened fire before fleeing the scene. The murder triggered protests and demands for swift action against those responsible.

The Gogi gang later claimed responsibility for the killing. The gang cited Baliyan's purported links with its rivals and referred to a song associated with the singer as among the reasons for the attack.

A post from the Instagram account of Bholu Shahpuria, reportedly linked to the gang, read, “This is just the beginning, everyone’s turn will come.” The gang also issued a threat to the Uttar Pradesh Police, warning of more attacks similar to Baliyan’s killing.
Police, however, are continuing to investigate the motive and are examining several possible angles, including old rivalries and political or election-related connections.
TWO SHOOTERS CONDUCTED RECCE BEFORE KILLING: POLICE

Amitabh Yash, Additional Director General (ADG) of Law & Order and the Special Task Force (STF), Uttar Pradesh. said two shooters linked to the Gogi gang had conducted reconnaissance of Ankit Baliyan’s movements in Shamli on August 20, days before the singer was killed.
The two shooters allegedly travelled to Shamli and stayed at the Surya Hotel, where they provided documents including their Aadhaar cards during check-in.
Police subsequently examined CCTV footage from the hotel, which reportedly provided crucial leads in the investigation.
Yash also reiterated the Uttar Pradesh government's stated policy of zero tolerance towards crime and warned against testing the administration's resolve.

Following the murder, Meerut Zone ADG Bhanu Bhaskar directed an intensified investigation into the case. The Uttar Pradesh Police had formed eight teams to conduct raids in Haryana and other locations, trace the suspects and recover weapons believed to have been used in the crime.
Investigators are also examining CCTV footage, call records and other evidence to establish the sequence of events leading up to the shooting.

Hyderabad: The protest led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, in the last couple of months was over systemic flaws and not corruption alone, RSS leader Sunil Ambekar said in Gudilova, Visakhapatnam at an event Friday.

Ambekar, the RSS’ Akhil Bharatiya Prachar Pramukh (all-India publicity chief), and C R Mukunda, the Sah Prachar Pramukh (joint publicity chief) called for a constructive approach to “improve the system”.

“Addressing systemic flaws requires vigilance and effort from both the government and society. Whether it involves issues like NEET or other systemic problems, such matters cause anxiety among Gen Z regarding their future. It is essential to understand this anxiety and find solutions for it,” Mukunda said, responding to a media query.
Over three days, 32 wings of the RSS shared their experiences, future challenges, and the upcoming course of action, according to a release shared by the RSS.

In the backdrop of the protests in both New Delhi and Jharkhand, much of the RSS’ discussions seemed to focus on India’s Gen Z and their concerns on various social media platforms. Extensive discussions were held regarding the ideas, aspirations, and creative potential of Gen Z, their concerns about the future, and their role in nation-building, Ambekar said.

“Instead of merely engaging in didactic conversations with the youth, it is essential to connect with them directly, understand their sentiments and concerns, and foster a sense of affinity towards the nation, culture, and social values through dialogue,” Mukunda said, responding to media queries on how the RSS intends to respond to youth issues.

Continuing on the problems of today’s youth, the RSS discussed the need for society’s participation in eliminating drug consumption instead of relying on the police and the government alone. The Sangh said it believes in coordinated efforts involving educational institutions, parents, social organisations, the administration, the police, and other relevant stakeholders to create a drug-free society.

Ambekar and Mukunda spoke to the media Friday after the three-day RSS all-India coordination meeting held at a school in Gudilova, on the outskirts of Vizag. Briefing the media, they said their discussions revolved around social issues such as demographic imbalance, youth drug abuse, a review of the RSS Panch Parivartan framework (social harmony, family values, eco-friendly lifestyle, indigenous consciousness, and civic duty), alongside a development model for India’s future.

“Serious deliberations also took place regarding demographic changes and imbalances. The situation in India was discussed against the backdrop of challenges arising from aging populations and declining fertility rates in many countries across the world, the shifting population ratios across various regions and communities and their social impact, while also considering measures to maintain societal balance and harmony,” Mukunda said.

The meeting also featured a discussion on a development model rooted in an Indian perspective. Deliberations focused on ensuring that development is self-reliant, eco-friendly, and inclusive—encompassing all sections of society—and reviewed the experiences of organisations working in the economic sector.
Against the backdrop of the Sangh’s centenary year, a special discussion was held during the meeting regarding the various aspects of ‘Panch Parivartan’ aimed at societal change.
The RSS spokespersons also spoke of their fellow organisations’ work undertaken in the devastating Assam flood to provide relief to people and rehabilitate the flood victims.

Prominent office-bearers and activists from Sangh-inspired organisations working in various sectors for the benefit of society and the nation participated in this meeting. A total of 326 delegates were invited to the meeting, including women leaders from various organisations; 49 women delegates participated in the three-day event.
The invitees, participants, and senior RSS ideologues also studied the growing impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on society, the release said.

While discussing the positive opportunities offered by AI alongside the associated precautions and challenges, the need to view it through an Indian perspective and within the Indian social context was underscored. “Deliberations will continue about how to utilise technology for the welfare of society and how to raise public awareness regarding its potential adverse effects,” Mukunda said.

Responding to a question on the purpose of Sarsanghchalak Mohan Bhagwat’s proposed visit to the USA, Canada, and Britain, the spokespersons said the tour was part of the extensive global outreach initiative marking the Sangh’s centenary year. It has three primary objectives.

First—to present a fact-based, positive perspective amidst the misconceptions and propaganda circulating globally regarding India, Hindu society, and the RSS. Second—to convey the message of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam and universal oneness—teachings imparted by India’s sages and seers—to diverse societies across the globe. Third—to foster dialogue with mainstream societies in various countries regarding the interests and rights of Hindus and people of Indian origin residing in those countries.

175 dead in monster Nepal flash floods, 100 of 300 missing Indians located

Flash floods triggered by an avalanche in Nepal and Tibet have killed 175 people and left nearly 1,500 missing. Nepal's Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal said nearly 300 Indians are reportedly missing. Later, around 100 Indians were located.

Around 100 people were located on Thursday, hours after Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said that nearly 300 Indians were reportedly missing after devastating flash floods sent torrents of mud, rocks and water across Nepal and neighbouring Tibet. The devastating flash floods have left 175 dead.
However, there has been no confirmation of the exact number of Indians missing either from the Nepal government or India.

Khanal said authorities were still trying to ascertain the full extent of the disaster, with nearly 1,500 people, including at least 800 foreigners, reported missing across Nepal and Tibet. "Thousands of families have lost homes and are missing as of now. We are still trying to ascertain the full extent of the disaster," he said.
Nepal embassy sources, citing news agency ANI, said 175 people had been killed in the flash floods so far.
FOLLOW LIVE BLOG UPDATES OF NEPAL FLASH FLOODS

The flash floods struck Nepal and parts of Tibet after a possible avalanche near a Himalayan river sent catastrophic flash floods downstream. Gyirong Port, a land border crossing and trade post between Tibet and Nepal, was among the first towns to be hit before the swelling waters flowed further down to wreak havoc.
The flash floods gobbled up settlements and disrupted travel, while roads, bridges and hydropower projects across Nepal suffered extensive damage.

The flash floods struck three districts of Nepal – Rasuwa, Dhading and Nuwakot – on Wednesday after an avalanche blocked the flow of the Lhende tributary of the river Bhote Koshi. The torrent first hit Timure near Rasuwagadhi, along Nepal’s border with Tibet, before wreaking havoc downstream.

Nepal Police said the death toll could increase further as rescue teams resumed searches and more bodies were recovered. “This will go up, as we have resumed the search and more bodies are expected to be recovered,” Nepal Police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle told Reuters.

In Tibet’s Gyirong county, 558 people were reported missing, including 260 foreign nationals, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV. At least three people were killed and 265 remained missing after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port on the Nepal border, Chinese officials told Reuters.

The disaster swept through a rugged Himalayan region popular with trekkers and pilgrims travelling between Lhasa and Kathmandu. Several videos on social media showed massive torrents of water and debris sweeping through the border area, while homes, roads and power projects were washed away or damaged downstream.
Early reports from Nepali officials suggested that an earthquake in the region may have triggered the collapse of the lower part of a glacier, causing the floods.
Earlier, Nepali authorities had said that 133 Indians and 37 NRIs missing, including pilgrims travelling on the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, a major pilgrimage route for Hindus.
Nepal’s Flood Forecasting Division said there was no credible information indicating another major flood was about to hit Rasuwa or Nuwakot, though river levels could rise slightly due to rainfall.

Bihar, which shares a border with Nepal, was on high alert as authorities continue to monitor water levels and the flood situation. This morning, the situation partially stabilised as Valmikinagar Barrage recorded a discharge of 88,000 cusecs, down from 1.5 lakh cusecs at midnight.
India has stepped up humanitarian assistance to Nepal following the disaster.

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Thursday that a second flight carrying 37.5 tonnes of humanitarian assistance and disaster relief material, medicines and food packets had departed for Nepal.

India had sent its first military relief flight on Wednesday night, with an Indian Air Force C-130J aircraft carrying 10 tonnes of emergency supplies, including temporary shelters, blankets, hygiene kits, solar lamps and essential medicines.

On Wednesday, the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu issued emergency numbers for assistance and information related to Indian nationals affected by the flash floods. In a post on X, it said people can contact +977 985 131 6807 or +977 970 910 7500.

The Embassy of India has remained engaged with the relevant authorities of the Government of Nepal for early rescue and relief for Indian nationals affected by the flash floods that took place in Nepal, it said in another post on X, adding that rescue and relief efforts continue to be strengthened in coordination with the Nepal government.
The Nepal Tourism Board also issued similar numbers, including the toll-free emergency number 1234, the hotline 1144, and the Tourist Police number 9851289445 for help.
In Beijing, the Embassy of India also issued a helpline number, 0086 185 1428 4905, which can be contacted via WhatsApp.
NEPAL PM VISITS FLOOD-HIT NUWAKOT
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah travelled by road to flood-hit Nuwakot on Thursday morning for an on-site assessment of the damage.

The Nepal Prime Minister's Office said Shah would inspect affected and surrounding areas and meet local administrators, security officials and public representatives to discuss immediate relief, restoration and the reopening of blocked infrastructure.
Rescue and relief operations continued across the affected areas as authorities assessed the scale of destruction and searched for those still missing.
In the worst-hit districts, helicopters are dropping tents, food and other emergency supplies provided by India, Nepal Army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said.
More than 5,000 army and police personnel have joined rescue operations, which retrieved 125 people on Thursday, including 20 foreigners, Basnet said.
Woman, her newborn die after delivery. In video, she had pled against treatment

A distressing video showed the 25-year-old woman pleading to be taken away from the government hospital in Rewa before she and her newborn died. The deaths triggered protests, suspensions and an enquiry amid the family's negligence allegations.

A 25-year-old woman and her newborn died at a government hospital in Madhya Pradesh’s Rewa. Just hours before her delivery, a video that has since gone viral on social media, showed her pleading with her family to take her away from the hospital and expressing fear about continuing treatment there.
“Take me away from here. I won’t survive they will kill me,” Kalpana Mishra can be heard saying in the video.

Kalpana had been admitted to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital (SGMH), also known as Gandhi Memorial Hospital, on Tuesday. s per her family, she underwent a caesarean section the next day, following which she and her newborn died during treatment.
The family has alleged serious medical negligence, claiming that Kalpana repeatedly complained about her condition and that she and her relatives were not provided timely treatment.
They also alleged that doctors and nursing staff behaved rudely with them.

The video, which has sparked outrage, shows Kalpana visibly distressed as she pleads to take her away from the hospital. A family member appeared to console her, telling her that doctors were treating her and that she would be fine.
The deaths have triggered protests at the hospital. Grieving family members staged a sit-in outside the main gate, demanding action against those they held responsible.

Hospital authorities have denied allegations of negligence. Following the uproar, Dean Sunil Agarwal and Superintendent Rahul Mishra reached the spot and spoke to the family, assuring them of an impartial enquiry.
As a preliminary action, two nursing officers who were on duty have been suspended and a committee has been constituted to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

A panel of doctors from the district hospital is expected to conduct the post-mortem examinations. Officials said the exact cause of death of the mother and newborn would be established only after the post-mortem and inquiry reports.

BJP MLA from Mangawan, Narendra Prajapati, also visited the hospital and met the bereaved family. He spoke to hospital officials and assured the family that action would be taken if anyone was found responsible.

India rejects Court of Arbitration's Indus Waters Treaty award: ‘Illegally constituted, has no jurisdiction’
The MEA said the Hague-based court has no jurisdiction to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions and that the treaty will remain in abeyance.

India on Monday rejected the Permanent Court of Arbitration’s (PCA) order setting aside its decision to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan, saying it had never recognised the existence of the “illegally constituted” court in The Hague.
The Indian government also rejected the court order on interim measures prohibiting New Delhi from building certain structures of the Ratle hydroelectric project in Jammu and Kashmir.
“India’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance remains in force,” the external affairs ministry said in a statement that rejected the Court of Arbitration’s awards.
Also Read | Hormuz to Indus: The new water weapon isn't scarcity. It's uncertainty

India held the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance as part of a package of punitive diplomatic and economic measures unveiled in April 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terror attack, which was carried out by a proxy for Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). Pakistan, which has said any denial of its share of waters of cross-border rivers will be considered an act of war, approached the court in The Hague in March this year to determine the status of the water-sharing treaty.

The external affairs ministry described the “so-called Court of Arbitration” as illegally constituted and said: “This so-called Court was constituted by the World Bank in patent breach of the terms of the Treaty and India categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body.”

India has “never recognised the existence in law of this illegally-constituted and so-called Court of Arbitration”, and has always said the “very establishment of this alleged arbitral body constitutes a grave violation of the Indus Waters Treaty”, the statement said.
“Accordingly, India has never appeared before this body and has refused to take any cognisance of its earlier pronouncements,” it said.

The Court of Arbitration has “no jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions” and its “pronouncements, now or in the future, will have no effect on India’s actions in connection with the projects being undertaken by India”.
Also Read | ‘India could use water as weapon’: Pakistan minister warns amid Indus Water Treaty row

Since it suspended the treaty, the Indian side has stepped up work on several hydropower projects in Jammu and Kashmir that Pakistan opposed under the provisions of the 1960 pact. Among these are the Ratle and Kishenganga hydropower projects, over which Pakistan had sought the formation of a court of arbitration.

In a statement, the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) said that the court considered the meaning of India’s decision to suspend the treaty, “finding that it could only be a claim that the Indus Waters Treaty is either suspended or terminated”.

The court examined the potential grounds on which India can suspend or terminate the treaty, including grounds cited by New Delhi in its public statements. “In a unanimous decision, the Court found that none of these grounds could justify suspension or termination of the Treaty. Accordingly, the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force, and India must observe its obligations under the Treaty, including those relating to the design and operation of its hydro-electric projects on the Western Rivers,” the court said in a press release.

The Indus Waters Treaty, brokered by the World Bank, allocated the western rivers – Indus, Jhelum, Chenab – to Pakistan, and the eastern rivers – Ravi, Beas and Sutlej – to India. It also allowed each country certain uses of the rivers allocated to the other.

In its order on interim measures, the court considered Pakistan’s request for limiting construction works at the Ratle hydropower project pending a neutral expert’s decision on whether the project’s design complies with the treaty.

“In a unanimous decision, the Court decided to impose measures prohibiting India from concreting the RHEP dam wall and power intake structure above certain levels until 90 days after the Neutral Expert’s final decision, which is expected in July 2027,” the PCA press release said.
“The Court also imposed a reporting measure relating to the RHEP Construction Schedule until shortly after the Neutral Expert’s final decision,” it said.

The court also declined to grant two other measures requested by Pakistan – one that India would bear the risk of having to discontinue, modify or dismantle components of the Ratle hydropower project, and another that India should return to “full compliance” with the treaty pending the court’s decision on Pakistan’s application related to the status of the pact.
The court further said its decisions will be published on PCA’s website after completing a process with the two countries to “identify confidential information for redaction”.

The court of arbitration was chaired by Sean D Murphy of the US and its other members are Wouter Buytaert of Belgium, Jeffrey P Minear of the US, Awn Shawkat Al-Khasawneh of Jordan, and Donald Blackmore of Australia.
In July 2023, the court ruled it was competent to take up Pakistan’s case after rejecting India’s objections to its competence.

While Pakistan initially sought the appointment of a neutral expert to address objections to the Kishenganga and Ratle projects in 2015, it unilaterally retracted this request in 2016 and sought a court of arbitration. In 2016, the World Bank appointed both a neutral expert and the court of arbitration.
India attended meetings convened by the neutral expert till the treaty was suspended in 2025. It completely stayed away from proceedings of the court of arbitration, which it never recognised.

The proceedings before the neutral expert in relation to the Kishenganga and Ratle hydropower projects are ongoing, and the latest work programme issued by the expert envisages circulation of the final decision around July 16, 2027, the press release said.

The court said that while India did not participate by making written or oral submissions during proceedings, it took into account India’s positions on the issues “to the extent they could be discerned from India’s statements and conduct outside of these proceedings (including Indian government communications to Pakistan and to the neutral expert, and public statements made by Indian officials)”.

The court further noted that it looked “extremely seriously” into India’s allegation that “Pakistan’s sponsorship of cross-border terrorism had impeded its utilisation of rights” under the Indus Waters Treaty. “However, the Court found that even if India’s allegation was assumed to be true, they would not establish a material breach of the Treaty by Pakistan,” the press release said.

The treaty “does not address terrorism or the use of force and expressly indicates that it governs only the rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the use of the waters of the Indus Rivers System”. The court said it “did not find evidence that the alleged terrorism had impeded India’s ability to construct its HEPs on the Western Rivers and instead noted that India has built and is building many such HEPs”.

The Supreme Court on Monday refused to interfere with a Bombay High Court order cancelling the bail of the three co-owners of a Goa nightclub where a fire killed 25 people and injured more than 50 on December 6 last year.

Appearing for the Luthra brothers, senior advocates Abhishek M Singhvi and Siddharth Dave told the court that the case was not one of direct intentional offence and was at best one of alleged negligence. Dave said there was no act on the part of the Luthra brothers that led to the killings.

He told the court, "Section 304, part II (of IPC) is wholly and can never be applied to this case. There is no act of mine which has caused death. Maximum, if the prosecution wants to succeed in this case, then it can be under Section 304A (causing death by negligence)."

Justice Datta then asked Singhvi how many people had lost their lives in the restaurant. Singhvi replied that 25 people had died and submitted that the high court judgment suffered from two basic errors. He also said several other co-accused had been granted bail in the case.
Senior advocate Shyam Divan, appearing for Gupta, said his client had only a 10 per cent share in the business and had nothing to do with the incident.

A computer-based examination centre in Jaipur’s Sitapura area came under scrutiny on Monday (August 31, 2026) after technical problems disrupted an All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) recruitment exam, a day after an internal power failure at the same facility forced the cancellation of the NEET-PG 2026 exam for 2,445 candidates.
The developments have raised fresh questions on the reliability of power and technology infrastructure at centres conducting high-stakes national exams.

The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) had earlier said that the NEET-PG 2026 exam had been successfully conducted for the overwhelming majority of candidates on Sunday (August 29, 2026). More than 2.65 lakh candidates appeared at 1,111 centres across the country.
However, the exam could not be completed at two iON Digital Zone centres in Sitapura, Jaipur — test centre numbers 41682 and 41683 — because of an internal power supply failure.
NBEMS has scheduled a fresh examination for the 2,445 affected candidates on September 5 at 3 p.m. in Jaipur.

But the issue resurfaced on Monday (August 31). The same iON Digital Zone facility was being used for the AIIMS Common Recruitment Examination-5 (CRE-5). The institute cancelled the CRE-5 at two exam centres in Jaipur following a disruption caused by internal power supply issues, a source at AIIMS Delhi said.

The exam was conducted across the country on Monday (August 31), the source said. At the two affected centres — RJ0101 and RJ0102 at iON Digital Zone in Sitapura, Jaipur, operated by Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) — the test had commenced at 9 a.m. as scheduled.

However, the disruption subsequently affected the conduct of the examination, prompting AIIMS to cancel the test at the two centres. The decision, the institute said, was taken in the interest of the affected candidates and to ensure a fair, transparent and equitable recruitment process.
Around 2,000 candidates were registered at the two centres. Of these, 1,342 candidates appeared at the RJ0101 centre, and 436 at RJ0102.
AIIMS has scheduled a re-examination for the affected candidates on September 7, 2026.

The institute has also directed TCS, which operates the exam centres, to submit a detailed report on the incident. TCS has been instructed to preserve system logs, CCTV footage, and control room communications to facilitate a comprehensive assessment of the disruption.

The NEET-PG 2026 exam was successfully conducted for more than 2.63 lakh candidates across 1,111 centres in the country on Sunday (August 29), Venguswamy Ramaswamy, head of the iON Business Unit, TCS, said in a statement.

On Monday (August 31), the AIIMS CRE-5 was conducted for more than 21,000 candidates across 58 centres. The expert team from the vendors responsible for electrical maintenance was working on fixing the issue urgently. Further, all possible measures were being put in place to avoid recurrence of such issues in future, the TCS statement added.

“We deeply regret the inconvenience this has caused to the candidates undertaking the NEET-PG 2026 exam and AIIMS CRE at the centre and are working with the respective authorities to ensure that the candidates are able to complete these exams at the earliest,” the statement said.

Congress to hold massive protests over FIR against Rahul Gandhi: KC Venugopal
The FIR was registered by the Haldwani police on Sunday, a day after Rahul Gandhi addressed a press conference to seek a FIR over the ”purification ritual”

The FIR was registered by the Haldwani police on Sunday, a day after Gandhi addressed a press conference in New Delhi to demand that Prime Minister Narendra Modi order an FIR against those involved in the “purification” of the Ramlila ground at Haldwani.
Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said the FIR against Rahul Gandhi was a “shameless weaponisation of the state machinery” to target the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

Venugopal told the party’s state and district units to hold protest marches at the state and district headquarters on Monday evening to register their “vehement condemnation of this vendetta politics and to demand immediate legal action against the guilty BJP workers in Uttarakhand”.

The FIR, registered on a complaint by Amit Kumar, a member of Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas, accused Gandhi of offences under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and sections 196 (promoting enmity between classes) and 299 (malicious acts to outrage religious feelings) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The FIR said Gandhi wrongly described the cleaning and havan ritual as an act of “untouchability” and an atrocity against the Scheduled Caste community without verifying the facts.

Venugopal said the party’s fight against those who attack the values of social justice enshrined in the Constitution should continue and asked all party leaders at the state and district levels to participate in the protests.

He said party units should ensure the maximum mobilisation and media dissemination “to send an unyielding message: the Indian National Congress will not be intimidated by state-sponsored witch-hunts and will fight relentlessly for social justice, constitutional equality, and the dignity of every citizen.”

“The BJP’s blatant defence of this casteist behaviour and its shameless weaponisation of the state machinery to target the Leader of the Opposition unequivocally proves that they are the biggest perpetrators or protectors of social injustice today. They have demonstrated that they will deploy the entire might of the state to suppress anyone who dares to speak out against caste-based discrimination and Dalit atrocities,” he said.
Congress leaders Randeep Surjewala and Jairam Ramesh also attacked the BJP over the FIR.

In a post on X, Surjewala said, ”By registering an FIR against Shri Rahul Gandhi, the cowardly BJP government has revealed its true face. The Leader of the Opposition in the country and Congress President, Shri Mallikarjun Kharge ji, has publicly stated both inside and outside Parliament how the incident of purifying the stage after his speech deeply hurt his sentiments. Meanwhile, from CM Dhami to the BJP National General Secretary, they are all dispensing wisdom on the justification of this incident.”
Ramesh said Rahul Gandhi had raised the issue of injustice, humiliation, and discrimination faced by Dalits in his press conference, and the BJP-RSS took less than 24 hours to prove him right.

“He highlighted the issue of untouchability and humiliation carried out in the name of “purification” after the rally of Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge Ji in Uttarakhand, and demanded action against the BJP workers involved in it.

But this did not sit well with the BJP-RSS’s double-engine government in Uttarakhand. That’s why, even today, no action has been taken against the accused, but an FIR was filed against Rahul Gandhi Ji, who is demanding justice, the very next day,” said Jairam Ramesh.
