‘On our radar as threat’: Ex-army chief MM Naravane calls China India's competitor, Pakistan a security challenge
MM Naravane said China will serve as India's primary competitor across political, economic, trade, and military spheres in the coming years.

Former Army chief Manoj Mukund Naravane drew a comparison between the twin challenges of China and Pakistan that India faces on its borders. Naravane described China as India's "main competitor" in the years to come , while he said that Pakistan will continue to remain a key security challenge due to its support for terrorism.

Naravane made the remarks at the launch of his book The Curious and the Classified: Unearthing Myths and Mysteries in Pune on Friday. The former Army chief said India must distinguish between a competitor and an enemy, as he emphasised the need to resolve differences with China through dialogue while maintaining strong military deterrence.

"Pakistan and China are a totally different ballgame. We have fought wars with both of them. We have unsettled borders. So, they will always remain on our radar as a threat, as a challenge," Naravane was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.
On how India should deal with the two challenges, Naravane said the relative importance and priority accorded to the two would keep changing depending on the evolving situation.

"Because we have fought major wars with Pakistan and because of their continued support to terrorism, our attention is towards our western borders. But that attention towards the western borders is because of the terrorism angle," he was quoted as saying.

"That's the short-term aim and objective. I think we are very clear that in the long term and in the years to come, China is going to be our main competitor. And I purposely use the word competitor and not enemy," the former Army chief said.
‘China will compete with India’
He said that China would compete with India in multiple domains – political, economic, trade and military.

"Because they are going to be our main competitor in all fields. Political, economic, trade and of course military also. And wherever there is competition, there is always a little bit of conflict," he was quoted as saying.
Naravane stressed that India should seek to resolve such differences through talks and dialogue, with the use of force being the last resort.

"But it is up to us to try to resolve those conflicts, those differences through the mechanisms of talks, dialogues. And taking recourse to the use of force should always be the last resort. We should try our best to resolve disputes through dialogue," he said.
However, he maintained that a credible military deterrence is important.

"You have to have a strong deterrence to stop anybody from resorting to the use of force or any misadventure. And that is why the saying is there that if you want peace, prepare for war," Naravane said.
He also made remarks on situation in Pakistan and said that is for them to look into the internal matters.

"I think what is happening in Pakistan is for them to look at our policy of not interfering in the internal matters of neighbouring countries. Just as we don't like others interfering in our internal matters, I think we reciprocate by not interfering in the internal affairs of others," Naravane noted.
‘PoK an integral part of India’
On Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, he referred to India's parliamentary position and said the country's claim over the territory remains open-ended.
"As far as POK is concerned, there is a parliamentary resolution of sometime in the 80s, which says that POK is an integral part of the Union of India," he said.
He clarified that India's claim on POK did not necessarily imply the use of military force to capture the territory.

"It's not that it will be done by force of arms or forcefully; we will attack and capture POK. So, it is an open-ended resolution that we don't give up our claim on Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. That is part of the map of India, as we know it," he said.
On the question of the population in POK in the event of any future amalgamation, Naravane cited India's experience in the Northeast and said winning the confidence of people was a long-term process.

"As far as the populations are concerned, that will be, of course, a matter of concern. But it is up to us, just as we have won over the populations in our border states. Northeast was all insurgency," he said.

Bengal collects blood samples from relatives of people missing in Nepal flood
West Bengal is collecting blood samples from relatives of 37 people missing after the August 26 Nepal flash flood for DNA matching.

The West Bengal government has begun collecting blood samples from immediate family members of people missing in Nepal after the August 26 flash flood, with DNA profiles to be matched against those of bodies recovered during search operations.

“Blood samples are being collected from first-degree relatives of those who are still missing. The DNA profile reports will be sent to Nepal Police for matching with the DNA profile of the dead bodies recovered,” a senior police officer, aware of the developments, said.

At least 37 people from the state, mostly Kailash-Manasarovar pilgrims, remain missing. This includes an entire group of 30 pilgrims who were travelling with a Kolkata-based travel agency. The agency’s two staff members, who were travelling with the pilgrim team, also went missing.

“The blood sample of my mother-in-law was collected on Thursday. Officers from the local police station had come. There is still no news of my wife,” former TMC MLA Subhranshu Roy, son of former Union minister Mukul Roy, said.

Roy’s wife Sharmistha was a member of the pilgrim team that had left Kolkata on August 21. She had last contacted her family on the night of August 25. She spoke to her children. On August 26, the team was supposed to enter Tibet. They had reached the immigration centre at Kerung when the flash flood hit.
Also in the team was 61-year-old Subhash Chandra Ghosh, a former employee of Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) and a resident of Durgapur in West Burdwan.
“The police came and took us to the district hospital on Thursday where the blood sample was taken. They said that the DNA profiling would be done,” Ghosh’s elder daughter Gargi said.

“There is no news of Ghosh yet. He went alone with the team. His wife and two daughters didn’t go. He last updated his WhatsApp status from Rasuwa around 6:14 am on August 26. Thereafter his phone was found to be switched off,” Ghosh’s childhood friend Subhojit Sen told HT.

A senior officer of the state health department said that blood samples were being taken from first-degree relatives, which include father, mother, son and daughter, to prepare the autosomal STR DNA profile. All district hospitals and medical colleges have been authorised to collect the samples.
“The police and home department were coordinating. The samples are likely to be sent to the CFSL laboratory to get the profiling done,” a senior officer said.

India moves to buy 5 more S-400s after Op Sindoor success; Russia sends cost proposal

India’s decision to acquire five more S-400 Triumf air defence systems from Russia has gained further momentum with Moscow sending in Bill of Quantities (BOQ) proposal, which details the cost of construction and materials, to Delhi for the cost negotiations to begin.
The last of the five S-400 system contracted by the Narendra Modi government in 2018 at a cost of USD 5.43 billion will be reaching India in November this year.

The fifth S-400 system will be deployed in India’s eastern sector facing China.

During Operation Sindoor in May 2025, the S-400 system came out in flying colours with one of its long range missile targeting a Pakistan early airborne warning aircraft at a distance of 314 kilometers across the Indus in Pakistani heartland. Chennai: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government has been on a spree of cancelling several infrastructure projects approved or planned by the previous DMK regime, including the controversial Parandur airport, which was cancelled due to environmental concerns and to protect farmland. However, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on 30 August announced a thermal power plant in Thoothukudi.

The power plant will have two units of 800 MW each, a total of 1,600 MW, at an estimated cost of Rs 20,800 crore. It would be built under a public-private partnership at the existing Thoothukudi Thermal Power Station complex. The five old 210 MW units, operating since the late 1970s and adding up to 1,050 MW, will be progressively replaced. The net addition to capacity would be around 550 MW.

The announcement was not received well by conservationists since it further threatens the environment in Thoothukudi villages, which was the main reason the DMK did not go ahead with thermal power plants in the district.

G. Sundarrajan of Poovulagin Nanbargal, an NGO focused on environmental protection, pointed out that the ash pond of the five-decade-old Thoothukudi station was already full. He alleged that slurry was being dumped into the sea, which was an environmental violation that would only worsen with a new plant. “There will be no space for an ash pond if a new plant is built. This will affect the fishery and the fishing activity,” he said in a statement, post the announcement.

Tamil Nadu has committed to net-zero carbon emissions by 2050, which is ahead of India’s 2070 target, and aims for 50 percent of its energy from renewable sources of energy by 2030. A new thermal power plant directly contradicts the plan of the state on reducing carbon emissions.

In a video statement on X, Prabakaran Veera Arasu of the Poovulagin Nanbargal also noted that the pollution levels will increase in Thoothukudi and will be higher than that of Delhi if another power plant is installed.

He also stated that the previous DMK government had taken a policy decision not to start new thermal projects because of environmental concerns, choosing instead to complete only those already underway. He also said that people living in areas where thermal power plants are installed are severely affected.
Activists also emphasise that the TVK government should address issues in transmission of electricity produced out of solar panels, and focus on renewables.

Tamil Nadu, despite its strong potential for wind and solar power, lags behind major Indian states in renewable energy capacity addition. Its solar capacity stands at just 14,121 MW, far below Gujarat’s 33,763 MW and Rajasthan’s 44,135 MW.

While Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation Limited (TNGECL) has not invited fresh applications for new solar and wind projects since March, there is a need for new 400 kV or 765 kV substations in high-potential areas like Tirunelveli-Kanniyakumari.
The TVK government that cancelled previous-regime projects on environmental and livelihood grounds, ironically plans to expand the energy project that DMK avoided on the same grounds.

The government had stated that old units would be replaced with more efficient supercritical technology, and thermal power remained necessary for peak demand and grid stability. Meanwhile, the government is yet to respond to the issue on whether it would reconsider the decision on the new thermal power plant.

Congress replaces Bhupesh Baghel with Sachin Pilot as Punjab in-charge amid internal discord
The reshuffle comes ahead of Punjab’s 2027 assembly polls, with the party also assigning Randeep Surjewala to Gujarat and moving other state in-charges.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday removed Bhupesh Baghel as the general secretary in-charge of the poll-bound Punjab, replacing him with former Rajasthan deputy chief minister Sachin Pilot.
The party also appointed Randeep Surjewala as Gujarat in-charge, another state going to polls next year, shaking up the organisation ahead of the series of upcoming elections.
A total of three general secretaries have been allotted new states while another three leaders got dropped, according to a press release issued by party general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal.

The Congress has also moved its three more in-charges (apart from the general secretaries) to other states. A senior Congress leader remarked that this is one of the biggest reshuffles at the higher level of the party organisation.
Baghel, the former chief minister of Chhattisgarh, has been assigned Assam, where assembly elections were held in April this year.
The Congress, according to two insiders, “rewarded” Surjewala by bringing him to Gujarat while he will continue to hold “additional responsibility as in-charge of Karnataka”.

Karnataka gets fresh organisational focus
The reshuffle in Karnataka comes three months after DK Shivakumar was appointed the chief minister in June this year, replacing Siddaramaiah in a transition of power.

Appointed as Punjab in-charge in February 2025, Baghel’s removal comes amid his strained equation with former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi, who has been demanding that party’s Punjab unit chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring be replaced.
Channi had boycotted nearly all meetings chaired by Baghel in the past few months leading to an impasse that is affecting the poll preparations.

Baghel had backed status quo in Punjab

Last month, Baghel had submitted his report on Punjab to the party high command. It favoured no leadership change in the state. According to officials, Baghel was scheduled to go to Chandigarh on Sunday for further meetings.
In his tweet, Channi thanked the party leadership for the “important decision”.

“A warm welcome to Shri Sachin Pilot Ji on his appointment as General Secretary In-charge of Punjab Congress. Heartfelt thanks to the Congress Party High Command for this important decision,” Channi posted on X.

“Shri @bhupeshbaghel Ji has been a guide and mentor for @INCPunjab and all Congress workers in the state. His guidance has been instrumental in strengthening the party at the grassroots level. Personally, I have learnt a lot from him and will always remain indebted to him. Thankful for everything sir,” Warring wrote on X.
He also congratulated Pilot for his appointment. “His energy and dynamism will for sure add to the vigour of the party ahead of crucial assembly elections just a few months away.”

Punjab faces assembly election in early 2027.
In September 2021, the Congress had forced then Punjab chief minister Captain Amrinder Singh to resign and elevated Channi to the post before the polls in 2022.
Baghel’s removal also comes ahead of the proposed Punjab yatra of Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.
Baghel was deeply involved in the preparations for the yatra and held a meeting in Delhi last week.

“Gratitude to the top leadership for this new responsibility as the in-charge General Secretary of Assam Congress. Congratulations also to all newly appointed General Secretaries / State In-charges...We, all Congress workers of Chhattisgarh, are grateful for the able leadership of Congress General Secretary, the esteemed Shri Sachin Pilot Ji,” Baghel tweeted.

Pilot was handling party affairs in Chhattisgarh. A senior leader from Punjab told HT, “We now expect Channi to attend election-related meetings. The equation will also undergo a change as Pilot, 48, is younger to the 63-year-old Channi. The reshuffle was necessary as Channi is the head of the campaign committee.”
Pilot brings Rajasthan experience
Pilot brings considerable organisational experience to the assignment.

He served as Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee president from 2014 to 2020 and was deputy chief minister from 2018 to 2020. As PCC chief, he led the Congress campaign in Rajasthan after the party’s poor performance in the 2013 assembly elections and remained at the centre of the party’s organisational revival that culminated in its victory in the 2018 polls.

“His immediate task is likely to be less about organisational restructuring and more about ensuring that the competing factions work together on Rahul Gandhi’s proposed Punjab programme and the party’s election preparations,” said a Congress leader.
Pilot sets sights on Punjab polls
Meanwhile, Pilot said the upcoming election in Punjab would be an important opportunity for the party.

“I express my gratitude to the Congress President, the esteemed Shri@kharge ji, CPP Chairperson Smt. Sonia Gandhi ji, and the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Shri @RahulGandhi ji for assigning me the responsibility of Punjab in-charge. The elections to be held in the state in the coming days are an important opportunity for us. Our goal and resolve is to move forward with complete dedication and loyalty and to bring the party to power. I am confident that through collective efforts, a strong organization, and the hard work of the workers, we will strengthen the Congress in Punjab once again and pave the way for a return to power,” Pilot wrote on X.

More state in-charges reassigned
Congress MP Sukhdeo Bhagat has been given the charge of Chhattisgarh and Shrivel Prasad will handle Maharashtra affairs. PV Mohan, an AICC secretary, is made in charge of Andhra Pradesh.

Venugopal has announced that two general secretaries Jitendra Singh and party veteran Ramesh Chennithala have been dropped in the latest reshuffle. Tamil Nadu Congress president Manickam Tagore, who was in charge of Andhra Pradesh, has also been dropped.
Senior leader Mukul Wasnik will continue as General Secretary, AICC, Venugopal added.

Drug regulator cracks down after misbranded Abhayrab rabies vaccine seized in Delhi

A seized batch of Abhayrab rabies vaccine from an unlicensed Delhi premises was found misbranded and substandard. The finding has triggered tighter nationwide surveillance and legal action against unauthorised drug networks.

Regulatory and law enforcement agencies have intensified action against the illegal manufacture and distribution of spurious drugs after a batch of Abhayrab rabies vaccine was seized and later found to be misbranded, according to a notice from the Drugs Controller General of India.

The notice said the agencies are maintaining "strict and continuous surveillance" to identify and disrupt unauthorised drug supply networks and safeguard the quality and safety of medicines available to the public.

The action follows the seizure of Abhayrab rabies vaccine bearing batch number KE25012 from an unlicensed premises in Delhi's Mukherjee Nagar on April 22. The notice said the vaccine was found to be "misbranded" and "not manufactured by Indian Immunologicals Ltd.", while the Central Drugs Laboratory in Kasauli later reported it as "misbranded and not of standard quality".

As part of the enforcement action, Delhi Police's Crime Branch, along with drugs inspectors from the Delhi government's Drugs Control Department, searched the premises and seized the vaccine. Officials from the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation were then called in for legal sampling, and the samples were sent to the Central Drugs Laboratory, Kasauli, for examination. The laboratory's findings, including details of the misbranding detected in the seized product, were later communicated by the DCGI to states and Union territories for regulatory vigilance and necessary action.

In a communication dated August 27, the DCGI asked all state drug controllers to alert their inspectorate staff and maintain strict vigilance over the movement, distribution and availability of the affected batch. States were also asked to take appropriate regulatory action under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and the rules framed under it.

As a precautionary measure, the manufacturer of Abhayrab issued a public communication on the misbranded product and reaffirmed its commitment to quality, saying every batch of Abhayrab is released for sale only after independent testing and batch-release certification by the Central Drugs Laboratory, Kasauli.

The notice said vaccines given at hospitals, clinics and government healthcare facilities, or dispensed through licensed pharmacies, reach patients through the authorised and regulated supply chain after the prescribed quality-control and batch-release procedures. It also said no part of the batch in question was exported to any other country.

The seizure and follow-up action are part of an ongoing surveillance and enforcement mechanism to detect unauthorised manufacturing and distribution activities and prevent the circulation of misbranded and spurious medicines.

The development comes amid intensified scrutiny of the authenticity and quality of medicines supplied through unauthorised channels. "Four persons have been arrested by Delhi Police" in connection with the case, the notice said, adding that further investigation and appropriate legal action are being taken by the competent authorities.

Observing that the use of mobile phones is creating a negative impact among children, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday (September 5, 2026) said that mobile phones should be restricted in schools.

The Chief Minister who was addressing a gathering on the occasion of Teachers Day said that unless we address such issues there is no such significance of reforms in education or observing Teachers’ Day.

“My votes may perhaps decrease. But I will still say that the use of phones in schools needs to be regulated. In Gujarat, phones are not used in schools from Class I to Class XII,” Mr. Adhikari said. Earlier this year the Karnataka government had said that it was mulling over a law for restricting mobile phones for children under 16 years.

Speaking at the gathering in Kolkata the Chief Minister announced that two ‘CM Shri’ schools, modelled after PM Shri schools, will be opened in each district. “In these schools, admission will be given from Class VI based on merit. Like the Central Model School, the schools will have all modern facilities, including smart boards. Large sports-related institutions will be set up in the western and northern regions.” he said.
The Chief Minister also announced that his government would undertake teacher recruitment in a transparent manner in accordance with the directions of the Supreme Court and the Calcutta High Court.

“Merit will be the primary criterion for selection. We will recruit teachers in accordance with the directions of the Supreme Court and the Calcutta High Court. There is no need to worry. I have asked officials to ensure viva voce should not exceed five marks,” he said.

The Chief Minister said that his government has amended the OBC list and the fresh recruitment will be undertaken as per the amendment list. The West Bengal Legislative Assembly had recently passed two OBC amendment bills in June 2026, removing 77 communities (mostly added post-2010) and reverting the state’s OBC list back to the original 66 pre-2010 categories.

Allegations of corruption in the recruitment of teachers have surfaced in the previous Trinamool Congress government and several prominent leaders of the ruling party including former Education Minister Partha Chatterjee were arrested for the alleged involvement in the scam.

Jharkhand minister Sudivya Kumar dies of heart attack at 56
Jharkhand minister and senior JMM leader Sudivya Kumar died after a heart attack on Sunday. His sudden death has jolted the party and government, which called it an irreparable loss.
Jharkhand minister and senior Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) leader Sudivya Kumar died on Sunday, the party said. He was 56 and died of a heart attack, according to a JMM leader.

Kumar, a legislator from Giridih, held the Higher and Technical Education and Urban Development portfolios. He also had charge of Tourism, Arts and Culture, and Sports and Youth Affairs. His death has left the JMM and the Jharkhand government mourning the loss of a senior leader and minister.
In a condolence message posted on X, Chief Minister Hemant Soren shared a heartfelt tribute for Kumar, whom he referred to as "Sonu Bhaiya."

"Sonu Bhaiya was not just a senior colleague or political associate to me. He was like an elder brother – affectionate, guiding, and steadfastly standing by my side in every difficult time. The moments spent with him and the lessons learnt from him will always remain with me," he wrote (in Hindi).

The Jharkhand CM added, "As a dedicated soldier of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, he devoted his entire life to the fight for Jharkhand's identity, rights, and pride. His dedication to Jharkhandiyat and his indomitable spirit will always be remembered."

The JMM also expressed shock and grief over Kumar's death, calling it an "irreparable loss" to the party, the government and Jharkhand. "The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha family is stunned and heart-broken by the untimely demise of Sudivya Kumar, a dedicated comrade of JMM and a Minister in Jharkhand government," the party said in a post on X.
The party also conveyed condolences to Kumar’s family and prayed for peace to the departed soul. He is survived by two daughters and a son.

Kumar was first elected to the Jharkhand Assembly from Giridih in 2019. A close aide of Chief Minister Hemant Soren, he played a key role in managing crises within the JMM, including during Soren’s arrest in 2024 in connection with an alleged land fraud and money laundering case.

He had returned this week from Karnataka, where he led a Jharkhand government delegation to explore ways to improve tourism infrastructure management in the state. Jharkhand higher education minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu dies of cardiac arrest
Jharkhand Higher and Technical Education Minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu died of cardiac arrest at 56. The JMM leader was a two-term Giridih MLA.
Jharkhand Higher and Technical Education Minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu died of cardiac arrest at a private hospital in Giridih in the early hours of Sunday, people aware of the development said.
The 56-year-old Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) leader and two-term Giridih MLA had complained of discomfort at his residence before being rushed to the hospital, where he died during treatment.
“He was taken to a private hospital in Giridih but could not survive. Official announcement would be made soon,” a senior official said.

JMM leader and state transport minister Deepak Birua said in a social media post, “I am deeply saddened by the passing of my colleague and fellow minister in the Jharkhand government, Sudivya Sonu ji. His health suddenly deteriorated last night, and he passed away while undergoing treatment at the hospital. May God grant peace to his soul and give his family the strength to bear this grief. This is a huge loss for the JMM family. A tearful final ‘Johar’, brother,” said Birua.

Dinesh Sharma, ex-UP Deputy CM, appointed Andaman and Nicobar Lt Governor

BJP Rajya Sabha MP Dinesh Sharma has been appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The former Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister said the post was a commitment to the Constitution, the nation and public service.

BJP Rajya Sabha MP and former Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Dinesh Sharma was appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands on Saturday, the Rashtrapati Bhavan said in a late-night communique.
Sharma, 62, will succeed Admiral D K Joshi (retd), who has served as the Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory since October 8, 2017.
"The President of India is pleased to appoint Dr Dinesh Sharma as Lt Governor of Andaman and Nicobar Islands with effect from the date he assumes charge of his office," the Rashtrapati Bhavan said.
Following his appointment, Sharma expressed gratitude to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and the BJP's central leadership in a post on X.
"Hon'ble President, Hon'ble Prime Minister, Hon'ble Home Minister, and the party's central leadership -- my heartfelt thanks," Sharma said.

He thanked senior leaders, well-wishers, friends and citizens for their continued support and blessings, saying the new responsibility was not merely a position but a commitment to the Constitution, the nation and public service.
"I pledge to fulfill this duty with complete devotion, honesty, and dedication," he said, adding that he hoped their affection, trust and blessings would continue.

Sharma, a former deputy chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, is currently a BJP member of the Rajya Sabha and serves as its vice chairperson. His term in the Upper House was scheduled to end on November 25.
